<uig rom="belciger">ᠪᠡᠯᠴᠢᠭᠡᠷ</uig> pasturage < <uig rom="belcige-">ᠪᠡᠯᠴᠢᠭᠡ ᠎</uig> to pasture
<uig rom="irüger">ᠢᠷᠦᠭᠡᠷ</uig> > <uig rom="irügel">ᠢᠷᠦᠭᠡᠯ</uig> prayer, blessing < <uig rom="irüge-">ᠢᠷᠦᠭᠡ ᠎</uig> to bless

entry.title: Drittes Capitel - Regeln der Wortfügung oder Syntax - Rection des Verbi

paragraphs.paragraph: Mit dem Dativ und dessen Partikel <uig rom="">ᠳᠤᠷ</uig> können sich zwar nicht alle, doch aber eine gute Anzahl derjenigen Verba verbinden, die auch im Deutschen im Dative stehen. Dazu gehören:

a) Mehrere Verba, die ohne Person gebraucht werden können, als ᠨᠠᠳᠤᠷ ᠵᠣᠺᠢᠮᠤᠢ es bekommt mir, ᠨᠠᠳᠤᠷ ᠣᠴᠢᠷᠠᠮᠤᠢ es begegnet mir, ᠨᠠᠳᠤᠷ ᠳᠤᠳᠠᠮᠤᠢ es fehlt, gebricht, mangelt mir, ᠨᠠᠳᠤᠷ ᠳᠤᠰᠤᠯᠠᠮᠤᠢ es hilft oder nützt mir u. a. mehr. Andere Verba der Art werden indess im Mongolischen nur persönlich gebraucht, als ᠪᠢ ᠵᠢᠭᠰᠢᠮᠦᠢ mir ekelt (im Abl.), ᠪᠢ ᠵᠡᠭᠦᠳᠦᠯᠡᠮᠦᠢ mir träumt.

b) Viele Intransitiva, als ᠣᠴᠢᠷᠠᠬᠤ begegnen, ᠪᠠᠶᠢᠬᠤ bleiben, ᠳᠠᠭᠠᠯᠠᠬᠤ gefallen, Gefallen haben, ᠠᠳᠠᠯᠢᠳᠬᠤ gleichen, ᠱᠠᠩᠨᠠᠬᠤ lohnen, ᠣᠶᠢᠷᠠᠳᠠᠬᠤ nahen, ᠰᠢᠳᠠᠷᠳᠠᠬᠤ sich nähern, ᠥᠭᠦᠯᠡᠺᠦ sagen, sprechen, ᠰᠢᠳᠦᠺᠦ vertrauen, ᠡᠰᠡᠷᠭᠦᠴᠡᠺᠦ widerstehen, ᠬᠠᠨᠤᠬᠤ danken, sich zufrieden bezeigen, und viele andre, die alle im Deutschen gleichfalls den Dativ haben.
Mehrere, im Deutschen mit dem Dativ stehende, Verba haben im Mongolischen den Accusativ, als ᠢᠳᠡᠭᠡᠺᠦ glauben, ᠬᠠᠷᠢᠶᠠᠬᠤ fluchen, ᠵᠠᠨᠤᠬᠤ drohen, ᠴᠢᠩᠨᠠᠬᠤ horchen, ᠳᠠᠭᠤᠷᠢᠶᠠᠬᠤ nachahmen, noch andere den Ablativ, als ᠵᠠᠶᠢᠯᠠᠬᠤ ausweichen, ᠲᠤᠳᠠᠭᠠᠬᠤ fliehen. Andere Verba dieser Art sind zweifelhaft und finden sich sowohl im Dativ als im Accusativ, ohne dass man bis jetzt über die richtigere Stellung entscheiden könnte.
Suffix <uig rom="-ri">᠎ᠷᠢ</uig> .
Function: to form nouns designating place or result of an action.
<uig rom="saγuri">ᠰᠠᠭᠤᠷᠢ</uig> seat < <uig rom="saγu-">ᠰᠠᠭᠤ ᠎</uig> to sit
<uig rom="baγuri">ᠪᠠᠭᠤᠷᠢ</uig> slope < <uig rom="baγu-">ᠪᠠᠭᠤ ᠎</uig> to descend
<uig rom="nemeri">ᠨᠡᠮᠡᠷᠢ</uig> supplement < <uig rom="neme-">ᠨᠡᠮᠡ ᠎</uig> to add

entry.title: Drittes Capitel - Regeln der Wortfügung oder Syntax - Rection des Verbi

paragraphs.paragraph: Die Mongolischen Passiva haben das Eigenthümliche, dass die Mehrzahl derselben, die im Deutschen mit der Präposition von stehen, welches im Mongolischen der Ablativ wäre, mit dem Dativ gehen. So sagt man z. B. nicht ᠡᠴᠢᠭᠡ ᠡᠴᠡ ᠴᠣᠺᠢᠭᠳᠠᠪᠠᠢ sondern ᠡᠴᠢᠭᠡ ᠳ᠋ᠤᠷ ᠴᠣᠺᠢᠭᠳᠠᠪᠠᠢ er wurde vom Vater geschlagen, ferner ᠪᠠᠭᠰᠢ ᠳ᠋ᠤᠷ ᠮᠠᠭᠳᠠᠭᠳᠠᠪᠠᠢ er wurde vom Lehrer gelobt, ᠳᠠᠶᠢᠰᠤᠨ ᠳ᠋ᠤᠷ ᠠᠪᠳᠠᠪᠠᠢ er wurde vom Feinde entführt, ᠪᠦᠯᠡᠰ ᠲᠤᠷ ᠢᠶᠡᠨ ᠺᠦᠭᠡᠭᠳᠡᠪᠡᠢ er wurde von seinem Hausgesinde verjagt, ᠡᠪᠡᠰᠦᠨ ᠢᠨᠤ ᠮᠠᠯ ᠳ᠋ᠤᠷ ᠢᠳᠡᠭᠳᠡᠮᠦᠢ das Gras wird vom Vieh gegessen, ᠴᠡᠴᠡᠭ ᠢᠨᠤ ᠨᠢᠭᠡᠨ ᠺᠡᠦᠺᠡᠨ ᠳ᠋ᠤᠷ ᠳᠡᠭᠦᠭᠳᠡᠪᠡᠢ die Blume wurde von einem Kinde gepflückt, ᠣᠯᠠᠨ ᠳ᠋ᠤᠷ ᠳᠠᠨᠢᠭᠳᠠᠪᠠᠢ er wurde von Vielen erkannt. Dass übrigens mehrere Deutsche Intransitiva die vollkommene persönliche Passivform annehmen können, deren sie im Deutschen nicht fähig sind, ist bereits §124 bemerkt. Auch diese stehen grösstentheils mit dem Dativ.
Suffix <uig rom="-sun/-sün">᠎ᠰᠤᠨ</uig> .
Function: to form nouns designating results of an actions.
<uig rom="nilbusun">ᠨᠢᠯᠪᠤᠰᠤᠨ</uig> spittle < <uig rom="nilbu-">ᠨᠢᠯᠪᠤ ᠎</uig> to spit
<uig rom="kögesün">ᠺᠥᠭᠡᠰᠦᠨ</uig> foam < <uig rom="köge-">ᠺᠥᠭᠡ ᠎</uig> to foam, to rise
Suffix <uig rom="si">ᠰᠢ</uig> .
Function : to form nouns designating result or object of an action.
<uig rom="idesi">ᠢᠳᠡᠰᠢ</uig> food < <uig rom="ide-">ᠢᠳᠡ ᠎</uig> to eat
<uig rom="bulasi">ᠪᠤᠯᠠᠰᠢ</uig> grave, excavation < <uig rom="bula-">ᠪᠤᠯᠠ ᠎</uig> to dig
Suffix <uig rom="-si">᠎ᠰᠢ</uig> with the negative <uig rom="ügei">ᠦᠭᠡᠢ</uig> .
Function: to form nouns designating qualities rendering something unfit to act on.
<uig rom="dabasi ügei">ᠳᠠᠪᠠᠰᠢ ᠦᠭᠡᠢ</uig> unpassable < <uig rom="daba-">ᠳᠠᠪᠠ ᠎</uig> to pass
<uig rom="uγusi ügei">ᠤᠭᠤᠰᠢ ᠦᠭᠡᠢ</uig> not potable < <uig rom="uγu-">ᠤᠭᠤ ᠎</uig> to drink
Suffix <uig rom="-du/-dü">᠎ᠳᠤ</uig> added to adverbs of place.
Function: to form locative adjectives.
<uig rom="dooradu">ᠳᠣᠣᠷᠠᠳᠤ</uig> inferior, lower < <uig rom="door-a">ᠳᠣᠣᠷ᠎ᠠ</uig> below
<uig rom="degedü">ᠳᠡᠭᠡᠳᠦ</uig> upper cf. <uig rom="deger-e">ᠳᠡᠭᠡᠷ᠎ᠡ</uig> on, above
<uig rom="emünedü">ᠡᠮᠦᠨᠡᠳᠦ</uig> being in front < <uig rom="emün-e">ᠡᠮᠦᠨ᠎ᠡ</uig> before, in front of
<uig rom="dotoγadu">ᠳᠣᠲᠣᠭᠠᠳᠤ</uig> inner cf. <uig rom="dotor-a">ᠳᠣᠲᠣᠷ᠎ᠠ</uig> in, within
<uig rom="γadaγadu">ᠭᠠᠳᠠᠭᠠᠳᠤ</uig> outer cf. <uig rom="γadan-a">ᠭᠠᠳᠠᠨ᠎ᠠ</uig> outside
<uig rom="inadu">ᠢᠨᠠᠳᠤ</uig> being on this side cf. <uig rom="inaqsi">ᠢᠨᠠᠬᠰᠢ</uig> to this place
Suffix <uig rom="-ki">᠎ᠺᠢ</uig> added to various adverbs.
Function: to form adjectives expressing the same general idea as that of the primary adverb.
<uig rom="degereki">ᠳᠡᠭᠡᠷᠡᠺᠢ</uig> upper < <uig rom="deger-e">ᠳᠡᠭᠡᠷ᠎ᠡ</uig> on, above
<uig rom="dooraki">ᠳᠣᠣᠷᠠᠺᠢ</uig> lower < <uig rom="door-a">ᠳᠣᠣᠷ᠎ᠠ</uig> below, under
<uig rom="edügeki">ᠡᠳᠦᠭᠡᠺᠢ</uig> present < <uig rom="edüge">ᠡᠳᠦᠭᠡ</uig> now
<uig rom="endeki">ᠡᠨᠳᠡᠺᠢ</uig> being here < <uig rom="ende">ᠡᠨᠳᠡ</uig> here
<uig rom="tendeki">ᠲᠡᠨᠳᠡᠺᠢ</uig> being there < <uig rom="tende">ᠲᠡᠨᠳᠡ</uig> there
<uig rom="marγasiki">ᠮᠠᠷᠭᠠᠰᠢᠺᠢ</uig> taking place tomorrow < <uig rom="marγasi">ᠮᠠᠷᠭᠠᠰᠢ</uig> tomorrow

The pronouns consist of personal, possessive, demonstrative, interrogative, reflexive, and indefinite pronouns. The personal and demonstrative pronouns differ, morphologically, from the nouns in the respect that their nominative form and their stems are not identical.

The first person plural is <uig rom="bida">ᠪᠢᠳᠠ </uig> and <uig rom="ba">ᠪᠠ</uig> . The former is an inclusive pronoun "we" (including both the persons speaking and the audience), the latter is an exclusive pronoun "we" (including only the persons speaking and excluding the audience). The nominative <uig rom="ba">ᠪᠠ</uig> occurs in ancient books. In modern books this is replaced by <uig rom="bida">ᠪᠢᠳᠠ</uig> , whereas the oblique cases are still used.

The nominative *i "he" and *a "they" are not attested even in the most ancient books. Of the oblique cases, only the genitive is used in modern books, but some of the remaining oblique cases are attested in books of the pre-classical period.
The possessive pronouns are derived with the suffix <uig rom="-qai">᠎ᠬᠠᠢ</uig> from the genitive of the personal pronouns.
<uig rom="minuqai">ᠮᠢᠨᠤᠬᠠᠢ</uig> mine < <uig rom="minu">ᠮᠢᠨᠤ</uig> , gen. of <uig rom="bi">ᠪᠢ</uig>
<uig rom="cinuqai">ᠴᠢᠨᠤᠬᠠᠢ</uig> thine < <uig rom="cinu">ᠴᠢᠨᠤ</uig> , gen. of <uig rom="ci">ᠴᠢ</uig>
<uig rom="bidanuqai">ᠪᠢᠳᠠᠨᠤᠬᠠᠢ</uig> (rare) ours < <uig rom="bidan-u">ᠪᠢᠳᠠᠨ ᠤ</uig> , gen. of <uig rom="bida">ᠪᠢᠳᠠ</uig>
<uig rom="manuqai">ᠮᠠᠨᠤᠬᠠᠢ</uig> (usual) ours < <uig rom="manu">ᠮᠠᠨᠤ</uig> gen. of <uig rom="ba">ᠪᠠ</uig>
<uig rom="tanuqai">ᠲᠠᠨᠤᠬᠠᠢ</uig> yours < <uig rom="tanu">ᠲᠠᠨᠤ</uig> , gen. of <uig rom="ta">ᠲᠠᠨ</uig>

Sometimes the back vocalic forms <uig rom="minuqai">ᠮᠢᠨᠤᠬᠠᠢ</uig> and <uig rom="cinuqai">ᠴᠢᠨᠤᠬᠠᠢ</uig> are replaced by front vocalic forms <uig rom="minükei">ᠮᠢᠨᠦᠺᠡᠢ</uig> and <uig rom="cinükei">ᠴᠢᠨᠦᠺᠡᠢ</uig> .

There are no possessive pronouns derived from the personal pronouns of the third person. Instead the forms <uig rom="tegünükei">ᠲᠡᠭᠦᠨᠦᠺᠡᠢ</uig> "his" and <uig rom="tedenükei">ᠲᠡᠳᠡᠨᠦᠺᠡᠢ</uig> "theirs", which are derived from the demonstrative pronouns, are used.
There are the following demonstrative pronouns
<uig rom="ene">ᠡᠨᠡ</uig> this, stem <uig rom="egün">ᠡᠭᠦᠨ</uig>
<uig rom="ede">ᠡᠳᠡ</uig> these, stem <uig rom="eden ">ᠡᠳᠡᠨ</uig>
<uig rom="edeger">ᠡᠳᠡᠭᠡᠷ</uig> these, stem <uig rom="edeger">ᠡᠳᠡᠭᠡᠷ</uig>
<uig rom="ele">ᠡᠯᠡ</uig> this (indeclinable)
<uig rom="eyimü">ᠡᠶᠢᠮᠦ</uig> such as this, stem <uig rom="eyimü">ᠡᠶᠢᠮᠦ</uig>
<uig rom="edüi">ᠡᠳᠦᠢ</uig> as much as this, stem <uig rom="edüi">ᠡᠳᠦᠢ</uig>
<uig rom="edün">ᠡᠳᠦᠨ</uig> as many as these, stem <uig rom="edün">ᠡᠳᠦᠨ</uig> (only in ancient language)
<uig rom="tere">ᠲᠡᠷᠡ</uig> that, stem <uig rom="tegün">ᠲᠡᠭᠦᠨ</uig>
<uig rom="tede">ᠲᠡᠳᠡ</uig> those, stem <uig rom="teden">ᠲᠡᠳᠡᠨ</uig>
<uig rom="tedeger">ᠲᠡᠳᠡᠭᠡᠷ</uig> those, stem <uig rom="tedeger">ᠲᠡᠳᠡᠭᠡᠷ</uig>
<uig rom="teyimü">ᠲᠡᠶᠢᠮᠦ</uig> like that, stem <uig rom="teyimü">ᠲᠡᠶᠢᠮᠦ</uig>
<uig rom="tedüi">ᠲᠡᠳᠦᠢ</uig> as much as that, stem <uig rom="tedüi">ᠲᠡᠳᠦᠢ</uig>
<uig rom="tedün">ᠲᠡᠳᠦᠨ</uig> as many as those, stem <uig rom="tedün">ᠲᠡᠳᠦᠨ</uig> (only in ancient language)
<uig rom="mön">ᠮᠥᠨ</uig> the same, just this, stem <uig rom="mön">ᠮᠥᠨ</uig>
<uig rom="möd">ᠮᠥᠳ</uig> (in ancient language) these same, just these, stem <uig rom="möd">ᠮᠥᠳ</uig>
<uig rom="önö">ᠥᠨᠦ</uig> or <uig rom="önüge">ᠥᠨᠦᠭᠡ</uig> this (indeclinable)

The pronouns <uig rom="ene">ᠡᠨᠡ</uig> , <uig rom="ede">ᠡᠳᠡ</uig> , <uig rom="edeger">ᠡᠳᠡᠭᠡᠷ</uig> , <uig rom="tere">ᠲᠡᠷᠡ</uig> , <uig rom="tede">ᠲᠡᠳᠡ</uig> , <uig rom="tedeger">ᠲᠡᠳᠡᠭᠡᠷ</uig> replace the personal pronouns of the third person.
There are diminutive forms <uig rom="eneken">ᠡᠨᠡᠺᠡᠨ</uig> "this" and <uig rom="tereken">ᠲᠡᠷᠡᠺᠡᠨ</uig> "that".

entry.title: Derivation - Pronouns - Interrogative pronouns and adverbs

paragraphs.paragraph: The nominative forms and the stems of the interrogative pronouns coincide with few exceptions.
<uig rom="ken">ᠺᠡᠨ</uig> who (singular)
<uig rom="ked">ᠺᠡᠳ</uig> who (plural)
<uig rom="kedüi">ᠺᠡᠳᠦᠢ</uig> (singular) how much
<uig rom="kedün">ᠺᠡᠳᠦᠨ</uig> (plural) how many
<uig rom="ker">ᠺᠡᠷ</uig> (indeclinable) how
<uig rom="keli">ᠺᠡᠯᠢ</uig> (indeclinable) when (pre-classical)
<uig rom="kejiy-e">ᠺᠡᠵᠢᠶ᠎ᠡ</uig> (stem kejiyen) when
<uig rom="yaγun">ᠶᠠᠭᠤᠨ</uig> (as adjective and substantive) what
<uig rom="yambar">ᠶᠠᠮᠪᠠᠷ</uig> (indeclinable, only as adjective) what
<uig rom="yan">ᠶᠠᠨ</uig> (in pre-classical language) what
<uig rom="ali">ᠠᠯᠢ</uig> (stem alin) which
In the pre-classical language the interrogative pronouns are used also as relative pronouns.
There are the following reflexive pronouns:
<uig rom="öber-iyen">ᠥᠪᠡᠷ᠎ᠢᠶᠡᠨ</uig> (stem <uig rom="öber">ᠥᠪᠡᠷ</uig> ) self
<uig rom="öbesüd-iyen">ᠥᠪᠡᠰᠦᠳ᠎ᠢᠶᠡᠨ</uig> or (seldom) <uig rom="ögesüd-iyen">ᠥᠭᠡᠰᠦᠳ᠎ᠢᠶᠡᠨ</uig> (stems <uig rom="öbesüd">ᠥᠪᠡᠰᠦᠳ</uig> and <uig rom="ögesüd">ᠥᠭᠡᠰᠦᠳ</uig> ) selves

The indefinite pronouns are derived from the interrogative pronouns with the particles <uig rom="ba">ᠪᠠ</uig> , <uig rom="ber">ᠪᠡᠷ</uig> , <uig rom="cu">ᠴᠤ</uig> . The particle <uig rom="cu">ᠴᠤ</uig> occurs mainly in the modern language whereas the particles <uig rom="ba">ᠪᠠ</uig> and <uig rom="ber">ᠪᠡᠷ</uig> are more characteristic of the classical language.
<uig rom="ken ba">ᠺᠡᠨ ᠪᠠ</uig> whoever, somebody, someone, anybody
<uig rom="ked ba">ᠺᠡᠳ ᠪᠠ</uig> (plural)
<uig rom="ken ber">ᠺᠡᠨ ᠪᠡᠷ</uig> whoever, somebody, someone, anybody
<uig rom="ked ber">ᠺᠡᠳ ᠪᠡᠷ</uig> (plural)
<uig rom="ken cu">ᠺᠡᠨ ᠴᠤ</uig> whoever, somebody, someone, anybody
<uig rom="ked cu">ᠺᠡᠳ ᠴᠤ</uig> (plural)
<uig rom="kedüi ba">ᠺᠡᠳᠦᠢ ᠪᠠ</uig> any quantity
<uig rom="kedüi ber">ᠺᠡᠳᠦᠢ ᠪᠡᠷ</uig>
<uig rom="kedüi cu">ᠺᠡᠳᠦᠢ ᠴᠤ</uig>
<uig rom="yaγun ba">ᠶᠠᠭᠤᠨ ᠪᠠ</uig> or <uig rom="yaγuba">ᠶᠠᠭᠤᠪᠠ</uig> whatever
<uig rom="yaγun ber">ᠶᠠᠭᠤᠨ ᠪᠡᠷ</uig>
<uig rom="yaγun cu">ᠶᠠᠭᠤᠨ ᠴᠤ</uig>
<uig rom="yambar ba">ᠶᠠᠮᠪᠠᠷ ᠪᠠ</uig> whatever, any
<uig rom="yambar ber">ᠶᠠᠮᠪᠠᠷ ᠪᠡᠷ</uig>
<uig rom="yambar cu">ᠶᠠᠮᠪᠠᠷ ᠴᠤ</uig>
<uig rom="aliba">ᠠᠯᠢᠪᠠ</uig> whoever, whatever, anybody
<uig rom="ali ber">ᠠᠯᠢ ᠪᠡᠷ</uig>
<uig rom="alin cu ">ᠠᠯᠢᠨ ᠴᠤ</uig>
The pronoun <uig rom="yaγuma">ᠶᠠᠭᠤᠮᠠ</uig> or <uig rom="yaγum-a">ᠶᠠᠭᠤᠮ᠎ᠠ</uig> "something", "anything", also "thing" is formed with <uig rom="-ma">᠎ᠮᠠ</uig> .
The indefinite pronouns occur with the negative <uig rom="ügei">ᠦᠭᠡᠢ</uig>
<uig rom="ken ba ügei">ᠺᠡᠨ ᠪᠠ ᠦᠭᠡᠢ</uig> or <uig rom="ken ber ügei">ᠺᠡᠨ ᠪᠡᠷ ᠦᠭᠡᠢ</uig> or <uig rom="ken cu ügei">ᠺᠡᠨ ᠴᠤ ᠦᠭᠡᠢ</uig> nobody
<uig rom="yaγun ba ügei">ᠶᠠᠭᠤᠨ ᠪᠠ ᠦᠭᠡᠢ</uig> or <uig rom="yaγun ber ügei">ᠶᠠᠭᠤᠨ ᠪᠡᠷ ᠦᠭᠡᠢ</uig> or <uig rom="yaγun cu ügei">ᠶᠠᠭᠤᠨ ᠴᠤ ᠦᠭᠡᠢ</uig> nothing
The numerals are classified as cardinal, ordinal, collective, distributive, multiplicative, and diminutive numerals.
When used as substantives, they are declinable and can form the plural.
The cardinal numerals are the following :
1 <uig rom="nigen">ᠨᠢᠭᠡᠨ</uig> (ancient pronunciation niken)
2 <uig rom="qoyar">ᠬᠣᠶᠠᠷ</uig>
3 <uig rom="γurban">ᠭᠤᠷᠪᠠᠨ</uig>
4 <uig rom="dörben">ᠳᠥᠷᠪᠡᠨ</uig>
5 <uig rom="tabun">ᠲᠠᠪᠤᠨ</uig>
6 <uig rom="jirγuγan">ᠵᠢᠷᠭᠤᠭᠠᠨ</uig>
7 <uig rom="doloγan">ᠳᠣᠯᠣᠭᠠᠨ</uig>
8 <uig rom="naiman">ᠨᠠᠢᠮᠠᠨ</uig>
9 <uig rom="yisün">ᠶᠢᠰᠦᠨ</uig>
10 <uig rom="arban">ᠠᠷᠪᠠᠨ</uig>
11 <uig rom="arban nigen">ᠠᠷᠪᠠᠨ ᠨᠢᠭᠡᠨ</uig> (ancient pronunciation arban niken)
20 <uig rom="qorin">ᠬᠣᠷᠢᠨ</uig>
30 <uig rom="γucin">ᠭᠤᠴᠢᠨ</uig>
40 <uig rom="döcin">ᠳᠥᠴᠢᠨ</uig>
50 <uig rom="tabin">ᠲᠠᠪᠢᠨ</uig>
60 <uig rom="jiran">ᠵᠢᠷᠠᠨ</uig>
70 <uig rom="dalan">ᠳᠠᠯᠠᠨ</uig>
80 <uig rom="nayan">ᠨᠠᠶᠠᠨ</uig>
90 <uig rom="yeren">ᠶᠡᠷᠡᠨ</uig>
100 <uig rom="jaγun">ᠵᠠᠭᠤᠨ</uig>
1000 <uig rom="mingγan">ᠮᠢᠩᠭᠠᠨ</uig>
10 000 <uig rom=tümen"">ᠲᠦᠮᠡᠨ</uig>
100 000 <uig rom="bum">ᠪᠤᠮ</uig>
1 000 000 <uig rom="say-a">ᠰᠠᠶ᠎ᠠ</uig>
The last three numerals (<uig rom="tümen">ᠲᠦᠮᠡᠨ</uig> , <uig rom="bum">ᠪᠤᠮ</uig> , and <uig rom="say-a">ᠰᠠᠶ᠎ᠠ</uig> ) do not have ordinal or any other forms.
The Mongolian figures are written from left to right, as Arabic figures :
In ancient texts there occurs another numeral, <uig rom="jirin">ᠵᠢᠷᠢᠨ</uig> "two", which is used in reference to women: <uig rom="jirin qatud">ᠵᠢᠷᠢᠨ ᠬᠠᠲᠤᠳ</uig> "two dames".
The higher numerals are of Tibetan origin
100,000 <uig rom="bum">ᠪᠤᠮ</uig> < Tib. 'bum
1,000,000 <uig rom="say-a">ᠰᠠᠶ᠎ᠠ</uig> < Tib. sa-ya
10,000,000 <uig rom="bsiba">ᠪᠰᠢᠪᠠ</uig> or <uig rom="biyeba">ᠪᠢᠶᠡᠳᠠ</uig> (pronounced jiva) < Tib. bye ba
100,000,000 <uig rom="düngsiür">ᠳᠦᠩᠰᠢᠦᠷ</uig> (pronounced düngsür) < Tib. dung 'phyur
In modern books, especially those published in Outer Mongolia, the European word <uig rom="miliyon">ᠮᠢᠯᠢᠶᠣᠨ</uig> "million" is used.
Ten thousand is either <uig rom="tümen">ᠲᠦᠮᠡᠨ</uig> or <uig rom="arban mingγan">ᠠᠷᠪᠠᠨ ᠮᠢᠩᠭᠠᠨ</uig> . The former also expresses immense quantities.

The numbers 20,000, 30,000, etc. are composed of 2 or 3 and <uig rom="tümen">ᠲᠦᠮᠡᠨ</uig> or of 20 or 30 and <uig rom="mingγan">ᠮᠢᠩᠭᠠᠨ:</uig> : 20,000 <uig rom="qoyar tümen">ᠬᠣᠶᠠᠷ ᠲᠦᠮᠡᠨ</uig> or <uig rom="qorin mingγan">ᠬᠣᠷᠢᠨ ᠮᠢᠩᠭᠠᠨ</uig> : 30,000 <uig rom="γurban tümen">ᠭᠤᠷᠪᠠᠨ ᠲᠦᠮᠡᠨ</uig> or <uig rom="γucin mingγan">ᠭᠤᠴᠢᠨ ᠮᠢᠩᠭᠠᠨ</uig>
The composite numerals 11 to 19 are composed of <uig rom="arban">ᠠᠷᠪᠠᠨ</uig> and <uig rom="nigen">ᠨᠢᠭᠡᠨ</uig> , etc.; 21 to 29 is <uig rom="qorin nigen">ᠬᠣᠷᠢᠨ ᠨᠢᠭᠡᠨ</uig> etc.'
Suffix <uig rom="-duγar/-düger">ᠳᠤᠭᠠᠷ/ᠳᠦᠭᠡᠷ</uig> with the final consonant and the ending <uig rom=" -γan">ᠭᠠᠨ</uig> of the cardinal numeral dropped.
<uig rom="nigedüger">ᠨᠢᠭᠡᠳᠦᠭᠡᠷ</uig> first
<uig rom="qoyaduγar">ᠬᠣᠶᠠᠳᠤᠭᠠᠷ</uig> second
<uig rom="γurbaduγar">ᠭᠤᠷᠪᠠᠳᠤᠭᠠᠷ</uig> third
<uig rom="dörbedüger">ᠳᠥᠷᠪᠡᠳᠦᠭᠡᠷ</uig> fourth
<uig rom="tabuduγar">ᠲᠠᠪᠤᠳᠤᠭᠠᠷ</uig> fifth
<uig rom="jirγuduγar">ᠵᠢᠷᠭᠤᠳᠤᠭᠠᠷ</uig> sixth
<uig rom="doloduγar">ᠳᠣᠯᠣᠳᠤᠭᠠᠷ</uig> seventh
<uig rom="naimaduγar">ᠨᠠᠢᠮᠠᠳᠤᠭᠠᠷ</uig> eighth
<uig rom="yisüdüger">ᠶᠢᠰᠦᠳᠦᠭᠡᠷ</uig> ninth
<uig rom="arbaduγar">ᠠᠷᠪᠠᠳᠤᠭᠠᠷ</uig> tenth
In both the pre-classical and classical languages the ordinal numerals "third", "fourth", and "fifth" usually occur in the following forms:
<uig rom="γutuγar">ᠭᠤᠲᠤᠭᠠᠷ</uig> third, <uig rom="dötüger">ᠳᠥᠲᠦᠭᠡᠷ</uig> fourth, <uig rom="tabtaγar">ᠲᠠᠪᠲᠠᠭᠠᠷ</uig> fifth
Instead of the ordinal numerals <uig rom="nigedüger">ᠨᠢᠭᠡᠳᠦᠭᠡᠷ</uig> and <uig rom="qoyaduγar">ᠬᠣᠶᠠᠳᠤᠭᠠᠷ</uig> , in many cases the following words are used:
first <uig rom="angqaduγar">ᠠᠩᠬᠠᠳᠤᠭᠠᠷ</uig> < <uig rom="angqan">ᠠᠩᠬᠠᠨ</uig> beginning
first <uig rom="terigün">ᠲᠡᠷᠢᠭᠦᠨ</uig> head, beginning
first <uig rom="ekin">ᠡᠺᠢᠨ</uig> beginning, (in pre-classical texts) head
second <uig rom="nögüge">ᠨᠥᠭᠦᠭᠡ</uig> next, following
second <uig rom="ded">ᠳᠡᠳ</uig> the following, the succeeding
Although not a numeral, the word <uig rom="kedüi">ᠺᠡᠳᠦᠢ</uig> or <uig rom="kedün">ᠺᠡᠳᠦᠨ</uig> "how much, many" occurs in the ordinal form <uig rom="kedüdüger">ᠺᠡᠳᠦᠳᠦᠭᠡᠷ</uig> "which number?"
Suffix <uig rom="-γula(n)/-güle(n)">᠎ᠭᠤᠯᠠᠨ/᠎ᠭᠦᠯᠡᠨ</uig> with the final consonant and the ending <uig rom="">ᠭᠠᠨ</uig> -γan of the cardinal numeral dropped.
Function : to form numerals with the meaning of "two together", "three together", etc.
<uig rom="qoyaγula(n)">ᠬᠣᠶᠠᠭᠤᠯᠠᠨ</uig> both, two together
<uig rom="γurbaγula(n)">ᠭᠤᠷᠪᠠᠭᠤᠯᠠᠨ</uig> all three, three together
<uig rom="dörbegüle(n)">ᠳᠥᠷᠪᠡᠭᠦᠯᠡᠨ</uig> all four, four together
<uig rom="tabuγula(n) ">ᠲᠠᠪᠤᠭᠤᠯᠠᠨ</uig> all five, five together
<uig rom="jirγuγula(n)">ᠵᠢᠷᠭᠤᠭᠤᠯᠠᠨ</uig> all six, six together
<uig rom="doloγula(n)">ᠳᠣᠯᠣᠭᠤᠯᠠᠨ</uig> all seven, seven together
<uig rom="naimaγula(n)">ᠨᠠᠢᠮᠠᠭᠤᠯᠠ</uig> all eight, eight together
<uig rom="yisügüle(n)">ᠶᠢᠰᠦᠭᠦᠯᠡᠨ</uig> all nine, nine together
<uig rom="arbaγula(n)">ᠠᠷᠪᠠᠭᠤᠯᠠᠨ</uig> all ten, ten together
Although they are not numerals, the words <uig rom="olan">ᠣᠯᠠᠨ</uig> "many" and <uig rom="kedün">ᠺᠡᠳᠦᠨ</uig> "how many" sometimes occur in collective forms.
<uig rom="olaγula(n)">ᠣᠯᠠᠭᠤᠯᠠᠨ</uig> many together, all af them
<uig rom="kedügüle(n)">ᠺᠡᠳᠦᠭᠦᠯᠡᠨ</uig> how many together
Suffix <uig rom="-γad/-ged">᠎ᠭᠠᠳ/᠎ᠭᠡᠳ</uig> with the final consonant and ending <uig rom="-γan">᠎ᠭᠠᠨ</uig> of the cardinal numeral dropped.
Function: to form numerals with the meaning of "by twos", "in twos", "by threes", "in threes", and so on.
The numerals <uig rom="nigen">ᠨᠢᠭᠡᠨ</uig> and <uig rom="qoyar">ᠬᠣᠶᠠᠷ</uig> have irregular forms.
<uig rom="nijiged">ᠨᠢᠵᠢᠭᠡᠳ</uig> one and one
<uig rom="qosiyaγad">ᠬᠣᠰᠢᠶᠠᠭᠠᠳ</uig> by twos
<uig rom="γurbaγad">ᠭᠤᠷᠪᠠᠭᠠᠳ</uig> by threes
<uig rom="dörbeged">ᠳᠥᠷᠪᠡᠭᠡᠳ</uig> by fours
<uig rom="tabuγad">ᠲᠠᠪᠤᠭᠠᠳ</uig> by fives
<uig rom=" jirγuγad">ᠵᠢᠷᠭᠤᠭᠠᠳ</uig> by sixes
<uig rom="doloγad">ᠳᠣᠯᠣᠭᠠᠳ</uig> by sevens
<uig rom="naimaγad">ᠨᠠᠢᠮᠠᠭᠠᠳ</uig> by eights
<uig rom="yisüged">ᠶᠢᠰᠦᠭᠡᠳ</uig> by nines
<uig rom="arbaγad">ᠠᠷᠪᠠᠭᠠᠳ</uig> by tens
Suffix <uig rom="-ta/-te">᠎ᠲᠠ</uig> .
Function: to form numerals meaning "one time", "two times or twice", etc.
<uig rom="nigente">ᠨᠢᠭᠡᠨᠲᠡ</uig> once
<uig rom="qoyarta">ᠬᠣᠶᠠᠷᠲᠠ</uig> twice
<uig rom="γurbanta">ᠭᠤᠷᠪᠠᠨᠲᠠ</uig> three times
<uig rom="dörbente">ᠳᠥᠷᠪᠡᠨᠲᠡ</uig> four times
<uig rom="tabunta">ᠲᠠᠪᠤᠨᠲᠠ</uig> five times

Although <uig rom="olan">ᠣᠯᠠᠨ</uig> "many" and <uig rom="kedün">ᠺᠡᠳᠦᠨ</uig> "how many" are not numerals, there exist the forms <uig rom="olanta">ᠣᠯᠠᠨᠲᠠ</uig> "many times" and <uig rom="kedünte">ᠺᠡᠳᠦᠨᠲᠡ</uig> "how many times".
Another form of the multiplicative numerals is that without the final consonant n of the cardinal form.
<uig rom="nige">ᠨᠢᠭᠡ</uig> once
<uig rom="qoyar">ᠬᠣᠶᠠᠷ</uig> twice
<uig rom="γurba">ᠭᠤᠷᠪᠠ</uig> three times
The diminutive or limitative numerals are formed with the diminutive suffix <uig rom="-qan/-ken">᠎ᠬᠠᠨ/᠎ᠺᠡᠨ</uig> (see §124).
Function: to form numerals meaning "only one", "only two"; and so on.
<uig rom="nigeken">ᠨᠢᠭᠡᠺᠡᠨ</uig> only one
<uig rom="qoyarqan">ᠬᠣᠶᠠᠷᠬᠠᠨ</uig> only two
<uig rom="γurbaqan">ᠭᠤᠷᠪᠠᠬᠠᠨ</uig> only three
There are a ords which, while not being numerals, manifest a certain affinity with numerals. Such words, here called numerical words, express quantities, mainly indefinite quantities.
<uig rom="γaqca">ᠭᠠᠬᠴᠠ</uig> sole, single, the only
<uig rom="qaγas">ᠬᠠᠭᠠᠰ</uig> half
<uig rom="örügesün">ᠥᠷᠦᠭᠡᠰᠦᠨ</uig> one of a pair
<uig rom="örügele">ᠥᠷᠦᠭᠡᠯᠡ</uig> half
The word <uig rom="tümen">ᠲᠦᠮᠡᠨ</uig> "immense quantity, ten thousand" is also a numerical word.
All these words have neither ordinal nor other forms.
The adverbs are words of nominal origin: nouns, pronouns, or numerals. Therefore, they will now be discussed in connection with nouns.
There are primary and secondary adverbs. The adverbs do not change their forms except for a few fossilized case forms.
The adverbs are classified as local, temporal, and modal adverbs.
They will now be discussed in connection with their suffixes.
Suffix <uig rom="-a/-e">᠎ᠡ</uig>
This is the old dative suffix. The original nominative of a few derivatives with this suffix no longer exists. Adverbs with this suffix are mainly adverbs of manner.
<uig rom="ilangγui-a">ᠢᠯᠠᠩᠭᠤᠢ᠎ᠠ</uig> particularly, especially < *ilangγui
<uig rom="maγui-a">ᠮᠠᠭᠤᠢ᠎ᠠ</uig> badly < <uig rom="maγui">ᠮᠠᠭᠤᠢ</uig> bad
<uig rom="qataγui-a">ᠬᠠᠲᠠᠭᠤᠢ᠎ᠠ</uig> cruelly < <uig rom="qataγui">ᠬᠠᠲᠠᠭᠤᠢ</uig> cruel
Suffix <uig rom="-car/-cer">᠎ᠴᠠᠷ</uig>
This suffix occurs in but a few adverbs of manner (cf. §113).
<uig rom="busucar">ᠪᠤᠰᠤᠴᠠᠷ</uig> otherwise, in another manner < <uig rom="busu">ᠪᠤᠰᠤ</uig> another
Suffix <uig rom="-da/-de">᠎ᠳᠠ</uig>
This suffix occurs in local, temporal, and modal adverbs.
a) Local adverbs
<uig rom="ende">ᠡᠨᠳᠡ</uig> here, ablative <uig rom="endece">ᠡᠨᠳᠡᠴᠡ</uig> from here
<uig rom="tende">ᠲᠡᠨᠳᠡ</uig> there, ablative <uig rom="tendece">ᠲᠡᠨᠳᠡᠴᠡ</uig> from there
<uig rom="qotalada">ᠬᠣᠲᠠᠯᠠᠳᠠ</uig> everywhere, throughout < <uig rom="qotala">ᠬᠣᠲᠠᠯᠠ</uig> common, general
<uig rom="dergede">ᠳᠡᠷᠭᠡᠳᠡ</uig> at, beside, by < *derge
b) Temporal adverbs
<uig rom="marγada">ᠮᠠᠷᠭᠠᠳᠠ</uig> tomorrow cf. <uig rom="marγasi">ᠮᠠᠷᠭᠠᠰᠢ</uig>
<uig rom="urtuda">ᠤᠷᠲᠤᠳᠠ</uig> always, for a long time < <uig rom="urtu">ᠤᠷᠲᠤ</uig> long
<uig rom="önide">ᠥᠨᠢᠳᠡ</uig> long ago < <uig rom="öni">ᠥᠨᠢ</uig> ancient
<uig rom="urida">ᠤᠷᠢᠳᠠ</uig> formerly < *uri
<uig rom="kejiyede">ᠺᠡᠵᠢᠶᠡᠳᠡ</uig> always < <uig rom="kejiy-e">ᠺᠡᠵᠢᠶ᠎ᠡ</uig> when
<uig rom="nasuda">ᠨᠠᠰᠤᠳᠠ</uig> always < <uig rom="nasun">ᠨᠠᠰᠤᠨ</uig> age, lifetime
c) Modal adverbs
<uig rom="batuda">ᠪᠠᠲᠤᠳᠠ</uig> firmly < <uig rom="batu">ᠪᠠᠲᠤ</uig> firm
<uig rom="nutada">ᠨᠤᠲᠠᠳᠠ</uig> firmly < <uig rom="nuta">ᠨᠤᠲᠠ</uig> firm
<uig rom="γuu-a-da">ᠭᠤᠤ᠎ᠠ ᠎ᠳᠠ</uig> nicely, beautifully < <uig rom="γuu-a">ᠭᠤᠤ᠎ᠠ</uig> nice, beautiful
<uig rom="masida">ᠮᠠᠰᠢᠳᠠ</uig> very, exceedingly < <uig rom="masi">ᠮᠠᠰᠢ</uig> id.
Suffix <uig rom=" -γa/-ge">᠎ᠭᠠ/᠎ᠭᠡ</uig>
This suffix occurs in local and temporal adverbs.
a) Local adverbs
<uig rom="γadaγ-a">ᠭᠠᠳᠠᠭ᠎ᠠ</uig> out of doors < *γada
<uig rom="qamiγ-a">ᠬᠠᠮᠢᠭ᠎ᠠ</uig> where < *qami
b) Temporal adverbs
<uig rom="edüge">ᠡᠳᠦᠭᠡ</uig> now < *edü, cf. <uig rom="edüi">ᠡᠳᠦᠢ</uig> as much as this
<uig rom="kejiye">ᠺᠡᠵᠢᠶᠡ</uig> < *kedige when < *kedi, cf. <uig rom="kedüi">ᠺᠡᠳᠦᠢ</uig> how much, cf. ancient <uig rom="keli">ᠺᠡᠯᠢ</uig> when
Suffix <uig rom="-γar/-ger">᠎ᠭᠠᠷ/᠎ᠭᠡᠷ</uig>
This suffix occurs in local, temporal, and modal adverbs. It is an old variant of the instrumental suffix -*γar || -bar || -iyar < -*iγar.
a) Local adverbs
<uig rom="qotalaγar">ᠬᠣᠲᠠᠯᠠᠭᠠᠷ</uig> everywhere < <uig rom="qotala">ᠬᠣᠲᠠᠯᠠ</uig> common, general
b) Temporal adverbs
<uig rom="manaγar">ᠮᠠᠨᠠᠭᠠᠷ</uig> tomorrow < <uig rom="manan">ᠮᠠᠨᠠᠨ</uig> mist, fog (primary meaning, probably, "with the morning fog")
c) Modal converbs
<uig rom="γaqcaγar">ᠭᠠᠬᠴᠠᠭᠠᠷ</uig> alone < <uig rom="γaqca">ᠭᠠᠬᠴᠠ</uig> sole, single
<uig rom="yosuγar">ᠶᠣᠰᠤᠭᠠᠷ</uig> according to < <uig rom="yosun">ᠶᠣᠰᠤᠨ</uig> rule, law
<uig rom="busuγar">ᠪᠤᠰᠤᠭᠠᠷ</uig> otherwise, in another manner < <uig rom="busu">ᠪᠤᠰᠤ</uig> another
Suffix <uig rom="-qsi/-gsi"᠎ᠬᠰᠢ/᠎ᠭᠰᠢ</uig>
This suffix occurs in local adverbs answering the question "whither?"
<uig rom="dotoqsi">ᠳᠣᠲᠣᠬᠰᠢ</uig> into < *dotu < *dota, cf. <uig rom="dotor-a">ᠳᠣᠲᠣᠷ᠎ᠠ</uig> within
<uig rom="doγoqsi">ᠳᠣᠭᠣᠬᠰᠢ</uig> down < *doyo, cf. <uig rom="doγodu">ᠳᠣᠭᠣᠳᠤ</uig> inferior
<uig rom="inaqsi">ᠢᠨᠠᠬᠰᠢ</uig> hitherward < *ina, cf. <uig rom="inadu">ᠢᠨᠠᠳᠤ</uig> on this side
<uig rom="cinaqsi">ᠴᠢᠨᠠᠬᠰᠢ</uig> thitherward < *cina, cf. <uig rom="cinadu">ᠴᠢᠨᠠᠳᠤ</uig> on that side
<uig rom="degegsi">ᠳᠡᠭᠡᠭᠰᠢ</uig> upwards < *dege, cf. <uig rom="deger-e">ᠳᠡᠭᠡᠷ᠎ᠡ</uig> above, on
Suffix <uig rom="-γur/-gür">᠎ᠭᠤᠷ/᠎ᠭᠦᠷ</uig>
This suffix occurs in local and temporal adverbs only in the modern written language influenced by the spoken dialects.
a) Local adverbs
<uig rom="doγoγur">ᠳᠣᠭᠣᠭᠤᠷ</uig> under < *doγo, cf. <uig rom="doγoqsi">ᠳᠣᠭᠣᠬᠰᠢ</uig> down
<uig rom="qoyiγur">ᠬᠣᠶᠢᠭᠤᠷ</uig> along the background, behind < *qoyi, cf. <uig rom="qoyin-a">ᠬᠣᠶᠢᠨ᠎ᠠ</uig> behind
<uig rom="degegür">ᠳᠡᠭᠡᠭᠦᠷ</uig> over < *dege, ef. <uig rom="degegsi">ᠳᠡᠭᠡᠭᠰᠢ</uig> upwards
b) Temporal adverbs
<uig rom="üglügegür">ᠦᠭᠯᠦᠭᠡᠭᠦᠷ</uig> early in the morning < <uig rom="üglüge">ᠦᠭᠯᠦᠭᠡ</uig> - <uig rom="ürlüge">ᠦᠷᠯᠦᠭᠡ</uig> morning, <uig rom="ür">ᠦᠷ</uig> aurora
Suffix <uig rom=" -na/-ne">᠎ᠨᠠ</uig>
This suffix occurs mainly in local adverbs.
<uig rom="qoyin-a">ᠬᠣᠶᠢᠨ᠎ᠠ</uig> behind < *qoyi, cf. <uig rom="qoyitu">ᠬᠣᠶᠢᠲᠤ</uig> behind, northern
<uig rom="γadan-a">ᠭᠠᠳᠠᠨ᠎ᠠ</uig> without (opposite of within) < *γada, cf. <uig rom="γadaγadu">ᠭᠠᠳᠠᠭᠠᠳᠤ</uig> outer
<uig rom="ecin-e">ᠡᠴᠢᠨ᠎ᠡ</uig> seeretly < *eci
<uig rom="emün-e">ᠡᠮᠦᠨ᠎ᠡ</uig> in front of < *emü
These adverbs form also an ablative :
<uig rom="qoyin-a-aca">ᠬᠣᠶᠢᠨ᠎ᠠ ᠡᠴᠡ</uig> from behind
<uig rom="emün-e-ece">ᠡᠮᠦᠨ᠎ᠡ ᠡᠴᠡ</uig> from the front
<uig rom="γadan-a-aca">ᠭᠠᠳᠠᠨ᠎ᠠ ᠡᠴᠡ</uig> from the outside
Suffix <uig rom="-ra/-re">᠎ᠷᠠ</uig>
This suffix occurs in local adverbs answering the question "where?" Originally such adverbs must have been dative forms in -a of stems ending in -r (e. g., γadar "outside").
<uig rom="door-a">ᠳᠣᠣᠷ᠎ᠠ</uig> below < *do, cf. <uig rom="doγoqsi">ᠳᠣᠭᠣᠬᠰᠢ</uig> down
<uig rom="deger-e">ᠳᠡᠭᠡᠷ᠎ᠡ</uig> on, above < *dege, cf. <uig rom="degegsi">ᠳᠡᠭᠡᠭᠰᠢ</uig> upwards
<uig rom="dotor-a">ᠳᠣᠲᠣᠷ᠎ᠠ</uig> within < *dota, cf. <uig rom="dotoqgi">ᠳᠣᠲᠣᠬᠭᠢ</uig> into
Suffix <uig rom=" -ru/-rü">᠎ᠷᠤ</uig>
The suffix -ru occurs in adverbs used also as postpositions.
<uig rom="inaru">ᠢᠨᠠᠷᠤ</uig> prior, before < *ina, cf. <uig rom="inaqsi">ᠢᠨᠠᠬᠰᠢ</uig> hitherward
<uig rom="cinaru">ᠴᠢᠨᠠᠷᠤ</uig> after < *cina, cf. <uig rom="cinaqsi">ᠴᠢᠨᠠᠬᠰᠢ</uig> thitherward
<uig rom="tedrü">ᠲᠡᠳᠷᠦ</uig> (pre-classical) to the contrary < *ted
<uig rom="asuru">ᠠᠰᠤᠷᠤ</uig> very < *asu
The suffix <uig rom="-si">᠎ᠰᠢ</uig> plays a role similar to that of the suffix <uig rom="qsi">᠎ᠬᠰᠢ</uig> -.
a) Local adverbs
<uig rom="qamiγasi">ᠬᠠᠮᠢᠭᠠᠰᠢ</uig> whither < <uig rom="qamiγ-a">ᠬᠠᠮᠢᠭ᠎ᠠ</uig> where
<uig rom="qoyisi">ᠬᠣᠶᠢᠰᠢ</uig> backward, after < <uig rom="qoyin-a">ᠬᠣᠶᠢᠨ᠎ᠠ</uig> behind
<uig rom="eyisi">ᠡᠶᠢᠰᠢ</uig> hitherward < <uig rom="eyin">ᠡᠶᠢᠨ</uig> in this manner, so
<uig rom="teyisi">ᠲᠡᠶᠢᠰᠢ</uig> thitherward < <uig rom="teyin">ᠲᠡᠶᠢᠨ</uig> in that manner
b) Temporal adverbs
<uig rom="marγasi">ᠮᠠᠷᠭᠠᠰᠢ</uig> tomorrow < <uig rom="marγada">ᠮᠠᠷᠭᠠᠳᠠ</uig>
<uig rom="manaγarsi">ᠮᠠᠨᠠᠭᠠᠷᠰᠢ</uig> tomorrow < <uig rom="manaγar">ᠮᠠᠨᠠᠭᠠᠷ</uig>
Suffix <uig rom="-ta/-te">᠎ᠲᠠ</uig>
This suffix occurs in adverbs of manner.
<uig rom="uγuγata">ᠤᠭᠤᠭᠠᠲᠠ</uig> completely, cf. <uig rom="uq">ᠤᠬ</uig> origin
<uig rom="genedte">ᠭᠡᠨᠡᠳᠲᠡ</uig> suddenly < *gened
<uig rom="joriγuta">ᠵᠣᠷᠢᠭᠤᠲᠠ</uig> purposely < <uig rom="joriγu">ᠵᠣᠷᠢᠭᠤ</uig> intending
Cf. the multiplicative numerals <uig rom="nigente">ᠨᠢᠭᠡᠨᠲᠡ,</uig> , <uig rom="qoyarta">ᠬᠣᠶᠠᠷᠲᠠ</uig> (see §201).
Adverbs Ending in <uig rom="-b"> ᠎ᠪ</uig>

There are modal adverbs with the meaning "completely", derived by reduplication of the first syllable of the word with the inserted consonant <uig rom="-b">᠎ᠪ</uig> . If the first syllable of the word concerned is <uig rom="no">ᠨᠣ</uig> , the adverb is <uig rom="nob">ᠨᠣᠪ</uig> ; if the first syllable is <uig rom="qa">ᠬᠠ</uig> , the adverb is <uig rom="qab">ᠬᠠᠪ</uig> , and so on.
<uig rom="qab qar-a">ᠬᠠᠪ ᠬᠠᠷ᠎ᠠ</uig> completely black
<uig rom="qab qarangγui">ᠬᠠᠪ ᠬᠠᠷᠠᠩᠭᠤᠢ</uig> pitch dark
<uig rom="sib sir-a">ᠰᠢᠪ ᠰᠢᠷ᠎ᠠ</uig> completely yellow
<uig rom="ub ulaγan">ᠤᠪ ᠤᠯᠠᠭᠠᠨ</uig> completely red
<uig rom="cab caγan">ᠴᠠᠪ ᠴᠠᠭᠠᠨ</uig> snow-white
<uig rom="nob noγuγan">ᠨᠣᠪ ᠨᠣᠭᠤᠭᠠᠨ</uig> grass green
<uig rom="küb küren">ᠺᠦᠪ ᠺᠦᠷᠡᠨ</uig> completely or dark brown
<uig rom="köb köke">ᠺᠥᠪ ᠺᠥᠺᠡ</uig> completely blue
<uig rom="geb genedte">ᠭᠡᠪ ᠭᠡᠨᠡᠳᠲᠡ</uig> unexpectedly
<uig rom="ab ali">ᠠᠪ ᠠᠯᠢ</uig> anybody, whoever
<uig rom="keb kejiy-e">ᠺᠡᠪ ᠺᠡᠵᠢᠶ᠎ᠡ</uig> always
<uig rom="dub duγui">ᠳᠤᠪ ᠳᠤᠭᠤᠢ</uig> dead silent
The postpositions have a function similar to that of the prepositions in European languages with the difference that they follow the word which they govern.
The postpositions are nouns, adverbs, and even verbs in origin. Most of these words can act as independent words as well as postpositions. A few postpositions are used only as such.
The postpositions will be discussed under syntax. (See § 418.) A few examples, however, will be given here.
Nouns as postpositions :
<uig rom="ucir-a">ᠤᠴᠢᠷ᠎ᠠ</uig> because of, a dative of <uig rom="ucir">ᠤᠴᠢᠷ</uig> cause
<uig rom="siltaγa-bar">ᠰᠢᠯᠲᠠᠭᠠ ᠎ᠪᠠᠷ</uig> in consequence of, an instrumental of <uig rom="siltaγan">ᠰᠢᠯᠲᠠᠭᠠᠨ</uig> cause, reason
Adverbs as postpositions:
<uig rom="deger-e">ᠳᠡᠭᠡᠷ᠎ᠡ</uig> on, as adverb "above"
<uig rom="dotor-a">ᠳᠣᠲᠣᠷ᠎ᠠ</uig> in, as adverb "within"
Verbal forms as postpositions:
<uig rom="kürtele">ᠺᠦᠷᠲᠡᠯᠡ</uig> till, unto, a converb of <uig rom="kür-">ᠺᠦᠷ ᠎</uig> to reach
<uig rom="boltala">ᠪᠣᠯᠲᠠᠯᠠ</uig> till, a converb of <uig rom="bol-">ᠪᠣᠯ ᠎</uig> to become
Postpositions which are only postpositions:
<uig rom="tula">ᠲᠤᠯᠠ</uig> or <uig rom="tulada">ᠲᠤᠯᠠᠳᠠ</uig> for
The secondary verbs are derived from verbs, nouns, pronouns, adverbs, and interjections.

There are two groups of deverbal verbs. To the first group belong those which can be derived from all verbs. Such secondary verbs are nothing but voices or genera verbi like the active or passive of the European verbs. To the other group belong secondary verbs which can be derived from a limited group of verbs.
To this group belong the factitive, passive, reciprocal, co-operative, and plural verbs.

entry.title: Derivation - Verbs - Deverbal verbs
entry.title2: Verbs - Deverbal verbs - Factitive and transitive verbs

paragraphs.paragraph: In general, these verbs express the idea of causing (letting, ordering, permitting) someone to perform the action expressed by the primary verb.

entry.title: Derivation - Verbs - Deverbal verbs
entry.title2: Verbs - Deverbal verbs - Factitive and transitive verbs

paragraphs.paragraph: Suffix <uig rom="-γa-/-ge-">᠎ᠭᠠ/᠎ᠭᠡ᠎</uig> (the vowel of the suffix is pronounced long) on intransitive stems ending in vowels.
Function: to make transitive verbs.
<uig rom="qataγa-">ᠬᠠᠲᠠᠭᠠ ᠎</uig> to dry something < <uig rom="qata-">ᠬᠠᠲᠠ ᠎</uig> to become dry
<uig rom="jobaγa-">ᠵᠣᠪᠠᠭᠠ ᠎</uig> to torment someone < <uig rom="joba-">ᠵᠣᠪᠠ ᠎</uig> to suffer
<uig rom="unaγa-">ᠤᠨᠠᠭᠠ ᠎</uig> to overthrow < <uig rom="una-">ᠤᠨᠠ ᠎</uig> to fall
<uig rom="untaraγa-">ᠤᠨᠲᠠᠷᠠᠭᠠ ᠎</uig> to extinguish < <uig rom="untara-">ᠤᠨᠲᠠᠷᠠ ᠎</uig> to go out (of fire)
<uig rom="bütüge-">ᠪᠦᠲᠦᠭᠡ ᠎</uig> to fulfill, to accomplish < <uig rom="bütü-">ᠪᠦᠲᠦ ᠎</uig> to be fulfilled
<uig rom="üledege-">ᠦᠯᠡᠳᠡᠭᠡ ᠎</uig> to leave (something behind) < <uig rom="ülede-">ᠦᠯᠡᠳᠡ ᠎</uig> to remain

entry.title: Derivation - Verbs - Deverbal verbs
entry.title2: Verbs - Deverbal verbs - Factitive and transitive verbs

paragraphs.paragraph: Suffix <uig rom="-γa-/-ge-">ᠭᠠ/᠎ᠭᠡ᠎</uig> (the vowel of the suffix is short) on both the transitive and intransitive verbs ending in the consonant l or r; suffix <uig rom="-qa-/-ke-">ᠬᠠ/᠎ᠺᠡ</uig> on both the transitive and intransitive verbs ending in b, d, or s.
Function: to make primary intransitive verbs transitive, primary transitive verbs factitive verbs ("to cause to do something").
<uig rom="surγa-">ᠰᠤᠷᠭᠠ ᠎ᠲᠣ</uig> to teach < <uig rom="sur-">ᠰᠤᠷ ᠎</uig> to learn
<uig rom="kürge-">ᠺᠦᠷᠭᠡ ᠎</uig> to deliver < <uig rom="kür-">ᠺᠦᠷ ᠎</uig> to arrive
<uig rom="γarγa-">ᠭᠠᠷᠭᠠ ᠎</uig> to take out, to let out < <uig rom="γar-">ᠭᠠᠷ ᠎</uig> to go out
<uig rom="bolγa-">ᠪᠣᠯᠭᠠ ᠎</uig> to make < <uig rom="bol-">ᠪᠣᠯ ᠎</uig> to become
<uig rom="ködelge-">ᠺᠥᠳᠡᠯᠭᠡ ᠎</uig> to move (someone) < <uig rom="ködel-">ᠺᠥᠳᠡᠯ ᠎</uig> to move
<uig rom="kötelge-">ᠺᠥᠲᠡᠯᠭᠡ ᠎</uig> to cause to lead, to cause to direct < <uig rom="kötel-">ᠺᠥᠲᠡᠯ ᠎</uig> to lead, to direct
<uig rom="getülge-">ᠭᠡᠲᠦᠯᠭᠡ ᠎</uig> to cause to cross a river, to rescue < <uig rom="getül-">ᠭᠡᠲᠦᠯ ᠎</uig> to cross a river
<uig rom="bosqa-">ᠪᠣᠰᠬᠠ ᠎</uig> to erect< <uig rom="bos-">ᠪᠣᠰ ᠎</uig> to rise
<uig rom="öske-">ᠥᠰᠺᠡ ᠎</uig> to breed, to raise (cattle) < <uig rom="ös-">ᠥᠰ ᠎</uig> to become numerous
<uig rom="usadqa-">ᠤᠰᠠᠳᠬᠠ ᠎</uig> to liquidate< <uig rom="usad-">ᠤᠰᠠᠳ ᠎</uig> to vanish
<uig rom="cadqa-">ᠴᠠᠳᠬᠠ ᠎</uig> to satiate< <uig rom="cad-">ᠴᠠᠳ ᠎</uig> to be satisfied

entry.title: Derivation - Verbs - Deverbal verbs
entry.title2: Verbs - Deverbal verbs - Factitive and transitive verbs

paragraphs.paragraph: Suffix <uig rom="-γul-/-gül-">ᠭᠤᠯ/ᠭᠦᠯ</uig> added to transitive and intransitive verbal Steins ending in vowels.
Function : to make intransitive verbs transitive, transitive primary verbs factitive.
<uig rom="oroγul-">ᠣᠷᠣᠭᠤᠯ ᠎</uig> to let in < <uig rom="oro-">ᠣᠷᠣ ᠎</uig> to go in
<uig rom="üjegül-">ᠦᠵᠡᠭᠦᠯ ᠎</uig> to show < <uig rom="üje-">ᠦᠵᠡ ᠎</uig> to see
<uig rom="idegül-">ᠢᠳᠡᠭᠦᠯ ᠎</uig> to feed < <uig rom="ide-">ᠢᠳᠡ ᠎</uig> to eat
<uig rom="ükügül-">ᠦᠺᠦᠭᠦᠯ ᠎</uig> to cause to die < <uig rom="ükü-">ᠦᠺᠦ ᠎</uig> to die out
<uig rom="γarγaγul-">ᠭᠠᠷᠭᠠᠭᠤᠯ ᠎</uig> to cause to take < <uig rom="γarγa-">ᠭᠠᠷᠭᠠ ᠎</uig> to take out
<uig rom="bayiγul-">ᠪᠠᠶᠢᠭᠤᠯ ᠎</uig> to found< <uig rom="bayi-">ᠪᠠᠶᠢ ᠎</uig> to be

entry.title: Derivation - Verbs - Deverbal verbs
entry.title2: Verbs - Deverbal verbs - Factitive and transitive verbs

paragraphs.paragraph: Suffix <uig rom="-l-">ᠯ</uig> added to primary Steins ending in a syllable conaisting of γ (or g) + vowel. This suffix occurs only in the pre-classical language and its equivalent is now <uig rom="-lγa-"> ᠎ᠯᠭᠠ ᠎</uig> (see next section).
<uig rom="saγul-">ᠰᠠᠭᠤᠯ ᠎</uig> to set < <uig rom="saγu-">ᠰᠠᠭᠤ ᠎</uig> to sit down
<uig rom="uγul-">ᠤᠭᠤᠯ ᠎</uig> to give a drink < <uig rom="uγu-">ᠤᠭᠤ ᠎</uig> to drink

entry.title: Derivation - Verbs - Deverbal verbs
entry.title2: Verbs - Deverbal verbs - Factitive and transitive verbs

paragraphs.paragraph: Suffix <uig rom="-lγa-/-lge-">᠎ᠯᠭᠠ/᠎ᠯᠭᠡ</uig> added to intransitive and transitive primary stems ending in the syllable mentioned in § 227 and diphthongs and also to monosyllabic stems.
Function: to make intransitive verbs transitive, transitive primary stems factitive.
<uig rom="saγulγa-">ᠰᠠᠭᠤᠯᠭᠠ᠎</uig> to set < <uig rom="saγu-">ᠰᠠᠭᠤ ᠎</uig> to sit down
<uig rom="sitaγalγa-">ᠰᠢᠲᠠᠭᠠᠯᠭᠠ ᠎</uig> to make let burn < <uig rom="sitaγa-">ᠰᠢᠲᠠᠭᠠ ᠎</uig> to let burn
<uig rom="negülge-">ᠨᠡᠭᠦᠯᠭᠡ ᠎</uig> to let migrate, to move someone to another place < <uig rom="negü-">ᠨᠡᠭᠦ ᠎</uig> to migrate, to nomadize
<uig rom="baγulγa-">ᠪᠠᠭᠤᠯᠭᠠ ᠎</uig> to lower, to let down < <uig rom="baγu-">ᠪᠠᠭᠤ ᠎</uig> to descend
<uig rom="kilge-">ᠺᠢᠯᠭᠡ ᠎</uig> to cause to do, to let do < <uig rom="ki-">ᠺᠢ ᠎</uig> to do
<uig rom="qarayilγa-">ᠬᠠᠷᠠᠶᠢᠯᠭᠠ ᠎</uig> to let jump < <uig rom="qarayi-">ᠬᠠᠷᠠᠶᠢ ᠎</uig> to jump
<uig rom="bayilγa-">ᠪᠠᠶᠢᠯᠭᠠ ᠎</uig> to let be < <uig rom="bayi-">ᠪᠠᠶᠢ ᠎</uig> to be

Passive verbs can be formed from both transitive and intransitive verbs. If the primary verb is transitive, its passive form has the same function as the passive voice of an English verb, e. g., "to be killed". If the primary verb is an intransitive verb, e. g., "to go", such a form cannot be translated into English literally and an approximate translation would be "to be the object of someone's going". Yet often such passive intransitive verbs also have another function: to express the idea of the necessity of an action, e. g., not "to be the object of someone's going" but "to be obliged to go".
Suffix <uig rom="-γda- / -gde-">ᠬᠳᠠ/᠎ᠭᠳᠡ</uig> added to stems ending in vowels and sometimes in the consonant l. In the latter case the connective vowel u/ü is inserted.
<uig rom="alaγda-">ᠠᠯᠠᠬᠳᠠ ᠎</uig> to be killed < <uig rom="ala-">ᠠᠯᠠ ᠎</uig> to kill
<uig rom="bariγda-">ᠪᠠᠷᠢᠬᠳᠠ ᠎</uig> to be seized < <uig rom="bari-">ᠪᠠᠷᠢ ᠎</uig> to seize
<uig rom="üjegde-">ᠦᠵᠡᠭᠳᠡ ᠎</uig> to be seen < <uig rom="üje-">ᠦᠵᠡ ᠎</uig> to see
<uig rom="yabuγda-">ᠶᠠᠪᠤᠬᠳᠠ ᠎</uig> to be the object of someone's going< <uig rom="yabu-">ᠶᠠᠪᠤ ᠎</uig> to go
<uig rom="tayiluγda-">ᠲᠠᠶᠢᠯᠤᠬᠳᠠ ᠎</uig> to be explained < <uig rom="tayil-">ᠲᠠᠶᠢᠯ ᠎</uig> to explain
Suffix <uig rom="-da-/-de-">᠎ᠳᠠ/᠎ᠳᠡ</uig> added to verbs ending in l; suffix <uig rom="-ta-/-te-">ᠲᠠ/ᠲᠡ</uig> added to stems ending in b, s, d, g, r.
<uig rom="olda-">ᠣᠯᠳᠠ ᠎</uig> to be found < <uig rom="ol-">ᠣᠯ ᠎</uig> to find
<uig rom="bolda-">ᠪᠣᠯᠳᠠ ᠎</uig> to be obliged to be < <uig rom="bol-">ᠪᠣᠯ ᠎</uig> to be
<uig rom="abta-">ᠠᠪᠲᠠ ᠎</uig> to be taken < <uig rom="ab-">ᠠᠪ ᠎</uig> to take
<uig rom="ögte-">ᠥᠭᠲᠡ ᠎</uig> to be given < <uig rom="ög-">ᠥᠭ ᠎</uig> to give
<uig rom="γarta-">ᠭᠠᠷᠲᠠ ᠎</uig> to be surpassed < <uig rom="γar-">ᠭᠠᠷ ᠎</uig> to surpass
Suffix <uig rom="-ldu-/-ldü-">ᠯᠳᠤ</uig> .
Function: to express mutual interaction, e. g., to kill each other.
<uig rom="alaldu-">ᠠᠯᠠᠯᠳᠤ ᠎</uig> to kill each other < <uig rom="ala-">ᠠᠯᠠ ᠎</uig> to kill
<uig rom="qarbuldu-">ᠬᠠᠷᠪᠤᠯᠳᠤ ᠎</uig> to shoot at each other < <uig rom="qarbu-">ᠬᠠᠷᠪᠤ ᠎</uig> to shoot
<uig rom="bayildu-">ᠪᠠᠶᠢᠯᠳᠤ ᠎</uig> to fight < <uig rom="bayi-">ᠪᠠᠶᠢ ᠎</uig> to stand, to be
Suffix <uig rom="-lca-/-lce-">ᠯᠴᠠ</uig> .
Function : to express co-operation with others, taking part in joint action.
<uig rom="ungsilca-">ᠤᠩᠰᠢᠯᠴᠠ ᠎</uig> to read together < <uig rom="ungsi-">ᠤᠩᠰᠢ ᠎</uig> to read
<uig rom="saγulca-">ᠰᠠᠭᠤᠯᠴᠠ ᠎</uig> to be present at the meeting of others < <uig rom="saγu-">ᠰᠠᠭᠤ ᠎</uig> to sit down
<uig rom="idelce-">ᠢᠳᠡᠯᠴᠡ ᠎</uig> to take part in eating < <uig rom="ide-">ᠢᠳᠡ ᠎</uig> to eat
<uig rom="surulca-">ᠰᠤᠷᠤᠯᠴᠠ ᠎</uig> to learn togetherwith others < <uig rom="sur-">ᠰᠤᠷ ᠎</uig> to learn
Suffix <uig rom="-caγa-/-cege-">ᠴᠠᠭᠠ/ᠴᠡᠭᠡ</uig> .
Function: to express actions performed by many actors.
<uig rom="ungsicaγa-">ᠤᠩᠰᠢᠴᠠᠭᠠ ᠎</uig> to read (of many people) < <uig rom="ungsi-">ᠤᠩᠰᠢ ᠎</uig> to read
<uig rom="yabucaγa-">ᠶᠠᠪᠤᠴᠠᠭᠠ ᠎</uig> to go (of many people) < <uig rom="yabu-">ᠶᠠᠪᠤ ᠎</uig> to go

A verbal stem can carry more than one suffix at the same time, e. g., on a factitive stem there can be a passive suffix or on a reciprocal stem there can be a factitive suffix. Sometimes even three suffixes can be attached to a primary stem.
a) Factitive on factitive:
<uig rom="bosqaγul-">ᠪᠣᠰᠬᠠᠭᠤᠯ ᠎</uig> to cause to erect < <uig rom="bosqa-">ᠪᠣᠰᠬᠠ ᠎</uig> to erect < <uig rom="bos-">ᠪᠣᠰ ᠎</uig> to rise
<uig rom="cadqaγul-">ᠴᠠᠳᠬᠠᠭᠤᠯ ᠎</uig> to cause to satiate < <uig rom="cadqa-">ᠴᠠᠳᠬᠠ ᠎</uig> to satiate < <uig rom="cad-">ᠴᠠᠳ ᠎</uig> to be satisfied
<uig rom="bayiγulγa-">ᠪᠠᠶᠢᠭᠤᠯᠭᠠ ᠎</uig> to make found < <uig rom="bayiγul">ᠪᠠᠶᠢᠭᠤᠯ ᠎</uig> - to found < <uig rom="bayi-">ᠪᠠᠶᠢ ᠎</uig> to be
b) Passive on factitive :
<uig rom="bayiγuluqda-">ᠪᠠᠶᠢᠭᠤᠯᠤᠬᠳᠠ ᠎</uig> to be founded < <uig rom="bayiγul-">ᠪᠠᠶᠢᠭᠤᠯ ᠎</uig> to found < <uig rom="bayi-">ᠪᠠᠶᠢ ᠎</uig> to be
<uig rom="bolγaqda-">ᠪᠣᠯᠭᠠᠬᠳᠠ ᠎</uig> to be made < <uig rom="bolγa-">ᠪᠣᠯᠭᠠ ᠎</uig> to make <<uig rom="bol-">ᠪᠣᠯ ᠎</uig> to become
c) Factitive on passive:
<uig rom="alaqdaγul-">ᠠᠯᠠᠬᠳᠠᠭᠤᠯ ᠎</uig> to cause one to be killed < <uig rom="alaqda-">ᠠᠯᠠᠬᠳᠠ ᠎</uig> to be killed < <uig rom="ala-">ᠠᠯᠠ</uig> to kill
<uig rom="üjegdegül-">ᠦᠵᠡᠭᠳᠡᠭᠦᠯ ᠎</uig> to cause one to be seen < <uig rom="üjegde-">ᠦᠵᠡᠭᠳᠡ ᠎</uig> to be seen < <uig rom="üje-">ᠦᠵᠡ ᠎</uig> to see
d) Factitive on reciprocal:
<uig rom="barilduγul-">ᠪᠠᠷᠢᠯᠳᠤᠭᠤᠯ ᠎</uig> to let wrestle < <uig rom="barildu-">ᠪᠠᠷᠢᠯᠳᠤ ᠎</uig> to wrestle < <uig rom="bari-">ᠪᠠᠷᠢ ᠎</uig> to seize, to keep
<uig rom="bayilduγul-">ᠪᠠᠶᠢᠯᠳᠤᠭᠤᠯ ᠎</uig> to let fight < <uig rom="bayildu- ">ᠪᠠᠶᠢᠯᠳᠤ ᠎</uig> to fight < <uig rom="bayi-">ᠪᠠᠶᠢ ᠎</uig> to stand
e) Factitive on co-operative:
<uig rom="idelcegül-">ᠢᠳᠡᠯᠴᠡᠭᠦᠯ ᠎</uig> to cause to participate in eating < <uig rom="idelce-">ᠢᠳᠡᠯᠴᠡ ᠎</uig> to participate in eating < <uig rom="ide-">ᠢᠳᠡ ᠎</uig> to eat
<uig rom="saγulcaγul-">ᠰᠠᠭᠤᠯᠴᠠᠭᠤᠯ ᠎</uig> to cause to be present < <uig rom="saγulca-">ᠰᠠᠭᠤᠯᠴᠠ ᠎</uig> to be present < <uig rom="saγu-">ᠰᠠᠭᠤ</uig> to sit down
Suffix <uig rom="-l-"> ᠎ᠯ ᠎.</uig> .
Function : to express repeated actions.
<uig rom="cokil-">ᠴᠣᠺᠢᠯ ᠎</uig> to hit, to knock incessantly < <uig rom="coki-">ᠴᠣᠺᠢ ᠎</uig> to beat
<uig rom="cakil-">ᠴᠠᠺᠢᠯ ᠎</uig> to lighten, to flash < <uig rom="caki-">ᠴᠠᠺᠢ ᠎</uig> to strike fire
<uig rom="dusul-">ᠳᠤᠰᠤᠯ ᠎</uig> to drip < <uig rom="dusu-">ᠳᠤᠰᠤ ᠎</uig> to fall (of drops)

entry.title: Derivation - Verbs - Deverbal verbs
entry.title2: Verbs - Deverbal verbs - Middle verbs (verba media)

paragraphs.paragraph: Suffix <uig rom="-ra-/-re-">ᠷᠠ</uig> .
Function: to express an action by the subject in relation to himself or the undergoing of an action not caused by anyone other than the subject, e. g., "to betake oneself", "to go to pieces".
<uig rom="asqara-">ᠠᠰᠬᠠᠷᠠ ᠎</uig> to be spilled < <uig rom="asqa-">ᠠᠰᠬᠠ ᠎</uig> to apill
<uig rom="ebdere-">ᠡᠪᠳᠡᠷᠡ ᠎</uig> to go to pieces < <uig rom=ebde-"">ᠡᠪᠳᠡ ᠎</uig> to break
Suffix <uig rom="-balja-">ᠪᠠᠯᠵᠠ᠎</uig> or <uig rom="-γalja-">᠎ᠭᠠᠯᠵᠠ</uig> .
Function: to express lasting actions.
<uig rom="sanaγalja-">ᠰᠠᠨᠠᠭᠠᠯᠵᠠ ᠎</uig> to reflect on < <uig rom="sana-">ᠰᠠᠨᠠ ᠎</uig> to think
<uig rom="anibalja-">ᠠᠨᠢᠪᠠᠯᠵᠠ ᠎</uig> to twinkle < <uig rom="ani-">ᠠᠨᠢ ᠎</uig> to shut his eyes
Suffix <uig rom="-lja-/-lje-">ᠯᠵᠠ</uig> on stems expressing motions.
Function: to express rhythmic motions.
<uig rom="nayiγulja-">ᠨᠠᠶᠢᠭᠤᠯᠵᠠ ᠎</uig> to bob up and down < <uig rom="nayiγu-">ᠨᠠᠶᠢᠭᠤ ᠎</uig> to swing
<uig rom="γangqulja-">ᠭᠠᠩᠬᠤᠯᠵᠠ ᠎</uig> to rock < <uig rom="γangqu-">ᠭᠠᠩᠬᠤ ᠎</uig> to swing
Suffix <uig rom="-cila-/-cile-">ᠴᠢᠯᠠ</uig> .
Function: to indicate that the object is rendered into, made into, or made like the thing or quality designated by the primary word.
<uig rom="boγolcila-">ᠪᠣᠭᠣᠯᠴᠢᠯᠠ ᠎</uig> to enslave < <uig rom="boγol">ᠪᠣᠭᠣᠯ</uig> slave
<uig rom="köbegüncile-">ᠺᠥᠪᠡᠭᠦᠨᠴᠢᠯᠡ ᠎</uig> to take someone as his son < <uig rom="köbegün">ᠺᠥᠪᠡᠭᠦᠨ</uig> son
<uig rom="tarbaγacila-">ᠲᠠᠷᠪᠠᠭᠠᠴᠢᠯᠠ ᠎</uig> to hunt marmots < <uig rom="tarbaγan">ᠲᠠᠷᠪᠠᠭᠠᠨ</uig> marmot
Suffix <uig rom="-d-">᠎ᠳ</uig> .
Function: to express the acquirement of the quality designated by the primary word (intransitive verbs).
<uig rom="urtud-">ᠤᠷᠲᠤᠳ ᠎</uig> to become long < <uig rom="urtu">ᠤᠷᠲᠤ</uig> long
<uig rom="sulad-">ᠰᠤᠯᠠᠳ ᠎</uig> to weaken < <uig rom="sula">ᠰᠤᠯᠠ</uig> weak
<uig rom="boγonid-">ᠪᠣᠭᠣᠨᠢᠳ ᠎</uig> to become short < <uig rom="boγoni">ᠪᠣᠭᠣᠨᠢ</uig> short
<uig rom="örged-">ᠥᠷᠭᠡᠳ ᠎</uig> to become large < <uig rom="örgen">ᠥᠷᠭᠡᠨ</uig> large, broad
Suffix <uig rom="-da-/-de-">᠎ᠳᠠ</uig> .
Function: to express the use of the object designated by the primary word (mostly transitive verbs).
<uig rom="daγuda-">ᠳᠠᠭᠤᠳᠠ ᠎</uig> to call < <uig rom="daγun">ᠳᠠᠭᠤᠨ</uig> voice
<uig rom="buuda-">ᠪᠤᠤᠳᠠ ᠎</uig> to shoot < <uig rom="buu">ᠪᠤᠤ</uig> rifle
<uig rom="degermede-">ᠳᠡᠭᠡᠷᠮᠡᠳᠡ ᠎</uig> to rob < <uig rom="degerme">ᠳᠡᠭᠡᠷᠮᠡ</uig> robbery
<uig rom="arγada-">ᠠᠷᠭᠠᠳᠠ ᠎</uig> to outwit < <uig rom="arγa">ᠠᠷᠭᠠ</uig> trick
Suffix <uig rom="-ji-"> ᠎ᠵᠢ</uig> .
Function: to express the acquirement of whatever designated by the primary word. (See § 244 below.)
<uig rom="bayaji-">ᠪᠠᠶᠠᠵᠢ ᠎</uig> to become rich < <uig rom="bayan">ᠪᠠᠶᠠᠨ</uig> rich
<uig rom="üreji-">ᠦᠷᠡᠵᠢ ᠎</uig> to increase < <uig rom="üre">ᠦᠷᠡ</uig> descendant
<uig rom="amurji-">ᠠᠮᠤᠷᠵᠢ ᠎</uig> to be peaceful, to enjoy < <uig rom=amur"">ᠠᠮᠤᠷ</uig> rest, peace peace
Suffix <uig rom="-jira-/-jire-">᠎ᠵᠢᠷᠠ</uig> .
Function: the same as that in § 243.
<uig rom="sayijira-">ᠰᠠᠶᠢᠵᠢᠷᠠ ᠎</uig> to improve < <uig rom="sayin">ᠰᠠᠶᠢᠨ</uig> good
<uig rom="anggijira-">ᠠᠩᠭᠢᠵᠢᠷᠠ ᠎</uig> to separate < <uig rom="anggi">ᠠᠩᠭᠢ</uig> separate
<uig rom="maγujira-">ᠮᠠᠭᠤᠵᠢᠷᠠ ᠎</uig> to deteriorate < <uig rom="maγu">ᠮᠠᠭᠤ</uig> bad
Suffix <uig rom="-la-/-le-">ᠯᠠ᠎</uig> or <uig rom="-na-/-ne-">᠎ᠨᠠ᠎</uig> when added to sounds ng and m.
<uig rom="emegelle-">ᠡᠮᠡᠭᠡᠯᠯᠡ ᠎</uig> to saddle < <uig rom="emegel">ᠡᠮᠡᠭᠡᠯ</uig> saddle
<uig rom="gerle-">ᠭᠡᠷᠯᠡ ᠎</uig> to marry (to found a house of his own) < <uig rom="ger">ᠭᠡᠷ</uig> house
<uig rom="usula-">ᠤᠰᠤᠯᠠ ᠎</uig> to water < <uig rom="usun">ᠤᠰᠤᠨ</uig> water
<uig rom="altala-">ᠠᠯᠲᠠᠯᠠ ᠎</uig> to gild < <uig rom="altan">ᠠᠯᠲᠠᠨ</uig> gold
<uig rom="sibaγula-">ᠰᠢᠪᠠᠭᠤᠯᠠ ᠎</uig> to hunt bird < <uig rom="sibaγun">ᠰᠢᠪᠠᠭᠤᠨ</uig> bird
<uig rom="qurdula-">ᠬᠤᠷᠳᠤᠯᠠ ᠎</uig> to rush, to be quick < <uig rom="qurdun">ᠬᠤᠷᠳᠤᠨ</uig> quick
<uig rom="angna-">ᠠᠩᠨᠠ ᠎</uig> to hunt < <uig rom="ang">ᠠᠩ</uig> game
<uig rom="emne-">ᠡᠮᠨᠡ ᠎</uig> to cure < <uig rom="em">ᠡᠮ</uig> medicine
Suffix <uig rom="-ra-/-re-">᠎ᠷᠠ᠎</uig> or <uig rom="-la-/-le-">ᠯᠠ᠎</uig> (dissimilation) when added containing the consonant r.
Function: to denote acquirement of a quality.
<uig rom="kökere-">ᠺᠥᠺᠡᠷᠡ ᠎</uig> to become blue < <uig rom="köke">ᠺᠥᠺᠡ</uig> blue
<uig rom="kögsire-">ᠺᠥᠭᠰᠢᠷᠡ ᠎</uig> to become old < <uig rom="kögsin">ᠺᠥᠭᠰᠢᠨ</uig> old
<uig rom="ügeyire-">ᠦᠭᠡᠶᠢᠷᠡ ᠎</uig> to become poor < <uig rom="ügei">ᠦᠭᠡᠢ</uig> poor
<uig rom="sirala-">ᠰᠢᠷᠠᠯᠠ ᠎</uig> to become yellow < <uig rom="sir-a">ᠰᠢᠷ᠎ᠠ</uig> yellow
Suffix <uig rom="-rqa-/-rke-">᠎ᠷᠬᠠ/᠎ᠷᠺᠡ</uig> with the final consonant of the dropped.
Function : to denote possession of something in
<uig rom="bayarqa">ᠪᠠᠶᠠᠷᠬᠠ ᠎</uig> - to be proud of one's richness < <uig rom="bayan">ᠪᠠᠶᠠᠨ</uig> rich
<uig rom="omorqa-">ᠣᠮᠣᠷᠬᠠ ᠎</uig> to be proud < <uig rom="omoq">ᠣᠮᠣᠬ</uig> pride
<uig rom="cilegerke-">ᠴᠢᠯᠡᠭᠡᠷᠺᠡ ᠎</uig> to be ill < <uig rom="cilegen">ᠴᠢᠯᠡᠭᠡᠨ</uig> illness, ailment
<uig rom="ejerke-">ᠡᠵᠡᠷᠺᠡ ᠎</uig> to impose one's rule upon someone < <uig rom="ejen">ᠡᠵᠡᠨ</uig> master
Suffix <uig rom="-si-">᠎ᠰᠢ</uig> .
Function : to express attainment of a quality or condition.
<uig rom="aldarsi-">ᠠᠯᠳᠠᠷᠰᠢ ᠎</uig> to become glorious < <uig rom="aldar">ᠠᠯᠳᠠᠷ</uig> glory
<uig rom="nutuqsi-">ᠨᠤᠲᠤᠬᠰᠢ ᠎</uig> to get settled < <uig rom="nutuq">ᠨᠤᠲᠤᠬ</uig> country
<uig rom="saγurisi-">ᠰᠠᠭᠤᠷᠢᠰᠢ ᠎</uig> to lead a sedentary life < <uig rom="saγuri">ᠰᠠᠭᠤᠷᠢ</uig> seat
Suffix <uig rom="-siya-/-siye-">ᠰᠢᠶᠠ</uig> .
Function: to express aknoledgment of qualities expressed by the primary noum.
<uig rom="sayisiya-">ᠰᠠᠶᠢᠰᠢᠶᠠ ᠎</uig> to approve < <uig rom="sayin">ᠰᠠᠶᠢᠨ</uig> good
<uig rom="jöbsiye-">ᠵᠥᠪᠰᠢᠶᠡ ᠎</uig> to agree < <uig rom="jöb">ᠵᠥᠪ</uig> right
<uig rom="aldarsiya-">ᠠᠯᠳᠠᠷᠰᠢᠶᠠ ᠎</uig> to praise < <uig rom="aldar">ᠠᠯᠳᠠᠷ</uig> glory, fame
<uig rom="maγusiya-">ᠮᠠᠭᠤᠰᠢᠶᠠ ᠎</uig> to blame, to slander < <uig rom="maγu">ᠮᠠᠭᠤ</uig> bad
Suffix <uig rom="-ta-/-te-">ᠲᠠ᠎</uig> or <uig rom="-tu-/-tü-">ᠲᠤ</uig> .
Function: to express acquirement of the condition expressed by the primary noun.
<uig rom="gemte-">ᠭᠡᠮᠲᠡ ᠎</uig> to be damaged < <uig rom="gem">ᠭᠡᠮ</uig> damage, harm
<uig rom="kirte-">ᠺᠢᠷᠲᠡ ᠎</uig> to become dirty < <uig rom="kir">ᠺᠢᠷ</uig> dirt
<uig rom="oyiratu-">ᠣᠶᠢᠷᠠᠲᠤ ᠎</uig> to approach < <uig rom="oyir-a">ᠣᠶᠢᠷ᠎ᠠ</uig> near

entry.title: Derivation - Verbs - Verbs of pronominal origin

paragraphs.paragraph: The following demonstrative verbs are derived from roots of demonstrative pronouns.
<uig rom="eyi-">ᠡᠶᠢ ᠎</uig> to act in this manner, cf. <uig rom="eyimü">ᠡᠶᠢᠮᠦ</uig> such as this
<uig rom="teyi-">ᠲᠡᠶᠢ ᠎</uig> to act in that manner, cf. <uig rom="teyimü">ᠲᠡᠶᠢᠮᠦ</uig> such as that
<uig rom="cingge-">ᠴᠢᠩᠭᠡ ᠎</uig> to act in that manner < colloquial language
The following interrogative verbs are derived from roots of the interrogative pronouns.
<uig rom="yaγaki-">ᠶᠠᠭᠠᠺᠢ ᠎</uig> to do what, cf. <uig rom="yaγun">ᠶᠠᠭᠤᠨ</uig> what?
<uig rom="yeyi-">ᠶᠡᠶᠢ ᠎</uig> to do what
<uig rom="yeki-">ᠶᠡᠺᠢ ᠎</uig> to do what

entry.title: Derivation - Verbs - Verbs of adverbial origin

paragraphs.paragraph: Suffix <uig rom="-ci-">᠎ᠴᠢ</uig> .
Function: to express actions performed energetically or with strength (transitive verbs).
<uig rom="suγuci- ">ᠰᠤᠭᠤᠴᠢ ᠎</uig> to pull out < <uig rom="suγu">ᠰᠤᠭᠤ</uig> off
<uig rom="tasuci-">ᠲᠠᠰᠤᠴᠢ ᠎</uig> to tear to pieces < <uig rom="tasu">ᠲᠠᠰᠤ</uig> asunder
<uig rom="kemkeci-">ᠺᠡᠮᠺᠡᠴᠢ ᠎</uig> to break in pieces < <uig rom="kemke">ᠺᠡᠮᠺᠡ</uig> in pieces

entry.title: Derivation - Verbs - Verbs of adverbial origin

paragraphs.paragraph: Suffix <uig rom="-l-">ᠯ</uig> .
Function : to form transitive verbs expressing destructive actions.
<uig rom="suγul-">ᠰᠤᠭᠤᠯ ᠎</uig> to pull out < <uig rom="suγu">ᠰᠤᠭᠤ</uig> out, off
<uig rom="quγul-">ᠬᠤᠭᠤᠯ ᠎</uig> to break asunder < <uig rom="quγu">ᠬᠤᠭᠤ</uig> asunder
<uig rom="tasul-">ᠲᠠᠰᠤᠯ ᠎</uig> to tear to pieces < <uig rom="tasu">ᠲᠠᠰᠤ</uig> asunder

entry.title: Derivation - Verbs - Verbs of adverbial origin

paragraphs.paragraph: Suffix <uig rom="-ra-/-re-">ᠷᠠ</uig> .
Function: to form intransitive (middle) verbs (verba media).
<uig rom="suγura-">ᠰᠤᠭᠤᠷᠠ ᠎</uig> to fall out < <uig rom="suγu">ᠰᠤᠭᠤ</uig> out, off
<uig rom="tasura-">ᠲᠠᠰᠤᠷᠠ ᠎</uig> to be pulled off < <uig rom="tasu">ᠲᠠᠰᠤ</uig> asunder
<uig rom="qaγara-">ᠬᠠᠭᠠᠷᠠ ᠎</uig> to burst < <uig rom="qaγa">ᠬᠠᠭᠠ</uig> asunder

entry.title: Derivation - Verbs - Verbs derived from interjections

paragraphs.paragraph: Suffix <uig rom="-cigina- /-cigine-">ᠴᠢᠭᠢᠨᠠ</uig> .
Function : to form onomatopoetic verbs expressing various sounds. (See §257 and §258 below.)
<uig rom="tarcigina-">ᠲᠠᠷᠴᠢᠭᠢᠨᠠ ᠎</uig> to rattle, to crackle < <uig rom="tar">ᠲᠠᠷ</uig>
<uig rom="sarcigina-">ᠰᠠᠷᠴᠢᠭᠢᠨᠠ ᠎</uig> to rush, to rustle < <uig rom="sar">ᠰᠠᠷ</uig>

entry.title: Derivation - Verbs - Verbs derived from interjections

paragraphs.paragraph: Suffix <uig rom="-gi-."> ᠎ᠭᠢ</uig>
Function: the same.
<uig rom="cuugi-">ᠴᠤᠤᠭᠢ ᠎</uig> to make noise < <uig rom="cuu">ᠴᠤᠤ</uig>
<uig rom="sagi-">ᠰᠠᠭᠢ ᠎</uig> to rustle < <uig rom="sa">ᠰᠠ</uig>

entry.title: Derivation - Verbs - Verbs derived from interjections

paragraphs.paragraph: Suffix <uig rom="-gina-/-gine-">᠎ᠭᠢᠨᠠ᠎</uig>
Function: the same.
<uig rom="ganggina-">ᠭᠠᠩᠭᠢᠨᠠ᠎</uig> to make noise < <uig rom="qang">ᠬᠠᠩ</uig>
<uig rom="ginggine-">ᠭᠢᠩᠭᠢᠨᠡ᠎</uig> to roar, to bellow, to cry < <uig rom="ging">ᠭᠢᠩ</uig>

entry.title: Derivation - Verbs - Verbs derived from interjections

paragraphs.paragraph: Suffix <uig rom="-kira-/-kire-."> ᠎ᠺᠢᠷᠠ ᠎ / ᠎ᠺᠢᠷᠡ ᠎.</uig>
Function: to form verbs expressing shouting, bellowing, etc.
<uig rom="qaskira-to">ᠬᠠᠰᠺᠢᠷᠠ ᠎ᠲᠣ</uig> shout < <uig rom="qas">ᠬᠠᠰ</uig>
<uig rom="barkira-">ᠪᠠᠷᠺᠢᠷᠠ ᠎</uig> to roar, to bellow, to cry < <uig rom="bar">ᠪᠠᠷ</uig>

Only words acting as substantives have a plural form, but words expressing qualities and numerals used as substantives can form a plural. The plural stem is, at the same time, the nominative plural. Suffixes of oblique cases follow the plural suffix.

The plural presents a varied picture. There are several plural suffixes, but their use often depends neither upon the final sound of the stem nor upon the function of the respective word. There are words having more than one form and their different plural forms have different functions. Certain suffixes even alter the meaning of the word and transform the latter into another word with the function of a singular, even though it is formally a plural.

The suffix <uig rom="-nar/-ner">᠎ᠨᠠᠷ</uig> may be added to a limited number of stems ending in vowels and diphthongs with i and denoting human beings (mainly relatives and respected people) and deities. This suffix is written separately from the stem.
<uig rom="aq-a-nar">ᠠᠬ᠎ᠠ ᠎ᠨᠠᠷ</uig> elder brothers < <uig rom="aq-a">ᠠᠬ᠎ᠠ</uig> elder brother
<uig rom="degüü-ner">ᠳᠡᠭᠦᠦ ᠎ᠨᠡᠷ</uig> younger brothers < <uig rom="degüü">ᠳᠡᠭᠦᠦ</uig> younger brother
<uig rom="egeci-ner">ᠡᠭᠡᠴᠢ ᠎ᠨᠡᠷ</uig> elder sisters < <uig rom="egeci">ᠡᠭᠡᠴᠢ</uig> elder sister
<uig rom="aci-nar">ᠠᠴᠢ ᠎ᠨᠠᠷ</uig> grandsons < <uig rom="aci">ᠠᠴᠢ</uig> son of the brother, grandson
<uig rom="jici-ner">ᠵᠢᠴᠢ ᠎ᠨᠡᠷ</uig> great-grandsons < <uig rom="jici">ᠵᠢᠴᠢ</uig> great-grandson
<uig rom="γuci-nar">ᠭᠤᠴᠢ ᠎ᠨᠠᠷ</uig> the children of <uig rom="jici">ᠵᠢᠴᠢ</uig> < <uig rom="γuci">ᠭᠤᠴᠢ</uig> the son of jiei
<uig rom="döci-ner">ᠳᠥᠴᠢ ᠎ᠨᠡᠷ</uig> the children of yuci < <uig rom="döci">ᠳᠥᠴᠢ</uig> the son of yuci
<uig rom="jige-ner">ᠵᠢᠭᠡ ᠎ᠨᠡᠷ</uig> sons of the daughter < <uig rom="jige">ᠵᠢᠭᠡ</uig> son of the daughter
<uig rom="böle-ner">ᠪᠥᠯᠡ ᠎ᠨᠡᠷ</uig> children of sisters < <uig rom="böle">ᠪᠥᠯᠡ</uig> child of the sister
<uig rom="abaγ-a-nar">ᠠᠪᠠᠭ᠎ᠠ ᠎ᠨᠠᠷ</uig> uncles, brothers of the father < <uig rom="abaγ-a">ᠠᠪᠠᠭ᠎ᠠ</uig> uncle
<uig rom="naγacu-nar">ᠨᠠᠭᠠᠴᠤ ᠎ᠨᠠᠷ</uig> maternal uncles < <uig rom="naγacu">ᠨᠠᠭᠠᠴᠤ</uig> the brother of the mother
<uig rom="abuγai-nar">ᠠᠪᠤᠭᠠᠢ ᠎ᠨᠠᠷ</uig> gentlemen < <uig rom="abuγai">ᠠᠪᠤᠭᠠᠢ</uig> gentleman
<uig rom="baqsi-nar">ᠪᠠᠬᠰᠢ ᠎ᠨᠠᠷ</uig> teachers < <uig rom="baqsi">ᠪᠠᠬᠰᠢ</uig> teacher
<uig rom="sabi-nar">ᠰᠠᠪᠢ ᠎ᠨᠠᠷ</uig> pupils < <uig rom="sabi">ᠰᠠᠪᠢ</uig> pupil
<uig rom="blam-a-nar">ᠪᠯᠠᠮ᠎ᠠ ᠎ᠨᠠᠷ</uig> lamas < <uig rom="blam-a">ᠪᠯᠠᠮ᠎ᠠ</uig> lama
<uig rom="bandi-nar">ᠪᠠᠨᠳᠢ ᠎ᠨᠠᠷ</uig> novices < <uig rom="bandi">ᠪᠠᠨᠳᠢ</uig> novice
<uig rom="bandita-nar">ᠪᠠᠨᠳᠢᠲᠠ ᠎ᠨᠠᠷ</uig> pundits < <uig rom="bandita">ᠪᠠᠨᠳᠢᠲᠠ</uig> pundit
<uig rom="gabju-nar">ᠭᠠᠪᠵᠤ ᠎ᠨᠠᠷ</uig> the gabjus < <uig rom="gabju">ᠭᠠᠪᠵᠤ</uig> a learned degree of Buddhist monks, Tibetan dka'-bcu
<uig rom="kiy-a-nar">ᠺᠢᠶ᠎ᠠ ᠎ᠨᠠᠷ</uig> pages, bodyguards < <uig rom="kiy-a">ᠺᠢᠶ᠎ᠠ</uig> page, bodyguard
<uig rom="lojava-nar">ᠯᠣᠵᠠᠸᠠ ᠎ᠨᠠᠷ</uig> learned translators < <uig rom="lojava">ᠯᠣᠵᠠᠸᠠ</uig> learned translator of Buddhist literature
<uig rom="böge-ner">ᠪᠥᠭᠡ ᠎ᠨᠡᠷ</uig> shamans < <uig rom="böge">ᠪᠥᠭᠡ</uig> shaman
<uig rom="tngri-ner">ᠲᠩᠷᠢ ᠎ᠨᠡᠷ</uig> gods < <uig rom="tngri">ᠲᠩᠷᠢ</uig> god, deity
<uig rom="asuri-nar">ᠠᠰᠤᠷᠢ ᠎ᠨᠠᠷ</uig> Asuri-ghosts < <uig rom="asuri">ᠠᠰᠤᠷᠢ</uig> Asuri ghost

The word <uig rom="eke-ner">ᠡᠺᠡ ᠎ᠨᠡᠷ</uig> "woman" is formally a plural of <uig rom="eke">ᠡᠺᠡ</uig> "mother", but it is used as singular, never expressing the idea "mothers". The plural of eke "mother" is <uig rom="ekes">ᠡᠺᠡᠰ</uig> "mothers".

The suffix <uig rom="-nad/-ned">ᠨᠠᠳ</uig> occurs only in the language of the Secret History of the Mongols, which is not Written Mongolian, although it may also occur in some ancient Written Mongolian texts as yet undiscovered. It is used instead of the suffix <uig rom="-nar/-ner">ᠨᠠᠷ</uig> .
<uig rom="aq-a-nad">ᠠᠬ᠎ᠠ ᠎ᠨᠠᠳ</uig> elder brothers < <uig rom="aq-a">ᠠᠬ᠎ᠠ</uig>
<uig rom="degüü-ned">ᠳᠡᠭᠦᠦ ᠎ᠨᠡᠳ</uig> younger brothers < <uig rom="degüü">ᠳᠡᠭᠦᠦ</uig>

The suffix <uig rom="-mad/-med">ᠮᠠᠳ</uig> (cf. § 129) occurs on a few stems ending in vowels and denoting people. Originally this was a suffix of collective nouns, but it is becoming fossilized and can be found in few words no longer having the plural meaning. Sometimes it acts, however, as a plural suffix.
<uig rom="aqamad">ᠠᠬᠠᠮᠠᠳ</uig> seniors, headmen, authorities < <uig rom="aq-a">ᠠᠬ᠎ᠠ</uig> elder brother
The suffix <uig rom="-s">᠎ᠰ</uig> occurs on stems ending in vowels or in the diphthong ai, replacing i. The use of this suffix is independent of the meaning of the nouns concerned.
<uig rom="emes">ᠡᠮᠡᠰ</uig> women < <uig rom="em-e">ᠡᠮ᠎ᠡ</uig> woman
<uig rom="ekes">ᠡᠺᠡᠰ</uig> mothers < <uig rom="eke">ᠡᠺᠡ</uig> mother
<uig rom="eres">ᠡᠷᠡᠰ</uig> men < <uig rom="er-e">ᠡᠷ᠎ᠡ</uig> man
<uig rom="nilqas">ᠨᠢᠯᠬᠠᠰ</uig> infants < <uig rom="nilqa">ᠨᠢᠯᠬᠠ</uig> infant
<uig rom="aqas">ᠠᠬᠠᠰ</uig> older people < <uig rom="aq-a">ᠠᠬ᠎ᠠ</uig> elder brother
<uig rom="üges">ᠦᠭᠡᠰ</uig> words < <uig rom="üge">ᠦᠭᠡ</uig> word
<uig rom="üres">ᠦᠷᠡᠰ</uig> fruit, berries < <uig rom="ür-e">ᠦᠷ᠎ᠡ</uig> fruit, berry
<uig rom="aγulas">ᠠᠭᠤᠯᠠᠰ</uig> mountains < <uig rom="aγula">ᠠᠭᠤᠯᠠ</uig> mountain
<uig rom="baqas">ᠪᠠᠬᠠᠰ</uig> toads < <uig rom="baq-a">ᠪᠠᠬ᠎ᠠ</uig> toad
<uig rom="noqas">ᠨᠣᠬᠠᠰ</uig> dogs < <uig rom="noqai">ᠨᠣᠬᠠᠢ</uig> dog
<uig rom="γaqas">ᠭᠠᠬᠠᠰ</uig> pigs < <uig rom="γaqai">ᠭᠠᠬᠠᠢ</uig> pig

Of words ending in the consonant n only <uig rom="kümün">ᠺᠦᠮᠦᠨ</uig> "man" has a plural in <uig rom="-s"> ᠎ᠰ</uig> : <uig rom="kümün-nügüd">ᠺᠦᠮᠦᠨ ᠎ᠨᠦᠭᠦᠳ</uig> or <uig rom="kümüs">ᠺᠦᠮᠦᠰ</uig> "people."

Suffix <uig rom="-d">᠎ᠳ</uig> . This suffix may be added to stems ending in various sounds. Words ending in the consonant n, as a rule, form the plural with this suffix. The final n of the stem is dropped.
<uig rom="noyad">ᠨᠣᠶᠠᠳ</uig> princes, nobles < <uig rom="noyan">ᠨᠣᠶᠠᠨ</uig> prince, nobleman
<uig rom="qaγad">ᠬᠠᠭᠠᠳ</uig> khaghans < <uig rom="qaγan">ᠬᠠᠭᠠᠨ</uig> khaghan
<uig rom="qatud">ᠬᠠᠲᠤᠳ</uig> wives of khans, queens < <uig rom="qatun">ᠬᠠᠲᠤᠨ</uig> the wife of a khan, queen
<uig rom="burqad">ᠪᠤᠷᠬᠠᠳ</uig> Buddhas < <uig rom="burqan">ᠪᠤᠷᠬᠠᠨ</uig> Buddha
<uig rom="ebüged">ᠡᠪᠦᠭᠡᠳ</uig> old men < <uig rom="ebügen">ᠡᠪᠦᠭᠡᠨ</uig> old man
<uig rom="sibaγud">ᠰᠢᠪᠠᠭᠤᠳ</uig> birds < <uig rom="sibaγun">ᠰᠢᠪᠠᠭᠤᠨ</uig> bird
<uig rom="morid">ᠮᠣᠷᠢᠳ</uig> horses < <uig rom="morin">ᠮᠣᠷᠢᠨ</uig> horae
<uig rom="usud">ᠤᠰᠤᠳ</uig> waters < <uig rom="usun">ᠤᠰᠤᠨ</uig> water
<uig rom="modud">ᠮᠣᠳᠤᠳ</uig> trees < <uig rom="modun">ᠮᠣᠳᠤᠨ</uig> tree

In pre-classical texts the plural of <uig rom="modun">ᠮᠣᠳᠤᠨ</uig> "tree" is <uig rom="mod">ᠮᠣᠳ</uig> "trees." The plural of <uig rom="keüken">ᠺᠡᠦᠺᠡᠨ</uig> "child, girl" is <uig rom="keüked">ᠺᠡᠦᠺᠡᠳ</uig> "children" or "boy" (the latter is a singular).
The word <uig rom="sayid">ᠰᠠᠶᠢᠳ</uig> "minister" is, formally, a plural of <uig rom="sayin">ᠰᠠᠶᠢᠨ</uig> "good" but in function it is a singular.
Some names of tribes are plural forms in -d.
<uig rom="dörbed">ᠳᠥᠷᠪᠡᠳ</uig> Dörbet < <uig rom="dörben">ᠳᠥᠷᠪᠡᠨ</uig> four
<uig rom="bayad">ᠪᠠᠶᠠᠳ</uig> Bayat < <uig rom="bayan">ᠪᠠᠶᠠᠨ</uig> rich
The suffix <uig rom="-d"> ᠎ᠳ</uig> occurs on dissyllabic words ending in r with the latter dropped.
<uig rom="γajad">ᠭᠠᠵᠠᠳ</uig> countries < <uig rom="γajar">ᠭᠠᠵᠠᠷ</uig> country
<uig rom="nököd">ᠨᠥᠺᠥᠳ</uig> friends < <uig rom="nökör">ᠨᠥᠺᠥᠷ</uig> friend
<uig rom="siküd">ᠰᠢᠺᠦᠳ</uig> umbrellas < <uig rom="sikür">ᠰᠢᠺᠦᠷ</uig> umbrella
<uig rom="singqud">ᠰᠢᠩᠬᠤᠳ</uig> falcons < <uig rom="singqur">ᠰᠢᠩᠬᠤᠷ</uig> falcon
In pre-classical language monosyllabic words ending in r also take the suffix <uig rom="-d">ᠳ</uig> .
<uig rom="möd">ᠮᠥᠳ</uig> ways < <uig rom="mör">ᠮᠥᠷ</uig> way
In the pre-classical language words ending in l sometimes also take the suffix <uig rom="-d">ᠳ</uig> . The final l is dropped.
<uig rom="tursiγud">ᠲᠤᠷᠰᠢᠭᠤᠳ</uig> spies < <uig rom="tursiγul">ᠲᠤᠷᠰᠢᠭᠤᠯ</uig> spy
<uig rom="turγaγud">ᠲᠤᠷᠭᠠᠭᠤᠳ</uig> the name of Chinggis Khan's daytime bodyguard < <uig rom="turγaγul">ᠲᠤᠷᠭᠠᠭᠤᠯ</uig> standing
<uig rom="kebtegüd">ᠺᠡᠪᠲᠡᠭᠦᠳ</uig> the name of Chinggis Khan's nighttime bodyguard < <uig rom="kebtegül">ᠺᠡᠪᠲᠡᠭᠦᠯ</uig> lying

In the modern language only the word <uig rom="tüsimel">ᠲᠦᠰᠢᠮᠡᠯ</uig> "official" takes the suffix <uig rom="-d">ᠳ</uig> : <uig rom="tüsimed">ᠲᠦᠰᠢᠮᠡᠳ</uig> "officials." The latter form is used as pluralis majestatis and means "official" (singular). As plural only the form <uig rom="tüsimel-nügüd">ᠲᠦᠰᠢᠮᠡᠯ ᠎ᠨᠦᠭᠦᠳ</uig> is used.

In the classical language words ending in the syllable <uig rom=" -sun"> ᠎ᠰᠤᠨ</uig> form their plural by dropping the syllable <uig rom="-sun"> ᠎ᠰᠤᠨ</uig> and adding the suffix <uig rom="-d"> ᠎ᠳ</uig> to the stem.
<uig rom="nuγud">ᠨᠤᠭᠤᠳ</uig> ducks < <uig rom="nuγusun">ᠨᠤᠭᠤᠰᠤᠨ</uig> duck
<uig rom="qubcad">ᠬᠤᠪᠴᠠᠳ</uig> clothes, dresses < <uig rom="qubcasun">ᠬᠤᠪᠴᠠᠰᠤᠨ</uig> cloth, dress
A few words ending in vowels take the suffix <uig rom=" -d">ᠳ</uig>.
<uig rom="busud">ᠪᠤᠰᠤᠳ</uig> the others < <uig rom="busu">ᠪᠤᠰᠤ</uig> another
<uig rom="berid">ᠪᠡᠷᠢᠳ</uig> sisters-in-law < <uig rom="beri">ᠪᠡᠷᠢ</uig> sister-in-law
All nouns ending in <uig rom="-ci">ᠴᠢ</uig> , <uig rom="-γaci/-geci">ᠭᠠᠴᠢ/᠎ᠭᠡᠴᠢ</uig> , and <uig rom="-γci/-gci">᠎ᠬᠴᠢ/᠎ᠭᠴᠢ</uig> form the plural with the suffix <uig rom="-d">᠎ᠳ</uig> .
<uig rom="elcid">ᠡᠯᠴᠢᠳ</uig> ambassadors, messengers < <uig rom="elci">ᠡᠯᠴᠢ</uig> ambassador, messenger
<uig rom="aduγucid">ᠠᠳᠤᠭᠤᠴᠢᠳ</uig> horse grooms < <uig rom="aduγuci">ᠠᠳᠤᠭᠤᠴᠢ</uig> horse groom
<uig rom="emcid">ᠡᠮᠴᠢᠳ</uig> physicians < <uig rom="emci">ᠡᠮᠴᠢ</uig> physician
<uig rom="bicigecid">ᠪᠢᠴᠢᠭᠡᠴᠢᠳ</uig> scribes, clerks < <uig rom="bicigeci">ᠪᠢᠴᠢᠭᠡᠴᠢ</uig> clerk
<uig rom="suruqcid">ᠰᠤᠷᠤᠬᠴᠢᠳ</uig> pupils < <uig rom="suruqci">ᠰᠤᠷᠤᠬᠴᠢ</uig> pupil

The suffix <uig rom="-n">ᠨ</uig> is added to words ending in <uig rom="-ci">᠎ᠴᠢ</uig> , <uig rom="-γaci/-geci">᠎ᠭᠠᠴᠢ/᠎ᠭᠡᠴᠢ</uig> , and <uig rom="-γci/-gci">ᠬᠴᠢ/᠎ᠭᠴᠢ</uig> in both ancient and modern texts.
<uig rom="elcin">ᠡᠯᠴᠢᠨ</uig> ambassadors, messengers < <uig rom="elci">ᠡᠯᠴᠢ</uig> ambassador, messenger
<uig rom="aduγucin">ᠠᠳᠤᠭᠤᠴᠢᠨ</uig> horse grooms < <uig rom="aduγuci">ᠠᠳᠤᠭᠤᠴᠢ</uig> horse groom
<uig rom="ködelmüricin">ᠺᠥᠳᠡᠯᠮᠦᠷᠢᠴᠢᠨ</uig> workers < <uig rom="ködelmürici">ᠺᠥᠳᠡᠯᠮᠦᠷᠢᠴᠢ</uig> workers
<uig rom="bicigecin">ᠪᠢᠴᠢᠭᠡᠴᠢᠨ</uig> scribes, clerks < <uig rom="bicigeci">ᠪᠢᠴᠢᠭᠡᠴᠢ</uig> clerk
<uig rom="küsegcin">ᠺᠦᠰᠡᠭᠴᠢᠨ</uig> those who wish < <uig rom="küsegci">ᠺᠦᠰᠡᠭᠴᠢ</uig> wishing
The suffix <uig rom="-n"> ᠎ᠨ</uig> is also added to words ending in <uig rom="tai/-tei">ᠲᠠᠢ</uig> - in both ancient and modern texts. The final i of the ending is dropped (cf. § 139).
<uig rom="moritan">ᠮᠣᠷᠢᠲᠠᠨ</uig> horsemen < <uig rom="moritai">ᠮᠣᠷᠢᠲᠠᠢ</uig> horseman
<uig rom="erdemten">ᠡᠷᠳᠡᠮᠲᠡᠨ</uig> learned people < <uig rom="erdemtei">ᠡᠷᠳᠡᠮᠲᠡᠢ</uig> scholar
The suffix <uig rom="-n"> ᠎ᠨ</uig> occurs, in ancient books, on all stems ending in the vowel i or in the diphthong ai/ei or ui/üi with the final i dropped.
<uig rom="cerbin">ᠴᠡᠷᠪᠢᠨ</uig> cherbies < <uig rom="cerbi">ᠴᠡᠷᠪᠢ</uig> cherby (a title in the thirteenth century)
<uig rom="γaqan">ᠭᠠᠬᠠᠨ</uig> pigs < <uig rom="γaqai">ᠭᠠᠬᠠᠢ</uig> pig
<uig rom="qulaγan">ᠬᠤᠯᠠᠭᠠᠨ</uig> thieves < <uig rom="qulaγai">ᠬᠤᠯᠠᠭᠠᠢ</uig> thief
<uig rom="maγun">ᠮᠠᠭᠤᠨ</uig> villains < <uig rom="maγui">ᠮᠠᠭᠤᠢ</uig> villain
<uig rom="yabuqun">ᠶᠠᠪᠤᠬᠤᠨ</uig> those going < <uig rom="yabuqui">ᠶᠠᠪᠤᠬᠤᠢ</uig> one going
Suffix <uig rom="-ud/-üd">ᠤᠳ</uig> added to stems ending in consonants other than n.
<uig rom="tölüb-üd">ᠲᠥᠯᠦᠪ ᠤᠳ</uig> forms, patterns < <uig rom="tölüb">ᠲᠥᠯᠦᠪ</uig> form, pattern
<uig rom="bicig-üd">ᠪᠢᠴᠢᠭ ᠤᠳ</uig> letters < <uig rom="bicig">ᠪᠢᠴᠢᠭ</uig> letter
<uig rom="bulaγ-ud">ᠪᠤᠯᠠᠭ ᠤᠳ</uig> springs, wells < <uig rom="bulaγ">ᠪᠤᠯᠠᠭ</uig> spring, well
<uig rom="ulus-ud">ᠤᠯᠤᠰ ᠤᠳ</uig> peoples < <uig rom="ulus">ᠤᠯᠤᠰ</uig> people
<uig rom="nom-ud">ᠨᠣᠮ ᠤᠳ</uig> books < <uig rom="nom">ᠨᠣᠮ</uig> book
<uig rom="debter-üd">ᠳᠡᠪᠲᠡᠷ ᠤᠳ</uig> copy books < <uig rom="debter">ᠳᠡᠪᠲᠡᠷ</uig> copy book
In books of the seventeenth century (and earlier) the suffix <uig rom="-γud/-güd">᠎ᠭᠤᠳ/᠎ᠭᠦᠳ</uig> is added to stems ending in vowels and n.
<uig rom="caγaqciγud">ᠴᠠᠭᠠᠬᠴᠢᠭᠤᠳ</uig> white mares < <uig rom="caγaqcin">ᠴᠠᠭᠠᠬᠴᠢᠨ</uig> white mare
<uig rom="tayijiγud">ᠲᠠᠶᠢᠵᠢᠭᠤᠳ</uig> Taijigud (name of a tribe) < <uig rom="tayiji">ᠲᠠᠶᠢᠵᠢ</uig> son of a prince
<uig rom="alaqciγud">ᠠᠯᠠᠬᠴᠢᠭᠤᠳ</uig> motley bows < <uig rom="alaqci">ᠠᠯᠠᠬᠴᠢ</uig> motley bow
The suffix <uig rom="-nuγud/-nügüd">᠎ᠨᠤᠭᠤᠳ/᠎ᠨᠦᠭᠦᠳ</uig> occurs on any stems regardless of their final sounds.
<uig rom="dalai-nuγud">ᠳᠠᠯᠠᠢ ᠎ᠨᠤᠭᠤᠳ</uig> seas < <uig rom="dalai">ᠳᠠᠯᠠᠢ</uig> sea
<uig rom="noqai-nuγud">ᠨᠣᠬᠠᠢ ᠎ᠨᠤᠭᠤᠳ</uig> dogs < <uig rom="noqai">ᠨᠣᠬᠠᠢ</uig> dog
<uig rom="bicig-nügüd">ᠪᠢᠴᠢᠭ ᠎ᠨᠦᠭᠦᠳ</uig> letters < <uig rom="bicig">ᠪᠢᠴᠢᠭ</uig> letter
<uig rom="naγur-nuγud">ᠨᠠᠭᠤᠷ ᠎ᠨᠤᠭᠤᠳ</uig> lakes < <uig rom="naγur">ᠨᠠᠭᠤᠷ</uig> lake
<uig rom="kümün-nügüd">ᠺᠦᠮᠦᠨ ᠎ᠨᠦᠭᠦᠳ</uig> people < <uig rom="kümün">ᠺᠦᠮᠦᠨ</uig> man
<uig rom="üker-nügüd">ᠦᠺᠡᠷ ᠎ᠨᠦᠭᠦᠳ</uig> oxen < <uig rom="üker">ᠦᠺᠡᠷ</uig> ox
The suffix <uig rom="-cud/-cüd">ᠴᠤᠳ</uig> occurs on stems ending in vowels, in n or l, or the syllable -güi, and denoting human beings.
<uig rom="jalaγucud">ᠵᠠᠯᠠᠭᠤᠴᠤᠳ</uig> young people, youth < <uig rom="jalaγu">ᠵᠠᠯᠠᠭᠤ</uig> young
<uig rom="baγacud">ᠪᠠᠭᠠᠴᠤᠳ</uig> children < <uig rom="baγ-a">ᠪᠠᠭ᠎ᠠ</uig> little
<uig rom="bayacud">ᠪᠠᠶᠠᠴᠤᠳ</uig> rich people < <uig rom="bayan">ᠪᠠᠶᠠᠨ</uig> rich
<uig rom="mongγolcud">ᠮᠣᠩᠭᠣᠯᠴᠤᠳ</uig> Mongols < <uig rom="mongγol">ᠮᠣᠩᠭᠣᠯ</uig> Mongol
<uig rom="büsügüyicüd">ᠪᠦᠰᠦᠭᠦᠶᠢᠴᠦᠳ</uig> women < <uig rom="büsügüi">ᠪᠦᠰᠦᠭᠦᠢ</uig> woman
A word can have several plural forms, as said above, but sometimes with semantic differentiation.
<uig rom="aq-a">ᠠᠬ᠎ᠠ</uig> elder brother -
<uig rom="aq-a-nar">ᠠᠬ᠎ᠠ ᠎ᠨᠠᠷ</uig> elder brothers
<uig rom="aqas">ᠠᠬᠠᠰ</uig> older people
<uig rom="aqamad">ᠠᠬᠠᠮᠠᠳ</uig> seniors, authorities
On the other hand, a word can take more than one plural suffix at the same time.
<uig rom="blam-a-nar-ud">ᠪᠯᠠᠮ᠎ᠠ ᠎ᠨᠠᠷ ᠤᠳ</uig> lamas
<uig rom="qaγad-ud">ᠬᠠᠭᠠᠳ ᠤᠳ</uig> khaghans
<uig rom="eres-üd">ᠡᠷᠡᠰ ᠤᠳ</uig> men
There are the following cases : nominative, genitive, dative-locative, accusative, ablative, instrumental, and comitative.

The case suffixes are the same in the singular and plural. They are written separately from the stem, which coincides with the nominative. Stems ending in n may lose the latter in certain cases or they may also retain it in all cases.
There are two principal kinds of declension: the simple declension and a declension with the reflexive-possessive suffix indicating the possessor of the object concerned.
Besides, certain case forms may take an additional suffix of another case. Such combined forms are called double cases.
The simple declension is the same as the declension in Indo-European languages. This is a system of forms expressing various relations of the object in question to other objects or actions.
The nominative ("who?," "what?") has no suffix and coincides with the stem. Under the influence of the colloquial language stems ending in n may drop the final n.
The nominative of the plural ends in one of the plural suffixes.
<uig rom="kümün">ᠺᠦᠮᠦᠨ</uig> man
<uig rom="ger">ᠭᠡᠷ</uig> house
<uig rom="morin">ᠮᠣᠷᠢᠨ</uig> or <uig rom="mori">ᠮᠣᠷᠢ</uig> horse
<uig rom="ulus">ᠤᠯᠤᠰ</uig> state
<uig rom="dalai">ᠳᠠᠯᠠᠢ</uig> sea
<uig rom="aγula">ᠠᠭᠤᠯᠠ</uig> mountain
See also §441, §495
The genitive ("whose?") has several suffixes. Their use depends upon the final sound of the stem.
Stems ending in vowels or diphthongs take the suffix <uig rom="-yin">᠎ᠶᠢᠨ</uig> .
<uig rom="aq-a-yin">ᠠᠬ᠎ᠠ ᠎ᠶᠢᠨ</uig> of the elder brother
<uig rom="aγula-yin">ᠠᠭᠤᠯᠠ ᠎ᠶᠢᠨ</uig> of the mountain
<uig rom="er-e-yin">ᠡᠷ᠎ᠡ ᠎ᠶᠢᠨ</uig> of the man
<uig rom="dalai-yin">ᠳᠠᠯᠠᠢ ᠎ᠶᠢᠨ</uig> of the sea
<uig rom="cinu-a-yin">ᠴᠢᠨᠤ᠎ᠠ ᠎ᠶᠢᠨ</uig> of the Wolf
See also §500
Stems ending in the consonant n take the suffix <uig rom="-u/-ü"> ᠤ</uig> .
<uig rom="noyan-u">ᠨᠣᠶᠠᠨ ᠤ</uig> of the prince
<uig rom="keüken-ü">ᠺᠡᠦᠺᠡᠨ ᠤ</uig> of the child
<uig rom="morin-u">ᠮᠣᠷᠢᠨ ᠤ</uig> of the horse
<uig rom="sün-ü">ᠰᠦᠨ ᠤ</uig> of the milk
Stems ending in the remaining consonants take the suffix <uig rom="-un/-ün"> ᠤᠨ</uig> .
<uig rom="ulus-un">ᠤᠯᠤᠰ ᠤᠨ</uig> of the people, of the state
<uig rom="γajar-un">ᠭᠠᠵᠠᠷ ᠤᠨ</uig> of the country
<uig rom="γal-un">ᠭᠠᠯ ᠤᠨ</uig> of the fire
<uig rom="bicig-ün">ᠪᠢᠴᠢᠭ ᠤᠨ</uig> of the letter
<uig rom="jobalang-un">ᠵᠣᠪᠠᠯᠠᠩ ᠤᠨ</uig> of the sufferance
<uig rom="em-ün">ᠡᠮ ᠤᠨ</uig> of the medicine
In the non-classical language, especially in the language influenced by dialects, there occur other genitive suffixes.
The suffixes <uig rom="-yin"> ᠎ᠶᠢᠨ</uig> , <uig rom="-u"> ᠤ</uig> , and <uig rom="-un"> ᠤᠨ</uig> are used at random
<uig rom="surγaγuli-u">ᠰᠤᠷᠭᠠᠭᠤᠯᠢ ᠤ</uig> of the school
<uig rom="γajar-yin">ᠭᠠᠵᠠᠷ ᠶᠢᠨ</uig> of the country
Instead of the suffix <uig rom="-u"> ᠤ</uig> the colloquial suffix <uig rom="-i"> ᠢ</uig> is used
<uig rom="qaγan-i">ᠬᠠᠭᠠᠨ ᠢ</uig> of the khaghan
<uig rom="morin-i">ᠮᠣᠷᠢᠨ ᠢ</uig> of the horse
Instead of the suffix <uig rom="-u"> ᠤ</uig> another colloquial suffix <uig rom="-ai/-ei">᠎ᠠᠢ</uig> is sometimes used:
<uig rom="qaγanai">ᠬᠠᠭᠠᠨᠠᠢ</uig> of the khaghan
<uig rom="usunai">ᠤᠰᠤᠨᠠᠢ</uig> of the water
Stems ending in diphthongs or long vowels sometimes take the colloquial suffix <uig rom="-giyin"> ᠎ᠭᠢᠶᠢᠨ</uig> instead of the classical suffix <uig rom="-yin"> ᠎ᠶᠢᠨ</uig> :
<uig rom="buluu-giyin">ᠪᠤᠯᠤᠤ ᠎ᠭᠢᠶᠢᠨ</uig> of the club
The dative-locative ("to whom?," "where?") is formed with the suffixes <uig rom="-dur/-dür">ᠳ᠋‍‍ᠤ‍ᠷ</uig> , <uig rom="-tur/-tür">᠎ᠲᠤᠷ</uig> , and <uig rom="-a/-e">᠎ᠡ</uig> .

Stems ending in vowels, in all sorts of diphthongs, and in the consonants n, ng, l, and m take the suffix <uig rom="-dur/-dür"> ᠳ᠋‍‍ᠤ‍ᠷ</uig> . Stems ending in any of the remaining consonants, i. e., γ, b, s, d, g, and r take the suffix <uig rom="-tur/-tür"> ᠎ᠲᠤᠷ</uig> . The suffix <uig rom="-dur"> ᠳ᠋‍‍ᠤ‍ᠷ</uig> is written with the medial character for d, the suffix <uig rom="-tur"> ᠎ᠲᠤᠷ</uig> is written with the initial character for t.
<uig rom="dalai-dur">ᠳᠠᠯᠠᠢ ᠳ᠋‍‍ᠤ‍ᠷ</uig> to the sea, in the sea
<uig rom="aq-a-dur">ᠠᠬ᠎ᠠ ᠳ᠋‍‍ᠤ‍ᠷ</uig> to the elder brother
<uig rom="em-e-dür">ᠡᠮ᠎ᠡ ᠳ᠋‍‍ᠤ‍ᠷ</uig> to the woman
<uig rom="tüsimel-dür">ᠲᠦᠰᠢᠮᠡᠯ ᠳ᠋‍‍ᠤ‍ᠷ</uig> to the official
<uig rom="qadum-dur">ᠬᠠᠳᠤᠮ ᠳ᠋‍‍ᠤ‍ᠷ</uig> to the father-in-law
<uig rom="qaγan-dur">ᠬᠠᠭᠠᠨ ᠳ᠋‍‍ᠤ‍ᠷ</uig> to the khaghan
<uig rom="jirγalang-dur">ᠵᠢᠷᠭᠠᠯᠠᠩ ᠳ᠋‍‍ᠤ‍ᠷ</uig> to the happiness
<uig rom="adaq-tur">ᠠᠳᠠᠬ ᠎ᠲᠤᠷ</uig> in the end
<uig rom="tölöb-tür">ᠲᠥᠯᠥᠪ ᠎ᠲᠤᠷ</uig> to the pattern
<uig rom="ulus-tur">ᠤᠯᠤᠰ ᠎ᠲᠤᠷ</uig> to the people
<uig rom="nököd-tür">ᠨᠥᠺᠥᠳ ᠎ᠲᠤᠷ</uig> to the friends
<uig rom="bicig-tür">ᠪᠢᠴᠢᠭ ᠎ᠲᠤᠷ</uig> in the letter
<uig rom="nökör-tür">ᠨᠥᠺᠥᠷ ᠎ᠲᠤᠷ</uig> to the friend
See also §504
In the non-classical language the suffixes <uig rom="-du/-dü"> ᠎ᠳᠤ</uig> and <uig rom=" -tu/-tü"> ᠎ᠲᠤ</uig> or <uig rom="-da/-de"> ᠎ᠳᠠ</uig> and <uig rom="-ta/-te"> ᠎ᠲᠠ</uig> are used.
<uig rom="morin-du">ᠮᠣᠷᠢᠨ ᠎ᠳᠤ</uig> or <uig rom="ᠮᠣᠷᠢᠨ ᠎ᠳᠠ"></uig> morin-da to the horse
<uig rom="γajar-tu">ᠭᠠᠵᠠᠷ ᠎ᠲᠤ</uig> or <uig rom="γajar-ta">ᠭᠠᠵᠠᠷ ᠎ᠲᠠ</uig> in the country

Another dative-locative suffix is <uig rom="-a/-e">᠎ᠡ</uig> . In the modern language this is less used than in the classical and especially in the pre-classical language, where it was widely used. There is no difference between the function of this suffix and that of the suffixes discussed in the previous sections.
The suffix <uig rom="-a/-e">᠎ᠡ</uig> occurs with stems ending in consonants and in diphthongs with final i.
<uig rom="γajar-a">ᠭᠠᠵᠠᠷ᠎ᠠ</uig> to or in the country
<uig rom="yabuqui-a">ᠶᠠᠪᠤᠬᠤᠢ᠎ᠠ</uig> in order to go
<uig rom="edür-e">ᠡᠳᠦᠷ᠎ᠡ</uig> to the day
<uig rom="taulai-a">ᠲᠠᠤᠯᠠᠢ᠎ᠠ</uig> to the hare
<uig rom="qaγan-a">ᠬᠠᠭᠠᠨ᠎ᠠ</uig> to the khaghan
<uig rom="dalai-a">ᠳᠠᠯᠠᠢ᠎ᠠ</uig> to the sea

The accusative ("whom?," "what?") is formed with the suffix <uig rom="-yi"> ᠎ᠶᠢ</uig> which is added to stems ending in vowels and diphthongs or with the suffix <uig rom="-i"> ᠢ</uig> which is added to stems ending in consonants. The final n of the stem may be dropped and in this case the suffix is <uig rom=""> ᠎ᠶᠢ.</uig> -yi.
<uig rom="aq-a-yi">ᠠᠬ᠎ᠠ ᠎ᠶᠢ</uig> the elder brother
<uig rom="modun-i">ᠮᠣᠳᠤᠨ ᠢ</uig> or <uig rom="modu-yi">ᠮᠣᠳᠤ ᠎ᠶᠢ</uig> the tree
<uig rom="noqai-yi">ᠨᠣᠬᠠᠢ ᠎ᠶᠢ</uig> the dog
<uig rom="nökör-i">ᠨᠥᠺᠥᠷ ᠢ</uig> the friend
<uig rom="morin-i">ᠮᠣᠷᠢᠨ ᠢ</uig> or <uig rom="mori-yi">ᠮᠣᠷᠢ ᠎ᠶᠢ</uig> the horse
<uig rom="ulus-i">ᠤᠯᠤᠰ ᠢ</uig> the people
See also §512

In the non-classical language the suffixes <uig rom="-yi"> ᠎ᠶᠢ</uig> and <uig rom="-i"> ᠢ</uig> are sometimes used indifferently. Words ending in long vowels or diphthongs may take the colloquial suffix <uig rom="-gi"> ᠎ᠭᠢ</uig> or <uig rom="-yigi"> ᠎ᠶᠢᠭᠢ</uig> .
<uig rom="γajar-i">ᠭᠠᠵᠠᠷ ᠢ</uig> or <uig rom="γajar-yi">ᠭᠠᠵᠠᠷ ᠎ᠶᠢ</uig> the country
<uig rom="noqai-gi">ᠨᠣᠬᠠᠢ ᠎ᠭᠢ</uig> or <uig rom="noqai-yigi">ᠨᠣᠬᠠᠢ ᠎ᠶᠢᠭᠢ</uig> the dog
The ablative ("from whom?," "whence?") has the suffix <uig rom="-aca/-ece">ᠡᠴᠡ</uig> written with the medial letter for a/e.
<uig rom="aq-a-aca">ᠠᠬ᠎ᠠ ᠡᠴᠡ</uig> from the elder brother
<uig rom="dalai-aca">ᠳᠠᠯᠠᠢ ᠡᠴᠡ</uig> from the sea
<uig rom="em-e-ece">ᠡᠮ᠎ᠡ ᠡᠴᠡ</uig> from the woman
<uig rom="qaγan-aca">ᠬᠠᠭᠠᠨ ᠡᠴᠡ</uig> from the khaghan
<uig rom="ger-ece">ᠭᠡᠷ ᠡᠴᠡ</uig> from the house
See also §524

In the pre-classical language the suffix is often <uig rom="-ca/-ce">᠎ᠴᠠ</uig> . The suffix <uig rom="-aca/-ece">ᠡᠴᠡ</uig> is a compound ending consisting of the ancient dative-locative suffix <uig rom="-a/-e">᠎ᠡ</uig> and the primary ablative suffix <uig rom="-ca/-ce">᠎ᠴᠡ.</uig> .
<uig rom="morin-ca">ᠮᠣᠷᠢᠨ ᠎ᠴᠠ</uig> from the horse
<uig rom="ger-ce">ᠭᠡᠷ ᠎ᠴᠡ</uig> from the house
n modern popular books the colloquial suffix <uig rom="-asa/-ese">᠎ᠡᠰᠡ</uig> sometimes occurs.
<uig rom="usunasa">ᠤᠰᠤᠨᠠᠰᠠ</uig> from the water

The instrumental ("with whom?," "by whom?," "through what?," "by means of what?") is formed with the suffixes <uig rom="-bar/-ber">᠎ᠪᠡᠷ</uig> or <uig rom="-iyar/-iyer"> ᠢᠶᠠᠷ</uig> . Stems ending in vowels or diphthongs take the suffix <uig rom="-bar/-ber">᠎ᠪᠡᠷ</uig> .
<uig rom="kituγa-bar">ᠺᠢᠲᠤᠭᠠ ᠎ᠪᠠᠷ</uig> with the knife
<uig rom="dalai-bar">ᠳᠠᠯᠠᠢ ᠎ᠪᠠᠷ</uig> by sea
<uig rom="kele-ber">ᠺᠡᠯᠡ ᠎ᠪᠡᠷ</uig> by means of the tongue
See also §531, §682

Stems ending in consonants take the suffix <uig rom="-iyar/-iyer"> ᠢᠶᠠᠷ</uig> . If the final n of the stem is dropped, the suffix is <uig rom="-bar/-ber">᠎ᠪᠡᠷ</uig> . If the final n is retained, the suffix is <uig rom="-iyar/-iyer"> ᠢᠶᠠᠷ</uig> .
<uig rom="γar-iyar">ᠭᠠᠷ ᠢᠶᠠᠷ</uig> with the hand
<uig rom="köl-iyer">ᠺᠥᠯ ᠢᠶᠡᠷ</uig> with the foot
<uig rom="morin-iyar">ᠮᠣᠷᠢᠨ ᠢᠶᠠᠷ</uig> or mori-bar by horse
The comitative ("with whom?," "together with whom?") has the suffix <uig rom="-luγ-a/-lüge"> ᠎ᠯᠤᠭ᠎ᠠ/᠎ᠯᠦᠭᠡ</uig> .
<uig rom="aq-a-luγ-a">ᠠᠬ ᠠ ᠯᠤᠭ ᠠ</uig> with the elder brother
<uig rom="qaγan-luγ-a">ᠬᠠᠭᠠᠨ ᠯᠤᠭ ᠠ</uig> with the khaghan
<uig rom="keüken-lüge">ᠺᠡᠦᠺᠡᠨ ᠯᠦᠭᠡ</uig> with the child
<uig rom="eme-lüge">ᠡᠮᠡ ᠯᠦᠭᠡ</uig> with the woman
In modern popular books and manuscripts by semi-literate people, the colloquial suffix <uig rom="-la/-le"> ᠎ᠯᠠ</uig> occurs.
<uig rom="keükenle">ᠺᠡᠦᠺᠡᠨᠯᠡ</uig> with the child
See also §538
In modern books influenced by the colloquial language, the colloquial suffix <uig rom="-tai/-tei"> ᠎ᠲᠠᠢ</uig> , with the final n of the stem dropped, is used (cf. §138).
<uig rom="aq-a-tai">ᠠᠬ᠎ᠠ ᠎ᠲᠠᠢ</uig> with the elder brother
<uig rom="ekener-tei">ᠡᠺᠡᠨᠡᠷ ᠎ᠲᠡᠢ</uig> with the woman
<uig rom="mori-tai">ᠮᠣᠷᠢ ᠎ᠲᠠᠢ</uig> with the horse

The following words will be declined here : <uig rom="aq-a">ᠠᠬ᠎ᠠ</uig> "elder brother," <uig rom="eke">ᠡᠺᠡ</uig> "mother," <uig rom="noqai">ᠨᠣᠬᠠᠢ</uig> "dog," <uig rom="morin">ᠮᠣᠷᠢᠨ</uig> or <uig rom="mori">ᠮᠣᠷᠢ</uig> "horse," <uig rom="jobalang">ᠵᠣᠪᠠᠯᠠᠩ</uig> "suffering," <uig rom="γajar">ᠭᠠᠵᠠᠷ</uig> "country," <uig rom="ulus">ᠤᠯᠤᠰ</uig> "people," and <uig rom="bulaq">ᠪᠤᠯᠠᠬ</uig> "spring, well."

Case||||;; Nominative|ᠠᠬ ᠠ|ᠡᠺᠡ|ᠨᠣᠬᠠᠢ|ᠮᠣᠷᠢᠨ or ᠮᠣᠷᠢ;; Genitive|ᠠᠬ ᠠ ᠶᠢᠨ|ᠡᠺᠡ ᠶᠢᠨ|ᠨᠣᠬᠠᠢ ᠶᠢᠨ|ᠮᠣᠷᠢᠨ ᠤ;; Dative_Locative|ᠠᠬ ᠠ ᠳ᠋ᠤᠷ
or
ᠠᠬ ᠠ ᠎ᠳᠤ|ᠡᠺᠡ ᠳ᠋ᠤᠷ
or
ᠡᠺᠡ ᠎ᠳᠦ|ᠨᠣᠬᠠᠢ ᠳ᠋ᠤᠷ
or
ᠨᠣᠬᠠᠢ ᠎ᠳᠤ|ᠮᠣᠷᠢᠨ ᠳ᠋ᠤᠷ
or
ᠮᠣᠷᠢᠨ ᠎ᠳᠤ;; Accusative|ᠠᠬ ᠠ ᠶᠢ|ᠡᠺᠡ ᠶᠢ|ᠨᠣᠬᠠᠢ ᠶᠢ|ᠮᠣᠷᠢᠨ ᠢ
or
ᠮᠣᠷᠢ ᠶᠢ;; Ablative|ᠠᠬ ᠠ ᠡᠴᠡ|ᠡᠺᠡ ᠡᠴᠡ|ᠨᠣᠬᠠᠢ ᠡᠴᠡ|ᠮᠣᠷᠢᠨ ᠡᠴᠡ;; Instrumental|ᠠᠬ ᠠ ᠎ᠪᠠᠷ|ᠡᠺᠡ ᠎ᠪᠡᠷ|ᠨᠣᠬᠠᠢ ᠎ᠪᠠᠷ|ᠮᠣᠷᠢᠨ ᠢᠶᠠᠷ
or
ᠮᠣᠷᠢ ᠎ᠪᠠᠷ;; Comitative|ᠠᠬ ᠠ ᠯᠤᠭ ᠠ|ᠡᠺᠡ ᠯᠦᠭᠡ|ᠨᠣᠬᠠᠢ ᠯᠤᠭ ᠠ|ᠮᠣᠷᠢᠨ ᠯᠤᠭ ᠠ Case||||;; Nominative|ᠵᠣᠪᠠᠯᠠᠩ|ᠭᠠᠵᠠᠷ|ᠤᠯᠤᠰ|ᠪᠤᠯᠠᠭ;; Genitive|ᠵᠣᠪᠠᠯᠠᠩ ᠤᠨ|ᠭᠠᠵᠠᠷ ᠤᠨ|ᠤᠯᠤᠰ ᠤᠨ|ᠪᠤᠯᠠᠭ ᠤᠨ;; Dative_Locative|ᠵᠣᠪᠠᠯᠠᠩ ᠳ᠋ᠤᠷ
or
ᠵᠣᠪᠠᠯᠠᠩ ᠎ᠳᠤ
or
ᠵᠣᠪᠠᠯᠠᠩ ᠠ|ᠭᠠᠵᠠᠷ ᠲᠤᠷ
or
ᠭᠠᠵᠠᠷ ᠎ᠲᠤ
or
ᠭᠠᠵᠠᠷ ᠠ|ᠤᠯᠤᠰ ᠲᠤᠷ
or
ᠤᠯᠤᠰ ᠎ᠲᠤ
or
ᠤᠯᠤᠰ ᠠ|ᠪᠤᠯᠠᠭ ᠲᠤᠷ
or
ᠪᠤᠯᠠᠭ ᠎ᠲᠤ
or
ᠪᠤᠯᠠᠭ ᠠ;; Accusative|ᠵᠣᠪᠠᠯᠠᠩ ᠢ|ᠭᠠᠵᠠᠷ ᠢ|ᠤᠯᠤᠰ ᠢ|ᠪᠤᠯᠠᠭ ᠢ;; Ablative|ᠵᠣᠪᠠᠯᠠᠩ ᠡᠴᠡ|ᠭᠠᠵᠠᠷ ᠡᠴᠡ|ᠤᠯᠤᠰ ᠡᠴᠡ|ᠪᠤᠯᠠᠭ ᠡᠴᠡ;; Instrumental|ᠵᠣᠪᠠᠯᠠᠩ ᠢᠶᠠᠷ|ᠭᠠᠵᠠᠷ ᠢᠶᠠᠷ|ᠤᠯᠤᠰ ᠢᠶᠠᠷ|ᠪᠤᠯᠠᠭ ᠢᠶᠠᠷ;; Comitative|ᠵᠣᠪᠠᠯᠠᠩ ᠯᠤᠭ ᠠ|ᠭᠠᠵᠠᠷ ᠯᠤᠭ ᠠ|ᠤᠯᠤᠰ ᠯᠤᠭ ᠠ|ᠪᠤᠯᠠᠭ ᠯᠤᠭ ᠠ

To certain case forms suffixes of other cases can be added. Thus double case forms arise. Such double cases are the following: 1) the genitive-dative (-locative), 2) the dative- (locative-) ablative, 3) the comitative-instrumental, and 4) almost all cases of the comitative in <uig rom="-tai/-tei."> ᠎ᠲᠠᠢ</uig>

The genitive-dative-locative ("to whom?," "at whose?," e. g., English "at father's"), which is rarely used, is an influence of the colloquial language where such forms are usual. Only the genitive in <uig rom="-yin"> ᠎ᠶᠢᠨ</uig> or <uig rom="-ai">᠎ᠠᠢ</uig> can take a dative-locative suffix. The combined genitive-dative-locative suffix is <uig rom="-yin-du(r)"> ᠎ᠶᠢᠨ ᠎ᠳᠤᠷ</uig> or <uig rom=" -ai-du(r)">᠎ᠠᠢ ᠎ᠳᠤᠷ</uig>.
<uig rom="baqsi-yin-dur">ᠪᠠᠬᠰᠢ ᠎ᠶᠢᠨ ᠳ᠋‍‍ᠤ‍ᠷ</uig> to the teacher's, at the teacher's
<uig rom="eke-yin-dür">ᠡᠺᠡ ᠎ᠶᠢᠨ ᠳ᠋‍‍ᠤ‍ᠷ</uig> to mother's, at mother's
<uig rom="noyan-ai-dur">ᠨᠣᠶᠠᠨ᠎ᠠᠢ ᠳ᠋‍‍ᠤ‍ᠷ</uig> to the prince's, at the prince's

The usual ablative suffix <uig rom="-aca/-ece">ᠡᠴᠡ</uig> is, as indicated in § 291 above, a combination of the original dative-locative suffix <uig rom="-a/-e">᠎ᠡ</uig> and the ancient ablative suffix <uig rom=" -ca/-ce">ᠴᠡ</uig>. Now, there is another combination of the preclassical dative-locative suffix and the ablative suffix <uig rom=" -ca/-ce">᠎ᠴᠡ</uig>. This is the combined suffix <uig rom=" -daca/-dece">ᠳ᠋ᠡᠴᠡ</uig>, <uig rom="-taca/-tece">᠎ᠲᠡᠴᠡ</uig> which sometimes occurs in the pre-classical language. Very few words, however, are now used in this form.
<uig rom="ger-tece">ᠭᠡᠷ ᠎ᠲᠡᠴᠡ</uig> from the house
<uig rom="morin-daca">ᠮᠣᠷᠢᠨ ᠳ᠋ᠠᠴᠠ</uig> from the horse (pre-classical)
<uig rom="usun-daca">ᠤᠰᠤᠨ ᠳ᠋ᠠᠴᠠ</uig> from the water
The comitative-instrumental has the same function as the simple comitative.
<uig rom="noyan-luγ-a-bar">ᠨᠣᠶᠠᠨ ᠯᠤᠭ ᠠ ᠎ᠪᠠᠷ</uig> together with the prince
<uig rom="baqsi-luγ-a-bar">ᠪᠠᠬᠰᠢ ᠯᠤᠭ ᠠ ᠎ᠪᠠᠷ</uig> together with the teacher
In the non-classical language the double comitative-instrumental suffix is <uig rom="-lar/-ler"> ᠎ᠯᠠᠷ</uig> .
<uig rom="qatun-lar">ᠬᠠᠲᠤᠨ ᠎ᠯᠠᠷ</uig> together with the queen

The colloquial comitative with the suffix <uig rom="-tai/-tei"> ᠎ᠲᠠᠢ</uig> , which was originally a denominal noun with the meaning "possessing something" (see § 138), can take almost all case suffixes.
Comitative <uig rom="-tai/-tei"> ᠎ᠲᠠᠢ</uig> with someone, he and another person
Comitative-Genitive <uig rom="-tai-yin">᠎ᠲᠠᠢ ᠶᠢᠨ</uig> someone's and another person's
Comitative-Dative-Locative <uig rom="-tai-dur">᠎ᠲᠠᠢ ᠳ᠋ᠤᠷ</uig> to someone and another person
Comitative-Accusative <uig rom="-tai-yi">᠎ᠲᠠᠢ ᠎ᠶᠢ</uig> someone with another person
Comitative-Ablative <uig rom="-tai-aca">᠎ᠲᠠᠢ ᠡᠴᠡ</uig> from someone and another person
Comitative-Instrumental <uig rom="-tai-bar">᠎ᠲᠠᠢ ᠎ᠪᠠᠷ</uig> or <uig rom="-tayiyar">᠎ᠲᠠᠶᠢᠶᠠᠷ</uig> with someone

The reflexive-possessive declension is a system of case forms not only indicating the relations of the object concerned to other objects (or actions) but also indicating that the object belongs to the person acting. While <uig rom="aq-a-dur">ᠠᠬ ᠠ ᠳ᠋ᠤᠷ</uig> merely means "to the elder brother," not indicating to whose brother, the correaponding reflexive-possessive form signifies "to his own (i. e., the subject's) elder brother." The cases of this declension differ from the eases of the plain declension in having an additional suffix which expresses the idea "his" (Latin suus). This "his" refers to the subject. For instance in the sentence "He took his book," "his" refers to "he." In English there is no special reflexive possessive pronoun. Therefore "his" can express in English two different ideas "his," i. e., "the subject's" and "another person's."
The reflexive-possessive declension does not have a nominative.

entry.title: Accidence - Nouns - Reflexive possessive declension
entry.title2: Nouns - Declension - Reflexive possessive declension - Genitive

paragraphs.paragraph: All nouns, regardless of the final sound of the stem, can take the suffix <uig rom="-yuγan/-yügen">᠎ᠶᠤᠭᠠᠨ/ ᠎ᠶᠦᠭᠡᠨ</uig>.
<uig rom="γar-yuγan">ᠭᠠᠷ ᠎ᠶᠤᠭᠠᠨ</uig> of his own hand
<uig rom="naγacu-yuγan">ᠨᠠᠭᠠᠴᠤ ᠎ᠶᠤᠭᠠᠨ</uig> of his own (maternal) uncle
<uig rom="ger-yügen">ᠭᠡᠷ ᠎ᠶᠦᠭᠡᠨ</uig> of his own house

entry.title: Accidence - Nouns - Reflexive possessive declension
entry.title2: Nouns - Declension - Reflexive possessive declension - Genitive

paragraphs.paragraph: Nouns ending in consonants can take the suffix <uig rom="-iyan/-iyen">ᠢᠶᠠᠨ/ ᠢᠶᠡᠨ</uig>; those ending in vowels take the suffix <uig rom="-ban/-ben">᠎ᠪᠠᠨ/ ᠎ᠪᠡᠨ</uig>.
<uig rom="naγacu-ban">ᠨᠠᠭᠠᠴᠤ ᠎ᠪᠠᠨ</uig> of his own uncle
<uig rom="γar-iyan">ᠭᠠᠷ ᠢᠶᠠᠨ</uig> of his own hand
<uig rom="ger-iyen">ᠭᠡᠷ ᠢᠶᠡᠨ</uig> of his own house

entry.title: Accidence - Nouns - Reflexive possessive declension
entry.title2: Nouns - Declension - Reflexive possessive declension - Genitive

paragraphs.paragraph: A third possible form includes the usual genitive suffixes and <uig rom="-iyan/-iyen">ᠢᠶᠠ</uig> or <uig rom="-ban/-ben">᠎ᠪᠠᠨ</uig>.
