If the genitive suffix ends in n (<uig rom="-un">ᠤᠨ</uig> or <uig rom="-yin">ᠶᠢᠨ</uig>) the reflexive-possessive suffix is <uig rom="-iyan">ᠢᠶᠠᠨ</uig>; if the genitive suffix ends in a vowel (suffix <uig rom="-u">ᠤ</uig>) the possessive suffix <uig rom="-ban/-ben">᠎ᠪᠠᠨ</uig> is added. Thus there are the following combinations: <uig rom="-un-iyan/-ün-iyen">ᠤᠨ ᠢᠶᠠᠨ</uig>, <uig rom="-yin-iyan/-yin-iyen">ᠶᠢᠨ ᠢᠶᠠᠨ</uig>, and <uig rom="-u-ban/-ü-ben">ᠤ ᠎ᠪᠠᠨ</uig>.
<uig rom="naγacu-yin-iyan">ᠨᠠᠭᠠᠴᠤ ᠶᠢᠨ ᠢᠶᠠᠨ</uig> of his own uncle
<uig rom="ger-ün-iyen">ᠭᠡᠷ ᠤᠨ ᠢᠶᠡᠨ</uig> of his own house
<uig rom="morin-u-ban">ᠮᠣᠷᠢᠨ ᠤ ᠎ᠪᠠᠨ</uig> of his own horse

entry.title: Accidence - Nouns - Reflexive possessive declension
entry.title2: Nouns - Declension - Reflexive possessive declension - Dative-locative

paragraphs.paragraph: The usual dative-locative with the suffix <uig rom="-dur/-dür"> ᠳ᠋‍‍ᠤ‍ᠷ</uig> (and <uig rom="-tur/-tür"> ᠎ᠲᠤᠷ</uig> ) takes the reflexive-possessive suffix <uig rom="-iyan/-iyen">ᠢᠶᠠᠨ</uig>. The non-ciassical form in <uig rom="-du/-dü"> ᠳ᠋‍‍ᠤ</uig> or <uig rom="-tu/-tü">᠎ᠲᠤ</uig> takes the other suffix, <uig rom="-ban/-ben">᠎ᠪᠠᠨ</uig>.
The dative-locative in <uig rom=" -a/-e">᠎ᠡ</uig> does not occur in this declension.
<uig rom="naγacu-dur-iyan">ᠨᠠᠭᠠᠴᠤ ᠳ᠋ᠤᠷ ᠢᠶᠠᠨ</uig> to his own (maternal) uncle
<uig rom="γar-tur-iyan">ᠭᠠᠷ ᠲᠤᠷ ᠢᠶᠠᠨ</uig> in his own hand
<uig rom="naγacu-du-ban">ᠨᠠᠭᠠᠴᠤ ᠎ᠳᠤ ᠎ᠪᠠᠨ</uig> to his own (maternal) uncle
<uig rom="γar-tu-ban">ᠭᠠᠷ ᠎ᠲᠤ ᠎ᠪᠠᠨ</uig> in his own hand

entry.title: Accidence - Nouns - Reflexive possessive declension
entry.title2: Nouns - Declension - Reflexive possessive declension - Dative-locative

paragraphs.paragraph: The usual dative-locative suffix is <uig rom="-daγan/-degen">ᠳ᠋ᠠᠭᠠᠨ/ ᠳ᠋ᠡᠭᠡᠨ</uig>, <uig rom="-taγan/-tegen">᠎ᠲᠠᠭᠠᠨ/ ᠎ᠲᠡᠭᠡᠨ</uig>. (The latter occurs on stems ending in γ, b, s, d, g, and r.)
This suffix is a combined ending consisting of the pre-classical dative-locative suffix <uig rom="-da/-de">ᠳ᠋ᠠ</uig> and the reflexive-possessive suffix (-*γan).
<uig rom="naγacu-daγan">ᠨᠠᠭᠠᠴᠤ ᠳ᠋ᠠᠭᠠᠨ</uig> to his own uncle
<uig rom="γar-taγan">ᠭᠠᠷ ᠎ᠲᠠᠭᠠᠨ</uig> in his own hand
<uig rom="eke-degen">ᠡᠺᠡ ᠳ᠋ᠡᠭᠡᠨ</uig> to his own mother
<uig rom="ger-tegen">ᠭᠡᠷ ᠎ᠲᠡᠭᠡᠨ</uig> in his own house

entry.title: Accidence - Nouns - Reflexive possessive declension
entry.title2: Nouns - Declension - Reflexive possessive declension - Accusative

paragraphs.paragraph: The accusative ending in <uig rom="-i">ᠢ</uig> or <uig rom="-yi"> ᠎ᠶᠢ</uig> takes the possessive suffix <uig rom="-ban/-ben"> ᠎ᠪᠠᠨ</uig> .
<uig rom="γar-i-ban">ᠭᠠᠷ ᠢ ᠎ᠪᠠᠨ</uig> his own hand
<uig rom="naγacu-yi-ban">ᠨᠠᠭᠠᠴᠤ ᠶᠢ ᠎ᠪᠠᠨ</uig> his own uncle

entry.title: Accidence - Nouns - Reflexive possessive declension
entry.title2: Nouns - Declension - Reflexive possessive declension - Accusative

paragraphs.paragraph: Another possible form is that coinciding with the genitive: the suffix is either <uig rom="-yuγan/-yügen">᠎ᠶᠤᠭᠠᠨ/ ᠎ᠶᠦᠭᠡᠨ</uig> or <uig rom="-iyan/-iyen">ᠢᠶᠠᠨ</uig> and <uig rom="-ban/-ben"> ᠎ᠪᠠᠨ</uig> according to the rules given in reference to the genitive.
<uig rom="naγacu-yuγan">ᠨᠠᠭᠠᠴᠤ ᠎ᠶᠤᠭᠠᠨ</uig> or <uig rom="naγacu-ban">ᠨᠠᠭᠠᠴᠤ ᠎ᠪᠠᠨ</uig> his own (maternal) uncle
<uig rom="γar-yuγan">ᠭᠠᠷ ᠎ᠶᠤᠭᠠᠨ</uig> or <uig rom="γar-iyan">ᠭᠠᠷ ᠢᠶᠠᠨ</uig> his own hand
<uig rom="ger-yügen">ᠭᠡᠷ ᠎ᠶᠦᠭᠡᠨ</uig> or <uig rom="ger-iyen">ᠭᠡᠷ ᠢᠶᠡᠨ</uig> his own house
<uig rom="em-e-yügen">ᠡᠮ ᠡ ᠎ᠶᠦᠭᠡᠨ</uig> or <uig rom="em-e-ben">ᠡᠮ ᠡ ᠎ᠪᠡᠨ</uig> his own wife

entry.title: Accidence - Nouns - Reflexive possessive declension
entry.title2: Nouns - Declension - Reflexive possessive declension - Ablative

paragraphs.paragraph: The usual ablative suffix takes the possessive suffix <uig rom=" -ban/-ben"> ᠎ᠪᠠᠨ</uig>.
<uig rom="naγacu-aca-ban">ᠨᠠᠭᠠᠴᠤ ᠡᠴᠡ ᠎ᠪᠠᠨ</uig> from his own uncle
<uig rom="ger-ece-ben">ᠭᠡᠷ ᠡᠴᠡ ᠎ᠪᠡᠨ</uig> from his own house

entry.title: Accidence - Nouns - Reflexive possessive declension
entry.title2: Nouns - Declension - Reflexive possessive declension - Ablative

paragraphs.paragraph: Another possible form includes the combined suffix <uig rom="-acaγan/-ecegen">ᠡᠴᠡᠭᠠᠨ/ ᠡᠴᠡᠭᠡᠨ</uig>.
<uig rom="naγacu-acaγan">ᠨᠠᠭᠠᠴᠤ ᠡᠴᠡᠭᠠᠨ</uig> from his own uncle
<uig rom="ger-ecegen">ᠭᠡᠷ ᠡᠴᠡᠭᠡᠨ</uig> from his own house

entry.title: Accidence - Nouns - Reflexive possessive declension
entry.title2: Nouns - Declension - Reflexive possessive declension - Instrumental

paragraphs.paragraph: To the usual instrumental forms, the possessive suffix <uig rom="-iyan/-iyen">ᠢᠶᠠᠨ</uig> is added.
<uig rom="jida-bar-iyan">ᠵᠢᠳᠠ ᠎ᠪᠠᠷ ᠢᠶᠠᠨ</uig> with his own spear
<uig rom="köl-iyer-iyen">ᠺᠥᠯ ᠢᠶᠡᠷ ᠢᠶᠡᠨ</uig> with his own foot

entry.title: Accidence - Nouns - Reflexive possessive declension
entry.title2: Nouns - Declension - Reflexive possessive declension - Comitative

paragraphs.paragraph: The comitative ending in <uig rom="-luγ-a/-lüge">ᠯᠤᠭ ᠠ/ ᠯᠦᠭᠡ</uig> takes the possessive suffix <uig rom="-ban /-ben"> ᠎ᠪᠠᠨ</uig> .
<uig rom="naγacu-luγ-a-ban">ᠨᠠᠭᠠᠴᠤ ᠯᠤᠭ ᠠ ᠎ᠪᠠᠨ</uig> together with his own (maternal) uncle
<uig rom="em-e-lüge-ben">ᠡᠮ ᠡ ᠯᠦᠭᠡ ᠎ᠪᠡᠨ</uig> together with his own wife

entry.title: Accidence - Nouns - Reflexive possessive declension
entry.title2: Nouns - Declension - Reflexive possessive declension - Comitative

paragraphs.paragraph: The colloquial comitative ending in <uig rom="-la/-le"> ᠎ᠯᠠ</uig> takes the suffix <uig rom="-γan/-gen">᠎ᠭᠠᠨ/᠎ᠭᠡᠨ</uig> .
<uig rom="baqsi-laγan">ᠪᠠᠬᠰᠢ ᠎ᠯᠠᠭᠠᠨ</uig> together with his own teacher
<uig rom="em-e-legen">ᠡᠮ ᠡ ᠎ᠯᠡᠭᠡᠨ</uig> together with his own wife

entry.title: Accidence - Nouns - Reflexive possessive declension
entry.title2: Nouns - Declension - Reflexive possessive declension - Comitative

paragraphs.paragraph: The other colloquial comitative ending in <uig rom="-tai/-tei"> ᠲᠠᠢ</uig> takes either the suffix <uig rom="-ban/-ben"> ᠪᠠᠨ</uig> or <uig rom="-γan/-gen">᠎ᠭᠠᠨ/ ᠎ᠭᠡᠨ</uig>. In the latter case the combined suffix is <uig rom="-tayiγan /-teyigen">᠎ᠲᠠᠶᠢᠭᠠᠨ / ᠎ᠲᠡᠶᠢᠭᠡᠨ</uig>.
<uig rom="baqsitayiγan">ᠪᠠᠬᠰᠢᠲᠠᠶᠢᠭᠠᠨ</uig> or <uig rom="baqsi-tai-ban">ᠪᠠᠬᠰᠢ ᠎ᠲᠠᠢ ᠎ᠪᠠᠨ</uig> together with his own teacher
<uig rom="emeteyigen">ᠡᠮᠡᠲᠡᠶᠢᠭᠡᠨ</uig> or <uig rom="em-e-tei-ben">ᠡᠮ ᠡ ᠎ᠲᠡᠢ ᠎ᠪᠡᠨ</uig> together with his own wife

The case suffixes in the declension of pronouns are the same as in the declension of nouns, but the stems of the personal and demonstrative pronouns vary in different cases. There is, in Mongolian, the factor of suppletion. The pronouns have two declensions : a simple declension and a declension with the possessive suffix.

The personal pronouns are as follows: <uig rom="bi">ᠪᠢ</uig> "I", <uig rom="ci">ᠴᠢ</uig> "thou", *i "he", <uig rom="ba">ᠪᠠ</uig> "we" (exclusive), <uig rom="bida">ᠪᠢᠳᠠ</uig> "we" (inclusive), <uig rom="ta">ᠲᠠ</uig> "you", and *a "they".

ᠨᠠᠳᠠ ᠎ᠪᠠᠷ|ᠴᠢᠮᠠ ᠎ᠪᠠᠷ|ᠢᠮᠠ ᠎ᠪᠠᠷ|ᠪᠢᠳᠠᠨ ᠢᠶᠠᠷ|ᠮᠠᠨ ᠢᠶᠠᠷ|ᠲᠠᠨ ᠢᠶᠠᠷ|*an-iyar;; Comitative|ᠨᠠᠮᠠ ᠯᠤᠭ ᠠ|ᠴᠢᠮᠠ ᠯᠤᠭ ᠠ|ᠢᠮᠠ ᠯᠤᠭ ᠠ|ᠪᠢᠳᠠᠨ ᠯᠤᠭ ᠠ
or
ᠪᠢᠳᠡᠨ ᠯᠦᠭᠡ|ᠮᠠᠨ ᠯᠤᠭ ᠠ|ᠲᠠᠨ ᠯᠤᠭ ᠠ|*an-luγ-a

Forms marked with an asterisk are reconstructed forms not attested in texts. Except for the genitive, no forms of the third person of the singular are used in the modern or classical language, though they occur in manuscripts of the pre-classical period.
The genitive of the third person singular is <uig rom="inu">ᠢᠨᠤ</uig> . In the non-classical language this is sometimes <uig rom="ni">ᠨᠢ</uig> , when used in post-nominal position.

Besides <uig rom="">ᠪᠢᠳᠠ</uig> bida and <uig rom="">ᠲᠠ</uig> ta there are, in the modern language, the forms <uig rom="">ᠪᠢᠳᠠ ᠎ᠨᠠᠷ</uig> bida-nar "we" (a pleonastic form of the plural) and <uig rom="">ᠲᠠᠨᠠᠷ</uig> tanar "you" (also with the plural suffix <uig rom=""> ᠎ᠨᠠᠷ</uig> -nar). In the modern language <uig rom="ta">ᠲᠠ</uig> "you" is used in addressing one person and <uig rom="tanar">ᠲᠠᠨᠠᠷ</uig> is "you" when addressing many people. The declension of both <uig rom="bida-nar">ᠪᠢᠳᠠ ᠎ᠨᠠᠷ</uig> and <uig rom="tanar">ᠲᠠᠨᠠᠷ</uig> is normal.
The pronouns of the first and second person are given here in Mongolian script.

The demonstrative pronouns are as follows : <uig rom="ene">ᠡᠨᠡ</uig> "this," <uig rom="ede">ᠡᠳᠡ</uig> or <uig rom="edeger">ᠡᠳᠡᠭᠡᠷ</uig> "these," <uig rom="tere">ᠲᠡᠷᠡ</uig> "that," <uig rom="tede">ᠲᠡᠳᠡ</uig> or <uig rom="tedeger">ᠲᠡᠳᠡᠭᠡᠷ</uig> "those," <uig rom="eyimü">ᠡᠶᠢᠮᠦ</uig> "such as this," and <uig rom="teyimü">ᠲᠡᠶᠢᠮᠦ</uig> "such as that."

Case;; Nominative|ᠡᠨᠡ|ᠲᠡᠷᠡ|ᠡᠳᠡ|ᠡᠳᠡᠭᠡᠷ|ᠡᠶᠢᠮᠦ;; Genitive|ᠡᠭᠦᠨ ᠤ|ᠲᠡᠭᠦᠨ ᠤ|ᠡᠳᠡᠨ ᠤ|ᠡᠳᠡᠭᠡᠷ ᠤᠨ|ᠡᠶᠢᠮᠦ ᠶᠢᠨ;; Dative_Locative|ᠡᠭᠦᠨ ᠳ᠋ᠤᠷ

ᠡᠭᠦᠨ ᠡ|ᠲᠡᠭᠦᠨ ᠳ᠋ᠤᠷ

ᠲᠡᠭᠦᠨ ᠡ|ᠡᠳᠡᠨ ᠳ᠋ᠤᠷ

ᠡᠳᠡᠨ ᠡ|ᠡᠳᠡᠭᠡᠷ ᠲᠤᠷ|ᠡᠶᠢᠮᠦ ᠳ᠋ᠤᠷ;; Accusative|ᠡᠭᠦᠨ ᠢ|ᠲᠡᠭᠦᠨ ᠢ|ᠡᠳᠡᠨ ᠢ|ᠡᠳᠡᠭᠡᠷ ᠢ|ᠡᠶᠢᠮᠦ ᠶᠢ;; Ablative|ᠡᠭᠦᠨ ᠡᠴᠡ

ᠡᠭᠦᠨᠴᠡ|ᠲᠡᠭᠦᠨ ᠡᠴᠡ

ᠲᠡᠭᠦᠨᠴᠡ|ᠡᠳᠡᠨ ᠡᠴᠡ|ᠡᠳᠡᠭᠡᠷ ᠡᠴᠡ|ᠡᠶᠢᠮᠦ ᠡᠴᠡ;; Instrumental|ᠡᠭᠦᠨ ᠢᠶᠡᠷ

ᠡᠭᠦᠪᠡᠷ|ᠲᠡᠭᠦᠨ ᠢᠶᠡᠷ

ᠲᠡᠭᠦᠪᠡᠷ|ᠡᠳᠡᠨ ᠢᠶᠡᠷ|ᠡᠳᠡᠭᠡᠷ ᠢᠶᠡᠷ|ᠡᠶᠢᠮᠦ ᠎ᠪᠡᠷ;; Comitative|ᠡᠭᠦᠨ ᠯᠦᠭᠡ|ᠲᠡᠭᠦᠨ ᠯᠦᠭᠡ|ᠡᠳᠡᠨ ᠯᠦᠭᠡ|ᠡᠳᠡᠭᠡᠷ ᠯᠦᠭᠡ|ᠡᠶᠢᠮᠦ ᠯᠦᠭᠡ

The pronouns <uig rom="tede">ᠲᠡᠳᠡ</uig> , <uig rom="tedeger">ᠲᠡᠳᠡᠭᠡᠷ</uig> , and <uig rom="teyimü">ᠲᠡᠶᠢᠮᠦ</uig> are declined in the same manner as <uig rom="ede">ᠡᠳᠡ</uig> , <uig rom="edeger">ᠡᠳᠡᠭᠡᠷ</uig> , and <uig rom="eyimü">ᠡᠶᠢᠮᠦ</uig> . The remaining demonstrative pronouns are declined according to the general rules.
The same demonstrative pronouns are given here in Mongolian script.

The declension of the interrogative pronouns <uig rom="ken">ᠺᠡᠨ</uig> "who," <uig rom="yaγun">ᠶᠠᠭᠤᠨ</uig> "what," and <uig rom="ali">ᠠᠯᠢ</uig> (stem <uig rom="alin">ᠠᠯᠢᠨ</uig>) "which" is carried on according to the general rules.

The indefinite pronouns are derived from the interrogative pronouns with the particles <uig rom="ba">ᠪᠠ</uig> , <uig rom="ber">ᠪᠡᠷ</uig> or <uig rom="cu">ᠴᠤ</uig> . In the declension the case suffixes occupy the place between the pronoun and the particle.
manque tableau

As the particle <uig rom="cu">ᠴᠤ</uig> is the one most used in the modern language, the words with which it is used have been chosen as examples. The remaining particles <uig rom="ba">ᠪᠠ</uig> and <uig rom="ber">ᠪᠡᠷ</uig> occupy the same place as the particle <uig rom="cu">ᠴᠤ</uig> .
The pronouns also occur in this declension. The meaning of such forms is similar to that of the English "to his own," "from his own," and so on.
All pronouns occur in this declension.

entry.title: Accidence - Pronouns - Reflexive possessive declension
entry.title2: Pronouns - Declension - Reflexive-possessive declension - Personal pronouns

paragraphs.paragraph: Only the declension of the pronouns <uig rom="bi">ᠪᠢ</uig> "I", <uig rom="ci">ᠴᠢ</uig> "thou", and <uig rom="ta">ᠲᠠ</uig> "you" will be given here.
manque tableau

entry.title: Accidence - Pronouns - Reflexive possessive declension
entry.title2: Pronouns - Declension - Reflexive-possessive declension - Demonstrative pronouns

paragraphs.paragraph: The reflexive pronouns <uig rom="öber-iyen">ᠥᠪᠡᠷ ᠢᠶᠡᠨ</uig> "himself" and <uig rom="öbesüd-iyen">ᠥᠪᠡᠰᠦᠳ ᠢᠶᠡᠨ</uig> (<uig rom="ögesüdiyen">ᠥᠭᠡᠰᠦᠳᠢᠶᠡᠨ</uig>) "themselves" do not occur in the simple declension. They have only this reflexive-possessive declension, with the exception of the genitive, which is a simple one.

<tbl>Case||;;Nominaitive|<uig rom="öber-iyen">ᠥᠪᠡᠷ ᠢᠶᠡᠨ</uig>|<uig rom="öbesüd-iyen">ᠥᠪᠡᠰᠦᠳ ᠢᠶᠡᠨ</uig>;;Genitive|<uig rom="öber-ün">ᠥᠪᠡᠷ ᠤᠨ</uig>|<uig rom="öbesüd-ün">ᠥᠪᠡᠰᠦᠳ ᠤᠨ</uig>;;Dative-Locative|<uig rom="öber-tegen">ᠥᠪᠡᠷ ᠎ᠲᠡᠭᠡᠨ</uig>|<uig rom="öbesüd-tegen">ᠥᠪᠡᠰᠦᠳ ᠎ᠲᠡᠭᠡᠨ</uig>;;Accusative|<uig rom="öber-iyen">ᠥᠪᠡᠷ ᠢᠶᠡᠨ</uig>|<uig rom="öbesüd-iyen">ᠥᠪᠡᠰᠦᠳ ᠢᠶᠡᠨ</uig>;;Ablative|<uig rom="öber-ecegen">ᠥᠪᠡᠷ ᠡᠴᠡᠭᠡᠨ</uig>|<uig rom="öbesüd-ecegen">ᠥᠪᠡᠰᠦᠳ ᠡᠴᠡᠭᠡᠨ</uig>;;Instrumental|<uig rom="öber-iyer-iyen">ᠥᠪᠡᠷ ᠢᠶᠡᠷ ᠢᠶᠡᠨ</uig>|<uig rom="öbesüd-iyer-iyen">ᠥᠪᠡᠰᠦᠳ ᠢᠶᠡᠷ ᠢᠶᠡᠨ</uig>;;Commitative|<uig rom="öber-lüge-ben">ᠥᠪᠡᠷ ᠯᠦᠭᠡ ᠎ᠪᠡᠨ</uig>|<uig rom="öbesüd-lüge-ben">ᠥᠪᠡᠰᠦᠳ ᠯᠦᠭᠡ ᠎ᠪᠡᠨ</uig></tbl>
The verbal forms are classified as
(a) those serving as the predicate of a completed sentence (finite verbs),
(b) those serving as subject, object, attribute or predicate of a sentence, and
(c) those serving as attribute to verbs or logical (not grammatical) predicates of incomplete sentences.
To the first group belong the imperative and optative forms and all indicative forms. To the second group belong the verbal nouns. To the third group belong the converba.
The imperative and optative forms express orders and wishes. These are as follows: the imperative, prescriptive, voluntative, optative, and dubitative.
The verbal nouns are more or less the same as the participles of the Indo-European languages.
The converbs do not serve as predicates of completed sentences.

entry.title: Accidence - Verbs - Imperative and optative forms

paragraphs.paragraph: The imperative of the second peraon expresses a atrict order addressed to one person (thou) or to several persons (you). This form has suffix and coincides with the stem of the verb.
<uig rom="yabu">ᠶᠠᠪᠤ</uig> go!
<uig rom="ungsi">ᠤᠩᠰᠢ</uig> read!
<uig rom="kele">ᠺᠡᠯᠡ</uig> say !
<uig rom="ire">ᠢᠷᠡ</uig> come !

entry.title: Accidence - Verbs - Imperative and optative forms

paragraphs.paragraph: The imperative of the second person of the plural, or the so-called person or to benedictive, expresses a polite entreaty addressed to one several persons.
The suffix is <uig rom="-qtun/-gtün">ᠬᠲᠤᠨ/᠎ᠭᠲᠦᠨ</uig> , a plural in <uig rom="-n"> ᠎ᠨ</uig> of <uig rom="-qtui/-gtüi">ᠬᠲᠤᠢ/ᠭᠲᠦᠢ</uig> (see § 335). Verbs ending in consonants take a union vowel.
<uig rom="yabuqtun">ᠶᠠᠪᠤᠬᠲᠤᠨ</uig> Please go!
<uig rom="kelegtün">ᠺᠡᠯᠡᠭᠲᠦᠨ</uig> Please say!
<uig rom="yabuγuluqtun">ᠶᠠᠪᠤᠭᠤᠯᠤᠬᠲᠤᠨ</uig> (<uig rom="yabuγul-">ᠶᠠᠪᠤᠭᠤᠯ</uig> ) Please send!
<uig rom="öggügtün">ᠥᠭᠭᠦᠭᠲᠦᠨ</uig> (<uig rom="ög-">ᠥᠭ</uig> ) Please give!

entry.title: Accidence - Verbs - Imperative and optative forms

paragraphs.paragraph: In the pre-classical language the suffix is usually <uig rom="-dqun/-dkün">ᠳᠬᠤᠨ/ᠳᠺᠦᠨ</uig> , which is added to stems ending in consonants with the union vowel -u-/-ü-.
<uig rom="yabudqun">ᠶᠠᠪᠤᠳᠬᠤᠨ</uig> Please go!
<uig rom="keledkün">ᠺᠡᠯᠡᠳᠺᠦᠨ</uig> Please say !

entry.title: Accidence - Verbs - Imperative and optative forms

paragraphs.paragraph: The suffix <uig rom="-qtui/-gtüi">ᠬᠲᠤᠢ/ᠭᠲᠦᠢ</uig> occurs mainly in Buriat manuscripts. Originally this was an imperative of the singular (the plural was <uig rom="-qtun/-gtün">ᠬᠲᠤᠨ/ᠭᠲᠦᠨ</uig> , see § 333) but in the modern language it is used instead of the form in <uig rom="-qtun/-gtün">ᠬᠲᠤᠨ/ᠭᠲᠦᠨ</uig> .
<uig rom="yabuqtui">ᠶᠠᠪᠤᠬᠲᠤᠢ</uig> Please go !
<uig rom="kelegtüi">ᠺᠡᠯᠡᠭᠲᠦᠢ</uig> Please say!

entry.title: Accidence - Verbs - Imperative and optative forms

paragraphs.paragraph: The prescriptive occurs only in the language influenced by the dialects. This form expresses a commission or a wiah addressed to a second person. The action which the person concerned is ordered to perform may be done later on, if not immediately.
The suffix is <uig rom="-γarai/-gerei">ᠭᠠᠷᠠᠢ/ᠭᠡᠷᠡᠢ</uig> , after a final consonant <uig rom="-uγarai/-ügerei">ᠤᠭᠠᠷᠠᠢ/ᠤᠭᠡᠷᠡᠢ</uig> .
<uig rom="yabuγarai">ᠶᠠᠪᠤᠭᠠᠷᠠᠢ</uig> go!
<uig rom="kelegerei">ᠺᠡᠯᠡᠭᠡᠷᠡᠢ</uig> say!
<uig rom="yabuγuluγarai">ᠶᠠᠪᠤᠭᠤᠯᠤᠭᠠᠷᠠᠢ</uig> (<uig rom="yabuγul-">ᠶᠠᠪᠤᠭᠤᠯ ᠎</uig>) send!

entry.title: Accidence - Verbs - Imperative and optative forms
entry.title2: Verbs - Conjugation - Imperative of the third person

paragraphs.paragraph: This form expresses an order to be executed by a third person ("let him do!," "he must do!").
The suffix is <uig rom="-tuγai/-tügei">ᠲᠤᠭᠠᠢ/᠎ᠲᠦᠭᠡᠢ</uig> .
<uig rom="yabutuγai">ᠶᠠᠪᠤᠲᠤᠭᠠᠢ</uig> He must go !
<uig rom="keletügei">ᠺᠡᠯᠡᠲᠦᠭᠡᠢ</uig> Let him say ! He must say !
<uig rom="yabuγultuγai">ᠶᠠᠪᠤᠭᠤᠯᠲᠤᠭᠠᠢ</uig> Let him send! He must send!

entry.title: Accidence - Verbs - Imperative and optative forms

paragraphs.paragraph: The voluntative expresses a wish to perform an action ("let me do!," "let us do!").
The voluntative suffix of the singular is <uig rom="-suγai/-sügei">ᠰᠤᠭᠠᠢ/ᠰᠦᠭᠡᠢ</uig> , in the pre-classical language <uig rom="-su/-sü">ᠰᠤ</uig> .
<uig rom="yabusuγai">ᠶᠠᠪᠤᠰᠤᠭᠠᠢ</uig> Let me go !
<uig rom="kelesügei">ᠺᠡᠯᠡᠰᠦᠭᠡᠢ</uig> Let me say !
<uig rom="yabuγulsuγai">ᠶᠠᠪᠤᠭᠤᠯᠰᠤᠭᠠᠢ</uig> Let me send!

entry.title: Accidence - Verbs - Imperative and optative forms

paragraphs.paragraph: In modern books the suffixes <uig rom="-suγai/-sügei">ᠰᠤᠭᠠᠢ/ᠰᠦᠭᠡᠢ</uig> and <uig rom="-tuγai/-tügei">ᠲᠤᠭᠠᠢ/ᠲᠦᠭᠡᠢ</uig> (see § 337) are sometimes confused and used indiscriminately in reference to both the first and third person.

entry.title: Accidence - Verbs - Imperative and optative forms

paragraphs.paragraph: The voluntative of the first person of the plural is formed with the suffix <uig rom="-y-a/-y-e">᠎ᠶ᠎ᠡ</uig> , which is added to stems ending in consonants with the union vowel -u-/-ü-.
In modern books and newspapers this form is often used in reference to both the singular and plural.
<uig rom="yabuy-a">ᠶᠠᠪᠤᠶ᠎ᠠ</uig> Let us go!
<uig rom="keley-e">ᠺᠡᠯᠡᠶ᠎ᠡ</uig> Let us say!
<uig rom="yabuγuluy-a">ᠶᠠᠪᠤᠭᠤᠯᠤᠶ᠎ᠠ</uig> (<uig rom="yabuγul-">ᠶᠠᠪᠤᠭᠤᠯ ᠎</uig>) Let us send!

entry.title: Accidence - Verbs - Imperative and optative forms

paragraphs.paragraph: The optative occurs only in popular books. It expresses a wish, usually impossible of attainment, and refers to all persons ("Ah, if he did !").
The auffix is <uig rom="-γasai/-gesei">ᠭᠠᠰᠠᠢ/ᠭᠡᠰᠡᠢ</uig> , which is added to stems ending in consonants, with the union vowel -u-/-ü-.
<uig rom="yabuγasai">ᠶᠠᠪᠤᠭᠠᠰᠠᠢ</uig> Ah, if he went !
<uig rom="kelegesei">ᠺᠡᠯᠡᠭᠡᠰᠡᠢ</uig> Ah, if he said !
<uig rom="yabuγuluγasai">ᠶᠠᠪᠤᠭᠤᠯᠤᠭᠠᠰᠠᠢ</uig> Ah, if he sent !

entry.title: Accidence - Verbs - Imperative and optative forms

paragraphs.paragraph: The dubitative expresses the fear that someone might perform an action, which is conaidered undesirable ("But what if he, nevertheleas, does?").
The suffix is <uig rom="-γujai/-güjei">ᠭᠤᠵᠠᠢ/ᠭᠦᠵᠡᠢ</uig> with this union vowel -u-/-ü- on stems ending in consonants.
<uig rom="yabuγujai">ᠶᠠᠪᠤᠭᠤᠵᠠᠢ</uig> What if he comes?
<uig rom="kelegüjei">ᠺᠡᠯᠡᠭᠦᠵᠡᠢ</uig> What if he says?
<uig rom="yabuγuluγujai">ᠶᠠᠪᠤᠭᠤᠯᠤᠭᠤᠵᠠᠢ</uig> What if he sends?

The indicative forms express present, future, or past actions. They are equivalent to the present, future, or past tenses of the English verb. Each form may refer to any of the persons, singular or plural.

There are the following indicative forms:
(a) three different forms of the present tense and
(b) three forms of the past tense.

There are two narrative present forms and a deductive form. The narrative present forms express actions which take place either at the time of speaking (present tense) or will take place in the future. In other words this is a praesens and futurum.

The first narrative present takes the suffix <uig rom="-mui/-müi">ᠮᠤᠢ</uig> , with the union vowel -u-/-ü-, which is added to stems ending in consonants. This form also occurs with the interrogative particle <uig rom="uu/üü">ᠤᠤ</uig> , in which case the suffix and the particle fuse into <uig rom="-muu/-müü">᠎ᠮᠤᠤ</uig> .
<uig rom="yabumui">ᠶᠠᠪᠤᠮᠤᠢ</uig> He goes, or He will go.
<uig rom="kelemüi">ᠺᠡᠯᠡᠮᠦᠢ</uig> He says, or He will say.
<uig rom="yabuγulumui">ᠶᠠᠪᠤᠭᠤᠯᠤᠮᠤᠢ</uig> (<uig rom="yabuγul-">ᠶᠠᠪᠤᠭᠤᠯ ᠎</uig>) He sends, or He will send.
<uig rom="yabumui-uu">ᠶᠠᠪᠤᠮᠤᠢ ᠤᠤ</uig> or <uig rom="yabumuu">ᠶᠠᠪᠤᠮᠤᠤ</uig> Does he go? or Will he go?
In the pre-classical period the ending was <uig rom="-m"> ᠎ᠮ</uig> or <uig rom="-mu/-mü">᠎ᠮᠤ</uig>.
<uig rom="yabum">ᠶᠠᠪᠤᠮ</uig> He goes, or He will go.
<uig rom="yabumu">ᠶᠠᠪᠤᠮᠤ</uig> He goes, or He will go.
Another suffix of the narrative present, less usual in the classical language, is <uig rom="-nam/-nem">᠎ᠨᠠᠮ</uig> with the union vowel -u-/-ü-.
The function of this form is that of the present tense.
<uig rom="yabunam">ᠶᠠᠪᠤᠨᠠᠮ</uig> He goes.
<uig rom="kelenem">ᠺᠡᠯᠡᠨᠡᠮ</uig> He says.
See also §585
In popular books, instead of the suffix <uig rom="-nam/-nem">ᠨᠠᠮ</uig> , the suffix <uig rom="-nai/-nei">᠎ᠨᠠᠢ</uig> is used.
With the interrogative particle this is <uig rom="-nuu/-nüü">᠎ᠨᠤᠤ</uig> .
<uig rom="yabunai">ᠶᠠᠪᠤᠨᠠᠢ</uig> He goes, or He will go.
<uig rom="kelenei">ᠺᠡᠯᠡᠨᠡᠢ</uig> He says, or He will say.
<uig rom="yabunuu">ᠶᠠᠪᠤᠨᠤᠤ</uig> Does he go?, or Will he go?
The deductive present expresses actions considered a logical result of previous actions or antitheses to the latter ("Consequently he does," or "Consequently he will do," "Hence he does").
The suffix is <uig rom="-yu/-yü">᠎ᠶᠤ</uig> ; with the union vowel -u-/-ü-, it is added to stems ending in consonants.
<uig rom="yabuyu">ᠶᠠᠪᠤᠶᠤ</uig> Consequently he goes, or Consequently he will go. In accordance with the previous actions he goes
<uig rom="medeyü">ᠮᠡᠳᠡᠶᠦ</uig> Hence he knows.
<uig rom="yabuγuluyu">ᠶᠠᠪᠤᠭᠤᠯᠤᠶᠤ</uig> (<uig rom="yabuγul-">ᠶᠠᠪᠤᠭᠤᠯ</uig> ) Hence he sends.
See also §587
There are three forms of the past. Of these the primary form of the past tense is a perfect referring to the recent past.
The suffix is <uig rom="-ba/-be">᠎ᠪᠠ</uig> or <uig rom="-bai/-bei">᠎ᠪᠠᠢ</uig> . Only verbs ending in b or r take a union vowel -u-/-ü-.
With the interrogative particle uu the suffix is <uig rom="-ba-uu/-be-üü">᠎ᠪᠠ ᠤᠤ</uig> or <uig rom=" -buu/-büü">᠎ᠪᠤᠤ</uig>.
<uig rom="yabuba">ᠶᠠᠪᠤᠪᠠ</uig> or <uig rom="yabubai">ᠶᠠᠪᠤᠪᠠᠢ</uig> He has gone.
<uig rom="irebe">ᠢᠷᠡᠪᠡ</uig> or <uig rom="irebei">ᠢᠷᠡᠪᠡᠢ</uig> He has come.
<uig rom="ögbe">ᠥᠭᠪᠡ</uig> or <uig rom="ögbei">ᠥᠭᠪᠡᠢ</uig> He has given.
<uig rom="asaqba">ᠠᠰᠠᠬᠪᠠ</uig> or <uig rom="asaqbai">ᠠᠰᠠᠬᠪᠠᠢ</uig> He has asked.
<uig rom="bosba">ᠪᠣᠰᠪᠠ</uig> or <uig rom="bosbai">ᠪᠣᠰᠪᠠᠢ</uig> He has risen.
<uig rom="odba">ᠣᠳᠪᠠ</uig> or <uig rom="odbai">ᠣᠳᠪᠠᠢ</uig> He has gone, He has departed.
<uig rom="abuba">ᠠᠪᠤᠪᠠ</uig> or <uig rom="abubai">ᠠᠪᠤᠪᠠᠢ</uig> (<uig rom="ab-">ᠠᠪ</uig> ) He has taken.
<uig rom="γaruba">ᠭᠠᠷᠤᠪᠠ</uig> or <uig rom="γarubai">ᠭᠠᠷᠤᠪᠠᠢ</uig> (<uig rom="γar-">ᠭᠠᠷ</uig> ) He has gone out.
<uig rom="yabuba-uu">ᠶᠠᠪᠤᠪᠠ ᠤᠤ</uig> or <uig rom="yabubuu">ᠶᠠᠪᠤᠪᠤᠤ</uig> Has he gone?

Another past form expresses actions which, without any doubt, have taken (or will take) place. The action is supposed to have been witnessed by the person speaking; at any rate, the latter owes his knowledge of the action to a reliable source.
The suffix is <uig rom="-luγa/-lüge">ᠯᠤᠭᠠ/ᠯᠦᠭᠡ</uig> in the classical language, with the union vowel -u-/-ü-, added to stems ending in consonants.
In the pre-classical language the suffix is <uig rom="-luγai/-lügei">ᠯᠤᠭᠠᠢ/᠎ᠯᠦᠭᠡᠢ</uig> or sometimes <uig rom="-laγa/-lege">ᠯᠠᠭᠠ/ᠯᠡᠭᠡ</uig> .

In modern popular books the suffix is often <uig rom="-la/-le">ᠯᠠ</uig> or <uig rom="-lai/-lei">ᠯᠠᠢ</uig> . With the interrogative particle it is <uig rom="-la-uu/-le-üü">ᠯᠠ ᠤᠤ</uig> or <uig rom="-luu/-lüü">᠎ᠯᠤᠤ</uig> .
<uig rom="yabuluγa">ᠶᠠᠪᠤᠯᠤᠭᠠ</uig> He has gone.
<uig rom="ükülügei">ᠦᠺᠦᠯᠦᠭᠡᠢ</uig> He has died.
<uig rom="medelüü">ᠮᠡᠳᠡᠯᠦᠦ</uig> Did he know?

The third past tense form expresses actions which took place before other actions. In certain cases this is a pluperfect. The speaker claims to have witnessed the action and to have been surprised when making the discovery of the action as a fait accompli. This past tense is usually used with reference to the second and third persons.
The suffix is <uig rom="-juqui/-jüküi">ᠵᠤᠬᠤᠢ/ᠵᠦᠺᠦᠢ</uig> ; when added to stems ending in γ, b, e, d, g, and r it is <uig rom="-cuqui/-cüküi">ᠴᠤᠬᠤᠢ/ᠴᠦᠺᠦᠢ</uig> .
<uig rom="yabujuqui">ᠶᠠᠪᠤᠵᠤᠬᠤᠢ</uig> He was found to have gone.
<uig rom="üküjüküi">ᠦᠺᠦᠵᠦᠺᠦᠢ</uig> It was unexpectedly discovered that he had died.
<uig rom="γarcuqui">ᠭᠠᠷᠴᠤᠬᠤᠢ</uig> He was found to have gone out.
In the pre-classical language the suffix is either ᠵᠤᠭᠤ/ᠵᠦᠭᠦ or ᠵᠤᠭᠤᠢ/ᠵᠦᠭᠦᠢ (ᠴᠤᠭᠤ/ᠴᠦᠭᠦ or ᠴᠤᠭᠤᠢ/ᠴᠦᠭᠦᠢ ). In the modern and classical language only the verb ᠠ ᠎ "to be" occurs with the suffix ᠵᠤᠭᠤ .
Another ancient ending is <uig rom="-jiγai/-jigei">ᠵᠢᠭᠠᠢ/ᠵᠢᠭᠡᠢ</uig> .
<uig rom="yabujuγu">ᠶᠠᠪᠤᠵᠤᠭᠤ</uig> or <uig rom="yabujuγui">ᠶᠠᠪᠤᠵᠤᠭᠤᠢ</uig> He was found to have gone.
<uig rom="ajuγu">ᠠᠵᠤᠭᠤ</uig> He had been.
<uig rom="yabujiγai">ᠶᠠᠪᠤᠵᠢᠭᠠᠢ</uig> He was found to have gone.
In modern popular books the suffix is often <uig rom="-ji/ci">ᠵᠢ/ᠴᠢ</uig> .
<uig rom="yabuji">ᠶᠠᠪᠤᠵᠢ</uig> He was found to have gone.
<uig rom="γarci">ᠭᠠᠷᠴᠢ</uig> He was found to have gone out.

The verbal nouns are declinable and possess all characteristics of nouns. On the other hand, they are verbal forms and can serve as predicates. Verbal nouns, although to some extent comparable, differ from the participles of the European languages in that the area of their syntactical use is larger.

entry.title: Accidence - Verbs - Verbal nouns
entry.title2: Verbs - Conjugation - Verbal nouns - Nomen Actoris

paragraphs.paragraph: The nomen actoris designates the person acting and sometimes the process of an action. It ia used as subject, object, attribute, and, with a copula, as predicate.

The suffix is <uig rom="-qci/-gci">ᠬᠴᠢ</uig> , with a union vowel, added to stems ending in consonants. The plural form is either <uig rom="-qcin/-gcin">ᠬᠴᠢᠨ</uig> or <uig rom="-qcid/-gcid">ᠬᠴᠢᠳ</uig> .
<uig rom="yabuqci">ᠶᠠᠪᠤᠬᠴᠢ</uig> going, goer, one who goes, process of going
<uig rom="kelegci">ᠺᠡᠯᠡᠭᠴᠢ</uig> saying, one who says, process of saying
<uig rom="kelegcid">ᠺᠡᠯᠡᠭᠴᠢᠳ</uig> or kelegcin those who say

entry.title: Accidence - Verbs - Verbal nouns
entry.title2: Verbs - Conjugation - Verbal nouns - Nomen Praesentis

paragraphs.paragraph: The nomen praesentis is a sort of present participle. In the classical and modern language it occurs very seldom and only a few verbs occur in this form. This is used as attribute, object, and predicate.
The suffix is <uig rom="-i">ᠢ</uig> after a final vowel of the stem, e. g., <uig rom="kemegdei">ᠺᠡᠮᠡᠭᠳᠡᠢ</uig> "is said," but with a connective vowel -u-/-ü- after a final consonant:
<uig rom="ayisui">ᠠᠶᠢᠰᠤᠢ</uig> (<uig rom="ayis-">ᠠᠶᠢᠰ</uig> ) approaching
<uig rom="odui">ᠣᠳᠤᠢ</uig> (<uig rom="od-">ᠣᠳ</uig> ) going, departing
<uig rom="bolui">ᠪᠣᠯᠤᠢ</uig> (<uig rom="bol-">ᠪᠣᠯ</uig> ) becoming
<uig rom="γarui">ᠭᠠᠷᠤᠢ</uig> (<uig rom="γar-">ᠭᠠᠷ</uig> ) exceeding

entry.title: Accidence - Verbs - Verbal nouns
entry.title2: Verbs - Conjugation - Verbal nouns - Nomen Usus

paragraphs.paragraph: The nomen usus expresses a customary, habitual, or usual action, e. g., "someone who usually comes," "the usual visitor." This form is used as subject, object, attribute, and, with a copula, as predicate.
The suffix is <uig rom="-daq/-deg">᠎ᠳᠠᠬ/ᠳᠡᠭ</uig> , with the union vowel -u-/-ü- when the stem ends in a consonant.
<uig rom="yabudaq">ᠶᠠᠪᠤᠳᠠᠬ</uig> someone who usually goes, the usual goer, the usual act of going, he usually goes
<uig rom="keledeg">ᠺᠡᠯᠡᠳᠡᠭ</uig> someone who usually says, the act of usually saying, he usually says

entry.title: Accidence - Verbs - Verbal nouns
entry.title2: Verbs - Conjugation - Verbal nouns - Nomen Futuri

paragraphs.paragraph: The nomen futuri expresses an action which will take place in the future or an action of any time other than future. This form is used as subject, object, attribute, and predicate (with a copula). It is frequently referred to as the infinitive of the verb, a profound error.
The suffix is <uig rom="-qu/-kü">ᠬᠤ/ᠺᠦ</uig> without the union vowel.
<uig rom="yabuqu">ᠶᠠᠪᠤᠬᠤ</uig> one who will go, going in the future, he will go
<uig rom="kelekü">ᠺᠡᠯᠡᠺᠦ</uig> one who will say, saying in the future, he will say
See also §558

entry.title: Accidence - Verbs - Verbal nouns
entry.title2: Verbs - Conjugation - Verbal nouns - Nomen Futuri

paragraphs.paragraph: Another suffix is <uig rom="-qui/-küi">ᠬᠤᠢ/ᠺᠦᠢ</uig> . In the pre-classical language <uig rom="-qu"> ᠎ᠬᠤ</uig> and <uig rom="-qui"> ᠎ᠬᠤᠢ</uig> were used indiscriminately, but in the modern and classical language forms in <uig rom="-qui"> ᠎ᠬᠤᠢ</uig> are used only as substantive nouns, i. e., they serve as subject and object but not as attribute or predicate.
<uig rom="yabuqui">ᠶᠠᠪᠤᠬᠤᠢ</uig> the process of going
<uig rom="keleküi">ᠺᠡᠯᠡᠺᠦᠢ</uig> the process of saying

entry.title: Accidence - Verbs - Verbal nouns
entry.title2: Verbs - Conjugation - Verbal nouns - Nomen Futuri

paragraphs.paragraph: The plural of the form in <uig rom="-qui/-küi">ᠬᠤᠢ/ᠺᠦᠢ</uig> is <uig rom="-qun/-kün">ᠬᠤᠨ/ᠺᠦᠨ</uig> in the pre-classical language.
<uig rom="yabuqun">ᠶᠠᠪᠤᠬᠤᠨ</uig> those who will go
<uig rom="kelekün">ᠺᠡᠯᠡᠺᠦᠨ</uig> those who will say

entry.title: Accidence - Verbs - Verbal nouns
entry.title2: Verbs - Conjugation - Verbal nouns - Nomen Imperfecti

paragraphs.paragraph: The nomen imperfecti with the suffix <uig rom="-γa/-ge">ᠭᠠ/ᠭᠡ</uig> expresses an unfinished action which started in the past and continues into the present, e. g., "someone who has sat down and is still sitting." This form is used as any part of sentence, although mainly as attribute and predicate.
<uig rom="yabuγa">ᠶᠠᠪᠤᠭᠠ</uig> someone who started going and is still going
<uig rom="kelege">ᠺᠡᠯᠡᠭᠡ ᠦᠭᠡᠢ</uig> ügei someone who has not yet said

entry.title: Accidence - Verbs - Verbal nouns
entry.title2: Verbs - Conjugation - Verbal nouns - Nomen Imperfecti

paragraphs.paragraph: In the pre-classical language the suffix is sometimes <uig rom="-γai/-gei">ᠭᠠᠢ/ᠭᠡᠢ</uig> .
<uig rom="yabuγai">ᠶᠠᠪᠤᠭᠠᠢ</uig> someone who has gone and is still going

entry.title: Accidence - Verbs - Verbal nouns
entry.title2: Verbs - Conjugation - Verbal nouns - Nomen Perfecti

paragraphs.paragraph: The nomen perfecti expresses a completed past action, e. g., "someone who has died" or "is dead." This form is used as subject, object, attribute, and predicate.
The suffix is <uig rom="-γsan/-gsen">ᠬᠰᠠᠨ/ᠭᠰᠡᠨ</uig> with the union vowel -u-/-ü- when the stem ends in a consonant.
<uig rom="yabuγsan">ᠶᠠᠪᠤᠬᠰᠠᠨ</uig> one who has gone (and is no longer here)
<uig rom="kelegsen">ᠺᠡᠯᠡᠭᠰᠡᠨ</uig> one who has said (and is no longer speaking)
See also §565

The converbs do not serve as predicates of complete sentences, but only as attributes of verbs, indicating the manner in which the action is being performed, or as logical (not grammatical) predicates of word groups rendered in European languages as subordinate clauses.

The converbs are classified into two groups: the genuine and the pseudo-converbs. The former are fossilized oblique case forms of verbal nouns; the latter are, from the historical viewpoint, purely verbal forms.

The genuine and pseudo-converbs manifest a syntactical difference: while the actor is always designated by the nominative case in constructions with pseudo-converbs he can, under certain circumstances, be designated by the genitive (or accusative) in constructions with genuine converbs.

The genuine converbs are the following : converbum terminale, converbum abtemporale, converbum contemporale, converbum successivum, converbum finale, and converbum praeparativum. The pseudo-converbs are: converbum conditionale, converbum concessivum, converbum imperfecti, converbum modale, and converbum perfecti.
The converbum conditionale expresses an action indicating the condition under which the main action is performed.
If the main action is a praesens or futurum the conditional converb expresses a condition, e. g., "if he does."
If the main action is a praeteritum (past tense form) the conditional converb indicates the time at which the main action takes place : "when he did."
The suffix is <uig rom="-basu/-besü">ᠪᠠᠰᠤ</uig> with the union vowel -u-/-ü- if the stem ends in b or r.
<uig rom="yabubasu">ᠶᠠᠪᠤᠪᠠᠰᠤ</uig> if he goes, when he went
<uig rom="γarubasu">ᠭᠠᠷᠤᠪᠠᠰᠤ</uig> (<uig rom="γar-">ᠭᠠᠷ</uig> ) if he goes out, when he went out
<uig rom="abubasu">ᠠᠪᠤᠪᠠᠰᠤ</uig> (<uig rom="ab-">ᠠᠪ</uig> ) if he takes, when he took
<uig rom="bosbasu">ᠪᠣᠰᠪᠠᠰᠤ</uig> if he rises, when he rose
<uig rom="ögbesü">ᠥᠭᠪᠡᠰᠦ</uig> if he gives, when he gave

In writings of the pre-classical and, sometimes, of the classical period this converb occurs with the particle <uig rom="ber">ᠪᠡᠷ</uig> . The latter does not change the meaning. But in the modern language this converb with the particle <uig rom="ber">ᠪᠡᠷ</uig> and a negative is a concessive converb (see § 370) : "although he does not," "although he did not."
<uig rom="yabubasu ber">ᠶᠠᠪᠤᠪᠠᠰᠤ ᠪᠡᠷ</uig> "if he goes" or "when he went" (in pre-classical language), "although he goes" or "although he went, nevertheless . . ." (in classical and modern language).
In the language of popular writings the suffix is <uig rom="-bala/-bele">ᠪᠠᠯᠠ</uig> , with the union vowel -u-/-ü- when the stem ends in b or r.
<uig rom="yabubala">ᠶᠠᠪᠤᠪᠠᠯᠠ</uig> if he goes (or) when he went
<uig rom="ᠠᠪᠤᠪᠠᠯᠠ"></uig> abubala (<uig rom="ab-">ᠠᠪ</uig> ) if he takes (or) when he took
<uig rom="ögbele">ᠥᠭᠪᠡᠯᠡ</uig> if he gives (or) when he gave

In the language of popular writings the suffix is sometimes <uig rom="-γasu/ -gesü">ᠭᠠᠰᠤ/ᠭᠡᠰᠦ</uig> with the union vowel -u-/-ü- when the stem ends in a consonant. In the classical language only the verb bü- "to be" takes this suffix.
<uig rom="yabuγasu">ᠶᠠᠪᠤᠭᠠᠰᠤ</uig> if he goes (or) when he went
<uig rom="bügesü">ᠪᠦᠭᠡᠰᠦ</uig> if he is (or) when he was
The concessive converb expresses an action, which, although performed, does not yield the expected result, e. g., "although he promised to come, he has not."
The suffix is <uig rom="-bacu/-becü">ᠪᠠᠴᠤ</uig> , with the union vowel -u-/-ü- when the stem ends in b or r.
<uig rom="yabubacu">ᠶᠠᠪᠤᠪᠠᠴᠤ</uig> although he goes
<uig rom="kelebecü">ᠺᠡᠯᠡᠪᠡᠴᠦ</uig> although he says

In the language of popular books the suffix is often <uig rom="-baci/-beci">ᠪᠠᠴᠢ</uig> . As to the suffix <uig rom="-bacu/-becü">ᠪᠠᠴᠤ</uig> , the particle <uig rom="cu">ᠴᠤ</uig> may precede the converb.
<uig rom="yabubaci">ᠶᠠᠪᠤᠪᠠᠴᠢ</uig> although he goes
<uig rom="tere cu kelebe">ᠲᠡᠷᠡ ᠴᠤ ᠺᠡᠯᠡᠪᠡ</uig> although he says
The converbum imperfecti expresses an action performed simultaneously with the main action.
The suffix is -ju/-jü when the stem ends in a vowel, diphthong, or the consonant l; -cu/-cü when it ends in γ, b, s, d, g, and r.
In non-classical language the suffix is sometimes <uig rom="-ji/-ci.">ᠵᠢ/ᠴᠢ</uig>
<uig rom="abcu">ᠠᠪᠴᠤ</uig> taking
<uig rom="olju">ᠣᠯᠵᠤ</uig> finding
<uig rom="boscu">ᠪᠣᠰᠴᠤ</uig> rising
<uig rom="ögcü">ᠥᠭᠴᠦ</uig> giving
<uig rom="kelejü">ᠺᠡᠯᠡᠵᠦ</uig> saying
<uig rom="yabuju">ᠶᠠᠪᠤᠵᠤ</uig> going
<uig rom="bosci">ᠪᠣᠰᠴᠢ</uig> (under colloquial influence) rising
<uig rom="yabuji">ᠶᠠᠪᠤᠵᠢ</uig> (under colloquial influence) going
See also §578

The modal converb expresses an action indicating the manner in which the main action is performed. The action of the converb and that of the main verb are closely related or fuse into one, e. g., "to arrive riding horseback."
The suffix is <uig rom="-n">᠎ᠨ</uig> with the union vowel -u-/-ü if the stem ends in a consonant.
<uig rom="nisün">ᠨᠢᠰᠦᠨ</uig> (<uig rom="nis-">ᠨᠢᠰ</uig>) flying in <uig rom="nisün irebe">ᠨᠢᠰᠦᠨ ᠢᠷᠡᠪᠡ</uig> He came flying.
<uig rom="güin">ᠭᠦᠢᠨ</uig> running in <uig rom="güin γaruba">ᠭᠦᠢᠨ ᠭᠠᠷᠤᠪᠠ</uig> He came out running, or He ran out.

The converbum modale is by origin a verbal noun. Its plural (with the suffix <uig rom="-d"> ᠎ᠳ</uig> replacing the final n of this converbal form) acted in Preclassical Mongolian as a form of the present tense (vide § 413).
See also §579
The converbum perfecti expresses an action completed before the main action starts, e.g., " he did and ...", "after doing ..."
the suffix <uig rom="-γag/-ged">᠎ᠭᠠᠭ/ ᠎ᠭᠡᠳ</uig> with a union vowel on stems ending in consonants
<uig rom="yabuγad">ᠶᠠᠪᠤᠭᠠᠳ</uig> after having gone
<uig rom="keleged">ᠺᠡᠯᠡᠭᠡᠳ</uig> he said and ..., after saying ...
See also §580

This converb expresses an action which marks the time limit of the main action. In certain combinations this form can also express an action which is being performed simultaneously with the main action. Thus it means "until he does" or "while he is doing."
The suffix is <uig rom="-tala/-tele.">᠎ᠲᠠᠯᠠ</uig>
<uig rom="yabutala">ᠶᠠᠪᠤᠲᠠᠯᠠ</uig> until he goes
<uig rom="keletele">ᠺᠡᠯᠡᠲᠡᠯᠡ</uig> while he was talking
See also §414

This converb expresses an action of which the inception marks the point of time at which the main action takes place, e. g., "since he died. . ." The action of this converb can be of long duration and in this case such a form means: "since the beginning and during the action," e. g., "while he was sitting."
The suffix is <uig rom="-qsaγar/-gseger">᠎ᠬᠰᠠᠭᠠᠷ/ᠭᠰᠡᠭᠡᠷ</uig> with the union vowel -u-/-ü-.
<uig rom="yabugsaγar">ᠶᠠᠪᠤᠭᠰᠠᠭᠠᠷ</uig> while he was going
<uig rom="törögseger">ᠲᠥᠷᠥᠭᠰᠡᠭᠡᠷ</uig> (<uig rom="törö-">ᠲᠥᠷᠥ</uig>) since he was born

This converb expresses an action of which the inception is immediately followed by the main action, or simultaneously contemporal with that of the main action, e. g., "scarcely had he done something, when. . ." The suffix is <uig rom="-maqca/-megce">ᠮᠠᠬᠴᠠ/ᠮᠡᠭᠴᠡ</uig> in the classical language, and <uig rom="-maci/-meci">ᠮᠠᠴᠢ/ᠮᠡᠴᠢ</uig> in the language influenced by colloquial dialects, with the union vowel-u-/-ü- when the stem ends in a consonant.
<uig rom="γarumaqca">ᠭᠠᠷᠤᠮᠠᠬᠴᠠ</uig> (<uig rom="γar-">ᠭᠠᠷ</uig>) he had scarcely gone out, when ...
<uig rom="iremegce">ᠢᠷᠡᠮᠡᠭᠴᠡ</uig> he had scarcely come, when ...
<uig rom="oromaqca">ᠣᠷᠣᠮᠠᠬᠴᠠ</uig> he had scarcely entered, when ...
<uig rom="barimaci">ᠪᠠᠷᠢᠮᠠᠴᠢ</uig> he had scarcely seized, when ...

The successive converb expresses an action of which the performance is immediately followed by that of the main action, e. g., "as soon as he did . . ." Sometimes this form replaces the conditional converb ("when he did. . .").
This converb does not occur in the classical language, as it is a typical colloquial form.
The suffix is <uig rom="-qula/-küle.">ᠬᠤᠯᠠ/ᠺᠦᠯᠡ</uig>
<uig rom="yabuqula">ᠶᠠᠪᠤᠬᠤᠯᠠ</uig> as soon as he started going
<uig rom="ireküle">ᠢᠷᠡᠺᠦᠯᠡ</uig> as soon as he came, simultaneously with the arrival
The final converb expresses the purpose of an action and corresponds to the Latin supinum ("in order to. . .").
The suffix is <uig rom="-r-a/-r-e">᠎ᠷ᠎ᠡ</uig> with the union vowel -u-/-ü- when the stem ends in a consonant.
<uig rom="yabur-a">ᠶᠠᠪᠤᠷ᠎ᠠ</uig> in order to go
<uig rom="üjer-e">ᠦᠵᠡᠷ᠎ᠡ</uig> in order to see
The preparative converb expresaes an action which is preparatory to and induces the main action: "in consequence of doing. . .," "as he did. . .," "because he did. . ."

This form is little used both in the classical and modern language and only a few verbs occur in this form. These are: <uig rom="ügüle-">ᠦᠭᠦᠯᠡ ᠎</uig> "to say, to speak," <uig rom="keme-">ᠺᠡᠮᠡ ᠎</uig> or geme- "to say" (seldom), <uig rom="bol-">ᠪᠣᠯ ᠎</uig> "to become" (only in the expression <uig rom="jarliq">ᠵᠠᠷᠯᠢᠬ ᠪᠣᠯ ᠎</uig> bol- "to order"), <uig rom="bü-">ᠪᠦ ᠎</uig> "to be," and <uig rom="üje-">ᠦᠵᠡ ᠎</uig> "to see." But in the pre-classical language this was a very common form.
The suffix is <uig rom="-r-un/-r-ün">᠎ᠷ ᠤᠨ</uig>
<uig rom="eyin kemen ügüler-ün">ᠡᠶᠢᠨ ᠺᠡᠮᠡᠨ ᠦᠭᠦᠯᠡᠷ ᠤᠨ</uig> as he said in this manner
<uig rom="qaγan jarliy bolur-un">ᠬᠠᠭᠠᠨ ᠵᠠᠷᠯᠢᠶ ᠪᠣᠯᠤᠷ ᠤᠨ</uig> as the khaghan ordered
<uig rom="barir-un">ᠪᠠᠷᠢᠷ ᠤᠨ</uig> in consequence of taking
<uig rom="jobaγulur-un">ᠵᠣᠪᠠᠭᠤᠯᠤᠷ ᠤᠨ</uig> in consequence of causing sufferings
<uig rom="bolγar-un">ᠪᠣᠯᠭᠠᠷ ᠤᠨ</uig> in consequence of doing
The auxiliary verbs <uig rom="a-">ᠠ ᠎</uig> "to be," <uig rom="bü-">ᠪᠦ ᠎</uig> "to be", and <uig rom="bol-">ᠪᠣᠯ ᠎</uig> "to become" have either irregular or defective conjugations.

entry.title: Accidence - Verbs - Auxiliary verbs
entry.title2: Verbs - Conjugation - Auxiliary verbs - Verb a-

paragraphs.paragraph: Not all forms of the verb <uig rom="a-">ᠠ ᠎</uig> "to be" occur. A few forms differ from the respective forms of other verbs.
The conjugation of the verb <uig rom="a-">ᠠ ᠎</uig> "to be" is as follows
Imperative of the 2nd pers. sing.: does not exist
Imperative of the 2 nd pers. plur. : <uig rom="aqtun">ᠠᠬᠲᠤᠨ</uig> or <uig rom="adqun">ᠠᠳᠬᠤᠨ</uig> (only pre-classical)
Voluntative of the 1 st pers. sing.: <uig rom="asuγai">ᠠᠰᠤᠭᠠᠢ</uig>
Voluntative of the 1 st pers. plur. : <uig rom="ay-a">ᠠᠶ᠎ᠠ</uig> (only pre-classical)
Imperative of the 3rd pers.: <uig rom="atuγai">ᠠᠲᠤᠭᠠᠢ</uig>
Optative : <uig rom="aγasai">ᠠᠭᠠᠰᠠᠢ</uig> (seldom)
Narrative present: <uig rom="amui">ᠠᠮᠤᠢ</uig>
Deductive present: <uig rom="ayu">ᠠᠶᠤ</uig> (only pre-classical)
First past : <uig rom="aba">ᠠᠪᠠ</uig> or <uig rom="abai">ᠠᠪᠠᠢ</uig>
Second past: <uig rom="aluγ-a">ᠠᠯᠤᠭ᠎ᠠ</uig> (only pre-classical)
Third past : <uig rom="ajuγu">ᠠᠵᠤᠭᠤ</uig> and (only pre-classical) <uig rom="ajuγui">ᠠᠵᠤᠭᠤᠢ</uig>
Nomen actoris : <uig rom="aqci">ᠠᠬᠴᠢ</uig>
Nomen usus : does not exist
Nomen futuri : <uig rom="aqu">ᠠᠬᠤ</uig> and <uig rom="aqui">ᠠᠬᠤᠢ</uig>, plur. (only pre-classical) <uig rom="aqun">ᠠᠬᠤᠨ</uig>
Nomen imperfecti: <uig rom="aγ-a">ᠠᠭ᠎ᠠ</uig> (only pre-classical)
Nomen perfecti: <uig rom="aqsan">ᠠᠬᠰᠠᠨ</uig>
Converbum conditionale : <uig rom="abasu">ᠠᠪᠠᠰᠤ</uig>
Converbum successivum: <uig rom="aqula">ᠠᠬᠤᠯᠠ</uig> (used as conditional)
Converbum concessivum: <uig rom="abacu">ᠠᠪᠠᠴᠤ</uig>
Converbum imperfecti: <uig rom="aju">ᠠᠵᠤ</uig>, in popular books <uig rom="aji">ᠠᠵᠢ</uig>
Converbum modale: does not exist
Converbum perfecti: <uig rom="aγad">ᠠᠭᠠᠳ</uig>
Converbum terminale: <uig rom="atala">ᠠᠲᠠᠯᠠ</uig>
Converbum abtemporale : <uig rom="aqsaγar">ᠠᠬᠰᠠᠭᠠᠷ</uig>
Converbum contemporale: does not exist
Converbum finale: does not exist
Converbum praeparativum : <uig rom="ar-un">ᠠᠷ ᠤᠨ</uig> (only pre-classical)

entry.title: Accidence - Verbs - Auxiliary verbs
entry.title2: Verbs - Conjugation - Auxiliary verbs - Verb bü-

paragraphs.paragraph: Only a few forms of the verb <uig rom="bü-">ᠪᠦ ᠎</uig> "to be" have been preserved, hence its conjugation is much more defective than that of the verb <uig rom="a-.">ᠠ ᠎.</uig>
Second past: <uig rom="bülüge">ᠪᠦᠯᠦᠭᠡ</uig>, in popular books <uig rom="bile">ᠪᠢᠯᠡ</uig> (pronounced bile)
Third past: <uig rom="büjügü">ᠪᠦᠵᠦᠭᠦ</uig> or <uig rom="büjüküi">ᠪᠦᠵᠦᠺᠦᠢ</uig> (only pre-classical and very rare)
Nomen perfecti: <uig rom="bügsen">ᠪᠦᠭᠰᠡᠨ</uig> (only pre-classical and very rare)
Nomen futuri: <uig rom="bükü">ᠪᠦᠺᠦ</uig> and <uig rom="büküi">ᠪᠦᠺᠦᠢ</uig>, plural (only pre-classical) <uig rom="bükün">ᠪᠦᠺᠦᠨ</uig>
Converbum conditionale : <uig rom="bügesü">ᠪᠦᠭᠡᠰᠦ</uig>
Converbum perfecti: <uig rom="büged">ᠪᠦᠭᠡᠳ</uig>
Converbum terminale: <uig rom="bügetele">ᠪᠦᠭᠡᠲᠡᠯᠡ</uig>
Converbum praeparativum: <uig rom="bür-ün">ᠪᠦᠷ ᠤᠨ</uig> (pre-classical and classical)

entry.title: Accidence - Verbs - Auxiliary verbs
entry.title2: Verbs - Conjugation - Auxiliary verbs - Verb bol-

paragraphs.paragraph: The verb <uig rom="bol-">ᠪᠣᠯ ᠎</uig> "to become" has a regular and complete conjugation with one exception: in the pre-classical language it had the nomen praesentis in <uig rom="-ui"> ᠤᠢ</uig>, which is a rare form. The nomen praesentis of this verb is <uig rom="bolui">ᠪᠣᠯᠤᠢ</uig>. It is used only as predicate and means "he is."
Another exceptional form is <uig rom="bolai">ᠪᠣᠯᠠᠢ</uig> "he is." No other verb has such a form.
In all other respects the conjugation of this verb is regular.

entry.title: Accidence - Verbs - Auxiliary verbs
entry.title2: Verbs - Conjugation - Auxiliary verbs - Verb bui-

paragraphs.paragraph: This verb has but this one form, <uig rom="bui">ᠪᠤᠢ</uig>, which is used as noun and verb. It serves as subject ("existence" or "the existing"), as object, as attribute ("existing"), and as predicate ("exists", "is").
The deductive present and the interrogative form is <uig rom="buyu">ᠪᠤᠶᠤ</uig> "is."
Under the influence of the colloquial language, this verb occurs sometimes in the form <uig rom="bi">ᠪᠢ</uig> or <uig rom="bei~bai">ᠪᠡᠢ~ᠪᠠᠢ</uig>.

entry.title: Syntax - Syntactical pecularities - Substantives and adjectives

paragraphs.paragraph: There are no morphological differences between the simple forms of substantives and of adjectives. Therefore, the substantives and adjectives are treated as one part of speech-nouns.

Almost all nouns can serve as attributes - that is, they can function attributively as the adjectives in the European languages, e. g., <uig rom="modun">ᠮᠣᠳᠤᠨ</uig> "tree" means "wooden" as an attribute. But as subject or object of a sentence <uig rom="modun">ᠮᠣᠳᠤᠨ</uig> serves as a substantive and means "tree." On the other hand, words expressing qualities can also serve as syntactical subject or object and, in such cases, they function as the substantives in European languages, e. g., <uig rom="sayin">ᠰᠠᠶᠢᠨ</uig> "good" as attribute or predicate and "goodness" as syntactical subject or object.
<uig rom="öndür modun">ᠥᠨᠳᠦᠷ ᠮᠣᠳᠤᠨ</uig> a high tree
<uig rom="modun bayising">ᠮᠣᠳᠤᠨ ᠪᠠᠶᠢᠰᠢᠩ</uig> a wooden building
<uig rom="sayin nökör">ᠰᠠᠶᠢᠨ ᠨᠥᠺᠥᠷ</uig> a good friend
<uig rom="tegün-ü sayin-i inu sinjilesügei">ᠲᠡᠭᠦᠨ ᠤ ᠰᠠᠶᠢᠨ ᠢ ᠢᠨᠤ ᠰᠢᠨᠵᠢᠯᠡᠰᠦᠭᠡᠢ</uig> I shall examine his goodness.
As a substantive, a noun is characterized by the following features

a) It is declinable.
b) It has a singular and a plural.
As an adjective, a noun is indeclinable and has a plural only in the pre-classical language.
<uig rom="maγus aran">ᠮᠠᠭᠤᠰ ᠠᠷᠠᠨ</uig> bad people
<uig rom="busud buyan-nuγud">ᠪᠤᠰᠤᠳ ᠪᠤᠶᠠᠨ ᠎ᠨᠤᠭᠤᠳ</uig> other benefits
<uig rom="bilig ügegün qulaγas">ᠪᠢᠯᠢᠭ ᠦᠭᠡᠭᠦᠨ ᠬᠤᠯᠠᠭᠠᠰ</uig> thieves having no intellect

entry.title: Syntax - Syntactical pecularities - Substantives and adjectives

paragraphs.paragraph: As shown above, a substantive may serve as subject, predicate, object, or attribute. It is obvious that a noun expressing a quality can serve as attribute, because words egpressing such ideas as "good" or "bad" are attributive words par excellence. But on the other hand, they can also serve as subject or object:
<uig rom="urtu inu tabun alda amui">ᠤᠷᠲᠤ ᠢᠨᠤ ᠲᠠᠪᠤᠨ ᠠᠯᠳᠠ ᠠᠮᠤᠢ</uig> Its length (<uig rom="urtu">ᠤᠷᠲᠤ</uig> "long") is five fathoms.
<uig rom="bi urtu-yi inu ese medemüi">ᠪᠢ ᠤᠷᠲᠤ ᠶᠢ ᠢᠨᠤ ᠡᠰᠡ ᠮᠡᠳᠡᠮᠦᠢ</uig> I do not know its length.

entry.title: Syntax - Syntactical pecularities - Substantives and adjectives

paragraphs.paragraph: Nouns indicating anything animate or inanimate can also express qualities, without undergoing any change in their grammatical form:
<uig rom="modun bayising">ᠮᠣᠳᠤᠨ ᠪᠠᠶᠢᠰᠢᠩ</uig> a wooden building (<uig rom="modun">ᠮᠣᠳᠤᠨ</uig> tree, wood)
<uig rom="kümün görügesün">ᠺᠦᠮᠦᠨ ᠭᠥᠷᠦᠭᠡᠰᠦᠨ</uig> monkey (a man animal, <uig rom="kümün">ᠺᠦᠮᠦᠨ</uig> man, <uig rom="görügesün">ᠭᠥᠷᠦᠭᠡᠰᠦᠨ</uig> animal)
Only nouns suitable from the point of view of their meaning can serve as attributes, e. g., surtal "doctrine" cannot serve as an attribute unless it changes its grammatical form.

entry.title: Syntax - Syntactical pecularities - Substantives and adjectives

paragraphs.paragraph: Nouns serving as attributes may be modified by adverbs. Of course, not all nouns may be modified by adverbs, but only those which express ideas of qualities which can be quantified, e. g., <uig rom="sayin">ᠰᠠᠶᠢᠨ</uig> "good" may be modified by the adverb <uig rom="masi">ᠮᠠᠰᠢ</uig> "very," but <uig rom="temür">ᠲᠡᠮᠦᠷ</uig> "iron" cannot be modified by an adverb, as it is impossible to say "a very iron tool" as an antithesis to a tool which is not "very iron."
<uig rom="masi türgen">ᠮᠠᠰᠢ ᠲᠦᠷᠭᠡᠨ</uig> very fast, very quick
<uig rom="cab caγan">ᠴᠠᠪ ᠴᠠᠭᠠᠨ</uig> completely white

entry.title: Syntax - Syntactical pecularities - Substantives and adjectives

paragraphs.paragraph: Many words expressing qualities can serve as adverbs.
<uig rom="yeke maγu">ᠶᠡᠺᠡ ᠮᠠᠭᠤ</uig> very bad (<uig rom="">ᠶᠡᠺᠡ</uig> yeke great, big)
<uig rom="türgen yabuqu">ᠲᠦᠷᠭᠡᠨ ᠶᠠᠪᠤᠬᠤ</uig> to go quickly (<uig rom="türgen">ᠲᠦᠷᠭᠡᠨ</uig> quiek, fast)
<uig rom="sayin ungsiqu">ᠰᠠᠶᠢᠨ ᠤᠩᠰᠢᠬᠤ</uig> to read well (<uig rom="sayin">ᠰᠠᠶᠢᠨ</uig> good)
Mongolian has a grammatical singular and plural. The latter is not so usual as in many other languages.
Singular
The singular is used in the following cases
a) When speaking of a single object:
<uig rom="manu baqsi irebe">ᠮᠠᠨᠤ ᠪᠠᠬᠰᠢ ᠢᠷᠡᠪᠡ</uig> Our teacher has come.
<uig rom="qaγan jarliq bolur-un">ᠬᠠᠭᠠᠨ ᠵᠠᠷᠯᠢᠬ ᠪᠣᠯᠤᠷ ᠤᠨ</uig> The khaghan said (lit., "ordered").
b) When speaking of things in general or of a multitude of indeterminate size or of things of which the number is supposed to be unimportant:
<uig rom="tere γajar-a kümün saγuju ülü bolumui">ᠲᠡᠷᠡ ᠭᠠᠵᠠᠷ ᠠ ᠺᠦᠮᠦᠨ ᠰᠠᠭᠤᠵᠤ ᠦᠯᠦ ᠪᠣᠯᠤᠮᠤᠢ</uig> In that country people (man) cannot live.
<uig rom="sine nom marγasi iremüi">ᠰᠢᠨᠡ ᠨᠣᠮ ᠮᠠᠷᠭᠠᠰᠢ ᠢᠷᠡᠮᠦᠢ</uig> New books (book) will come tomorrow.
<uig rom="ebügen qoni qariγulumui">ᠡᠪᠦᠭᠡᠨ ᠬᠣᠨᠢ ᠬᠠᠷᠢᠭᠤᠯᠤᠮᠤᠢ</uig> The old man pastures sheep.
<uig rom="sibaγu bariqci ebügen">ᠰᠢᠪᠠᠭᠤ ᠪᠠᠷᠢᠬᠴᠢ ᠡᠪᠦᠭᠡᠨ</uig> an old man catching birds (bird).
c) Words qualified by numerals or words expressing a multitude are usually used in the singular form. But the plural was used in the preclassical language in such cases (see § 393b):
<uig rom="doloγan ebügen">ᠳᠣᠯᠣᠭᠠᠨ ᠡᠪᠦᠭᠡᠨ</uig> Ursa Major (astron., lit., "the seven old men")
<uig rom="mingγan jil">ᠮᠢᠩᠭᠠᠨ ᠵᠢᠯ</uig> a thousand years
<uig rom="qoyar kümün">ᠬᠣᠶᠠᠷ ᠺᠦᠮᠦᠨ</uig> two people
<uig rom="olan kümün">ᠣᠯᠠᠨ ᠺᠦᠮᠦᠨ</uig> many people
<uig rom="kümün-ü ciγulγan">ᠺᠦᠮᠦᠨ ᠤ ᠴᠢᠭᠤᠯᠭᠠᠨ</uig> a gathering of people
d) Certain words always express a multitude and, therefore, have no plural:
<uig rom="aduγun">ᠠᠳᠤᠭᠤᠨ</uig> horses
<uig rom="mal">ᠮᠠᠯ</uig> cattle

<uig rom="aran">ᠠᠷᠠᠨ</uig> people (in the pre-classical language. In modern Mongolian it is replaced by a plural form <uig rom="arad">ᠠᠷᠠᠳ</uig> which means "ordinary man." Its plural is now <uig rom="arad-ud">ᠠᠷᠠᠳ ᠤᠳ</uig> "working people.")

e) Words designating objects existing normally only in pairs, not as single units (ears, hands), are never used in the plural. An exception may be a case in which it is necessary to state that somewhere the ground was littered with heads and arms of injured and slain people (e. g., a battle field). On the other hand, if it is necessary to say that someone has but one eye, the word <uig rom="örügesün">ᠥᠷᠦᠭᠡᠰᠦᠨ</uig> "single" (never <uig rom="nigen">ᠨᠢᠭᠡᠨ</uig> "one") is used :
<uig rom="örügesün nidün">ᠥᠷᠦᠭᠡᠰᠦᠨ ᠨᠢᠳᠦᠨ</uig> a single eye
<uig rom="örügesün köl-tei kümün">ᠥᠷᠦᠭᠡᠰᠦᠨ ᠺᠥᠯ ᠎ᠲᠡᠢ ᠺᠦᠮᠦᠨ</uig> a one-legged man

f) Neither the nominal predicate nor the attribute agrees in number with the word qualified and in the classical language the attribute and the nominal predicate are always singular (as in English). In the preclassical language they often agree.
<uig rom="sayin morid">ᠰᠠᠶᠢᠨ ᠮᠣᠷᠢᠳ</uig> good horses
<uig rom="mergen lam-a-nar">ᠮᠡᠷᠭᠡᠨ ᠯᠠᠮ ᠠ ᠎ᠨᠠᠷ</uig> wise lamas
<uig rom="enelkün amitan">ᠡᠨᠡᠯᠺᠦᠨ ᠠᠮᠢᠲᠠᠨ</uig> suffering creatures (pre-classical)
<uig rom="bilig-ten burqad">ᠪᠢᠯᠢᠭ ᠎ᠲᠡᠨ ᠪᠤᠷᠬᠠᠳ</uig> the wise Buddhas (pre-classical)
The plural is used in the following cases:
a) Mainly in reference to animate things, especially people and deities:
<uig rom="bodisadv-nar-un yabudal-nuγud">ᠪᠣᠳᠢᠰᠠᠳᠸ ᠎ᠨᠠᠷ ᠤᠨ ᠶᠠᠪᠤᠳᠠᠯ ᠎ᠨᠤᠭᠤᠳ</uig> the deeds of the Bodhisattvas
<uig rom="merged bagsi-nar">ᠮᠡᠷᠭᠡᠳ ᠪᠠᠭᠰᠢ ᠎ᠨᠠᠷ</uig> the wise teachers
<<uig rom="luus-un qaγad">ᠯᠤᠤᠰ ᠤᠨ ᠬᠠᠭᠠᠳ</uig> the kings of the dragons (Negas)
b) Words designating animate things are often used in the plural, even if they are qualified by numerals or other numerical words :
<uig rom="doloγan ebüged">ᠳᠣᠯᠣᠭᠠᠨ ᠡᠪᠦᠭᠡᠳ</uig> Ursa Major (lit., "seven old men")
<uig rom="mingγan burqad">ᠮᠢᠩᠭᠠᠨ ᠪᠤᠷᠬᠠᠳ</uig> thousand Buddhas
<uig rom="γucin γurban tngri-ner">ᠭᠤᠴᠢᠨ ᠭᠤᠷᠪᠠᠨ ᠲᠩᠷᠢ ᠎ᠨᠡᠷ</uig> thirty-three deities
<uig rom="olan cerig-üd">ᠣᠯᠠᠨ ᠴᠡᠷᠢᠭ ᠤᠳ</uig> many soldiers

c) Certain words are grammatically plural forms, but they denote single beings. If it is necessary to indicate the notion of multitude, these words take a plural suffix. Thus they will have two plural suffixes :
<uig rom="ekener">ᠡᠺᠡᠨᠡᠷ</uig> woman ~ <uig rom="ekener-üd">ᠡᠺᠡᠨᠡᠷ ᠤᠳ</uig> women
<uig rom="sayid">ᠰᠠᠶᠢᠳ</uig> minister ~ <uig rom="sayid-ud">ᠰᠠᠶᠢᠳ ᠤᠳ</uig> ministers
d) The plural of proper names indicates the person in question and all the people accompanying him :
<uig rom="sayid dorji-nar">ᠰᠠᠶᠢᠳ ᠳᠣᠷᠵᠢ ᠎ᠨᠠᠷ</uig> Minister Dorji and his retinue
e) The pluralis majestatis is used in reference to honorable people:
<uig rom="tüsimed">ᠲᠦᠰᠢᠮᠡᠳ</uig> official, sing. <uig rom="tüsimel">ᠲᠦᠰᠢᠮᠡᠯ</uig>

f) There are two pronouns of the second person of the plural: <uig rom="ta">ᠲᠠ</uig> "you" and <uig rom="tanar">ᠲᠠᠨᠠᠷ</uig> "you". The former is used when addressing a person who m'ay not be addressed with the familiar second singular form. The latter (<uig rom="tanar">ᠲᠠᠨᠠᠷ</uig> ) is used in reference to a multitude (German Ihr).
g) There are two pronouns of the first person of the plural: <uig rom="ba">ᠪᠠ</uig> "we" (exclusive) and <uig rom="bida">ᠪᠢᠳᠠ</uig> "we" (inclusive).
The pronoun of the first person in the expression "you and I" is either <uig rom="bi">ᠪᠢ</uig> "I" or <uig rom="bida">ᠪᠢᠳᠠ</uig> "we" :
<uig rom="bi ci qoyar">ᠪᠢ ᠴᠢ ᠬᠣᠶᠠᠷ</uig> I and you or
<uig rom="ci bida qoyar">ᠴᠢ ᠪᠢᠳᠠ ᠬᠣᠶᠠᠷ</uig> you and I (lit., "thou and we two") (See § 399.)
h) In the pre-classical language the attribute often agrees in number with the qualified word, but in the classical and modern language only a few words so agree:
<uig rom="ene kümüs">ᠡᠨᠡ ᠺᠦᠮᠦᠰ</uig> or <uig rom="ede kümüs">ᠡᠳᠡ ᠺᠦᠮᠦᠰ</uig> these people
<uig rom="tede baqsi-nar">ᠲᠡᠳᠡ ᠪᠠᠬᠰᠢ ᠎ᠨᠠᠷ</uig> those teachers
<uig rom="tede nököceldügcid">ᠲᠡᠳᠡ ᠨᠥᠺᠥᠴᠡᠯᠳᠦᠭᠴᠢᠳ</uig> those causes
<uig rom="busud buyan-nuγud">ᠪᠤᠰᠤᠳ ᠪᠤᠶᠠᠨ ᠎ᠨᠤᠭᠤᠳ</uig> other virtues
<uig rom="kilinglegsed cidküd">ᠺᠢᠯᠢᠩᠯᠡᠭᠰᠡᠳ ᠴᠢᠳᠺᠦᠳ</uig> angry devils
i) If the predicate is a plural verb (see § 234), the subject can be either a plural or a singular, as the verb indicates that a multitude is meant:
<uig rom="cerig yabucaγajuqui">ᠴᠡᠷᠢᠭ ᠶᠠᠪᠤᠴᠠᠭᠠᠵᠤᠬᠤᠢ</uig> The soldiers had gone.
The reflexive-possessive suffix refers to the person acting and functions in the same manner as the Latin pronoun suus:
<uig rom="sabi nom-iyan ungsimui">ᠰᠠᠪᠢ ᠨᠣᠮ ᠢᠶᠠᠨ ᠤᠩᠰᠢᠮᠤᠢ</uig> The pupil reads his book.
<uig rom="egüde-ben tayiluju ög">ᠡᠭᠦᠳᠡ ᠎ᠪᠡᠨ ᠲᠠᠶᠢᠯᠤᠵᠤ ᠥᠭ</uig> Open your door!
Even adverbs of place can take this suffix. In which case they indicate the place where the actor is or whither he is moving :
<uig rom="bi tende-ben saγumui">ᠪᠢ ᠲᠡᠨᠳᠡ ᠎ᠪᠡᠨ ᠰᠠᠭᠤᠮᠤᠢ</uig> I am living there - at my (place).
<uig rom="cerig cinaqsi-ban mordoba">ᠴᠡᠷᠢᠭ ᠴᠢᠨᠠᠬᠰᠢ ᠎ᠪᠠᠨ ᠮᠣᠷᠳᠣᠪᠠ</uig> The army rushed farther in its direction.

If the object concerned does not belong to the person acting or has nothing to do with the latter, the possessive suffix can not be used and the possessor of the object concerned must be indicated by the genitive either of a noun or of a personal pronoun :
<uig rom="ci minu nom buu ab">ᠴᠢ ᠮᠢᠨᠤ ᠨᠣᠮ ᠪᠤᠤ ᠠᠪ</uig> Do not take my book!
<uig rom="sabi tegün-ü nom ungsimui">ᠰᠠᠪᠢ ᠲᠡᠭᠦᠨ ᠤ ᠨᠣᠮ ᠤᠩᠰᠢᠮᠤᠢ</uig> The pupil reads his (not his own but someone else's) book.
<uig rom="baqsi ger-tür inu saγuju amui">ᠪᠠᠬᠰᠢ ᠭᠡᠷ ᠲᠤᠷ ᠢᠨᠤ ᠰᠠᠭᠤᠵᠤ ᠠᠮᠤᠢ</uig> The teacher is living in his (not his own but someone else's) house.

In such cases, the genitive of the personal pronoun of the third person <uig rom="inu">ᠢᠨᠤ</uig> (singular) or <uig rom="anu">ᠠᠨᠤ</uig> (plural) is used with the adverbs of place. This indicates the place of something which is not being identified with the person acting :
<uig rom="cinaqsi inu talbiba">ᠴᠢᠨᠠᠬᠰᠢ ᠢᠨᠤ ᠲᠠᠯᠪᠢᠪᠠ</uig> He put it farther (not farther from him but from its former place).
In general, the use of numerals does not differ from English usage, but there are two special uses of Mongolian numerals which should be discussed here. These are :

a) numerals in dates and
b) numerals as conjunctions.
Instead of ordinal numerals in dates only cardinal numerals are used:
a) Instead of Tibetan names of days new expressions consisting of the word <uig rom="graγ">ᠭᠷᠠᠭ</uig> "planet" and a cardinal number before it, in the same way as in modern Chinese, are used:
Sunday: <uig rom="sayin edür">ᠰᠠᠶᠢᠨ ᠡᠳᠦᠷ</uig> Good Day
Monday: <uig rom="nige graγ">ᠨᠢᠭᠡ ᠭᠷᠠᠭ</uig> First Planet
Tuesday: <uig rom="qoyar graγ">ᠬᠣᠶᠠᠷ ᠭᠷᠠᠭ</uig> Second Planet
Wednesday: <uig rom="γurban graγ">ᠭᠤᠷᠪᠠᠨ ᠭᠷᠠᠭ</uig> Third Planet
Thursday: <uig rom="dörben graγ">ᠳᠥᠷᠪᠡᠨ ᠭᠷᠠᠭ</uig> Fourth Planet
Friday : <uig rom="tabun graγ">ᠲᠠᠪᠤᠨ ᠭᠷᠠᠭ</uig> Fifth Planet
Saturday: <uig rom="jirγuγan graγ">ᠵᠢᠷᠭᠤᠭᠠᠨ ᠭᠷᠠᠭ</uig> Sixth Planet
b) The months, too, are designated by cardinal numerals.
January : <uig rom="nige sar-a">ᠨᠢᠭᠡ ᠰᠠᠷ᠎ᠠ</uig> First Month
February: <uig rom="qoyar sar-a">ᠬᠣᠶᠠᠷ ᠰᠠᠷ᠎ᠠ</uig> Second Month
March: <uig rom="γurban sar-a">ᠭᠤᠷᠪᠠᠨ ᠰᠠᠷ᠎ᠠ</uig> Third Month
April: <uig rom="dörben sar-a">ᠳᠥᠷᠪᠡᠨ ᠰᠠᠷ᠎ᠠ</uig> Fourth Month
May: <uig rom="tabun sar-a">ᠲᠠᠪᠤᠨ ᠰᠠᠷ᠎ᠠ</uig> Fifth Month
June: <uig rom="jirγuγan sar-a">ᠵᠢᠷᠭᠤᠭᠠᠨ ᠰᠠᠷ᠎ᠠ</uig> Sixth Month
July: <uig rom="doloγan sar-a">ᠳᠣᠯᠣᠭᠠᠨ ᠰᠠᠷ᠎ᠠ</uig> Seventh Month
August: <uig rom="naiman sar-a">ᠨᠠᠢᠮᠠᠨ ᠰᠠᠷ᠎ᠠ</uig> Eighth Month
September: <uig rom="yisün sar-a">ᠶᠢᠰᠦᠨ ᠰᠠᠷ᠎ᠠ</uig> Ninth Month
October: <uig rom="arban sar-a">ᠠᠷᠪᠠᠨ ᠰᠠᠷ᠎ᠠ</uig> Tenth Month
November: <uig rom="arban nige sar-a">ᠠᠷᠪᠠᠨ</uig> Eleventh Month
December: <uig rom="arban qoyar sar-a">ᠠᠷᠪᠠᠨ</uig> Twelfth Month
c) The dates of the month are also designated by cardinal numerals :
<uig rom="doloγan sar-a-yin qorin doloγan edür">ᠳᠣᠯᠣᠭᠠᠨ ᠰᠠᠷ ᠠ ᠶᠢᠨ ᠬᠣᠷᠢᠨ ᠳᠣᠯᠣᠭᠠᠨ ᠡᠳᠦᠷ</uig> the 27 th of July
<uig rom="dörben sar-a-yin arban yisün edür">ᠳᠥᠷᠪᠡᠨ ᠰᠠᠷ ᠠ ᠶᠢᠨ ᠠᠷᠪᠠᠨ ᠶᠢᠰᠦᠨ ᠡᠳᠦᠷ</uig> the 19th of April
<uig rom="naiman sar-a-yin qorin tabun edür">ᠨᠠᠢᠮᠠᠨ ᠰᠠᠷ ᠠ ᠶᠢᠨ ᠬᠣᠷᠢᠨ ᠲᠠᠪᠤᠨ ᠡᠳᠦᠷ</uig> the 25th of August
<uig rom="arban nige sar-a-yin dörben edür">ᠠᠷᠪᠠᠨ ᠨᠢᠭᠡ ᠰᠠᠷ ᠠ ᠶᠢᠨ ᠳᠥᠷᠪᠡᠨ ᠡᠳᠦᠷ</uig> the 4th of November

d) According to an ancient tradition, months are divided into three decades: the first decade is called <uig rom="sin-e">ᠰᠢᠨ᠎ᠡ</uig> "new" (this is the new moon), the second decade is <uig rom="tergel sar-a">ᠲᠡᠷᠭᠡᠯ ᠰᠠᠷ᠎ᠠ</uig> (this is the full moon), and the last decade is <uig rom="qaγucin">ᠬᠠᠭᠤᠴᠢᠨ</uig> "old" (this is the old moon).

According to this system, the second day of the first decade, i. e., the second of the month concerned, is <uig rom="sin-e-yin qoyar edür">ᠰᠢᠨ ᠡ ᠶᠢᠨ ᠬᠣᠶᠠᠷ ᠡᠳᠦᠷ</uig> "the second day of the new." The third day of the last decade is <uig rom="qaγucin-u γurban edür">ᠬᠠᠭᠤᠴᠢᠨ ᠤ ᠭᠤᠷᠪᠠᠨ ᠡᠳᠦᠷ</uig> "the third day of the old."
<uig rom="arban nige sar-a-yin sin-e-yin dörben edür">ᠠᠷᠪᠠᠨ ᠨᠢᠭᠡ ᠰᠠᠷ ᠠ ᠶᠢᠨ ᠰᠢᠨ ᠡ ᠶᠢᠨ ᠳᠥᠷᠪᠡᠨ ᠡᠳᠦᠷ</uig> the fourth day of the new (moon) of the eleventh month, i. e., the fourth of November
<uig rom="tabun sar-a-yin qaγucin-u γurban edür">ᠲᠠᠪᠤᠨ ᠰᠠᠷ ᠠ ᠶᠢᠨ ᠬᠠᠭᠤᠴᠢᠨ ᠤ ᠭᠤᠷᠪᠠᠨ ᠡᠳᠦᠷ</uig> the third day of the old (moon) of the fifth month, i. e., the twenty-third of May.
The word <uig rom="edür">ᠡᠳᠦᠷ</uig> "day" may be omitted :
<uig rom="tabun sar-a-yin γurban-a">ᠲᠠᠪᠤᠨ ᠰᠠᠷ ᠠ ᠶᠢᠨ ᠭᠤᠷᠪᠠᠨ ᠠ</uig> on the third of the fifth month

e) The years are always designated by ordinal numbers. There are two worda for "year" in Mongolian: <uig rom="on">ᠣᠨ</uig> and <uig rom="jil">ᠵᠢᠯ</uig>. The latter is used only with the names of the twelve-year animal cycle or to express the idea of the year as a space of time (365 days). Therefore this is used only in such expressions as :
<uig rom="">ᠡᠨᠡ ᠵᠢᠯ</uig> ene jil this year
<uig rom="önggeregsen jil">ᠥᠩᠭᠡᠷᠡᠭᠰᠡᠨ ᠵᠢᠯ</uig> last year
<uig rom="qoyitu jil">ᠬᠣᠶᠢᠲᠤ ᠵᠢᠯ</uig> next year
<uig rom="qorin jil-ün urida">ᠬᠣᠷᠢᠨ ᠵᠢᠯ ᠤᠨ ᠤᠷᠢᠳᠠ</uig> twenty years ago
<uig rom="olan jil boluqsan-u qoyin-a">ᠣᠯᠠᠨ ᠵᠢᠯ ᠪᠣᠯᠤᠬᠰᠠᠨ ᠤ ᠬᠣᠶᠢᠨ ᠠ</uig> after many years
<uig rom="tabun jil">ᠲᠠᠪᠤᠨ ᠵᠢᠯ</uig> five years
The names of the years of the twelve-year cycle are the following :
1. <uig rom="quluγan-a jil">ᠬᠤᠯᠤᠭᠠᠨ᠎ᠠ ᠵᠢᠯ</uig> mouse year
2. <uig rom="üker jil">ᠦᠺᠡᠷ ᠵᠢᠯ</uig> ox year
3. <uig rom="bars jil">ᠪᠠᠷᠰ ᠵᠢᠯ</uig> tiger year
4. <uig rom="taulai jil">ᠲᠠᠤᠯᠠᠢ ᠵᠢᠯ</uig> bare year
5. <uig rom="luu jil">ᠯᠤᠤ ᠵᠢᠯ</uig> dragon year
6. <uig rom="moγai jil">ᠮᠣᠭᠠᠢ ᠵᠢᠯ</uig> serpent year
7. <uig rom="morin jil">ᠮᠣᠷᠢᠨ ᠵᠢᠯ</uig> horse year
8. <uig rom="qonin jil">ᠬᠣᠨᠢᠨ ᠵᠢᠯ</uig> sheep year
9. <uig rom="becin jil">ᠪᠡᠴᠢᠨ ᠵᠢᠯ</uig> ape year
10. <uig rom="takiy-a jil">ᠲᠠᠺᠢᠶ᠎ᠠ ᠵᠢᠯ</uig> hen year
11. <uig rom="noqai jil">ᠨᠣᠬᠠᠢ ᠵᠢᠯ</uig> dog year
12. <uig rom="γaqai jil">ᠭᠠᠬᠠᠢ ᠵᠢᠯ</uig> hog year

f) The other word for "year" is <uig rom="on">ᠣᠨ</uig> . This expresses the idea of a year of a period or era. Therefore, this is used with numerals to denote a year of a period. Only ordinal numerals are used.
<uig rom="engke amuγulang-un arban qoyaduγar on">ᠡᠩᠺᠡ ᠠᠮᠤᠭᠤᠯᠠᠩ ᠤᠨ ᠠᠷᠪᠠᠨ ᠬᠣᠶᠠᠳᠤᠭᠠᠷ ᠣᠨ</uig> the twelfth year of K`anghsi, i. e., 1673

<uig rom="olan-a ergügdegsen-ü tabuduγar on">ᠣᠯᠠᠨ ᠠ ᠡᠷᠭᠦᠭᠳᠡᠭᠰᠡᠨ ᠤ ᠲᠠᠪᠤᠳᠤᠭᠠᠷ ᠣᠨ</uig> the fifth year of the "Proclaimed-by-Many" (the title of the first and last emperor of Outer Mongolia who died in 1924), i. e., 1915
<uig rom="mongγol ulus-un qoriduγar on">ᠮᠣᠩᠭᠣᠯ ᠤᠯᠤᠰ ᠤᠨ ᠬᠣᠷᠢᠳᠤᠭᠠᠷ ᠣᠨ</uig> the twentieth year of the Mongolian State, i. e., 1930
<uig rom="nige mingγ-a yisün jaγun döcin yisüdüger on">ᠨᠢᠭᠡ ᠮᠢᠩᠭ ᠠ ᠶᠢᠰᠦᠨ ᠵᠠᠭᠤᠨ ᠳᠥᠴᠢᠨ ᠶᠢᠰᠦᠳᠦᠭᠡᠷ ᠣᠨ</uig> the year 1949

Two or more words acting as equal members of a sentence can be connected by a numeral denoting the total of the persons or objects in question. The numeral follows the words to which it refers. The numeral is <uig rom=qoyar"">ᠬᠣᠶᠠᠷ</uig> "two," if the total of the persons in question is two; it is <uig rom="γurban ">ᠭᠤᠷᠪᠠᠨ</uig> "three," if the total is three, and so on. The numeral takes all the grammatical endings, and the nouns to which it refers have no case suffixes.

It is not exact to speak of numerals as conjunctions. It would be more nearly correct to call them aggregating terms denoting the total of the objects concerned. But this definition is too long and, therefore, with the above reservations, the numerals are here called "numerals as conjunctions."
<uig rom="bi ci qoyar">ᠪᠢ ᠴᠢ ᠬᠣᠶᠠᠷ</uig> I and you
<uig rom="ci bida qoyar">ᠴᠢ ᠪᠢᠳᠠ ᠬᠣᠶᠠᠷ</uig> you and I (lit., "thou and we two")
<uig rom="aq-a degüü qoyar-i">ᠠᠬ ᠠ ᠳᠡᠭᠦᠦ ᠬᠣᠶᠠᠷ ᠢ</uig> the elder and the younger brothers (accusative)
<uig rom="morin üker temegen γurban-dur">ᠮᠣᠷᠢᠨ ᠦᠺᠡᠷ ᠲᠡᠮᠡᠭᠡᠨ ᠭᠤᠷᠪᠠᠨ ᠳ᠋ᠤᠷ</uig> to the horse, ox, and camel (dative-locative)
<uig rom="qaγan qatun qoyar-aca">ᠬᠠᠭᠠᠨ ᠬᠠᠲᠤᠨ ᠬᠣᠶᠠᠷ ᠡᠴᠡ</uig> from the khaghan and the queen (ablative)
The duplication of a word expresses what in English can be expressed by the words "each" and "every."
A doubled subject means that each of the persons mentioned is acting. A doubled object refers to the action of each person acting.
<uig rom="tede bügüdeger jüg jüg-tür-iyen odbai">ᠲᠡᠳᠡ ᠪᠦᠭᠦᠳᠡᠭᠡᠷ ᠵᠦᠭ ᠵᠦᠭ ᠲᠤᠷ ᠢᠶᠡᠨ ᠣᠳᠪᠠᠢ</uig> They all started off, each in his direction. (Lit., "They all went in their direction-direction.")
<uig rom="γar γar-iyan barilcaγabai">ᠭᠠᠷ ᠭᠠᠷ ᠢᠶᠠᠨ ᠪᠠᠷᠢᠯᠴᠠᠭᠠᠪᠠᠢ</uig> They shook hands. (Lit., "They took their hands-hands.")
<uig rom="kümün kümün-dür nigen joγos ögbe">ᠺᠦᠮᠦᠨ ᠺᠦᠮᠦᠨ ᠳ᠋ᠤᠷ ᠨᠢᠭᠡᠨ ᠵᠣᠭᠣᠰ ᠥᠭᠪᠡ</uig> He gave a coin to each man. (Lit., "He gave one coin to man-man.")

The idea "each other" is expressed by the duplicated word <uig rom="bey-e">ᠪᠡᠶ᠎ᠡ</uig> "body" or <uig rom="nigen">ᠨᠢᠭᠡᠨ</uig> "one" in the appropriate case form. The former is always used with the reflexive-possessive suffix, but in the case of <uig rom="nigen">ᠨᠢᠭᠡᠨ</uig> the use of the suffix is optional.
<uig rom="tede kümüs bey-e bey-e-ben üjen yadamui">ᠲᠡᠳᠡ ᠺᠦᠮᠦᠰ ᠪᠡᠶ ᠡ ᠪᠡᠶ ᠡ ᠎ᠪᠡᠨ ᠦᠵᠡᠨ ᠶᠠᠳᠠᠮᠤᠢ</uig> Those people hate each other. (Lit., "Those people hate their body-body.")
<uig rom="bey-e bey-e-ben taγalaqu">ᠪᠡᠶ ᠡ ᠪᠡᠶ ᠡ ᠎ᠪᠡᠨ ᠲᠠᠭᠠᠯᠠᠬᠤ</uig> to caress each other
<uig rom="tedeger inu bey-e bey-e-degen beleg ergümi">ᠲᠡᠳᠡᠭᠡᠷ ᠢᠨᠤ ᠪᠡᠶ ᠡ ᠪᠡᠶ ᠡ ᠳ᠋ᠡᠭᠡᠨ ᠪᠡᠯᠡᠭ ᠡᠷᠭᠦᠮᠢ</uig> They present each other gifts.
<uig rom="nigen nigen-i ese üjebe">ᠨᠢᠭᠡᠨ ᠨᠢᠭᠡᠨ ᠢ ᠡᠰᠡ ᠦᠵᠡᠪᠡ</uig> They did not see each other.
<uig rom="nigen nigen-degen tusalamji üjegülümüi">ᠨᠢᠭᠡᠨ ᠨᠢᠭᠡᠨ ᠳ᠋ᠡᠭᠡᠨ ᠲᠤᠰᠠᠯᠠᠮᠵᠢ ᠦᠵᠡᠭᠦᠯᠦᠮᠦᠢ</uig> They help each other. (Lit., "One shows assistance to his one.")
Distributive numerals are often replaced by duplicated cardinal numbers.

<uig rom="tede kümüs-tür qoyar qoyar tögörig ögbei">ᠲᠡᠳᠡ ᠺᠦᠮᠦᠰ ᠲᠤᠷ ᠬᠣᠶᠠᠷ ᠬᠣᠶᠠᠷ ᠲᠥᠭᠥᠷᠢᠭ ᠥᠭᠪᠡᠢ</uig> He gave each of those people two tögrig. (Lit., "He gave those people two-two tögrig." Tögrig is an Outer Mongolian coin.)
Certain converbs, too, can be doubled. In such a case they express the gradual intensification of the action.
<uig rom="güicen güicen aldajuqui">ᠭᠦᠢᠴᠡᠨ ᠭᠦᠢᠴᠡᠨ ᠠᠯᠳᠠᠵᠤᠬᠤᠢ</uig> He almost overtook him. (Lit., "In overtaking he failed.")
The verbal nouns are participles but their functions are more varied than those of the participles of most European languages. They are used to designate :
a) the actor (English substantive: reader, author, speaker, and so on)
b) the process of an action (English gerund: the reading, writing, apeaking, and so on
c) the idea of an action as someone's characteristic (English participle: the reading pupil, the writing girl, and so on)
d) the idea of an action = verbum finitum (English indicative forms: he reads, he wrote, and so on)
There are the following verbal nouns :
a) Nomen actoris
b) Nomen praesentis
c) Nomen Usus
d) Nomen futuri
e) Nomen imper f ecti
f) Nomen per f ecti

As to the functions of these verbal nouns, it must be emphasized that they do not express any absolute time of action, but only the relative time. For example, the nomen futuri does not express any action taking place in the absolute future, but an action taking place in the future seen from the point of view of the absolute time of the predicate : if the latter is a present or a future tense, the nomen futuri is a future, but if the predicate is a past tense, the nomen futuri is a future in reference to the past. Verbal nouns express an absolute time only when they act as predicates.
<uig rom="bi qaγan-i jalaqsan">ᠪᠢ ᠬᠠᠭᠠᠨ ᠢ ᠵᠠᠯᠠᠬᠰᠠᠨ</uig> I invited the khaghan (absolute past).
<uig rom="jalaqdaqsan kümün irebe">ᠵᠠᠯᠠᠬᠳᠠᠬᠰᠠᠨ ᠺᠦᠮᠦᠨ ᠢᠷᠡᠪᠡ</uig> The invited man came (past in past). The man who had been invited came.
<uig rom="jalaqdaqsan kümün iremüi">ᠵᠠᠯᠠᠬᠳᠠᠬᠰᠠᠨ ᠺᠦᠮᠦᠨ ᠢᠷᠡᠮᠦᠢ</uig> The invited man will come. (Past in reference to the future: The man who has or will have been invited will come.)
<uig rom="sayin köbegün törökü em-e-yi abqu bui">ᠰᠠᠶᠢᠨ ᠺᠥᠪᠡᠭᠦᠨ ᠲᠥᠷᠥᠺᠦ ᠡᠮ ᠡ ᠶᠢ ᠠᠪᠬᠤ ᠪᠤᠢ</uig> He will take a wife who will bring forth a good boy (future).
<uig rom="sayin köbegün törökü em-e-yi abuba">ᠰᠠᠶᠢᠨ ᠺᠥᠪᠡᠭᠦᠨ ᠲᠥᠷᠥᠺᠦ ᠡᠮ ᠡ ᠶᠢ ᠠᠪᠤᠪᠠ</uig> He took a wife who would bring forth a good boy (future in reference to the past).
In the case of a predicate which is a present or future the nomen futuri <uig rom="irekü">ᠢᠷᠡᠺᠦ</uig> designates:
a) one who will come (comer in the future)
b) coming (as a process) in the future (future arrival)
c) coming in the future as someone's characteristic (The man who will come)
As a predicate the nomen futuri is always a future tense ; e. g., He will come.
On the other hand, if the predicate of the sentence concerned is in a past tense, the same nomen futuri designates:
a) one who had not come at that time but would come
b) coming as a process which at that time was being planned
c) coming as someone's characteristic which at that time was a future characteristic ("the man who would come")

Similarly the nomen perfecti does not express merely any action which took place in the absolute past, but an action which had been or has been or will have been completed, depending upon the absolute time of the finite verb.
Thus the nomen perfecti <uig rom="iregsen">ᠢᠷᠡᠭᠰᠡᠨ</uig> designates :
a) one who had come (if the predicate is a past tense)
one who has come (if the predicate is a present tense) one who will have come (if the predicate is a future)
b) someone's coming which had taken place (if the predicate is a past tense)
someone's coming which has taken place and can be now stated as an accoxnplished fact (if the predicate is a present tense)
someone's coming which would have taken place in the future (if the predicate is a future tense)
c) coming as a characteristic which had been acquired in the past (if the predicate is a past tense)
coming as a characteristic which has been acquired (if the predicate is a present tense)
coming as a characteristic which in the future will have been considered as having been acquired in the past (the person concerned will be one who has come, if the predicate is a future)
As a predicate <uig rom="iregsen">ᠢᠷᠡᠭᠰᠡᠨ</uig> is a perfect : He has come.
Verbal nouns may either designate the actor or express the process of an action. Consequently, they can serve as subjects and objects:
<uig rom="suruqci nom ungsimui">ᠰᠤᠷᠤᠬᠴᠢ ᠨᠣᠮ ᠤᠩᠰᠢᠮᠤᠢ</uig> The pupil (the learner) reads a book.
<uig rom="asida saγuqu-yi buu sedki">ᠠᠰᠢᠳᠠ ᠰᠠᠭᠤᠬᠤ ᠶᠢ ᠪᠤᠤ ᠰᠡᠳᠺᠢ</uig> Do not imagine that you will live forever. (Lit., "Do not imagine living forever.")

<uig rom="ene yirtincü-yin caq samuγu boluqsan-i daruγalan cidaqu qan törökü buyu">ᠡᠨᠡ ᠶᠢᠷᠲᠢᠨᠴᠦ ᠶᠢᠨ ᠴᠠᠬ ᠰᠠᠮᠤᠭᠤ ᠪᠣᠯᠤᠬᠰᠠᠨ ᠢ ᠳᠠᠷᠤᠭᠠᠯᠠᠨ ᠴᠢᠳᠠᠬᠤ ᠬᠠᠨ ᠲᠥᠷᠥᠺᠦ ᠪᠤᠶᠤ</uig> Will there be born any king able to suppress the upheaval of the time of this world?

<uig rom="aqai minu ene cinu-a yabuqu-yi medebüü ci">ᠠᠬᠠᠢ ᠮᠢᠨᠤ ᠡᠨᠡ ᠴᠢᠨᠤ ᠠ ᠶᠠᠪᠤᠬᠤ ᠶᠢ ᠮᠡᠳᠡᠪᠦᠦ ᠴᠢ</uig> Dad, do you realize that a wolf is running there? (Lit., "Dad, do you know the going of this wolf ?")
The verbal nouns express actions as someone's characteristic and, therefore, they serve as attributes :
<uig rom="ükügsen kümün">ᠦᠺᠦᠭᠰᠡᠨ ᠺᠦᠮᠦᠨ</uig> the dead man (lit., "a man who has died")
<uig rom="irekü jil ">ᠢᠷᠡᠺᠦ ᠵᠢᠯ</uig> next year (lit., "the coming year" or "the year which will come")
<uig rom="qoyin-a irekün jobalang-ud">ᠬᠣᠶᠢᠨ ᠠ ᠢᠷᠡᠺᠦᠨ ᠵᠣᠪᠠᠯᠠᠩ ᠤᠳ</uig> the sufferings which will come later on
<uig rom="burtaq-tu sinuqayiraqui sedkil">ᠪᠤᠷᠲᠠᠬ ᠎ᠲᠤ ᠰᠢᠨᠤᠬᠠᠶᠢᠷᠠᠬᠤᠢ ᠰᠡᠳᠺᠢᠯ</uig> the thought burning with passion for sin (lit., "the thought burning with passion for uncleanness")
<uig rom="quricaqci aran">ᠬᠤᠷᠢᠴᠠᠬᠴᠢ ᠠᠷᠠᠨ</uig> people burning with passion
<uig rom="busud-i jirγaγulqui küsel">ᠪᠤᠰᠤᠳ ᠢ ᠵᠢᠷᠭᠠᠭᠤᠯᠬᠤᠢ ᠺᠦᠰᠡᠯ</uig> the wish to give happiness to others
<uig rom="naran-u gerel-iyer delgeregülügsen jalaγu linqus">ᠨᠠᠷᠠᠨ ᠤ ᠭᠡᠷᠡᠯ ᠢᠶᠡᠷ ᠳᠡᠯᠭᠡᠷᠡᠭᠦᠯᠦᠭᠰᠡᠨ ᠵᠠᠯᠠᠭᠤ ᠯᠢᠨᠬᠤᠰ</uig> young lotusflowers unfolded by the rays of the sun
Verbal nouns express actions and, therefore, they can serve as finite verbs, i. e., as predicates of completed sentences:
<uig rom="manu baqsi irege ügei">ᠮᠠᠨᠤ ᠪᠠᠬᠰᠢ ᠢᠷᠡᠭᠡ ᠦᠭᠡᠢ</uig> Our teacher has not come as yet.
<uig rom="kümün-ü bey-e-yi ber qamiγ-a olqu">ᠺᠦᠮᠦᠨ ᠤ ᠪᠡᠶ ᠡ ᠶᠢ ᠪᠡᠷ ᠬᠠᠮᠢᠭ ᠠ ᠣᠯᠬᠤ</uig> But where will the human body be acquired?
<uig rom="nadur jobalang-un qoor-a inu daki yaγun j-a bolqu">ᠨᠠᠳᠤᠷ ᠵᠣᠪᠠᠯᠠᠩ ᠤᠨ ᠬᠣᠣᠷ ᠠ ᠢᠨᠤ ᠳᠠᠺᠢ ᠶᠠᠭᠤᠨ ᠵ ᠠ ᠪᠣᠯᠬᠤ</uig> What does the harm brought by these sufferings matter to me?
<uig rom="kerkin maγad tonilqu bi">ᠺᠡᠷᠺᠢᠨ ᠮᠠᠭᠠᠳ ᠲᠣᠨᠢᠯᠬᠤ ᠪᠢ</uig> How will I really be saved?
<uig rom="qamuγ amitan nigen bolur-a odqu">ᠬᠠᠮᠤᠭ ᠠᠮᠢᠲᠠᠨ ᠨᠢᠭᠡᠨ ᠪᠣᠯᠤᠷ ᠠ ᠣᠳᠬᠤ</uig> All living beings will become the same.
The verbal nouns are used with converbs :
<uig rom="abcu iregsen kümün">ᠠᠪᠴᠤ ᠢᠷᠡᠭᠰᠡᠨ ᠺᠦᠮᠦᠨ</uig> a man who has brought (lit., "a man who has come taking")
<uig rom="egürcü yabuqsan kümün">ᠡᠭᠦᠷᠴᠦ ᠶᠠᠪᠤᠬᠰᠠᠨ ᠺᠦᠮᠦᠨ</uig> a man who was carrying on his shoulders (lit., "a man who went carrying on his shoulders")
<uig rom="cinu noqai-yi qarbuju alaqu bi">ᠴᠢᠨᠤ ᠨᠣᠬᠠᠢ ᠶᠢ ᠬᠠᠷᠪᠤᠵᠤ ᠠᠯᠠᠬᠤ ᠪᠢ</uig> I shall shoot your dog. (Lit., "I shall kill shooting your dog.")

<uig rom="naran sar-a qoyar-i qamtu-bar jergecegülün oruγulun kigsen manglai caγan duγulγ-a-ban aca">ᠨᠠᠷᠠᠨ ᠰᠠᠷ ᠠ ᠬᠣᠶᠠᠷ ᠢ ᠬᠠᠮᠲᠤ ᠎ᠪᠠᠷ ᠵᠡᠷᠭᠡᠴᠡᠭᠦᠯᠦᠨ ᠣᠷᠤᠭᠤᠯᠤᠨ ᠺᠢᠭᠰᠡᠨ ᠮᠠᠩᠯᠠᠢ ᠴᠠᠭᠠᠨ ᠳᠤᠭᠤᠯᠭ ᠠ ᠎ᠪᠠᠨ ᠠᠴᠠ</uig> give your high white helmet made in such a manner that sun and moon were put in one beside the other!

Therefore, members of sentences can consist of a verbal noun preceded by one or more converbs. This makes the verbal nouns entirely different from deverbal nouns, i. e., nouns derived from verbs, as the latter are true nouns which can not be qualified by adverbs, whereas the verbal nouns possess all characteristics of both the nouns and verbs.
An important trait of the verbal nouns is that all of them, even verbal nouna of active verbs, funetion actively and passively.
<uig rom="yabuqsan kümün">ᠶᠠᠪᠤᠬᠰᠠᠨ ᠺᠦᠮᠦᠨ</uig> the man who has gone
<uig rom="yabuqsan jam">ᠶᠠᠪᠤᠬᠰᠠᠨ ᠵᠠᠮ</uig> the way someone has gone (lit., "the way gone")
<uig rom="miqa idegsen noqai">ᠮᠢᠬᠠ ᠢᠳᠡᠭᠰᠡᠨ ᠨᠣᠬᠠᠢ</uig> the dog which has eaten the meat
<uig rom="noqai-yin idegsen miqan">ᠨᠣᠬᠠᠢ ᠶᠢᠨ ᠢᠳᠡᠭᠰᠡᠨ ᠮᠢᠬᠠᠨ</uig> the meat eaten by the dog (lit., "the dog's. eaten meat")
<uig rom="namayi üjegsen kümün">ᠨᠠᠮᠠᠶᠢ ᠦᠵᠡᠭᠰᠡᠨ ᠺᠦᠮᠦᠨ</uig> the man who saw me
ᠮᠢᠨᠤ ᠦᠵᠡᠭᠰᠡᠨ ᠺᠦᠮᠦᠨ the man seen by me (lit., "my seen man")
Nomina verbalia of passive verbs occur often in the classical, but primarily in the pre-classical language.
<uig rom="taciyangγui-a endegüregüldegsen mungqaγ-ud">ᠲᠠᠴᠢᠶᠠᠩᠭᠤᠢ ᠠ ᠡᠨᠳᠡᠭᠦᠷᠡᠭᠦᠯᠳᠡᠭᠰᠡᠨ ᠮᠤᠩᠬᠠᠭ ᠤᠳ</uig> the fools misled by passion
<uig rom="nisvanis-ta abtaqsan amitan">ᠨᠢᠰᠸᠠᠨᠢᠰ ᠎ᠲᠠ ᠠᠪᠲᠠᠬᠰᠠᠨ ᠠᠮᠢᠲᠠᠨ</uig> the living beings obsessed by vanity
<uig rom="kücütü-de daruqdaqsan-u tulada">ᠺᠦᠴᠦᠲᠦ ᠳ᠋ᠡ ᠳᠠᠷᠤᠬᠳᠠᠬᠰᠠᠨ ᠤ ᠲᠤᠯᠠᠳᠠ</uig> because of being suppressed by a strong sensation

The converbs do not express any absolute time of action but only the circumstances under which the main action takes place. Therefore, there is no converb expressing present or past actions. The converbs cannot act as predicates of completed sentences, but they act as a part of the predicate and, used with verbal nouns, they act as components on any part of speech.

As to the time of the action of a converb, it depends upon the time of the finite verb. This means that the time of a converb is, when considered absolutely, the past, if the finite verb is in a past tense, or it is the present, if the finite verb is in the present tense.

The converbs express actions taking place either synchronically with the action of the finite verb or before the latter, actions regarded as a consequence of the action of the finite verb, actions supposed to be the aim of the action of the finite verb, and so on. An action synchronous with the action of the finite verb in the present tense is also a present, but an action synchronous with the action of the finite verb in a past tense refers, of course, to past time, if taken absolutely.
Certain converbs - the converba imperfecti, perfecti, and modalia - can act as predicates of a completed sentence if there is a copula:
<uig rom="dani-yin kümüs tariyalang-un ajil-i kijü bui">ᠳᠠᠨᠢ ᠶᠢᠨ ᠺᠦᠮᠦᠰ ᠲᠠᠷᠢᠶᠠᠯᠠᠩ ᠤᠨ ᠠᠵᠢᠯ ᠢ ᠺᠢᠵᠦ ᠪᠤᠢ</uig> The people of Denmark do agricultural work (lit., "are doing").
<uig rom="tere kümün bidan-i qaγurcu amui">ᠲᠡᠷᠡ ᠺᠦᠮᠦᠨ ᠪᠢᠳᠠᠨ ᠢ ᠬᠠᠭᠤᠷᠴᠤ ᠠᠮᠤᠢ</uig> That man deceives us.
<uig rom="bi tani mongγol kümün bolbauu gejü sanaju bülüge">ᠪᠢ ᠲᠠᠨᠢ ᠮᠣᠩᠭᠣᠯ ᠺᠦᠮᠦᠨ ᠪᠣᠯᠪᠠᠤᠤ ᠭᠡᠵᠦ ᠰᠠᠨᠠᠵᠤ ᠪᠦᠯᠦᠭᠡ</uig> I thought you were a Mongol.
<uig rom="nökör surγaγuli-dur oroγad bui">ᠨᠥᠺᠥᠷ ᠰᠤᠷᠭᠠᠭᠤᠯᠢ ᠳ᠋ᠤᠷ ᠣᠷᠣᠭᠠᠳ ᠪᠤᠢ</uig> The friend has already entered a school.
<uig rom="cerig jiqsaγad bayimui">ᠴᠡᠷᠢᠭ ᠵᠢᠬᠰᠠᠭᠠᠳ ᠪᠠᠶᠢᠮᠤᠢ</uig> The soldiers have formed into ranks.
The same converbs without a copula serve as predicates of incomplete, juxtaposed sentences within larger sentences.
<uig rom="γurban köbegün inu malaγa-ban abcu sögüdcü mörgübei">ᠭᠤᠷᠪᠠᠨ ᠺᠥᠪᠡᠭᠦᠨ ᠢᠨᠤ ᠮᠠᠯᠠᠭᠠ ᠎ᠪᠠᠨ ᠠᠪᠴᠤ ᠰᠥᠭᠦᠳᠴᠦ ᠮᠥᠷᠭᠦᠪᠡᠢ</uig> His three sons took off their caps, knelt down, and bowed.

<uig rom="senglün ebügen mal-iyan tuγuju arban oγoton-a egürcü nigen γar-taγan yisün salaγ-a-tu temür uruγa circü irebe">ᠰᠡᠩᠯᠦᠨ ᠡᠪᠦᠭᠡᠨ ᠮᠠᠯ ᠢᠶᠠᠨ ᠲᠤᠭᠤᠵᠤ ᠠᠷᠪᠠᠨ ᠣᠭᠣᠲᠣᠨ ᠠ ᠡᠭᠦᠷᠴᠦ ᠨᠢᠭᠡᠨ ᠭᠠᠷ ᠎ᠲᠠᠭᠠᠨ ᠶᠢᠰᠦᠨ ᠰᠠᠯᠠᠭ ᠠ ᠎ᠲᠤ ᠲᠡᠮᠦᠷ ᠤᠷᠤᠭᠠ ᠴᠢᠷᠴᠦ ᠢᠷᠡᠪᠡ</uig> Old man Senglun came, driving his cattle and carrying on his back ten oghotona (a rodent of the Lagomys family) and dragging with one hand an iron hook with nine prongs.
<uig rom="er-e kümün ger-tür törön keger-e ükükü">ᠡᠷ ᠡ ᠺᠦᠮᠦᠨ ᠭᠡᠷ ᠲᠤᠷ ᠲᠥᠷᠥᠨ ᠺᠡᠭᠡᠷ ᠡ ᠦᠺᠦᠺᠦ</uig> A man is born at home and dies in the steppe.
The converbum modale was once a verbal noun and was also used a.s an indicative form.

Its plural form has the ending -d which replaces the -n of the singular. Forms in -d occur in old documents of the pre-classical language. They were usually followed by the particle je, e. g., uqad je "will understand."
The remaining converbs express the cir cumstances under which the action of the finite verb takes place.

a) The converbum conditionale expresses, if the finite verb is in a past tense, the circumstances under which the main action takes place : "when. . ." ; if the main action is a present or a future, this converb expresses actions conditioning the main action: "if . . ."
b) The converbum concessivum expresses an action, which, although performed, does not have the desired result: "although . . ."
c) The converbum terminale expresses an action regarded as a temporal limit or result of the main action: "till . . .," "unto . . .," "so that..."
d) The converbum abtemporale expresses an action since the inception of which that of the finite verb takes place: "since . . ."
e) The converbum contemporale expresses an aetion which is immediately followed by the main action: "scarcely had he done that, when. . ."
See also §375

The converba imperfecti, modale, and perfecti can be used with verbal nouns. The latter can serve as any part of speech and, therefore, those converbs can act as components of compound parts of sentences : as a component of a subject, object, attribute, predicate. Thus <uig rom="niscü yabuqu">ᠨᠢᠰᠴᠦ ᠶᠠᠪᠤᠬᠤ:</uig> :
as a subject: flying, flight (Lit., "the going in flying")
as an object: id.
as an attribute : flying
as a predicate: He will fly. (Lit., "He will go in flying.")

Since certain converbs, as remarked above, express the circumstances under which the action of the predicate takes place, some of them have lost their original meanings and are now used as postpositions corresponding to the English prepositions :
<uig rom="boltala">ᠪᠣᠯᠲᠠᠯᠠ</uig> until (lit., "until he becomes," <uig rom="bol-">ᠪᠣᠯ ᠎</uig> to become)
<uig rom="kürtele">ᠺᠦᠷᠲᠡᠯᠡ</uig> till (lit., "until he reaches," <uig rom="kür-">ᠺᠦᠷ ᠎</uig> to reach)
Other converbs have become conjunctions:
<uig rom="bolun">ᠪᠣᠯᠤᠨ</uig> and (lit., "becoming," <uig rom="bol-">ᠪᠣᠯ ᠎</uig> to become)
<uig rom="büged">ᠪᠦᠭᠡᠳ</uig> and (lit., "having been,"<uig rom="bü-">ᠪᠦ ᠎</uig> to be)
<uig rom="kiged">ᠺᠢᠭᠡᠳ</uig> and (lit., "having done," <uig rom="ki-">ᠺᠢ ᠎</uig> to do)
The converbum modale of the verb ᠭᠡᠮᠡ ᠎ geme- or keme- "to say," ᠭᠡᠮᠡᠨ or kemen "saying," is used as the conjunction "that" :
<uig rom="iremüi gemen ögülebei">ᠢᠷᠡᠮᠦᠢ ᠭᠡᠮᠡᠨ ᠥᠭᠦᠯᠡᠪᠡᠢ</uig> "He said that he would come." (Lit., "He spoke, saying: `I shall come."' )

The converbs of the pronominal verb <uig rom="yaγaki-">ᠶᠠᠭᠠᠺᠢ ᠎</uig> "to do what?" and the fossilized converbs <uig rom="eyin">ᠡᠶᠢᠨ</uig> "doing in this manner," <uig rom="teyin">ᠲᠡᠶᠢᠨ</uig> "doing in that manner" are used as adverbs "how," "why," "so."
<uig rom="ci yaγakin irebei">ᠴᠢ ᠶᠠᠭᠠᠺᠢᠨ ᠢᠷᠡᠪᠡᠢ</uig> Why did you come? (Lit., "What doing didst thou come?")
<uig rom="eyin ögülebei">ᠡᠶᠢᠨ ᠥᠭᠦᠯᠡᠪᠡᠢ</uig> He said so. (Lit., "He said doing in this manner.")
The postpositions function in the same manner as prepositions in European languages. They follow the word they govern. Most of them are of nominal origin.

The postpositions govern various cases, but primarily the genitive case. Some of them govern the simple stem of the noun, e. g., <uig rom="γajar door-a">ᠭᠠᠵᠠᠷ ᠳᠣᠣᠷ᠎ᠠ</uig> "under the earth." The postpositions will be discussed in connection with the use of the case forms. (See §§ 503, 510, 530.) Here only one particular characteristic of the postpositions will be discussed.
Many postpositions can be accompanied by a personal pronoun in the genitive. This indicates the possessor of the object designated by the word governed by the postposition:
<uig rom="ger dergede">ᠭᠡᠷ ᠳᠡᠷᠭᠡᠳᠡ</uig> inu by his house
Sometimes the genitive forms <uig rom="inu">ᠢᠨᠤ</uig> and <uig rom="anu">ᠠᠨᠤ</uig> are only pleonastic elements:
<uig rom="tegün-ü ger dergede inu">ᠲᠡᠭᠦᠨ ᠤ ᠭᠡᠷ ᠳᠡᠷᠭᠡᠳᠡ ᠢᠨᠤ</uig> by his house (lit., "by his house his")
