<uig rom="ed-iyen quriyan abuγsan kümün">ᠡᠳ ᠢᠶᠡᠨ ᠬᠤᠷᠢᠶᠠᠨ ᠠᠪᠤᠭᠰᠠᠨ ᠺᠦᠮᠦᠨ</uig> a person who confiscated his own property (from the point of view of logic this sentence, of course, does not make any sense).

The passive also expresses the idea of the necessity to act. This is the case of the future noun (nomen futuri) with the ending <uig rom="-qui"> ᠎ᠬᠤᠢ</uig> (only this and never <uig rom="-qu"> ᠎ᠬᠤ</uig> ) of the passive verb.
<uig rom="tere inu eyin uqaγdaqui">ᠲᠡᠷᠡ ᠢᠨᠤ ᠡᠶᠢᠨ ᠤᠬᠠᠭᠳᠠᠬᠤᠢ</uig> That is to be understood in this manner.
ᠠᠮᠢᠲᠠᠨ ᠪᠦᠭᠦᠳᠡ ᠪᠤᠶᠠᠨ ᠺᠢᠭᠳᠡᠺᠦᠨ (plural of kigdeküi) All living beings must exercise virtue.
The passive voice also expresses actions caused by a subject unknown or unmentioned in the sentence.
<uig rom="ceceg-ün qur-a oroγuluγdaba">ᠴᠡᠴᠡᠭ ᠤᠨ ᠬᠤᠷ ᠠ ᠣᠷᠣᠭᠤᠯᠤᠭᠳᠠᠪᠠ</uig> A rain of flowers was rained down.

In this sentence the verb <uig rom="oroγuluγda-">ᠣᠷᠣᠭᠤᠯᠤᠬᠳᠠ ᠎</uig> is a passive of the factitive <uig rom="oroγul-">ᠣᠷᠣᠭᠤᠯ</uig> "to cause to rain" which is derived from <uig rom="oro-">ᠣᠷᠣ ᠎</uig> "to rain." Therefore, the literal translation should be "a rain of flowers was caused to rain." The rain was sent by someone who was, of course, a god or a ghost.

The factitive expresses the idea of causing an action. There are many verbs which cannot govern a direct object, e. g. <uig rom="ükü-">ᠦᠺᠦ ᠎</uig> "to die" or <uig rom="kebte-">ᠺᠡᠪᠲᠡ ᠎</uig> "to lie down." Yet the factitive of such verbs governs the accusative.
<uig rom="tegün-i ükügülbe">ᠲᠡᠭᠦᠨ ᠢ ᠦᠺᠦᠭᠦᠯᠪᠡ</uig> He let him (or caused him to) die.
<uig rom="tegün-i kebtegülbe">ᠲᠡᠭᠦᠨ ᠢ ᠺᠡᠪᠲᠡᠭᠦᠯᠪᠡ</uig> He let him lie, or He laid him.

Verbs which are intransitive become transitive when put in the factitive. This means that the factitive of such verbs does not express the idea of ordering to or letting act, but the idea of actions such as "to send," "to lay," "to raise," and so on, although in literal translation such factitive verbs mean "to let go," "to let lie," "to let rise," and so on.

<tbl>Intransitive|Transitive;;
<uig rom="oro-">ᠣᠷᠣ ᠎</uig>  to enter, to go in|<uig rom="oroγul-">ᠣᠷᠣᠭᠤᠯ ᠎</uig>  to let in, to lead in;;
<uig rom="yabu-">ᠶᠠᠪᠤ ᠎</uig>  to walk, to go|<uig rom="yabuγul-">ᠶᠠᠪᠤᠭᠤᠯ ᠎</uig>  to send;;
<uig rom="saγu-">ᠰᠠᠭᠤ ᠎</uig>  to sit down|<uig rom="saγulγa-">ᠰᠠᠭᠶᠤᠯᠭᠠ ᠎</uig>  to set, to plant;;
<uig rom="bayi-">ᠪᠠᠶᠢ ᠎</uig>  to stand, to be|<uig rom="bayiγul-">ᠪᠠᠶᠢᠭᠤᠯ ᠎</uig>  to found;;
<uig rom=" bol-">ᠪᠣᠯ ᠎</uig> to become|<uig rom="bolγa-">ᠪᠣᠯᠭᠠ ᠎</uig>  to do, to make;;
<uig rom="γar-">ᠭᠠᠷ ᠎</uig>  to go out|<uig rom="γarγa-">ᠭᠠᠷᠭᠠ ᠎</uig>  to take out, to lead out</tbl>
The factitive of an intransitive verb has only one direct object.
<uig rom="bi teqün-i oroγulba">ᠪᠢ ᠲᠡᠬᠦᠨ ᠢ ᠣᠷᠣᠭᠤᠯᠪᠠ</uig> I let him in.
<uig rom="mangγus tegün-i ükügülbe">ᠮᠠᠩᠭᠤᠰ ᠲᠡᠭᠦᠨ ᠢ ᠦᠺᠦᠭᠦᠯᠪᠡ</uig> Mangus killed him. (Lit., "Let him die.")
The factitive of transitive verbs has two direct objects: one expressing the person ordered to act and another expressing the object of the latter's action.
<uig rom="bi tegün-i nom ungsiγulba">ᠪᠢ ᠲᠡᠭᠦᠨ ᠢ ᠨᠣᠮ ᠤᠩᠰᠢᠭᠤᠯᠪᠠ</uig> I Jet him read a book.
<uig rom="qaγan inu tüsimel-i cerig-iyen abcu iregülbe">ᠬᠠᠭᠠᠨ ᠢᠨᠤ ᠲᠦᠰᠢᠮᠡᠯ ᠢ ᠴᠡᠷᠢᠭ ᠢᠶᠡᠨ ᠠᠪᠴᠤ ᠢᠷᠡᠭᠦᠯᠪᠡ</uig> The khaghan let the minister bring his army.

The person performing the action of a transitive verb in the factitive can also be expressed by a dative-locative. In such cases the factitive has a slightly different meaning. In such constructions the factitive does not express an order but, on the contrary, the idea of the helplessness of the grammatical subject to prevent the action. Thus, in the sentence <uig rom="bi tegün-i nom ungsiγulba">ᠪᠢ ᠲᠡᠭᠦᠨ ᠢ ᠨᠣᠮ ᠤᠩᠰᠢᠭᠤᠯᠪᠠ</uig> "I let him read a book," it was I who purposely let or ordered him to read, but, if we replace the accusative <uig rom="tegün-i">ᠲᠡᠭᠦᠨ ᠢ</uig> with the dative-locative, I become not the person who ordered him to read but the person who could not help letting him read. This can be illustrated by the following examples:
<uig rom="bi noqai-yi miqa idegülbe">ᠪᠢ ᠨᠣᠬᠠᠢ ᠶᠢ ᠮᠢᠬᠠ ᠢᠳᠡᠭᠦᠯᠪᠡ</uig> I let the dog eat meat (i. e., I purposely gave the dog meat).

<uig rom="bi miqan-i noqai-dur idegülbe">ᠪᠢ ᠮᠢᠬᠠᠨ ᠢ ᠨᠣᠬᠠᠢ ᠳ᠋ᠤᠷ ᠢᠳᠡᠭᠦᠯᠪᠡ</uig> I could not help letting the dog eat the meat (i. e., I did not give it to the dog but the dog itself took it and I was unable to prevent it from doing so).

Reciprocal verbs express mutual actions. Therefore, a reciprocal verb presumes at least two persons acting. The latter are expressed in the subjects or in the subject and the indirect object. The latter is, in such cases, a comitative.
<uig rom="qoyar quca mörgüldübe">ᠬᠣᠶᠠᠷ ᠬᠤᠴᠠ ᠮᠥᠷᠭᠦᠯᠳᠦᠪᠡ</uig> Two rams butt each other.
<uig rom="baγatur inu tere dayisun-luγ-a barilduba">ᠪᠠᠭᠠᠲᠤᠷ ᠢᠨᠤ ᠲᠡᠷᠡ ᠳᠠᠶᠢᠰᠤᠨ ᠯᠤᠭ ᠠ ᠪᠠᠷᠢᠯᠳᠤᠪᠠ</uig> The hero wrestled with that foe.

It is obvious that transitive verbs may occur in the reciprocal form, since logically each of the persons acting is an object of the action of the other person acting. Yet even intransitive verbs sometimes occur in this form, principally in the language of popular books. These do not express the idea of a reciprocal action, but the idea of an action performed in a co-operative manner.
<uig rom="tedener ebdereldübe">ᠲᠡᠳᠡᠨᠡᠷ ᠡᠪᠳᠡᠷᠡᠯᠳᠦᠪᠡ</uig> They quarreled: <uig rom="ebdereldü-">ᠡᠪᠳᠡᠷᠡᠯᠳᠦ</uig> , reciprocal of <uig rom="ebdere-">ᠡᠪᠳᠡᠷᠡ ᠎</uig> to fall to pieces

This explains the origin of many formally reciprocal verbs, such as <uig rom="bayildu-">ᠪᠠᠶᠢᠯᠳᠤ ᠎</uig> "to struggle, to make war" from <uig rom="bayi-">ᠪᠠᠶᠢ ᠎</uig> "to stand" (originally <uig rom="bayildu-">ᠪᠠᠶᠢᠯᠳᠤ ᠎</uig> meant "to stand against each other"), <uig rom="kereldü-">ᠺᠡᠷᠡᠯᠳᠦ ᠎</uig> "to quarrel" from a no longer extant verb *kere-, etc.
Co-operative verbs express the idea of participation in the actiona concerned. These verbs may be derived both from transitive and intransitive stems.
<uig rom="cai uγulcamui">ᠴᠠᠢ ᠤᠭᠤᠯᠴᠠᠮᠤᠢ</uig> He drinks tea (with other people).
<uig rom="sabi-nar ungsilcamui">ᠰᠠᠪᠢ ᠎ᠨᠠᠷ ᠤᠩᠰᠢᠯᠴᠠᠮᠤᠢ</uig> The pupils are reading together.
Many co-operative verbs lost their immediate connection with the meaning of the primary stem and became new words.
<uig rom="saγulca-">ᠰᠠᠭᠤᠯᠴᠠ ᠎</uig> to be present (at a meeting, lit., "to sit with others" - <uig rom="saγu-">ᠰᠠᠭᠤ ᠎</uig> to sit)

entry.title: Syntax - Genera verbi - Accumulation of voice suffixes
entry.title2: Genera verbi - Accumulation of voice suffixes

paragraphs.paragraph: A verbal stem may take more than one mark of voice: a reciprocal verb may take the suffix of a factitive, a passive may take the same factitive suffix, and so on.
<uig rom="barilduγul-">ᠪᠠᠷᠢᠯᠳᠤᠭᠤᠯ ᠎</uig> to let wrestle
<uig rom="idegdegül-">ᠢᠳᠡᠭᠳᠡᠭᠦᠯ ᠎</uig> to let be eaten
<uig rom="idelcegül-">ᠢᠳᠡᠯᠴᠡᠭᠦᠯ ᠎</uig> to let participate in eating
<uig rom="bayiγuluγda-">ᠪᠠᠶᠢᠭᠤᠯᠤᠬᠳᠠ ᠎ᠲᠣ</uig> to be founded
<uig rom="idegdegülügde">ᠢᠳᠡᠭᠳᠡᠭᠦᠯᠦᠭᠳᠡ ᠎</uig> - to be let be eaten
<uig rom="yabuγuluγda-">ᠶᠠᠪᠤᠭᠤᠯᠤᠬᠳᠠ ᠎</uig> to be sent
<uig rom="barilcaγul-">ᠪᠠᠷᠢᠯᠴᠠᠭᠤᠯ ᠎</uig> to let participate in catching
There are two kinds of interrogative sentences:
1. that in which the interrogation refers to the whole sentence (e. g., "Will our teacher come?") and
2. that in which the interrogation refers only to a single word (e. g., "When will he come?").

Sentences of the former category are interrogative sentences in general, and those of the latter category are sentences containing special interrogative words. The predicate in interrogative sentences is either a nominal or a verbal one. The latter is in an indicative form.

entry.title: Syntax - Interrogative sentences - Sentence generally interrogative

paragraphs.paragraph: The predicate of such sentences always takes the interrogative particle <uig rom="uu">ᠤᠤ</uig> . The latter is on the copula, or, in a predicate without a copula, on the predicative word.

entry.title: Syntax - Interrogative sentences - Sentence generally interrogative
entry.title2: Interrogative sentences - Sentence generally interrogative - Nominal predicate

paragraphs.paragraph: The predicate has a copula which may be omitted.
<uig rom="ta sayin bayimui uu">ᠲᠠ ᠰᠠᠶᠢᠨ ᠪᠠᠶᠢᠮᠤᠢ ᠤᠤ</uig> or <uig rom="ta sayin uu">ᠲᠠ ᠰᠠᠶᠢᠨ ᠤᠤ</uig> How are you? (Lit., "Are you well?")

entry.title: Syntax - Interrogative sentences - Sentence generally interrogative
entry.title2: Interrogative sentences - Sentence generally interrogative - Verbal predicate

paragraphs.paragraph: The verbal predicate in sentences generally interrogative takes the interrogative particle <uig rom="uu">ᠤᠤ</uig> .
<uig rom="bi cimadur ese kelelüü">ᠪᠢ ᠴᠢᠮᠠᠳᠤᠷ ᠡᠰᠡ ᠺᠡᠯᠡᠯᠦᠦ</uig> Did I not tell you?
<uig rom="ta mongγol kele medemüü">ᠲᠠ ᠮᠣᠩᠭᠣᠯ ᠺᠡᠯᠡ ᠮᠡᠳᠡᠮᠦᠦ</uig> Do you know Mongolian?

entry.title: Syntax - Interrogative sentences - Sentence generally interrogative
entry.title2: Interrogative sentences - Sentence generally interrogative - Converbal predicate

paragraphs.paragraph: In converbal predicates it is the copula which takes the interrogative particle.
<uig rom="ta sayin yabuju bayimui uu">ᠲᠠ ᠰᠠᠶᠢᠨ ᠶᠠᠪᠤᠵᠤ ᠪᠠᠶᠢᠮᠤᠢ ᠤᠤ</uig> Are you travelling well? (i, e., "Do you have a good journey?")

entry.title: Syntax - Interrogative sentences - Sentence with interrogative word
entry.title2: Interrogative sentences - Sentence with interrogative word

paragraphs.paragraph: Sentences partly interrogative contain interrogative words, such as "who," "when," "where," and so on. The latter are either pronouns, adverbs, or interrogative verbs (e. g., <uig rom="yaγaki-">ᠶᠠᠭᠠᠺᠢ ᠎</uig> "to do what?").
In such sentences the predicate does not take an interrogative particle.

entry.title: Syntax - Interrogative sentences - Sentence with interrogative word
entry.title2: Interrogative sentences - Sentence with interrogative word - Nominal predicate

paragraphs.paragraph: The nominal predicate of a sentence containing an interrogative word usually occurs with the copula bui.
<uig rom="ci qamiγ-a-aca iregsen bui">ᠴᠢ ᠬᠠᠮᠢᠭ ᠠ ᠡᠴᠡ ᠢᠷᠡᠭᠰᠡᠨ ᠪᠤᠢ</uig> From where did you come?
<uig rom="ci ken qaγan-u albatu bui">ᠴᠢ ᠺᠡᠨ ᠬᠠᠭᠠᠨ ᠤ ᠠᠯᠪᠠᠲᠤ ᠪᠤᠢ</uig> What khaghan's subject are you?
<uig rom="ci yaγun abqu bui">ᠴᠢ ᠶᠠᠭᠤᠨ ᠠᠪᠬᠤ ᠪᠤᠢ</uig> What will you take?
<uig rom="ta kejiy-e iregsen bui">ᠲᠠ ᠺᠡᠵᠢᠶ ᠡ ᠢᠷᠡᠭᠰᠡᠨ ᠪᠤᠢ</uig> When did you come?

entry.title: Syntax - Interrogative sentences - Sentence with interrogative word
entry.title2: Interrogative sentences - Sentence with interrogative word - Verbal predicate

paragraphs.paragraph: The verbal predicate of a sentence containing an interrogative word does not take an interrogative particle. It does not differ in its form from the predicate of a simple statement.
<uig rom="ci qamiγ-a-aca irebei">ᠴᠢ ᠬᠠᠮᠢᠭ ᠠ ᠡᠴᠡ ᠢᠷᠡᠪᠡᠢ</uig> From where did you come?
<uig rom="ci yaγun abumui">ᠴᠢ ᠶᠠᠭᠤᠨ ᠠᠪᠤᠮᠤᠢ</uig> What will you take?
<uig rom="bi yaγakimui">ᠪᠢ ᠶᠠᠭᠠᠺᠢᠮᠤᠢ</uig> What am I to do?

entry.title: Syntax - Interrogative sentences - Sentence with interrogative word
entry.title2: Interrogative sentences - Sentence with interrogative word - Converbal predicate

paragraphs.paragraph: The converbal predicate of a sentence partly interrogative (i. e., containing an interrogative word) has a copula which is a finite form either of an auxiliary verb or of a descriptive verb.
<uig rom="tere kümün qamiγ-a saγuju amui">ᠲᠡᠷᠡ ᠺᠦᠮᠦᠨ ᠬᠠᠮᠢᠭ ᠠ ᠰᠠᠭᠤᠵᠤ ᠠᠮᠤᠢ</uig> Where does that person live?
<uig rom="yambar sibaγun niscü irebei">ᠶᠠᠮᠪᠠᠷ ᠰᠢᠪᠠᠭᠤᠨ ᠨᠢᠰᠴᠦ ᠢᠷᠡᠪᠡᠢ</uig> What bird flew here?

A question may be a real one, asked to get necessary information, but it may also be a rhetorical one. Such rhetorical questions, in reality, are not questions at all, but affirmative statements only made in the form of a question. Such sentences are more or less the same as such English sentences as "Certainly, you know. Do you not?" in which the question implies that the person speaking does not doubt that the interlocutor knows what the situation is.
In such sentences the colloquial bisi or the Written Mongolian busu with the interrogative particle uu is used.
<uig rom="ci minu ekener bisüü">ᠴᠢ ᠮᠢᠨᠤ ᠡᠺᠡᠨᠡᠷ ᠪᠢᠰᠦᠦ</uig> (or <uig rom="bisiuu">ᠪᠢᠰᠢᠤᠤ</uig>) Are you not my wife?
<uig rom="cinggis qaγan minu ejen busu uu">ᠴᠢᠩᠭᠢᠰ ᠬᠠᠭᠠᠨ ᠮᠢᠨᠤ ᠡᠵᠡᠨ ᠪᠤᠰᠤ ᠤᠤ</uig> Is not Chingis Khaghan my master ?

entry.title: Syntax - Interrogative sentences - Disjunctive interrogative sentence

paragraphs.paragraph: Disjunctive interrogative sentences contain a double interrogation. Such sentences suppose an alternative, e. g., "Will you take this or that?". The disjunctive interrogative sentences consist of two juxtaposed interrogative sentences and each of them has a separate predicate of its own. Conjunctions are not used, except for a construction which may pass as one containing a conjunction (see §630).
<uig rom="ci abumui uu bi abumui uu">ᠴᠢ ᠠᠪᠤᠮᠤᠢ ᠤᠤ ᠪᠢ ᠠᠪᠤᠮᠤᠢ ᠤᠤ</uig> Will you take or shall I take? (Lit., "Will you take? Shall I take?")
<uig rom="ende bayimuu tende bayimuu">ᠡᠨᠳᠡ ᠪᠠᠶᠢᠮᠤᠤ ᠲᠡᠨᠳᠡ ᠪᠠᠶᠢᠮᠤᠤ</uig> Is it here or is it there? (Lit., "Is it here ? Is it there ? ")

entry.title: Syntax - Interrogative sentences - Disjunctive interrogative sentence

paragraphs.paragraph: The second of the juxtaposed interrogative sentences mentioned in § 629 may begin with the negative <uig rom="esebesü">ᠡᠰᠡᠪᠡᠰᠦ</uig> which is in origin a conditional converb of the negative verb *ese- "not to be" (see § 638).
<uig rom="geser amidu buyu esebesü ükügsen buyu">ᠭᠡᠰᠡᠷ ᠠᠮᠢᠳᠤ ᠪᠤᠶᠤ ᠡᠰᠡᠪᠡᠰᠦ ᠦᠺᠦᠭᠰᠡᠨ ᠪᠤᠶᠤ</uig> Is Geser alive or has he died? (Lit., "Is Geser alive? If not, has he died?")
Nouns and verbs take different negatives. The negatives with nouns are <uig rom="ügei">ᠦᠭᠡᠢ</uig> and <uig rom="busu">ᠪᠤᠰᠤ</uig> .
The word <uig rom="ügei">ᠦᠭᠡᠢ</uig> is a noun and may be declined. Its primary meaning is "absence."
Since all nouns may act as a predicate, the negative <uig rom="ügei">ᠦᠭᠡᠢ</uig> , too, may serve as a predicate, with or without the copula.
<uig rom="ende usun ügei">ᠡᠨᠳᠡ ᠤᠰᠤᠨ ᠦᠭᠡᠢ</uig> There is no water here.
<uig rom="nadur mönggün ügei">ᠨᠠᠳᠤᠷ ᠮᠥᠩᠭᠦᠨ ᠦᠭᠡᠢ</uig> bui I have no money.
A noun followed by <uig rom="ügei">ᠦᠭᠡᠢ</uig> expresses the same as English nouns ending in -less.
<uig rom="usu ügei γajar">ᠤᠰᠤ ᠦᠭᠡᠢ ᠭᠠᠵᠠᠷ</uig> a waterless country
<uig rom="mal ügei yadaγu kümün">ᠮᠠᠯ ᠦᠭᠡᠢ ᠶᠠᠳᠠᠭᠤ ᠺᠦᠮᠦᠨ</uig> a poor man having no cattle
The negative <uig rom="ügei">ᠦᠭᠡᠢ</uig> occurs with the verbal nouns and serves as the negative "not."
<uig rom="suruγsan inu dalai suruγ-a ügei inu balai">ᠰᠤᠷᠤᠬᠰᠠᠨ ᠢᠨᠤ ᠳᠠᠯᠠᠢ ᠰᠤᠷᠤᠭ ᠠ ᠦᠭᠡᠢ ᠢᠨᠤ ᠪᠠᠯᠠᠢ</uig> One who has studied is an ocean; one who has not studied is blind.
<uig rom="manu baγsi iregsen ügei">ᠮᠠᠨᠤ ᠪᠠᠭᠰᠢ ᠢᠷᠡᠭᠰᠡᠨ ᠦᠭᠡᠢ</uig> (or <uig rom="manu baγsi iregsen ügei amui">ᠮᠠᠨᠤ ᠪᠠᠭᠰᠢ ᠢᠷᠡᠭᠰᠡᠨ ᠦᠭᠡᠢ ᠠᠮᠤᠢ</uig>) Our teacher did not come.
The negative <uig rom="ügei">ᠦᠭᠡᠢ</uig> referring to a pair of words means the same as the English "as well ... and. . ."
<uig rom="jun ebül ügei">ᠵᠤᠨ ᠡᠪᠦᠯ ᠦᠭᠡᠢ</uig> summer and winter
<uig rom="edür söni ügei yabuba">ᠡᠳᠦᠷ ᠰᠥᠨᠢ ᠦᠭᠡᠢ ᠶᠠᠪᠤᠪᠠ</uig> He went day and night.

While the negative <uig rom="ügei">ᠦᠭᠡᠢ</uig> expresses the mere idea of absence or nonexistence of something, the negative <uig rom="busu">ᠪᠤᠰᠤ</uig> indicates that the object concerned, although existing or present, is not what it is believed to be. In other words, this is the same as the English "not ... but . . ."
The negative <uig rom="busu">ᠪᠤᠰᠤ</uig> is, in origin, a pronoun meaning "another."
<uig rom="modun busu">ᠮᠣᠳᠤᠨ ᠪᠤᠰᠤ</uig> not a tree but ...
<uig rom="ene bolbasu jiγasun busu bui">ᠡᠨᠡ ᠪᠣᠯᠪᠠᠰᠤ ᠵᠢᠭᠠᠰᠤᠨ ᠪᠤᠰᠤ ᠪᠤᠢ</uig> This is not a fish.
The negative <uig rom="ese">ᠡᠰᠡ</uig> is used only with verbs. It is placed before the verb.
This negative is used with all indicative forms, with the so-called nomen perfecti, converbum conditionale, and converbum concessivum.
<uig rom="manu baqsi ese irebe">ᠮᠠᠨᠤ ᠪᠠᠬᠰᠢ ᠡᠰᠡ ᠢᠷᠡᠪᠡ</uig> Our teacher did not come.
<uig rom="ese iregsen kümün">ᠡᠰᠡ ᠢᠷᠡᠭᠰᠡᠨ ᠺᠦᠮᠦᠨ</uig> a person who did not come
<uig rom="ta ese irebesü">ᠲᠠ ᠡᠰᠡ ᠢᠷᠡᠪᠡᠰᠦ</uig> if you will not come
<uig rom="ese irebecü">ᠡᠰᠡ ᠢᠷᠡᠪᠡᠴᠦ</uig> although he will not come
The negative <uig rom="ese">ᠡᠰᠡ</uig> is a fossilized verb and a few forms still exist. Its forms are used as adverbs such as the English "nevertheless," "otherwise," and so on.
Nomen futuri <uig rom="esekü">ᠡᠰᠡᠺᠦ</uig> or not (referring to future actions) : <uig rom="yabuqu esekü">ᠶᠠᠪᠤᠬᠤ ᠡᠰᠡᠺᠦ</uig> to go or not

Nomen perfecti <uig rom="esegsen">ᠡᠰᠡᠭᠰᠡᠨ</uig> or not (referring to past actions) : <uig rom="iregsen esegsen-i ülü medemüi">ᠢᠷᠡᠭᠰᠡᠨ ᠡᠰᠡᠭᠰᠡᠨ ᠢ ᠦᠯᠦ ᠮᠡᠳᠡᠮᠦᠢ</uig> It is unknown whether he came or not. (Lit., "One does not known the coming or not.")
Past tense <uig rom="esebe">ᠡᠰᠡᠪᠡ</uig> or not: <uig rom="ükübeüü esebeüü">ᠦᠺᠦᠪᠡᠦᠦ ᠡᠰᠡᠪᠡᠦᠦ</uig> Did he die or did he not?
Converbum conditionale <uig rom="esebesü">ᠡᠰᠡᠪᠡᠰᠦ</uig> if not, otherwise: <uig rom="esebesü bi absuγai">ᠡᠰᠡᠪᠡᠰᠦ ᠪᠢ ᠠᠪᠰᠤᠭᠠᠢ</uig> Otherwise I shall take (it).

Converbum successivum <uig rom="eseküle">ᠡᠰᠡᠺᠦᠯᠡ</uig> otherwise: <uig rom="eseküle ene jorilγ-a-yi güicedkejü bolqu ügei">ᠡᠰᠡᠺᠦᠯᠡ ᠡᠨᠡ ᠵᠣᠷᠢᠯᠭ ᠠ ᠶᠢ ᠭᠦᠢᠴᠡᠳᠺᠡᠵᠦ ᠪᠣᠯᠬᠤ ᠦᠭᠡᠢ</uig> Otherwise it will not be possible to achieve this aim.

Converbum concessivum <uig rom="esebecü">ᠡᠰᠡᠪᠡᠴᠦ</uig> in spite of, nevertheless : <uig rom="esebecü bi abciramui">ᠡᠰᠡᠪᠡᠴᠦ ᠪᠢ ᠠᠪᠴᠢᠷᠠᠮᠤᠢ</uig> And even so, I shall bring (it), or Nevertheleas, I shall bring (it).
The negative <uig rom="ülü">ᠦᠯᠦ</uig> is used with verbal forms and also is placed before the latter.
It occurs with all indicative forms, with the verbal nouns of the future and the actor (nomen futuri, nomen actoris), and with all converbs except for the converbum conditionale and concessivum.
<<uig rom="sabi ülü medemüi">ᠰᠠᠪᠢ ᠦᠯᠦ ᠮᠡᠳᠡᠮᠦᠢ</uig> The pupil does not know.
<uig rom="ülü irekü cinu yaγun bui">ᠦᠯᠦ ᠢᠷᠡᠺᠦ ᠴᠢᠨᠤ ᠶᠠᠭᠤᠨ ᠪᠤᠢ</uig> What does your not coming mean?
<uig rom="medejü">ᠮᠡᠳᠡᠵᠦ</uig> not knowing

There are two prohibitive particles: <uig rom="buu">ᠪᠤᠤ</uig> and <uig rom="bitegei">ᠪᠢᠲᠡᠭᠡᠢ</uig> . The latter is a colloquial form. Both are used with imperative and optative forms and with the dubitative.
These particles are placed before the verbal forms concerned.
<uig rom="buu ire">ᠪᠤᠤ ᠢᠷᠡ</uig> Do not come!
<uig rom="buu iretügei">ᠪᠤᠤ ᠢᠷᠡᠲᠦᠭᠡᠢ</uig> He must not come!
<uig rom="buu medegesei">ᠪᠤᠤ ᠮᠡᠳᠡᠭᠡᠰᠡᠢ</uig> Ah, if he did not know!

The predicate of a completed sentence is a finite verb and the person acting is expressed by the subject, which is a nominative. A sentence may relate to another sentence in the same manner as a single word relates to the rest of the sentence: a sentence may serve as a subject of the whole, as an object, and so on. In such cases a sentence becomes a nominal construction which is nothing other than an enlarged member of a sentence.

Thus, instead of a simple subject expressed by a single word, a sentence may have a subject expressed by a group of words, e. g., instead of "The premature death of our friend caused grief among us" there may be "What our teacher had told us about the premature death of our friend caused grief among us," where "What our teacher had told us about the premature death of our friend" is an enlarged subject of the whole.

A sentence, to become a nominal construction, loses its predicate and replaces it with a verbal noun (nomen verbale). The latter takes all the suffixes of that member of the sentence of which it has to play the role. This means that the verbal noun is followed by the designator of the subject (e. g., <uig rom="inu">ᠢᠨᠤ</uig> , <uig rom="anu">ᠠᠨᠤ</uig> , <uig rom="bolbasu">ᠪᠣᠯᠪᠠᠰᠤ</uig> , and so on), if it has to serve as subject of the whole, or it takes the ending of the appropriate oblique case, if it has to serve as an object, and so on.

Such a nominal construction has neither a grammatical predicate nor a grammatical subject. Therefore, these terms (subject, predicate) will be avoided. Instead, the terms "action" and "actor" will be used.

In such nominal constructions the actor is expressed by a genitive (genitivus actoris) or a nominative. The action is expressed by a verbal noun which has all the grammatical characteristics of a grammatical subject: it is a nominative and is followed by a subject designator.
<uig rom="tere kümün-ü kelegsen inu ünen bui">ᠲᠡᠷᠡ ᠺᠦᠮᠦᠨ ᠤ ᠺᠡᠯᠡᠭᠰᠡᠨ ᠢᠨᠤ ᠦᠨᠡᠨ ᠪᠤᠢ</uig> What that man said is true.

<uig rom="mongγol yasutan-u uγ ijaγur-un tuqai bicigsen inu edüge udal ügei neyitelegden γarumui">ᠮᠣᠩᠭᠣᠯ ᠶᠠᠰᠤᠲᠠᠨ ᠤ ᠤᠭ ᠢᠵᠠᠭᠤᠷ ᠤᠨ ᠲᠤᠬᠠᠢ ᠪᠢᠴᠢᠭᠰᠡᠨ ᠢᠨᠤ ᠡᠳᠦᠭᠡ ᠤᠳᠠᠯ ᠦᠭᠡᠢ ᠨᠡᠶᠢᠲᠡᠯᠡᠭᠳᠡᠨ ᠭᠠᠷᠤᠮᠤᠢ</uig> What was written about the origin of the Mongol tribes will be published soon.

A special case is a nominal construction of which the actor is expressed by an interrogative pronoun. Such constructions, seen from the point of view of their meaning, correspond to relative subordinate sentences of the European languages.
<uig rom="tegün-i ken deyilügsen inu abumui">ᠲᠡᠭᠦᠨ ᠢ ᠺᠡᠨ ᠳᠡᠶᠢᠯᠦᠭᠰᠡᠨ ᠢᠨᠤ ᠠᠪᠤᠮᠤᠢ</uig> He who has vanquished will take it.
Nominal constructions serving as attributes consist of a verbal noun (with an object, attribute, etc.). The verbal noun is a nominative. The actor is expressed by a genitive (genitivus actoris).
<uig rom="bi tegün-ü jokiyan bicigsen nom ungsimui">ᠪᠢ ᠲᠡᠭᠦᠨ ᠤ ᠵᠣᠺᠢᠶᠠᠨ ᠪᠢᠴᠢᠭᠰᠡᠨ ᠨᠣᠮ ᠤᠩᠰᠢᠮᠤᠢ</uig> I am reading a book written by him.
<uig rom="manu baqsi-yin mandur kelegsen üge ünen ajuγu">ᠮᠠᠨᠤ ᠪᠠᠬᠰᠢ ᠶᠢᠨ ᠮᠠᠨᠳᠤᠷ ᠺᠡᠯᠡᠭᠰᠡᠨ ᠦᠭᠡ ᠦᠨᠡᠨ ᠠᠵᠤᠭᠤ</uig> The words spoken to us by our teacher turned out to be true.

In nominal constructions serving as attributes the passive voice may be replaced by the active. The actor is expressed in passive constructions by the dative-locative (dativus actoris), while it is in the genitive (genitivus actoris) when the active voice is used.
<uig rom="noqai-dur idegdegsen miqan">ᠨᠣᠬᠠᠢ ᠳ᠋ᠤᠷ ᠢᠳᠡᠭᠳᠡᠭᠰᠡᠨ ᠮᠢᠬᠠᠨ</uig> the meat eaten by the dog
<uig rom="baγsi-yin bicigsen bicig">ᠪᠠᠭᠰᠢ ᠶᠢᠨ ᠪᠢᠴᠢᠭᠰᠡᠨ ᠪᠢᠴᠢᠭ</uig> a letter written by the teacher

Nominal constructions may serve as objects. In such constructions the action is expressed by an oblique case of a verbal noun. The oblique case is the same as that of an object represented by a single word. It may be accompanied by a postposition.

entry.title: Syntax - Nominal construction - As object
entry.title2: Nominal construction - As object in the genitive

paragraphs.paragraph: A nominal conatruction in the genitive serving as an object occurs only with postpositions.
<uig rom="bi erdem surqui-yin tulada surγaγuli-dur orobai">ᠪᠢ ᠡᠷᠳᠡᠮ ᠰᠤᠷᠬᠤᠢ ᠶᠢᠨ ᠲᠤᠯᠠᠳᠠ ᠰᠤᠷᠭᠠᠭᠤᠯᠢ ᠳ᠋ᠤᠷ ᠣᠷᠣᠪᠠᠢ</uig> I entered school with the purpose of studying science.

<uig rom="bida tanu baγsi-yin ükügsen-ü tuqai medegülügsen-i küliyen abuba">ᠪᠢᠳᠠ ᠲᠠᠨᠤ ᠪᠠᠭᠰᠢ ᠶᠢᠨ ᠦᠺᠦᠭᠰᠡᠨ ᠤ ᠲᠤᠬᠠᠢ ᠮᠡᠳᠡᠭᠦᠯᠦᠭᠰᠡᠨ ᠢ ᠺᠦᠯᠢᠶᠡᠨ ᠠᠪᠤᠪᠠ</uig> Wo received the message about the death of your teacher.

entry.title: Syntax - Nominal construction - As object
entry.title2: Nominal construction - As object in the accusative

paragraphs.paragraph: Nominal constructions in the accusative serve as direct objects. The actor is put in the genitive.
<uig rom="bi tegün-ü bicigsen-i ese ungsiba">ᠪᠢ ᠲᠡᠭᠦᠨ ᠤ ᠪᠢᠴᠢᠭᠰᠡᠨ ᠢ ᠡᠰᠡ ᠤᠩᠰᠢᠪᠠ</uig> I did not read what he had written.
<uig rom="bi qota-aca ger-tegen bucaju iregsen-iyen medegülümüi">ᠪᠢ ᠬᠣᠲᠠ ᠡᠴᠡ ᠭᠡᠷ ᠎ᠲᠡᠭᠡᠨ ᠪᠤᠴᠠᠵᠤ ᠢᠷᠡᠭᠰᠡᠨ ᠢᠶᠡᠨ ᠮᠡᠳᠡᠭᠦᠯᠦᠮᠦᠢ</uig> I am telling of my return home from town.

entry.title: Syntax - Nominal construction - As object
entry.title2: Nominal construction - As object in the accusative

paragraphs.paragraph: A apecial case is the accusative with a verbal noun corresponding to the Latin accusativus cum infinitivo. Here both the actor and the action are put in the accusative (see § 614).
<uig rom="geser-i yabuqu-yi üjebe">ᠭᠡᠰᠡᠷ ᠢ ᠶᠠᠪᠤᠬᠤ ᠶᠢ ᠦᠵᠡᠪᠡ</uig> He saw Geser go.

entry.title: Syntax - Nominal construction - As object
entry.title2: Nominal construction - As object in the accusative

paragraphs.paragraph: When the actor of the nominal construction is independent of the grammatical subject of the whole sentence, the action is put in the simple accusative, but when the actor of the nominal construction coincides with the subject, the action is put in the accusative with the reflexive-possessive suffix.
<uig rom="edüge bi tandur cinggis qaγan-u tuqai bicigsen-i ilegemüi">ᠡᠳᠦᠭᠡ ᠪᠢ ᠲᠠᠨᠳᠤᠷ ᠴᠢᠩᠭᠢᠰ ᠬᠠᠭᠠᠨ ᠤ ᠲᠤᠬᠠᠢ ᠪᠢᠴᠢᠭᠰᠡᠨ ᠢ ᠢᠯᠡᠭᠡᠮᠦᠢ</uig> Now I am sending you what was written about Chingis Khan.
<uig rom="edüge bi tandur cinggis qaγan-u tuqai bicigsen-iyen ilegemüi">ᠡᠳᠦᠭᠡ ᠪᠢ ᠲᠠᠨᠳᠤᠷ ᠴᠢᠩᠭᠢᠰ ᠬᠠᠭᠠᠨ ᠤ ᠲᠤᠬᠠᠢ ᠪᠢᠴᠢᠭᠰᠡᠨ ᠢᠶᠡᠨ ᠢᠯᠡᠭᠡᠮᠦᠢ</uig> Now I am sending you what I wrote about Chingis Khan.

entry.title: Syntax - Nominal construction - As object
entry.title2: Nominal construction - As object in the dative-locative

paragraphs.paragraph: Nominal constructions in the dative-locative correspond, in meaning, to temporal subordinate clauses of European languages and to the Latin ablativus absolutus. They are translated into English as "When the person concerned did (or will do) something . . ."

The action of such constructions is expressed by a verbal noun in the dative-locative. When the actor of the construction is the same as the grammatical subject of the whole period, the action is indicated by a dative-locative with the reflexive-possessive suffix.

The actor is put in the genitive (or in relatively rare cases, under the influence of the Colloquial, in the accusativus actoris, see § 517), when he is not the same as the subject of the whole sentence.
- The actor in the accusative:

<uig rom="manu nökör-i qota-dur irekü-dür tegün-ü olan tanil bayiqsan ajuγu">ᠮᠠᠨᠤ ᠨᠥᠺᠥᠷ ᠢ ᠬᠣᠲᠠ ᠳ᠋ᠤᠷ ᠢᠷᠡᠺᠦ ᠳ᠋ᠤᠷ ᠲᠡᠭᠦᠨ ᠤ ᠣᠯᠠᠨ ᠲᠠᠨᠢᠯ ᠪᠠᠶᠢᠬᠰᠠᠨ ᠠᠵᠤᠭᠤ</uig> When our friend came to town, there were many acquaintances of his there.
- The actor in the genitive:
<uig rom="manu nökör-ün irekü-dür bida bügüde masida bayasba">ᠮᠠᠨᠤ ᠨᠥᠺᠥᠷ ᠤᠨ ᠢᠷᠡᠺᠦ ᠳ᠋ᠤᠷ ᠪᠢᠳᠠ ᠪᠦᠭᠦᠳᠡ ᠮᠠᠰᠢᠳᠠ ᠪᠠᠶᠠᠰᠪᠠ</uig> When our friend came, all of us were very glad.
- The actor is the subject of the whole sentence:
<uig rom="bi qota-dur irekü-degen surγaγuli-dur oromui">ᠪᠢ ᠬᠣᠲᠠ ᠳ᠋ᠤᠷ ᠢᠷᠡᠺᠦ ᠳ᠋ᠡᠭᠡᠨ ᠰᠤᠷᠭᠠᠭᠤᠯᠢ ᠳ᠋ᠤᠷ ᠣᠷᠣᠮᠤᠢ</uig> When I come to town, I shall enter school.

entry.title: Syntax - Nominal construction - As object
entry.title2: Nominal construction - As object in the ablative

paragraphs.paragraph: Nominal constructions in the ablative function in the same manner as a simple ablative object. According to the various meanings of the ablative such constructions may be regarded as ablativus exclusivus, ablativus comparativus, etc.
The action is put in the ablative, and the actor, if he is not the Same as the subject of the whole sentence, in the genitive (and rarely in the accusative).

<uig rom="kilince üileddügsen-ece eldeb maγu jobalang bui boluqsan amui">ᠺᠢᠯᠢᠨᠴᠡ ᠦᠢᠯᠡᠳᠳᠦᠭᠰᠡᠨ ᠡᠴᠡ ᠡᠯᠳᠡᠪ ᠮᠠᠭᠤ ᠵᠣᠪᠠᠯᠠᠩ ᠪᠤᠢ ᠪᠣᠯᠤᠬᠰᠠᠨ ᠠᠮᠤᠢ</uig>In consequence of sins having been committed, various grave sufferings came into existence.

<uig rom="cinggis qan-u ügei boluγsan-aca qoyisi ügedei qan inu qaγan ergügdejüküi">ᠴᠢᠩᠭᠢᠰ ᠬᠠᠨ ᠤ ᠦᠭᠡᠢ ᠪᠣᠯᠤᠭᠰᠠᠨ ᠡᠴᠡ ᠬᠣᠶᠢᠰᠢ ᠦᠭᠡᠳᠡᠢ ᠬᠠᠨ ᠢᠨᠤ ᠬᠠᠭᠠᠨ ᠡᠷᠭᠦᠭᠳᠡᠵᠦᠺᠦᠢ</uig> After the death of Chingis Khan, Ugedei Khan was elected emperor.

entry.title: Syntax - Nominal construction - As object
entry.title2: Nominal construction - As object in the instrumental

paragraphs.paragraph: Nominal constructions in the instrumental usually act as causal subordinate clauses of European languages and, therefore, may be translated as "because of ...", "in consequence of ...", or "by doing so ...".

<uig rom="mongγol yasutan-u dotor-a eb ügei boluγsan-iyar teden-ü kücün anu neng baγurajuqui">ᠮᠣᠩᠭᠣᠯ ᠶᠠᠰᠤᠲᠠᠨ ᠤ ᠳᠣᠲᠣᠷ ᠠ ᠡᠪ ᠦᠭᠡᠢ ᠪᠣᠯᠤᠭᠰᠠᠨ ᠢᠶᠠᠷ ᠲᠡᠳᠡᠨ ᠤ ᠺᠦᠴᠦᠨ ᠠᠨᠤ ᠨᠡᠩ ᠪᠠᠭᠤᠷᠠᠵᠤᠬᠤᠢ</uig> In consequence of internal discord among the Mongolian tribes, their power declined still more.

<uig rom="eldeb jüil-ün buruγu arγ-a kemjiy-e-nügüd-i yabuγuluγsan-iyar eyimü süid boluγsan bui">ᠡᠯᠳᠡᠪ ᠵᠦᠢᠯ ᠤᠨ ᠪᠤᠷᠤᠭᠤ ᠠᠷᠭ ᠠ ᠺᠡᠮᠵᠢᠶ ᠡ ᠎ᠨᠦᠭᠦᠳ ᠢ ᠶᠠᠪᠤᠭᠤᠯᠤᠭᠰᠠᠨ ᠢᠶᠠᠷ ᠡᠶᠢᠮᠦ ᠰᠦᠢᠳ ᠪᠣᠯᠤᠭᠰᠠᠨ ᠪᠤᠢ</uig> In consequence of taking various wrong measures,such a disaster arose.

entry.title: Syntax - Nominal construction - As object
entry.title2: Nominal construction - As object in the comitative

paragraphs.paragraph: Nominal constructions in the comitative express events simultaneous with the action of the predicate of the whole sentence. They may be translated into English as "simultaneously with ...".
<uig rom="ür cayiqui-luγ-a qamtu mordoba">ᠦᠷ ᠴᠠᠶᠢᠬᠤᠢ ᠯᠤᠭ ᠠ ᠬᠠᠮᠲᠤ ᠮᠣᠷᠳᠣᠪᠠ</uig> He started with the break of dawn. (Lit., He started together with the dawning of the dawn.)
<uig rom="tere inu kitad ulus-un qubisqal-un manduqui-luγ-a tokiyalduba">ᠲᠡᠷᠡ ᠢᠨᠤ ᠺᠢᠲᠠᠳ ᠤᠯᠤᠰ ᠤᠨ ᠬᠤᠪᠢᠰᠬᠠᠯ ᠤᠨ ᠮᠠᠨᠳᠤᠬᠤᠢ ᠯᠤᠭ ᠠ ᠲᠣᠺᠢᠶᠠᠯᠳᠤᠪᠠ</uig> That coincided with the rise of the Chinese revolution.

entry.title: Syntax - Nominal construction - Order of the nominal construction
entry.title2: Nominal construction - Order of the nominal construction

paragraphs.paragraph: Nominal constructions are members of a sentence and they differ from simple members only in that they are groups of words while simple members are single words. Therefore, a nominal construction occupies the same place in a sentence as a simple member. This means that a nominal construction serving as a subject occupies the usual place of the subject, one serving as an object occupies the usual place of an object, and so on.
The usual order of words in sentences is : a-s-a-o-p, where a is attribute, s is subject, o is object, and p is predicate.

If we replace the symbols of simple members with symbols for nominal constructions serving as the members concerned, the formula is as follows : A-S-A-O-P, where A is an attributive nominal construction, S is a nominal construction serving as a subject, O is a nominal construction serving as an object, and P is a predicative nominal construction with a copula. Of course, in reality, there are very few sentences cf which all the members are nominal constructions. Usually only one or two members represent such groups of words while the remaining members are simple ones, e. g., a-s-O-p or S-a-O-p, and so on.
The imperfect, modal, and perfect converbs act as predicates of incomplete juxtaposed sentences or as parts of the main predicate.

<uig rom="negüdelcin arad bolbasu üker aduγu qoni imaγ-a jerge-yin mal öskejü usu belciger-i daγaju negüdel-iyer amiduramui">ᠨᠡᠭᠦᠳᠡᠯᠴᠢᠨ ᠠᠷᠠᠳ ᠪᠣᠯᠪᠠᠰᠤ ᠦᠺᠡᠷ ᠠᠳᠤᠭᠤ ᠬᠣᠨᠢ ᠢᠮᠠᠭ ᠠ ᠵᠡᠷᠭᠡ ᠶᠢᠨ ᠮᠠᠯ ᠥᠰᠺᠡᠵᠦ ᠤᠰᠤ ᠪᠡᠯᠴᠢᠭᠡᠷ ᠢ ᠳᠠᠭᠠᠵᠤ ᠨᠡᠭᠦᠳᠡᠯ ᠢᠶᠡᠷ ᠠᠮᠢᠳᠤᠷᠠᠮᠤᠢ</uig> Nomad people, raising cattle, horses, sheep, goats, and other animals, and following water and pastures, exist by transhumance.
<uig rom="bi ungsiju saγumui">ᠪᠢ ᠤᠩᠰᠢᠵᠤ ᠰᠠᠭᠤᠮᠤᠢ</uig> I am sitting and reading.

Most of the remaining converbs are, from the historical point of view, fossilized forms of oblique cases of various verbal nouns, some of which no longer exist as such. Since nominal constructions may act as certain members of a sentence, it is obvious that fossilized forms of original verbal nouns, too, must be able to act in a similar manner. Indeed, there are such groups of words in which the idea of an action is expressed by a converb.

entry.title: Syntax - Converbal construction - Historical survey
entry.title2: Converbal construction - Historical survey of some converbal forms

paragraphs.paragraph: As remarked in § 657, many converbs are fossilized forms of oblique cases of verbal nouns.

The converbum finale ending in <uig rom="-r-a"> ᠎ᠷ᠎ᠠ</uig> is the dative-locative (suffix <uig rom="-a">᠎ᠠ</uig> ) of a noun ending in <uig rom=""> ᠎ᠷ</uig> -r (cf. <uig rom="amur">ᠠᠮᠤᠷ</uig> "peace, rest" from <uig rom="amu-">ᠠᠮᠤ ᠎</uig> "to rest"). Originally such forms answered the same question as the dative-locative, e. g., <uig rom="ider-e">ᠢᠳᠡᠷ᠎ᠡ</uig> now "in order to eat" -formerly "to the eating" or "toward the eating." It should be remarked that this converb corresponds, from the point of view of meaning, to the dative-locative in <uig rom="-a">᠎ᠠ</uig> of the nomen futuri in <uig rom="-qui"> ᠎ᠬᠤᠢ</uig> , e. g., <uig rom="saγur-a">ᠰᠠᠭᠤᠷ᠎ᠠ =</uig> = <uig rom="saγuqui-a">ᠰᠠᠭᠤᠬᠤᠢ᠎ᠠ</uig> "in order to sit."

The same can be said of the converbum praeparativum in<uig rom="-r-un">᠎ᠷ ᠤᠨ</uig> . The latter was originally a genitive (suff. <uig rom=" -un"> ᠤᠨ</uig>) of a noun ending in <uig rom="-r"> ᠎ᠷ</uig> (cf. supra). Thus, <uig rom="amitan-i jobaγulur-un kilince üileddügsen amui">ᠠᠮᠢᠲᠠᠨ ᠢ ᠵᠣᠪᠠᠭᠤᠯᠤᠷ ᠤᠨ ᠺᠢᠯᠢᠨᠴᠡ ᠦᠢᠯᠡᠳᠳᠦᠭᠰᠡᠨ ᠠᠮᠤᠢ</uig> "He committed sins by causing sufferings to living beings," originally was "He committed sins of tormenting living beings." It should be added, however, that the genitive served in Ancient Mongolian or in Common Altaic both as genitive and instrumental.

The converbum terminale ending in <uig rom="-tala"> ᠎ᠲᠠᠯᠠ</uig> , e. g., <uig rom="ükütele">ᠦᠺᠦᠲᠡᠯᠡ</uig> "until he dies," was originally a dative-locative (with the suffix <uig rom="-a">᠎ᠠ</uig> ) of nouns ending in <uig rom="-tal"> ᠎ᠲᠠᠯ</uig> c.f. <uig rom="surtal">ᠰᠤᠷᠲᠠᠯ</uig> "doctrine" from <uig rom="sur-">ᠰᠤᠷ ᠎</uig> "to learn"). Thus, <uig rom="ükütele">ᠦᠺᠦᠲᠡᠯᠡ</uig> "until he dies" was originally "till the death" or "to the death."

The converbum abtemporale (suffix <uig rom="-γsaγar"> ᠎ᠬᠰᠠᠭᠠᠷ</uig> ) is a fossilized instrumental of the nomen perfecti. The ancient instrumental suffix <uig rom="-γar"> ᠎ᠭᠠᠷ</uig> still exists as the ending of certain adverbs, e. g. <uig rom="γaγcaγar">ᠭᠠᠬᠴᠠᠭᠠᠷ</uig> "alone, solely," <uig rom="manaγar">ᠮᠠᠨᠠᠭᠠᠷ</uig> "tomorrow," and so on. Thus, <uig rom="abuγsaγar">ᠠᠪᠤᠬᠰᠠᠭᠠᠷ</uig> now means "since he took," but originally it meant "through having taken."

The converbum contemporale with the ending <uig rom="-maγca"> ᠎ᠮᠠᠬᠴᠠ</uig> is a fossilized Casus aequativus (with the ancient suffix <uig rom="-ca"> ᠎ᠴᠠ</uig> related to the ablative suffix) of a deverbal noun ending in <uig rom="-maγ"> ᠎ᠮᠠᠭ</uig> (e. g., <uig rom="qayurmaγ">ᠬᠠᠶᠤᠷᠮᠠᠭ</uig> "fraud" from <uig rom="qayur-">ᠬᠠᠶᠤᠷ ᠎</uig> "to deceive").

Thus the forms of many converbs are fossilized oblique cases of verbal or deverbal nouns. Consequently, they do not differ in principle from living oblique cases of existing verbal nouns. Indeed, constructions with such converbs act in a manner similar to nominal constructions.
The idea of the action is expressed in such constructions by converbs. The actor is subject to the same rules as the actor of a nominal construction.

entry.title: Syntax - Converbal construction - Historical survey
entry.title2: Converbal construction - Historical survey of some converbal forms

paragraphs.paragraph: The actor is expressed in converbal constructions by the nominative or genitive (or even accusative), if the subject of the whole sentence does not coincide with the actor. Yet this is not obligatory and the nominative can be used in all cases.
<uig rom="boroγan ürlüge boltala oroju abai">ᠪᠣᠷᠣᠭᠠᠨ ᠦᠷᠯᠦᠭᠡ ᠪᠣᠯᠲᠠᠯᠠ ᠣᠷᠣᠵᠤ ᠠᠪᠠᠢ</uig> It rained till morning. (Lit., "Rain was falling until morning came.")
<uig rom="nökör-i oromaγca bügüdeger mendücilebe">ᠨᠥᠺᠥᠷ ᠢ ᠣᠷᠣᠮᠠᠭᠴᠠ ᠪᠦᠭᠦᠳᠡᠭᠡᠷ ᠮᠡᠨᠳᠦᠴᠢᠯᠡᠪᠡ</uig> As soon as the friend came in, all of them welcomed him.

<uig rom="mongγol arad ulus bayiγuluγdaqsaγar qorin jil bolba">ᠮᠣᠩᠭᠣᠯ ᠠᠷᠠᠳ ᠤᠯᠤᠰ ᠪᠠᠶᠢᠭᠤᠯᠤᠭᠳᠠᠬᠰᠠᠭᠠᠷ ᠬᠣᠷᠢᠨ ᠵᠢᠯ ᠪᠣᠯᠪᠠ</uig> Twenty years have elapsed since the Mongolian People's Republic was established.
Constructions with the converbum terminale express:
1. events during which the action of the main predicate takes place and
2. events before which the action of the predicate takes place.
In the latter case the converbum terminale indicates the time limit of the main action: "till ...," "until ...," "so that ..."

<uig rom="dorji tür küliyejü saγutala mönö buriyad morin terge abciraba">ᠳᠣᠷᠵᠢ ᠲᠦᠷ ᠺᠦᠯᠢᠶᠡᠵᠦ ᠰᠠᠭᠤᠲᠠᠯᠠ ᠮᠥᠨᠥ ᠪᠤᠷᠢᠶᠠᠳ ᠮᠣᠷᠢᠨ ᠲᠡᠷᠭᠡ ᠠᠪᠴᠢᠷᠠᠪᠠ</uig> "While Dorji sat for a while, waiting, the same Buriat brought a horse car.

<uig rom="noyitan modu-yi nocotala qaγurai modu-yi quγurtala jodoju bayiba">ᠨᠣᠶᠢᠲᠠᠨ ᠮᠣᠳᠤ ᠶᠢ ᠨᠣᠴᠣᠲᠠᠯᠠ ᠬᠠᠭᠤᠷᠠᠢ ᠮᠣᠳᠤ ᠶᠢ ᠬᠤᠭᠤᠷᠲᠠᠯᠠ ᠵᠣᠳᠣᠵᠤ ᠪᠠᠶᠢᠪᠠ</uig> He beat until the wet stick caught fire and the dry stick splintered.

The converbum abtemporale is the opposite of the converbum terminale. While the latter indicates the time limit of an action in the future (until ... ), this indicates the time limit in the past (since). Such converbal constructions indicate that the action of the predicate of the whole sentence starts from the beginning of the action of the converb and may last during the whole time during which the latter takes place. Therefore, the converbum abtemporale may be translated as "since someone did something" or "while someone was doing something."
<uig rom="manu surγaγuli angq-a bayiγuluγdaqsaγar tabun jil bolba">ᠮᠠᠨᠤ ᠰᠤᠷᠭᠠᠭᠤᠯᠢ ᠠᠩᠬ ᠠ ᠪᠠᠶᠢᠭᠤᠯᠤᠭᠳᠠᠬᠰᠠᠭᠠᠷ ᠲᠠᠪᠤᠨ ᠵᠢᠯ ᠪᠣᠯᠪᠠ</uig> Five years have elapsed since our school was established.

<uig rom="tendece nököd inu kereg-ün ucir-a ende tende saγuγsaγar qoyar sar-a ilegü jam yabuju sayi qota-dur kürcü irebei">ᠲᠡᠨᠳᠡᠴᠡ ᠨᠥᠺᠥᠳ ᠢᠨᠤ ᠺᠡᠷᠡᠭ ᠤᠨ ᠤᠴᠢᠷ ᠠ ᠡᠨᠳᠡ ᠲᠡᠨᠳᠡ ᠰᠠᠭᠤᠭᠰᠠᠭᠠᠷ ᠬᠣᠶᠠᠷ ᠰᠠᠷ ᠠ ᠢᠯᠡᠭᠦ ᠵᠠᠮ ᠶᠠᠪᠤᠵᠤ ᠰᠠᠶᠢ ᠬᠣᠲᠠ ᠳ᠋ᠤᠷ ᠺᠦᠷᠴᠦ ᠢᠷᠡᠪᠡᠢ</uig> Afterwards his friends, living here and there because of business, travelled more than two months and have just arrived in town.

The converbum contemporale expresses an action which takes place simultaneously with the beginning of the main action. Such converbal constructions may be translated as "as soon as he did something ..." or "immediately as ..."
<uig rom="nigen dabaγ-a dabamaγca nigen aγudam ködüge tala bayimui">ᠨᠢᠭᠡᠨ ᠳᠠᠪᠠᠭ ᠠ ᠳᠠᠪᠠᠮᠠᠭᠴᠠ ᠨᠢᠭᠡᠨ ᠠᠭᠤᠳᠠᠮ ᠺᠥᠳᠦᠭᠡ ᠲᠠᠯᠠ ᠪᠠᠶᠢᠮᠤᠢ</uig> As soon as they pass the summit, there will be a vast steppe.

The action of the converbum conditionale is the condition making the main action possible. Therefore, this converb is to be translated as "if ..." On the other hand, this converb indicates an action at the time of which the main action takes place, and, in this case, it may be translated as "when something took place ..."

The general rule is that this converb expresses a condition (if ... ) when the main verb is a present (or future) tense. When the main verb is a past tense, the converb expresses the time at which the main action takes place (when ... )

<uig rom="kümün ama-yin toγ-a-yi kedün mingγ-a kürtele olan ese bolγabasu mal-un ajil-i tuyil-dur kürtele bolbasuraγulun kögjigüljü cidaqu ügei bui">ᠺᠦᠮᠦᠨ ᠠᠮᠠ ᠶᠢᠨ ᠲᠣᠭ ᠠ ᠶᠢ ᠺᠡᠳᠦᠨ ᠮᠢᠩᠭ ᠠ ᠺᠦᠷᠲᠡᠯᠡ ᠣᠯᠠᠨ ᠡᠰᠡ ᠪᠣᠯᠭᠠᠪᠠᠰᠤ ᠮᠠᠯ ᠤᠨ ᠠᠵᠢᠯ ᠢ ᠲᠤᠶᠢᠯ ᠳ᠋ᠤᠷ ᠺᠦᠷᠲᠡᠯᠡ ᠪᠣᠯᠪᠠᠰᠤᠷᠠᠭᠤᠯᠤᠨ ᠺᠥᠭᠵᠢᠭᠦᠯᠵᠦ ᠴᠢᠳᠠᠬᠤ ᠦᠭᠡᠢ ᠪᠤᠢ</uig>If the size of the population is not increased by several thousand, it will be impossible to develop the cattle husbandry to the ultimate goal.
<uig rom="ene jorilγ-a-yi güicedkekü abasu manu aju aqui kögjijü bolumui">ᠡᠨᠡ ᠵᠣᠷᠢᠯᠭ ᠠ ᠶᠢ ᠭᠦᠢᠴᠡᠳᠺᠡᠺᠦ ᠠᠪᠠᠰᠤ ᠮᠠᠨᠤ ᠠᠵᠤ ᠠᠬᠤᠢ ᠺᠥᠭᠵᠢᠵᠦ ᠪᠣᠯᠤᠮᠤᠢ</uig> If this task is solved, our economy will develop.

<uig rom="tendece tedeger nököd inu jüg jüg-ece modun-u dergede quraγad üjebesü busud ber bürin ajuγu, emci-yin köbegün ügei">ᠲᠡᠨᠳᠡᠴᠡ ᠲᠡᠳᠡᠭᠡᠷ ᠨᠥᠺᠥᠳ ᠢᠨᠤ ᠵᠦᠭ ᠵᠦᠭ ᠡᠴᠡ ᠮᠣᠳᠤᠨ ᠤ ᠳᠡᠷᠭᠡᠳᠡ ᠬᠤᠷᠠᠭᠠᠳ ᠦᠵᠡᠪᠡᠰᠦ ᠪᠤᠰᠤᠳ ᠪᠡᠷ ᠪᠦᠷᠢᠨ ᠠᠵᠤᠭᠤ᠃ ᠡᠮᠴᠢ ᠶᠢᠨ ᠺᠥᠪᠡᠭᠦᠨ ᠦᠭᠡᠢ</uig> Thereafter, when those friends of his gathered by the forest and looked, all the others were present, but the son of the physician was not.
The Converbum conditionale is often followed by the particle <uig rom="ele">ᠡᠯᠡ</uig>, which does not change the meaning
<uig rom="tere γajar-a iregsen abasu ele nököd inu ügei ajuγu">ᠲᠡᠷᠡ ᠭᠠᠵᠠᠷ ᠠ ᠢᠷᠡᠭᠰᠡᠨ ᠠᠪᠠᠰᠤ ᠡᠯᠡ ᠨᠥᠺᠥᠳ ᠢᠨᠤ ᠦᠭᠡᠢ ᠠᠵᠤᠭᠤ</uig> As he came to that place, his friends, as it turned, had not been there.

When the predicate of the whole sentence has a negative, the converbum conditionale is followed by the particle <uig rom="ber">ᠪᠡᠷ</uig> and, in such cases, it expresses an action in spite of which the main action takes place (although . . .). But in positive sentences the particle ber does not change the meaning of the converb.

<uig rom="amusuγai kemen sedkibesü ber amur ügei amui">ᠠᠮᠤᠰᠤᠭᠠᠢ ᠺᠡᠮᠡᠨ ᠰᠡᠳᠺᠢᠪᠡᠰᠦ ᠪᠡᠷ ᠠᠮᠤᠷ ᠦᠭᠡᠢ ᠠᠮᠤᠢ</uig> And even if he longs for rest, there will be no rest, or Although he longs for rest, there is no rest.

<uig rom="tere γajar-a kürcü üjebesü ber nököd inu tende quraγad bürin ajuγu">ᠲᠡᠷᠡ ᠭᠠᠵᠠᠷ ᠠ ᠺᠦᠷᠴᠦ ᠦᠵᠡᠪᠡᠰᠦ ᠪᠡᠷ ᠨᠥᠺᠥᠳ ᠢᠨᠤ ᠲᠡᠨᠳᠡ ᠬᠤᠷᠠᠭᠠᠳ ᠪᠦᠷᠢᠨ ᠠᠵᠤᠭᠤ</uig> When he arrived at that place and looked, his friends had assembled and were all there.
This colloquial form ending in <uig rom="-qula/-küle">᠎ᠬᠤᠯᠠ/ ᠎ᠺᠦᠯᠡ</uig> (pronounced in Khalkha as -xlā/-xlē) functions in Written Mongolian as the converbum conditionale.

<uig rom="edüge darui arγ-a kemjiy-e-nügüd-i ese abqula tere dutaγdal-nuγud-i usadqaju cidaqu ügei bui">ᠡᠳᠦᠭᠡ ᠳᠠᠷᠤᠢ ᠠᠷᠭ ᠠ ᠺᠡᠮᠵᠢᠶ ᠡ ᠎ᠨᠦᠭᠦᠳ ᠢ ᠡᠰᠡ ᠠᠪᠬᠤᠯᠠ ᠲᠡᠷᠡ ᠳᠤᠲᠠᠭᠳᠠᠯ ᠎ᠨᠤᠭᠤᠳ ᠢ ᠤᠰᠠᠳᠬᠠᠵᠤ ᠴᠢᠳᠠᠬᠤ ᠦᠭᠡᠢ ᠪᠤᠢ</uig> If measures are not taken immediately, it will be impossible to remove those defects.
The converbum concessivum expresses an action in spite of which the main action of the predicate takes place. This converb is translated as "although . . .," "in spite of . . ."

<uig rom="caγan cerig-i qamiγ-a bayiqui-yi jüg büri-ece eribecü oγtu üjegdekü ügei bayiba">ᠴᠠᠭᠠᠨ ᠴᠡᠷᠢᠭ ᠢ ᠬᠠᠮᠢᠭ ᠠ ᠪᠠᠶᠢᠬᠤᠢ ᠶᠢ ᠵᠦᠭ ᠪᠦᠷᠢ ᠡᠴᠡ ᠡᠷᠢᠪᠡᠴᠦ ᠣᠭᠲᠤ ᠦᠵᠡᠭᠳᠡᠺᠦ ᠦᠭᠡᠢ ᠪᠠᠶᠢᠪᠠ</uig> Although they were looking everywhere for the White Army, it was not seen at all.
The particle <uig rom="cu">ᠴᠤ</uig> in the ending <uig rom="-bacu"> ᠎ᠪᠠᠴᠤ</uig> is sometimes written separately and may be placed before the verbal form.
<uig rom="tegün-i cu abuba gem ügei">ᠲᠡᠭᠦᠨ ᠢ ᠴᠤ ᠠᠪᠤᠪᠠ ᠭᠡᠮ ᠦᠭᠡᠢ</uig> Never mind if he did take it.
The converbum finale acts as the supine in Latin and expresses the aim of the action of the predicate. Therefore, it can be translated as "in order to ...'
<uig rom="tegün-i abur-a irebei">ᠲᠡᠭᠦᠨ ᠢ ᠠᠪᠤᠷ ᠠ ᠢᠷᠡᠪᠡᠢ</uig> He came to take him.
The converbum finale was originally a dative-locative of the verbal noun ending in <uig rom="-r"> ᠎ᠷ</uig> . It preserves its original meaning in pre-classical texts.
<uig rom="ükür-e oyiratuba">ᠦᠺᠦᠷ ᠡ ᠣᠶᠢᠷᠠᠲᠤᠪᠠ</uig> He was near death.

The converbum praeparativum is originally the genitive of a noun ending in <uig rom="-r"> ᠎ᠷ</uig> . In texts of the pre-classical period it expresses the cause of the action of the predicate of the whole sentence.

<uig rom="amitan-i jobaγulur-un nigül-i üileddümüi">ᠠᠮᠢᠲᠠᠨ ᠢ ᠵᠣᠪᠠᠭᠤᠯᠤᠷ ᠤᠨ ᠨᠢᠭᠦᠯ ᠢ ᠦᠢᠯᠡᠳᠳᠦᠮᠦᠢ</uig> He commits sin in tormenting living beings. (Lit., "He commits the sin of tormenting living beings.")

In the classical and modern language this converb is rarely used; the verbs <uig rom="ügüle-">ᠦᠭᠦᠯᠡ ᠎</uig> "to speak," <uig rom="sedki-">ᠰᠡᠳᠺᠢ ᠎</uig> "to think," and <uig rom="üje-">ᠦᠵᠡ ᠎</uig> "to see" are among the few which occur in this form.

<uig rom="tegün-i qaγan üjejü bürün sayin cirai-tu-yin minu ebedcin yeke bolbai kemebei">ᠲᠡᠭᠦᠨ ᠢ ᠬᠠᠭᠠᠨ ᠦᠵᠡᠵᠦ ᠪᠦᠷᠦᠨ ᠰᠠᠶᠢᠨ ᠴᠢᠷᠠᠢ ᠎ᠲᠤ ᠶᠢᠨ ᠮᠢᠨᠤ ᠡᠪᠡᠳᠴᠢᠨ ᠶᠡᠺᠡ ᠪᠣᠯᠪᠠᠢ ᠺᠡᠮᠡᠪᠡᠢ</uig> When the khaghan looked he said: "The illness of my Beautiful-Faced One has become grave."

Sentences expressing direct discourse usually occupy the place between the subject and the predicate of the whole sentence, being linked to the predicate by the converbum modale of the verb ᠺᠡᠮᠡ ᠎ (or geme-) "to say," i. e., ᠺᠡᠮᠡᠨ or gemen "saying." In other words, the direct discourse is inserted into a sentence. It is not always good, from the point of view of the English style, to translate direct discourse as such. Frequently direct discourse is translated as indirect. In such cases, the converb ᠺᠡᠮᠡᠨ (or gemen) "saying" is replaced in the translation by "that."
<uig rom="nökör marγasi iresügei kemen ügülebe">ᠨᠥᠺᠥᠷ ᠮᠠᠷᠭᠠᠰᠢ ᠢᠷᠡᠰᠦᠭᠡᠢ ᠺᠡᠮᠡᠨ ᠦᠭᠦᠯᠡᠪᠡ</uig> The friend said he would come tomorrow. (Lit., The friend told saying, "I shall come tomorrow.")

When the verb "to tell" or "to say" is a converbum praeparativum it is placed before direct discourse. But even in this event the direct discourse is followed by ᠺᠡᠮᠡᠨ (or gemen) and the latter by a finite form of a verbum dicendi.

<uig rom="qaγan ügüler-ün a köbegün minu a ci tere morin-i buu unu kemen (or gemen) kelebe">ᠬᠠᠭᠠᠨ ᠦᠭᠦᠯᠡᠷ ᠤᠨ ᠠ ᠺᠥᠪᠡᠭᠦᠨ ᠮᠢᠨᠤ ᠠ ᠴᠢ ᠲᠡᠷᠡ ᠮᠣᠷᠢᠨ ᠢ ᠪᠤᠤ ᠤᠨᠤ ᠺᠡᠮᠡᠨ ᠺᠡᠯᠡᠪᠡ</uig> When the khaghan spoke, he said (lit., "spoke saying,") "Ah, my son, do not ride that horse!"
The converb ᠺᠡᠮᠡᠨ (or gemen) may be replaced by a finite form of the verb ᠺᠡᠮᠡ ᠎ (geme-). In this event any other verbum dicendi is not necessary.
<uig rom="nökör bi marγasi iresügei kemebei">ᠨᠥᠺᠥᠷ ᠪᠢ ᠮᠠᠷᠭᠠᠰᠢ ᠢᠷᠡᠰᠦᠭᠡᠢ ᠺᠡᠮᠡᠪᠡᠢ</uig> The friend said: "I shall come tomorrow."

All verbs of thinking, seeing, hearing, saying, and so on (i. e., verba cogitandi, sentiendi, dicendi, etc.), are linked with the sentence expressing the result of any of these actions by the use of <uig rom="kemen">ᠺᠡᠮᠡᠨ</uig> in the same manner as in direct discourse.
<uig rom="tere inu marγasi iremüi kemen sedkibe">ᠲᠡᠷᠡ ᠢᠨᠤ ᠮᠠᠷᠭᠠᠰᠢ ᠢᠷᠡᠮᠦᠢ ᠺᠡᠮᠡᠨ ᠰᠡᠳᠺᠢᠪᠡ</uig> He thought that he would come tomorrow.
Indirect discourse is expressed in the same manner. In such constructions the converb ᠺᠡᠮᠡᠨ (gemen) functions as the English conjunction "that."
<uig rom="edüge tere inaγad iremüi kemen bicigsen-i ungsibai">ᠡᠳᠦᠭᠡ ᠲᠡᠷᠡ ᠢᠨᠠᠭᠠᠳ ᠢᠷᠡᠮᠦᠢ ᠺᠡᠮᠡᠨ ᠪᠢᠴᠢᠭᠰᠡᠨ ᠢ ᠤᠩᠰᠢᠪᠠᠢ</uig> He read a written statement that he would certainly come now.
The subject of a construction indicating indirect discourse may be expressed by an accusativus relationis (see § 515).
<uig rom="qaγan tegün-i iretügei kemen jarliγ bolba">ᠬᠠᠭᠠᠨ ᠲᠡᠭᠦᠨ ᠢ ᠢᠷᠡᠲᠦᠭᠡᠢ ᠺᠡᠮᠡᠨ ᠵᠠᠷᠯᠢᠭ ᠪᠣᠯᠪᠠ</uig> The khaghan ordered him to come.
The object of someone's perception may be expressed by an accusativus cum nomine verbali (see § 514).
<uig rom="qaγan inu tegün-i irekü-yi üjebe">ᠬᠠᠭᠠᠨ ᠢᠨᠤ ᠲᠡᠭᠦᠨ ᠢ ᠢᠷᠡᠺᠦ ᠶᠢ ᠦᠵᠡᠪᠡ</uig> The khaghan saw him come.

The converbal form ᠺᠡᠮᠡᠨ (gemen) is often used, in cases when there is no speech at all, to serve as the English conjurction "that" or "in order to." The verb indicating the aim of someorte's action is either a form of the direct discourse or a nomen futuri.

<uig rom="bi surγaγuli-dur erdem sursuγai kemen orobai">ᠪᠢ ᠰᠤᠷᠭᠠᠭᠤᠯᠢ ᠳ᠋ᠤᠷ ᠡᠷᠳᠡᠮ ᠰᠤᠷᠰᠤᠭᠠᠢ ᠺᠡᠮᠡᠨ ᠣᠷᠣᠪᠠᠢ</uig> I entered school in order to study. (Lit., I entered school saying, "I shall study science.")
<uig rom="bi surγaγuli-dur erdem surqu kemen orobai">ᠪᠢ ᠰᠤᠷᠭᠠᠭᠤᠯᠢ ᠳ᠋ᠤᠷ ᠡᠷᠳᠡᠮ ᠰᠤᠷᠬᠤ ᠺᠡᠮᠡᠨ ᠣᠷᠣᠪᠠᠢ</uig> I entered school in order to study. (Lit., I entered school saying, "To study science.")

Particles do not affect the forms of words. In this respect they are different from postpositions. Their role is to contribute additional emotional shades of meaning to the basic idea expressed by the words concerned. Some particles follow and others precede the word to which they refer.
This particle is placed after the word to which it refers. It is used as a mark of the grammatical subject.
<uig rom="bi ber mörgün namancilamui">ᠪᠢ ᠪᠡᠷ ᠮᠥᠷᠭᠦᠨ ᠨᠠᠮᠠᠨᠴᠢᠯᠠᠮᠤᠢ</uig> I am praying and making a bow.
See also §293, §531
See also §498
The particle <uig rom="ber">ᠪᠡᠷ</uig> is often used in antitheses and in such cases it may be translated as "but."

<uig rom="mergen inu ucir siltaγan bügüde-yi medemüi, mungqaγ ber teyimü busu bui">ᠮᠡᠷᠭᠡᠨ ᠢᠨᠤ ᠤᠴᠢᠷ ᠰᠢᠯᠲᠠᠭᠠᠨ ᠪᠦᠭᠦᠳᠡ ᠶᠢ ᠮᠡᠳᠡᠮᠦᠢ᠃ ᠮᠤᠩᠬᠠᠭ ᠪᠡᠷ ᠲᠡᠶᠢᠮᠦ ᠪᠤᠰᠤ ᠪᠤᠢ</uig> The sage knows what the matter is (lit., knows all the causes and circumstances) but the fool is not so.
The particle <uig rom="ber">ᠪᠡᠷ</uig> repeated after two or more words serves as a conjunction and may be translated as "as well as ..."

<uig rom="kümün amitan ber bayascu tngri-ner ber bayascu luus-un qaγad ber uyaraba">ᠺᠦᠮᠦᠨ ᠠᠮᠢᠲᠠᠨ ᠪᠡᠷ ᠪᠠᠶᠠᠰᠴᠤ ᠲᠩᠷᠢ ᠎ᠨᠡᠷ ᠪᠡᠷ ᠪᠠᠶᠠᠰᠴᠤ ᠯᠤᠤᠰ ᠤᠨ ᠬᠠᠭᠠᠳ ᠪᠡᠷ ᠤᠶᠠᠷᠠᠪᠠ</uig> People as well as living beings rejoiced and the deities rejoiced and the kings of the Nāga (dragons) were touched.
Interrogative pronouns with the particle <uig rom="ber">ᠪᠡᠷ</uig> are indefinite pronouns.
<uig rom="ali ber">ᠠᠯᠢ ᠪᠡᠷ</uig> whoever
<uig rom="ken ber">ᠺᠡᠨ ᠪᠡᠷ</uig> whoever
<uig rom="yaγun ber">ᠶᠠᠭᠤᠨ ᠪᠡᠷ</uig> whatever.
Indefinite pronouns with the particle <uig rom="ber">ᠪᠡᠷ</uig> in negative sentences are negative indefinite pronouns.
<uig rom="ken ber ese üjebe">ᠺᠡᠨ ᠪᠡᠷ ᠡᠰᠡ ᠦᠵᠡᠪᠡ</uig> Nobody saw.
<uig rom="nadur yaγun ber ügei">ᠨᠠᠳᠤᠷ ᠶᠠᠭᠤᠨ ᠪᠡᠷ ᠦᠭᠡᠢ</uig> I have nothing.
The converbum conditionale with the particle <uig rom="ber">ᠪᠡᠷ</uig> serves sometimes as converbum concessivum (see § 665).
<uig rom="emci-yi abcirabasu ber manu baqsi edegelcü ügei">ᠡᠮᠴᠢ ᠶᠢ ᠠᠪᠴᠢᠷᠠᠪᠠᠰᠤ ᠪᠡᠷ ᠮᠠᠨᠤ ᠪᠠᠬᠰᠢ ᠡᠳᠡᠭᠡᠯᠴᠦ ᠦᠭᠡᠢ</uig> Even if we bring a physician, our teacher will not recover.
<uig rom="qarabasu ber jam ügei bolqu">ᠬᠠᠷᠠᠪᠠᠰᠤ ᠪᠡᠷ ᠵᠠᠮ ᠦᠭᠡᠢ ᠪᠣᠯᠬᠤ</uig> Even if one seeks, there will be no road.

The particle <uig rom="cu">ᠴᠤ</uig>, too, is placed after the word to which it refers. Its function is similar to that of the particle ber. lt means often "also, too". It is not used as a mark of the subject nor is it used in antitheses.
The particle <uig rom="cu">ᠴᠤ</uig> after any word has the same meaning as the English "also" or "too."
<<uig rom="bi cu tegün-i medemüi">ᠪᠢ ᠴᠤ ᠲᠡᠭᠦᠨ ᠢ ᠮᠡᠳᠡᠮᠦᠢ</uig> I also know it.
<uig rom="bi tende cu yabuqu sanaγatai amui">ᠪᠢ ᠲᠡᠨᠳᠡ ᠴᠤ ᠶᠠᠪᠤᠬᠤ ᠰᠠᠨᠠᠭᠠᠲᠠᠢ ᠠᠮᠤᠢ</uig> I intend also to go there.
The particle <uig rom="cu">ᠴᠤ</uig> repeated after two or more words may be translated as "as well as ..."
<uig rom="tende modun cu bui jimis cu bui sayin ceceg-nügüd cu bui">ᠲᠡᠨᠳᠡ ᠮᠣᠳᠤᠨ ᠴᠤ ᠪᠤᠢ ᠵᠢᠮᠢᠰ ᠴᠤ ᠪᠤᠢ ᠰᠠᠶᠢᠨ ᠴᠡᠴᠡᠭ ᠎ᠨᠦᠭᠦᠳ ᠴᠤ ᠪᠤᠢ</uig> There are trees as well as fruits and beautiful flowers.
The particle <uig rom="cu">ᠴᠤ</uig> pepeated after two or more words in a sentence with a negative predicate may be translated as "neither ... nor ..."
<uig rom="tere inu üjebesü ekener inu cu ügei keüked inu cu ügei ajuγu">ᠲᠡᠷᠡ ᠢᠨᠤ ᠦᠵᠡᠪᠡᠰᠦ ᠡᠺᠡᠨᠡᠷ ᠢᠨᠤ ᠴᠤ ᠦᠭᠡᠢ ᠺᠡᠦᠺᠡᠳ ᠢᠨᠤ ᠴᠤ ᠦᠭᠡᠢ ᠠᠵᠤᠭᠤ</uig> When he looked, there were neither his wife nor his children
Interrogative pronouns with the particles <uig rom="cu">ᠴᠤ</uig> are indefinite. In negative sentences, they serve as negative indefinite pronouns.
<uig rom="alin cu">ᠠᠯᠢᠨ ᠴᠤ</uig> whosoever
<uig rom="ken cu">ᠺᠡᠨ ᠴᠤ</uig> whosoever
<uig rom="yaγun cu">ᠶᠠᠭᠤᠨ ᠴᠤ</uig> whatsoever
<uig rom="ken cu ese irebe">ᠺᠡᠨ ᠴᠤ ᠡᠰᠡ ᠢᠷᠡᠪᠡ</uig> Nobody came.
<uig rom="tende yaγun cu ügei bui">ᠲᠡᠨᠳᠡ ᠶᠠᠭᠤᠨ ᠴᠤ ᠦᠭᠡᠢ ᠪᠤᠢ</uig> There is nothing.
The past tense ending in <uig rom="-ba"> ᠎ᠪᠠ</uig> with the particle <uig rom="cu">ᠴᠤ</uig> is the converbum concessivum. The particle may be placed before the verb.
<uig rom="mangγus irebecü namayi olju ese cidamui">ᠮᠠᠩᠭᠤᠰ ᠢᠷᠡᠪᠡᠴᠦ ᠨᠠᠮᠠᠶᠢ ᠣᠯᠵᠤ ᠡᠰᠡ ᠴᠢᠳᠠᠮᠤᠢ</uig> Even if the Mangus comes, he will not be able to find me.
<uig rom="tere cu ükübe bi tegün-i erijü ocisuγai">ᠲᠡᠷᠡ ᠴᠤ ᠦᠺᠦᠪᠡ ᠪᠢ ᠲᠡᠭᠦᠨ ᠢ ᠡᠷᠢᠵᠦ ᠣᠴᠢᠰᠤᠭᠠᠢ</uig> Even if he died, I would go and seek him.

The imperative of the third person of the auxiliary verb <uig rom="a-">ᠠ ᠎</uig> "to be" and <uig rom="bol-">ᠪᠣᠯ ᠎</uig> "to become" with the particle <uig rom="cu">ᠴᠤ</uig> may be translated into English with the conjunctive "even if it be ..."
<uig rom="nadur morin keregtei bui. maγu cu atuγai bi absuγai">ᠨᠠᠳᠤᠷ ᠮᠣᠷᠢᠨ ᠺᠡᠷᠡᠭᠲᠡᠢ ᠪᠤᠢ᠅ ᠮᠠᠭᠤ ᠴᠤ ᠠᠲᠤᠭᠠᠢ ᠪᠢ ᠠᠪᠰᠤᠭᠠᠢ</uig> I need a horse. I shall take it even if it be a bad one.
The particle <uig rom="j-a">ᠵ᠎ᠠ</uig>, always written with the final letter for j and separately from its vowel, is placed after the word to which it refers.

This particle expresses doubt and is translated as "perhaps," "maybe." It occurs with the present tense ending in <uig rom="-mui"> ᠎ᠮᠤᠢ</uig> (or sometimes <uig rom="-m"> ᠎ᠮ</uig> ) and also with the defective verb <uig rom="bui">ᠪᠤᠢ</uig> .
The present tense with this particle is a potential (potentialis) which may be translated "it is possible that ...," "perhaps ..."
<uig rom="tngri ecige minu medemüi j-a">ᠲᠩᠷᠢ ᠡᠴᠢᠭᠡ ᠮᠢᠨᠤ ᠮᠡᠳᠡᠮᠦᠢ ᠵ ᠠ</uig> Probably my father, Heaven, knows.
<uig rom="tere inu marγasi irekü bui j-a">ᠲᠡᠷᠡ ᠢᠨᠤ ᠮᠠᠷᠭᠠᠰᠢ ᠢᠷᠡᠺᠦ ᠪᠤᠢ ᠵ ᠠ</uig> He will, perhaps, come tomorrow.
<uig rom="tere inu edüge tende bui j-a">ᠲᠡᠷᠡ ᠢᠨᠤ ᠡᠳᠦᠭᠡ ᠲᠡᠨᠳᠡ ᠪᠤᠢ ᠵ ᠠ</uig> He is now, perhaps, there.
The particle <uig rom="kü">ᠺᠦ</uig>, in emphatic pronunciation kö, stresses the meaning of the word to which it refers. This particle is also placed after the word to which it refers.
<uig rom="tere kü kümün">ᠲᠡᠷᠡ ᠺᠦ ᠺᠦᠮᠦᠨ</uig> precisely that man, that man indeed
<uig rom="ulaγan baγatur qotan-a ocimui kü">ᠤᠯᠠᠭᠠᠨ ᠪᠠᠭᠠᠲᠤᠷ ᠬᠣᠲᠠᠨ ᠠ ᠣᠴᠢᠮᠤᠢ ᠺᠦ</uig> I am really going to Ulan Bator.
The particle <uig rom="a">ᠠ</uig> or <uig rom="a-a">ᠠ ᠠ</uig> placed after the word to which it refers, is used in addressing people.
<uig rom="köbegün minu a">ᠺᠥᠪᠡᠭᠦᠨ ᠮᠢᠨᠤ ᠠ</uig> Ah, my son
The particle ᠡᠯᠡ , sometimes ᠯᠡ or la under the influence of the colloquial language, generalizes the meaning of the word to which it refers. It is placed after the word concerned.
<uig rom="sayin ele keüked">ᠰᠠᠶᠢᠨ ᠡᠯᠡ ᠺᠡᠦᠺᠡᠳ</uig> good girls in general
<uig rom="tere ele caγ-tur">ᠲᠡᠷᠡ ᠡᠯᠡ ᠴᠠᠭ ᠲᠤᠷ</uig> at that very time
This particle joins the converbum conditionale without changing its meaning (see § 664).
<uig rom="tere γajar-a iregsen abasu ele nököd inu ügei ajuγu">ᠲᠡᠷᠡ ᠭᠠᠵᠠᠷ ᠠ ᠢᠷᠡᠭᠰᠡᠨ ᠠᠪᠠᠰᠤ ᠡᠯᠡ ᠨᠥᠺᠥᠳ ᠢᠨᠤ ᠦᠭᠡᠢ ᠠᠵᠤᠭᠤ</uig> When he came to that place, his friends, as it turned out, had not been there
This is a colloquial particle and serves to emphasize the meaning of the word to which it refers. It is placed after the word concerned.
<uig rom="boluna da">ᠪᠣᠯᠤᠨᠠ ᠳᠠ</uig> (colloquial instead of <uig rom="bolumui j-a">ᠪᠣᠯᠤᠮᠤᠢ ᠵ ᠠ</uig>) It will be.

Wie in andern Sprachen, so auch im Mongolischen, haben viele Verba den Dativ der Person (das Zweckwort) und den Accusativ der Handlung oder des Gegenstandes (das Object), z. B. ᠮᠢᠨᠤ ᠡᠴᠡᠭᠡ ᠳ᠋ᠤᠷ ᠨᠢᠭᠡ ᠪᠢᠴᠢᠭ ᠪᠢᠴᠢᠪᠡᠢ er schrieb meinem Vater einen Brief,
ᠨᠠᠳᠤᠷ ᠨᠢᠭᠡ ᠮᠣᠷᠢ ᠥᠭᠪᠡᠢ er gab mir ein Pferd,
ᠴᠢᠮᠠᠳᠤᠷ ᠪᠤᠭᠤᠯ ᠢᠶᠠᠨ ᠢᠯᠡᠭᠡᠮᠦᠢ ich schicke dir meinen Sclaven,
ᠨᠠᠳᠤᠷ ᠦᠨᠡᠨ ᠢ ᠦᠭᠦᠯᠡ sage mir die Wahrheit!
Indessen können nicht alle Deutsche Sätze der Art auf die nämliche Weise im Mongolischen wiedergegeben werden.
So ist es z. B. nicht sehr sprachgemäss, zu sagen ᠨᠠᠳᠤᠷ ᠥᠪᠡᠷ ᠤᠨ ᠡᠴᠡᠭᠡ ᠶᠢᠨ ᠥᠺᠦᠯ ᠢ oder ᠦᠺᠦᠭᠰᠡᠨ ᠢ ᠮᠡᠳᠡᠭᠦᠯᠪᠡᠢ er meldete mir den Tod seines Vaters, sondern es heisst richtiger mit dem Gerundium ᠺᠡᠮᠡᠨ für die Conjunction dass (siehe §176) ᠮᠢᠨᠤ ᠡᠴᠡᠭᠡ ᠦᠺᠦᠪᠡᠢ ᠺᠡᠮᠡᠨ ᠨᠠᠳᠤᠷ ᠮᠡᠳᠡᠭᠦᠯᠪᠡᠢ er berichtete mir, dass sein Vater gestorben sey, oder wörtlich: mein Vater ist gestorben, also (sagend) er mir berichtete.

entry.title: Drittes Capitel - Regeln der Wortfügung oder Syntax - Rection des Verbi

paragraphs.paragraph: Der Accusativ als Object braucht nicht immer flectirt zu werden; er wird in dieser Eigenschaft häufig in der Form des Nominativs gefunden, ohne deshalb mit diesem verwechselt werden zu dürfen. Bei den, auf n ausgehenden, Hauptwörtern der zweiten Declination wird dieser mangelhafte Accusativ öfters dadurch kenntlich, dass bei ihm nebst der Casuspartikel ᠢ auch dieses End-n weggelassen wird, also ᠮᠣᠷᠢ statt ᠮᠣᠷᠢᠨ ᠢ; ᠮᠣᠳᠤ statt ᠮᠣᠳᠤᠨ ᠢ; ᠬᠣᠨᠢ statt ᠬᠣᠨᠢᠨ ᠢ; diess gilt indess nur vom ersten Accusativ und ist keineswegs allgemeine Regel, sondern höchstens erlaubte Willkühr; beim zweiten Accusativ, der das Pronomen possessivum vertritt, darf dessen Partikel ᠢᠶᠡᠨ oder ᠪᠠᠨ niemals wegbleiben (vergl. §48).

entry.title: Drittes Capitel - Regeln der Wortfügung oder Syntax - Rection des Verbi

paragraphs.paragraph: Als Object kann sich der Accusativ auch mit allen Activis verbinden, die den Locativ, ersten und zweiten Instrumental und den Ablativ regieren, welchen Declinationsfällen die Deutschen Präpositionen bei, zu, mit, nebst, nach, aus, von (mit dem Dativ), durch (mit dem Accusativ) und in, auf, an (mit dem Dativ und Accusativ) zum Grunde liegen. Hieraus folgt, dass, im Falle der Verbindung mit dem Object, die den Locativ und ersten Instrumental regierenden Verba entweder für Person und Sache den Dativ und Accusativ, oder auch für beide (Person und Sache) nur den Accusativ haben, wogegen der zweite Instrumental und der Ablativ stets den Dativ der Person mit dem Accusativ der Handlung oder Sache verbinden.

entry.title: Drittes Capitel - Regeln der Wortfügung oder Syntax - Rection des Verbi

paragraphs.paragraph:
Mit dem Locativ, der alle gebräuchlichen Flexionspartikeln des Dativs (siehe §46, §47 und §135) auf sich folgen lässt, dessen ungeachtet aber vom Dativ wohl unterschieden werden muss, verbinden sich alle diejenigen Verba, die sich auf irgend eine Oertlichkeit beziehen, oder eine thätige oder leidende Bewegung nach einem Orte anzeigen oder ausdrücken. Es sind diejenigen Verba, die im Deutschen mit den Präpositionen in, an, zu, nach, auf, bei gebraucht werden, es mögen solche Präpositionen übrigens den Dativ oder Accusativ regieren, z. B. ᠮᠢᠨᠤ ᠭᠡᠷ ᠲᠤᠷ in meinem Hause, ᠭᠡᠷ ᠲᠤᠷ ᠣᠷᠣ gehe in das Haus! ᠨᠠᠳᠤᠷ ᠢᠷᠡ komm zu mir! ᠭᠡᠷ ᠲᠤᠷ ᠰᠠᠭᠤ bleibe zu Hause! ᠨᠣᠳᠤᠭ ᠲᠤᠷ ᠺᠦᠷᠭᠡᠭᠴᠢ ᠵᠠᠮ der Weg nach der Heimath oder dem Wohnorte, ᠨᠥᠭᠡᠨ ᠳ᠋ᠤᠷ ᠬᠠᠶᠠ werfe es in das Loch! ᠮᠣᠳᠤᠨ ᠳ᠋ᠤᠷ ᠡᠯᠭᠦ hänge es an den Baum! ᠲᠡᠷᠭᠡᠨ ᠳ᠋ᠤᠷ ᠲᠠᠯᠪᠢ lege es auf den Wagen! ᠲᠡᠮᠡᠭᠡᠨ ᠳ᠋ᠤᠷ ᠠᠴᠢ lade es auf das Kameel! ᠤᠰᠤᠨ ᠳ᠋ᠤᠷ ᠣᠨᠣᠪᠠᠢ er fiel ins Wasser, ᠭᠠᠵᠠᠷ ᠲᠤᠷ ᠺᠡᠪᠳᠡᠮᠦᠢ er liegt auf der Erde, ᠭᠠᠵᠠᠷ ᠲᠤᠷ ᠪᠠᠭᠤᠪᠠᠢ er kam auf die Erde herab und viele andere.
Die Activa unter ihnen können nach §182 noch den Accusativ als Object annehmen, z. B. ᠬᠠᠷᠠ ᠴᠢᠯᠠᠭᠤᠨ ᠢ ᠤᠰᠤᠨ ᠳ᠋ᠤᠷ ᠬᠠᠶᠠᠪᠠᠢ er warf den schwarzen Stein ins Wasser, ᠬᠤᠪᠴᠠᠰᠤᠨ ᠢ ᠮᠣᠳᠤᠨ ᠳ᠋ᠤᠷ ᠡᠯᠭᠦᠪᠡᠢ er hing das Kleid an den Baum, ᠭᠡᠷ ᠤᠨ ᠪᠠᠷᠠᠭᠠ ᠶᠢ ᠲᠡᠮᠡᠭᠡᠨ ᠳ᠋ᠤᠷ ᠠᠴᠢᠪᠠᠢ er lud das Hausgeräthe auf das Kameel.

entry.title: Drittes Capitel - Regeln der Wortfügung oder Syntax - Rection des Verbi

paragraphs.paragraph:
Mit dem Ablativ und dessen Postposition ᠡᠴᠡ stehen alle diejenigen Verba, die im Deutschen mit der Präposition von und aus gebraucht werden, mit Ausnahme jedoch der nach §179 mit der Präposition von stehenden Passiva. Von diesen Verbis stehen im Mongolischen mehrere ausschliesslich im Ablativ, als ᠬᠠᠭᠠᠴᠠᠬᠤ sich trennen, ᠭᠠᠷᠬᠤ hinausgehen, ᠵᠠᠶᠢᠯᠠᠬᠤ ausweichen, ᠳᠣᠳᠠᠭᠠᠬᠤ fliehen (sowohl aus der Schlacht als vor dem Feinde); andere können auch zugleich mit dem Locativ stehen, als ᠢᠷᠡᠺᠦ kommen, ᠪᠠᠭᠤᠬᠤ herabkommen, ᠤᠨᠠᠬᠤ fallen, z. B. ᠺᠢᠲᠠᠳ ᠭᠠᠵᠠᠷ ᠡᠴᠡ ᠣᠷᠣᠰ ᠲᠤᠷ ᠢᠷᠡᠪᠡᠢ er kam aus China nach Russland, ᠣᠭᠲᠠᠷᠭᠤᠢ ᠡᠴᠡ ᠭᠠᠵᠠᠷ ᠲᠤᠷ ᠪᠠᠭᠤᠪᠠᠢ er kam vom Himmel auf die Erde herab, ᠮᠣᠳᠤᠨ ᠡᠴᠡ ᠤᠰᠤᠨ ᠳ᠋ᠤᠷ ᠣᠨᠤᠪᠠᠢ er fiel vom Baum ins Wasser.
Die Activa unter ihnen, als ᠠᠪᠬᠤ nehmen, ᠤᠳᠬᠠᠬᠤ schöpfen, ᠲᠠᠯᠪᠢᠬᠤ entlassen, loslassen, ᠲᠠᠳᠠᠬᠤ ziehen u. s. w. können auch den Accusativ als Object annehmen, z. B. ᠡᠴᠡᠭᠡ ᠡᠴᠡ ᠮᠥᠩᠭᠦ ᠠᠪᠬᠤ vom Vater Geld nehmen oder empfangen, ᠬᠤᠳᠳᠤᠭ ᠡᠴᠡ ᠤᠰᠤᠨ ᠣᠳᠬᠤᠬᠤ Wasser aus dem Brunnen schöpfen, ᠺᠦᠮᠦᠨ ᠢ ᠺᠢᠨᠳᠠᠨ ᠡᠴᠡ ᠲᠠᠯᠪᠢᠬᠤ den Menschen der Haft entlassen, ᠺᠡᠭᠦᠷ ᠢ ᠤᠰᠤᠨ ᠡᠴᠡ ᠲᠠᠳᠠᠬᠤ den Leichnam aus dem Wasser ziehen.
Da die Causalform, nach §90 und §127, die Neutra öfters transitiv macht, so gewinnt die Rection der aus mehreren, mit dem Ablativ stehenden, Neutris gebildeten Causal-Activa dadurch an Umfang. So können zum Beispiel die Verba ᠭᠠᠷᠬᠤ hinausgehen, ᠬᠠᠭᠠᠴᠠᠬᠤ sich trennen, ᠵᠠᠶᠢᠯᠠᠬᠤ ausweichen nur mit dem Ablativ stehen, ihre Causalia aber nehmen auch den Accusativ als Object an, z. B. ᠭᠡᠷ ᠳᠣᠲᠣᠷᠠ ᠠ ᠎ᠴᠠ ᠬᠠᠮᠤᠭ ᠬᠠᠭᠤᠴᠢᠨ ᠵᠠᠭᠠᠮ ᠠ ᠶᠢ ᠭᠠᠷᠭᠠᠪᠠᠢ er hat alles Alte aus dem Hause herausgeschafft, ᠮᠥᠷᠡᠨ ᠢᠨᠤ ᠬᠣᠶᠠᠷ ᠭᠠᠵᠠᠷ ᠢ ᠬᠠᠭᠠᠴᠠᠭᠤᠯᠮᠤᠢ der Strom trennt zwei Länder (von einander), ᠬᠠᠮᠤᠭ ᠢᠮᠠᠭ ᠠᠮᠠᠷᠠᠭ ᠤᠳ ᠢ ᠪᠡᠶ ᠡ ᠡᠴᠡ ᠵᠠᠶᠢᠯᠠᠭᠤᠯᠪᠠᠢ er hat alle Freunde von sich entfernt.
Die Causalia der Neutra ᠢᠷᠡᠺᠦ kommen, ᠪᠠᠭᠤᠬᠤ herabkommen, ᠤᠨᠠᠬᠤ fallen, können ihrer Eigenschaft nach überdiess noch den Locativ nebst dem ersten Instrumental annehmen, z. B. ᠪᠢ ᠲᠡᠭᠦᠦ ᠎ᠪᠡᠨ ᠺᠢᠲᠠᠳ ᠭᠠᠵᠠᠷ ᠡᠴᠡ ᠣᠷᠣᠰ ᠲᠤᠷ ᠢᠷᠡᠭᠦᠯᠪᠡᠢ ich liess meinen jüngern Bruder aus China nach Russland kommen, ᠠᠷᠭᠠᠮᠵᠢ ᠪᠡᠷ ᠺᠦᠪᠡᠭᠦᠨ ᠢᠶᠡᠨ ᠳᠡᠭᠡᠯᠪᠦᠷ ᠡᠴᠡ ᠭᠠᠵᠠᠷ ᠲᠤᠷ ᠪᠠᠭᠤᠯᠭᠠᠪᠠᠢ er liess seinen Knaben an einem Strick (vermittelst eines Strickes) vom Dache auf die Erde herab, ᠰᠤᠮᠤᠨ ᠢᠶᠠᠷ ᠴᠢᠨᠤ ᠠ ᠶᠢ ᠡᠷᠺᠢᠨ ᠡᠴᠡ ᠤᠰᠤᠨ ᠳ᠋ᠤᠷ ᠤᠨᠠᠭᠠᠪᠠᠢ er stürzte den Wolf durch einen Pfeilschuss vom Ufer ins Wasser hinab.

entry.title: Drittes Capitel - Regeln der Wortfügung oder Syntax - Rection des Verbi

paragraphs.paragraph: Der Ablativ wird statt des Locativs auch häufig da gebraucht, wo im Deutschen die Präpositionen bei oder an stehen, wo nämlich eine nähere Erklärung der Handlung oder des Objectes ausgedrückt wird, z. B. ᠨᠠᠮᠠᠶᠢ ᠭᠠᠷ ᠡᠴᠡ ᠪᠠᠷᠢᠪᠠᠢ er fasste mich bei den Händen (meine Hände), ᠨᠣᠬᠠᠢ ᠶᠢ ᠰᠡᠭᠦᠯ ᠡᠴᠡ ᠲᠠᠳᠠᠪᠠᠢ er zog den Hund beim (am) Schwanze, ᠺᠥᠯ ᠡᠴᠡ ᠮᠣᠳᠤᠨ ᠳ᠋ᠤᠷ ᠡᠯᠭᠦᠪᠡᠢ er hing ihn bei den Füssen an den Baum.

entry.title: Drittes Capitel - Regeln der Wortfügung oder Syntax - Rection des Verbi

paragraphs.paragraph: Der erste Instrumental verbindet sich mit solchen Verben, bei welchen im Deutschen die Präpositionen durch, mit, vermittelst, vermöge gebraucht werden (s. §137), z. B. ᠣᠯᠵᠠ ᠪᠠᠷ ᠪᠠᠶᠠᠵᠢᠪᠠᠢ er ist durch Beute reich geworden, ᠲᠡᠷᠭᠡᠨ ᠢᠶᠡᠷ ᠢᠷᠡᠺᠦ zu Wagen (vermittelst eines Wagens) kommen, ᠭᠠᠷ ᠢᠶᠠᠷ ᠪᠠᠷᠢᠬᠤ mit der Hand greifen, ᠦᠰᠦᠭ ᠢᠶᠡᠷ ᠪᠢᠴᠢᠺᠦ mit der Feder schreiben, ᠭᠠᠯ ᠢᠶᠠᠷ ᠲᠦᠯᠡᠺᠦ mit Feuer verbrennen, ᠺᠦᠷᠵᠡ ᠪᠡᠷ ᠡᠷᠦᠺᠦ mit der Schaufel graben u. s. w. Auch von diesen Verben können sich mehrere mit dem Accusativ als Object verbinden, z. B. ᠵᠢᠭᠠᠰᠤᠨ ᠢ ᠭᠠᠷ ᠢᠶᠠᠷ ᠪᠠᠷᠢᠪᠠᠢ er ergriff den Fisch mit den Händen, ᠺᠦᠷᠵᠡ ᠪᠡᠷ ᠨᠥᠭᠡᠨ ᠢ ᠡᠷᠦᠪᠡᠢ oder ᠮᠡᠯᠳᠡᠪᠡᠢ er grub mit der Schaufel ein Loch, ferner auch zugleich mit dem Dativ, z. B. ᠪᠢ ᠠᠬᠠ ᠳ᠋ᠠᠭᠠᠨ ᠡᠯᠴᠢ ᠪᠡᠷ ᠮᠥᠩᠺᠦ ᠢᠯᠡᠭᠡᠪᠡᠢ ich schickte meinem ältern Bruder Geld durch einen Boten; oder auch mit dem Locativ, als: ᠺᠦᠷᠵᠡ ᠪᠡᠷ ᠭᠠᠵᠠᠷ ᠲᠤᠷ ᠨᠥᠭᠡᠨ ᠢ ᠮᠡᠯᠳᠡᠪᠡᠢ er grub mit der Schaufel ein Loch in die Erde; oder auch nach §185 mit dem Ablativ: ᠵᠢᠭᠠᠰᠤᠨ ᠢ ᠰᠡᠭᠦᠯ ᠡᠴᠡ ᠭᠠᠷ ᠢᠶᠠᠷ ᠪᠡᠷᠢᠪᠠᠢer ergriff den Fisch mit den Händen beim Schwanz. Viele Verba, die als Primitiva einen andern Casus regieren, werden durch die Causalform mit dem ersten Instrumental verbunden, z. B. ᠪᠤᠭᠤᠯ ᠢᠶᠠᠷ ᠢᠶᠠᠨ ᠠᠪᠬᠤᠭᠤᠯᠪᠠᠢ ich liess es durch meinen Sclaven holen, ᠳᠥᠯᠭᠢᠭᠦᠷ ᠢᠶᠡᠷ ᠡᠭᠦᠳᠡᠨ ᠢ ᠨᠡᠭᠡᠯᠭᠡᠪᠡᠢ er liess vermittelst eines Schlüssels die Thüre öffnen, ᠪᠢᠴᠢᠭ ᠢ ᠪᠢᠴᠢᠭᠴᠢ ᠪᠡᠷ ᠪᠢᠴᠢᠭᠦᠯᠪᠡᠢ er liess den Brief durch einen Schreiber schreiben.

entry.title: Drittes Capitel - Regeln der Wortfügung oder Syntax - Rection des Verbi

paragraphs.paragraph: I. Sounds and letters.

We make our thoughts and ideas understandable to others by the use of words. Words are made up of sounds. Sounds are made by the sound governing organs; that is, the lungs, trachea, larynx, palate, tongue and lips.

That which symbolizes a sound on paper is called a letter. Our Mongol letters have come with modification from the Turkish letters. The original Turkish letters came from a branch of the Persian; that is, the Sogdian and upon further search it will be found that many of them are derivatives from European languages.

Because many of the Mongol letters, while having the same appearance, have different sounds, it is not always possible to write the word according to its true sound. So the Mongol written language up until the present in regard to becoming like the spoken has changed very little. For this reason our written language is very different from the spoken language.

This has been a very great hindrance and difficulty to the development of the cultural standard of the common people. If we wish to correct these problems at their source, it will be necessary to use new letters. But until that time we will have to use the old letters according to their correct usage and beyond this it will also be

entry.title: FIRST SECTION: REGARDING SOUNDS AND LETTERS
entry.title2: FIRST SECTION: REGARDING SOUNDS AND LETTERS - Sounds and letters

navigation.group: FIRST SECTION: REGARDING SOUNDS AND LETTERS

paragraphs.paragraph: II. Alphabet.
Comments: Some characters have definite names.
The letter <uig rom="">‍ᠠ‍</uig> is called <uig rom="">ᠠᠴᠤᠬ</uig> or <uig rom="">ᠨᠢᠳᠦ</uig> "tooth".
The letter <uig rom="">ᠵ‍</uig> is called <uig rom="">ᠰᠢᠯᠪᠢ</uig> or <uig rom="">ᠤᠷᠲᠤ ᠰᠢᠯᠪᠢ</uig> "long tooth".
The letter <uig rom="">‍᠊ᠡ</uig> is called <uig rom="">ᠣᠷᠺᠢᠴᠠ</uig> or <uig rom="">ᠬᠣᠶᠢᠰᠢ ᠪᠠᠨ ᠰᠡᠭᠦᠯ</uig> "backward tail".
The letter <uig rom="">᠎ᠠ</uig> is called <uig rom="">ᠴᠠᠴᠤᠯᠭ᠎ᠠ</uig> "offshoot".
The letter <uig rom="">᠊ᠣ</uig> is called <uig rom="">ᠭᠡᠳᠡᠰᠦ</uig> "naught", "abdomen".
The · of the letter <uig rom="">ᠨ</uig> is called <uig rom="">ᠴᠡᠭ</uig> or <uig rom="">ᠨᠢᠭᠡ ᠴᠡᠭ</uig> "dot".
The ∶ of the letter <uig rom="">ᠭ</uig> is called <uig rom="">ᠳᠤᠰᠤᠯ</uig> or <uig rom="">ᠬᠣᠶᠠᠷ ᠴᠡᠭ</uig> "two dots".

entry.title: FIRST SECTION: REGARDING SOUNDS AND LETTERS
entry.title2: FIRST SECTION: REGARDING SOUNDS AND LETTERS - Alphabet

navigation.group: FIRST SECTION: REGARDING SOUNDS AND LETTERS

paragraphs.paragraph: Der erste Instrumental wird auch bisweilen da gebraucht, wo im Deutschen die Präpositionen nach, gemäss, in Folge stehen, z. B. ᠮᠢᠨᠤ ᠦᠭᠡ ᠪᠡᠷ ᠦᠯᠦ ᠪᠣᠯᠤᠮᠤᠢer gehorcht mir nicht; wörtlich: er wird nicht (will nicht handeln) nach meinen Worten, welches aber auch mit dem Locativ heissen kann ᠮᠢᠨᠤ ᠦᠭᠡ ᠳ᠋ᠤᠷ ᠦᠯᠦ ᠣᠷᠤᠮᠤᠢ er geht nicht in meine Worte ein; ferner ᠲᠠᠨᠤ ᠵᠠᠷᠯᠢᠭ ᠢᠶᠠᠷ ᠲᠡᠭᠦᠰᠭᠡᠪᠡᠢ Euerm Befehle gemäss habe ich (es) vollendet; oder in Verbindung mit dem Object ᠲᠠᠨᠤ ᠵᠠᠷᠯᠢᠭ ᠢᠶᠠᠷ ᠳᠠᠭᠠᠯᠭᠠᠭᠰᠠᠨ ᠦᠢᠯᠡ ᠶᠢ ᠪᠦᠲᠦᠭᠡᠪᠡᠢ Euerm Befehle gemäss habe ich das aufgetragene Geschäft ausgeführt.

entry.title: Drittes Capitel - Regeln der Wortfügung oder Syntax - Rection des Verbi

paragraphs.paragraph:
Der zweite Instrumental steht mit solchen Verben, die eine Vereinigung oder Verbindung, oder eine gemeinschaftliche Handlung, oder auch eine Mischung zweier oder mehrerer Materien andeuten, welche Verba im Deutschen gemeiniglich die Präposition mit oder nebst haben. Die meisten derselben sind, wie ihre Natur es schon mit sich bringt, Cooperativa; indess finden sich unter ihnen auch einige wenige Primitiva und Causalia, als z. B. ᠪᠠᠯ ᠎ᠯᠤᠭᠠ ᠨᠡᠶᠢᠯᠡᠭᠦᠯᠦᠭᠰᠡᠨ ᠤᠰᠤᠨ mit Honig vermischtes Wasser, ᠴᠢᠨᠤ ᠠ ᠯᠤᠭ ᠠ ᠤᠴᠢᠷᠠᠬᠤ einem Wolfe begegnen (mit ihm zusammentreffen), ᠮᠠᠭᠤ ᠺᠦᠮᠦᠨ ᠯᠦᠭᠡ ᠨᠥᠭᠦᠴᠡᠺᠦ sich mit einem schlechten Menschen verbinden (dessen Freund oder Gefährte werden), ᠪᠢ ᠲᠡᠭᠦᠦ ᠪᠡᠨ ᠪᠣᠭᠤᠯ ᠎ᠯᠤᠭᠠ ᠶᠠᠪᠤᠭᠤᠯᠪᠠᠢ ich entliess meinen jüngern Bruder mit einem (in Begleitung eines) Sclaven.
Zu den Cooperativen, die mit dem zweiten Instrumental stehen, gehören ᠣᠳᠤᠯᠴᠠᠬᠤ mit einander kommen, ᠢᠷᠡᠯᠴᠡᠺᠦ zusammen kommen, ᠡᠪᠳᠡᠷᠡᠯᠳᠡᠺᠦ unter sich zerfallen, sich veruneinigen, ᠢᠨᠢᠶᠡᠯᠳᠡᠺᠦ mit einander lachen, ᠣᠶᠢᠯᠠᠯᠳᠠᠬᠤ oder ᠣᠶᠢᠯᠠᠯᠴᠠᠬᠤ mit einander weinen, ᠭᠡᠷᠡᠯᠳᠡᠺᠦ sich zanken, und viele andere Intransitiva mehr.
Die aus Activis gebildeten Cooperativa behalten die Eigenthümlichkeit ihrer Primitiva, ausser dem zweiten Instrumental auch den Accusativ zu regieren, z. B. ᠪᠢ ᠠᠬᠠ ᠲᠡᠭᠦᠦ ᠯᠦᠭᠡ ᠴᠢᠨᠤ ᠠ ᠶᠢ ᠦᠵᠡᠯᠴᠡᠪᠡᠢ ich und meine Brüder sahen den Wolf, ᠴᠢᠭᠤᠯᠠᠭᠰᠠᠳ ᠪᠡᠷ ᠱᠠᠪᠢᠨᠠᠷ ᠎ᠯᠤᠭᠠ ᠰᠡᠯᠲᠡ ᠪᠠᠭᠰᠢ ᠶᠢᠨ ᠵᠠᠷᠯᠢᠭ ᠢ ᠮᠠᠭᠳᠠᠯᠴᠠᠪᠠᠢ die Versammlung lobte im Verein mit den Schülern die Worte des Lehrers. Wird die gemeinschaftliche Handlung durch die Zahl der Handelnden bestimmt, so fällt sowohl bei transitiven als intransitiven Verben der zweite Instrumental weg, z. B. ᠪᠢᠳᠡ ᠬᠣᠶᠠᠭᠤᠯᠠ ᠴᠢᠨᠤ ᠠ ᠶᠢ ᠦᠵᠡᠯᠴᠡᠪᠡᠢ wir beide sahen den Wolf, ᠡᠳᠡ ᠭᠤᠷᠪᠠᠭᠤᠯᠠ ᠡᠪᠳᠡᠷᠡᠯᠳᠡᠪᠡᠢ sie oder alle Drei veruneinigten sich, ᠲᠠᠪᠤᠨ ᠡᠮ ᠡ ᠬᠤᠭᠤᠷ ᠳᠤᠮᠳᠠ ᠪᠠᠨ ᠭᠡᠷᠡᠯᠳᠡᠪᠡᠢ fünf Weiber zankten sich mit einander.

entry.title: Drittes Capitel - Regeln der Wortfügung oder Syntax - Rection des Verbi

paragraphs.paragraph: Da die einzelnen Postpositionen ᠳᠤᠷ, ᠡ, ᠲᠠᠭᠠᠨ, ᠢᠶᠠᠷ oder ᠪᠡᠷ, ᠯᠤᠭᠠ und ᠡᠴᠡ blos den Casus regieren, dem sie angehören und den sie bezeichnen, alle übrige aber den Genitiv oder den Locativ, so ist zu dem bereits §133 ff. Gesagten hier nichts Besonderes hinzuzufügen. Es stehe hier blos die Bemerkung, dass wenn mehrere Substantiva eine und dieselbe Postposition haben, diese nicht bei jedem Substantivum wiederholt werden darf, sondern nach der §159 erörterten Regel nur dem letzten nachgesetzt werden kann, z. B. ᠤᠬᠠᠭᠠᠨ ᠪᠢᠯᠢᠭ ᠺᠢᠭᠡᠳ ᠪᠤᠶᠠᠨ ᠢᠶᠠᠷ ᠢᠨᠤ ᠺᠦᠨᠳᠦᠯᠡᠯ ᠺᠢᠭᠡᠳ ᠠᠯᠲᠠᠷ ᠪᠠ ᠴᠤᠯᠠ ᠳ᠋ᠤᠷ ᠺᠦᠷᠪᠡᠢ durch Verstand, Weisheit und Tugend ist er zu Ehre, Ruhm und Würden gelangt. Die Subject-Partikel ᠢᠨᠤ nach dem ersten Instrumental steht hier nach §174 statt des persönlichen Fürwortes er, welches in diesem Satze das Subject bildet.

entry.title: Drittes Capitel - Regeln der Wortfügung oder Syntax - Rection des Verbi
Drittes Capitel - Regeln der Wortfügung oder Syntax - Bildung der Sätze

paragraphs.paragraph: Der reine Redesatz besteht, wie in andern Sprachen, aus dem Subject, dem Prädicat und der Copula, in der angegebenen Folgeordnung, z. B. ᠰᠢᠪᠠᠭᠤᠨ ᠠᠨᠤ ᠨᠢᠰᠦᠮᠦᠢ der Vogel fliegt, oder ᠰᠢᠪᠠᠭᠤᠨ ᠠᠨᠤ ᠨᠢᠰᠤᠨ ᠠᠮᠤᠢ der Vogel fliegend ist; ferner ᠭᠡᠷ ᠢᠨᠤ ᠶᠡᠺᠡ das Haus (ist) gross, oder ᠭᠡᠷ ᠢᠨᠤ ᠶᠡᠺᠡ ᠪᠤᠢ das Haus gross ist.

entry.title: Drittes Capitel - Regeln der Wortfügung oder Syntax - Bildung der Sätze

paragraphs.paragraph: Dieselbe Ordnung findet auch bei solchen zusammengesetzten reinen Sätzen Statt, wo mehrere Subjecte mit einem Prädicat verbunden werden, z. B. ᠮᠢᠬᠠᠨ ᠴᠢᠰᠤᠨ ᠠᠷᠢᠰᠤᠨ ᠺᠢᠭᠡᠳ ᠵᠠᠰᠤᠨ ᠠᠨᠤ ᠺᠦᠮᠦᠨ ᠤ ᠪᠡᠶ ᠡ ᠶᠢᠨ ᠺᠡᠰᠢᠭᠦᠳ ᠪᠤᠢ Fleisch, Blut, Haut und Knochen sind Bestandtheile des menschlichen Körpers.

entry.title: Drittes Capitel - Regeln der Wortfügung oder Syntax - Bildung der Sätze

paragraphs.paragraph: Das Subject ist entweder ein Substantivum, wozu auch die Participia und Infinitive gerechnet werden, oder ein Pronomen; ist es ein Adjectivum, so erhält dieses die volle Bedeutung eines Substantivs, z. B. ᠴᠠᠭᠠᠨ ᠠᠨᠤ ᠬᠠᠷᠠ ᠪᠤᠰᠤ weiss (das Weisse) ist nicht schwarz, ᠰᠠᠶᠢᠨ ᠠᠨᠤ ᠲᠤᠰᠠᠲᠤ ᠴᠤ ᠪᠤᠢ gut (das Gute) ist zugleich nützlich. Das Subject wird gewöhnlich, nach §44 und §174, durch die Partikeln ᠠᠨᠤ, ᠢᠨᠤ oder ᠪᠡᠷ die es meistens, jedoch nicht immer, unmittelbar auf sich folgen lässt, kenntlich gemacht. Folgen diese Partikeln auf einen andern Casus als den Nominativ, so ersetzen sie gemeiniglich ein mit dem Satze verschmolzenes Pronomen, in welchem das Subject liegt, vergl. §174 und §189.

entry.title: Drittes Capitel - Regeln der Wortfügung oder Syntax - Bildung der Sätze

paragraphs.paragraph: Das Prädicat ist entweder ein adjectivisches Verbum, als ᠰᠠᠨᠠᠮᠤᠢ er denkt oder ᠰᠠᠨᠠᠨ ᠠᠮᠤᠢ er ist denkend, oder ein Substantivum mit der Copula, als ᠺᠦᠮᠦᠨ ᠪᠤᠢ er ist ein Mensch.

entry.title: Drittes Capitel - Regeln der Wortfügung oder Syntax - Bildung der Sätze

paragraphs.paragraph:
Die Copula ist ein wichtiger und durchaus unentbehrlicher Satztheil für die an Conjunctionen so arme Mongolische Sprache. Sie kann sich zwar bisweilen mit dem Prädicat verschmelzen, tritt jedoch weit öfter sehr bestimmt hervor, und gibt den, oft durch viele Sätze fortlaufenden und nicht selten sehr verwickelten, Perioden ihre Rundung und Verständlichkeit. Wenn sie nicht mit dem Prädicat in der Form des Präsens, Imperfects oder Perfects verschmolzen ist, als ᠺᠡᠦᠺᠡᠨ ᠢᠨᠤ ᠢᠳᠡᠮᠦᠢ oder ᠢᠳᠡᠪᠡᠢ oder ᠢᠳᠡᠯᠦᠭᠡ das Kind isst oder ass oder hat gegessen, so zeigt sie sich immer in irgend einer Form eines Hülfsverbi, und zwar vorzüglich des Verbi ᠪᠦᠺᠦ seyn (siehe §118). Die gebräuchlichsten Formen desselben am Schlusse eines reinen Satzes sind ᠪᠤᠢ ist, welches oft mit dem gleichbedeutenden ᠪᠤᠶᠤ abwechselt, ᠪᠣᠯᠠᠢ ist, war, und ᠪᠦᠯᠦᠭᠡ war, ist gewesen, z. B. ᠺᠦᠮᠦᠨ ᠢᠨᠤ ᠠᠮᠢᠲᠠᠨ ᠤ ᠡᠷᠺᠢᠨ ᠪᠤᠢ᠃ ᠲᠡᠳᠡᠭᠡᠷ ᠤᠨ ᠡᠷᠺᠢᠨ ᠮᠥᠨ ᠪᠦᠺᠦ ᠶᠢᠨ ᠲᠤᠯᠠ᠃ ᠲᠡᠭᠦᠨ ᠤ ᠡᠷᠳᠡᠮ ᠤᠳ ᠴᠤ ᠶᠡᠺᠡ ᠪᠤᠶᠤ der Mensch ist das Vornehmste der Wesen; weil er das Vornehmste derselben (ihrer) ist, so sind seine Vorzüge auch gross. Im zweiten Satze, dem Hauptsatze zum dritten oder Nebensatze, erscheint die Copula im Infinitiv des genannten Verbi mit dem Genitiv, in Verbindung mit der Postposition ᠲᠤᠯᠠ, zum Ersatz der Conjunction weil (vergl. §98 und §155, a.). Solche leicht zu vermeidende Wiederholungen des bereits Gesagten, wovon der zweite Satz ein Beispiel liefert, finden sich übrigens in Mongolischen Schriften nicht selten.
— Die Copula ᠪᠣᠯᠠᠢ wird häufig da gebraucht, wo eben so gut ᠪᠤᠢ oder ᠪᠤᠶᠤ stehen könnte; sie findet sich meist am Ende einer Periode, oder auch, wo etwas längst Bestehendes und Unabänderliches ausgedrückt werden soll, z. B. ᠣᠭᠲᠠᠷᠭᠤᠢ ᠠᠨᠤ ᠲᠩᠷᠢ ᠎ᠨᠠᠷ ᠤᠨ ᠣᠷᠣᠨ ᠪᠣᠯᠠᠢ der Himmel ist der Sitz der Götter, ᠬᠤᠰᠤᠨ ᠺᠡᠮᠡᠺᠦ ᠢᠨᠤ ᠨᠢᠭᠡᠨ ᠮᠣᠳᠤᠨ ᠤ ᠨᠡᠷ ᠡ ᠪᠣᠯᠠᠢ Birke ist der Name eines Baumes; dagegen bezieht sich ᠪᠦᠯᠦᠭᠡ immer auf etwas Gewesenes oder Geschehenes, z. B. ᠡᠷᠲᠡ ᠴᠠᠭ ᠲᠤᠷ ᠡᠨᠡᠳᠺᠡᠭ ᠤᠨ ᠳᠤᠮᠳᠠ ᠎ᠳᠤ ᠣᠷᠣᠨ ᠳ᠋ᠤᠷ ᠨᠢᠭᠡ ᠬᠠᠭᠠᠨ ᠪᠦᠯᠦᠭᠡ in früher Zeit (vor Alters) war (lebte) im Mittelreiche Indiens ein König.

entry.title: Drittes Capitel - Regeln der Wortfügung oder Syntax - Bildung der Sätze

paragraphs.paragraph:
Auch das Hülfsverbum ᠠᠬᠤ seyn, vornehmlich das Präsens und Imperfectum desselben, dient zur Bildung der Copula, wenn das Prädicat ein adjectivisches Verbum oder Gerundium ist. Zwar ist sie meistens mit dem Präsens oder Imperfectum eines solchen Verbi verschmolzen, sie tritt jedoch nicht selten auch bestimmt hervor (vergl. §96). Eine besondere, häufig vorkommende, Copula-Bildung des genannten Hülfsverbi ist die Form ᠠᠵᠢᠭᠤ oder ᠠᠵᠤᠭᠤ, die sich auf vorausgesetztes, vermuthetes oder anscheinliches Seyn bezieht, und in welcher eine, keine Antwort fordernde, Halbfrage verborgen zu liegen scheint, z. B. ᠰᠠᠶᠢᠨ ᠺᠦᠮᠦᠨ ᠠᠵᠢᠭᠤ er ist (scheint zu seyn) ein guter Mensch, ᠡᠨᠡ ᠪᠡᠷ ᠢᠵᠠᠭᠤᠷᠲᠠᠨ ᠤ ᠺᠥᠪᠡᠭᠦᠨ ᠠᠵᠤᠭᠤ dieser ist (scheint zu seyn) von hoher Geburt (ein Sohn der Götter). *)

*) Siehe Saanang Ssetsen's Geschichte der Ostmongolen, S. 56.

entry.title: Drittes Capitel - Regeln der Wortfügung oder Syntax - Bildung der Sätze

paragraphs.paragraph: Wenn in einem Satze sich mehrere Verba als Prädicate befinden, so werden diese gewöhnlich durch die verschiedenen Formen des Gerundii mit einander verbunden, z. B. ᠺᠦᠮᠦᠨ ᠨᠥᠺᠦᠳ ᠲᠥᠷᠦᠭᠡᠳ ᠦᠰᠦᠨ ᠪᠠᠶᠢᠵᠤ ᠦᠳᠡᠯᠡᠭᠡᠳ ᠦᠺᠦᠮᠦᠢ oder ᠦᠺᠦᠳᠡᠭ die Menschen werden geboren, wachsen, altern und sterben (wörtlich: die Menschen geboren seyend, fortwachsend, gealtert seyend sterben).

entry.title: Drittes Capitel - Regeln der Wortfügung oder Syntax - Bildung der Sätze

paragraphs.paragraph: In Sätzen, wo eine Gradbestimmung oder Vergleichung Statt findet, steht der zur Vergleichung genommene, und im Deutschen durch die Conjunctionen als, wie verbundene, Theil nach §149, a) und §58 allemal im Ablativ, z. B. ᠬᠣᠨᠤᠯᠲᠠᠢ ᠰᠡᠳᠺᠢᠯ ᠢᠨᠤ ᠣᠯᠠᠨ ᠡᠳ᠋ ᠠᠭᠤᠷᠠᠰᠤᠨ ᠡᠴᠡ ᠦᠯᠡᠮᠵᠢ ᠳᠡᠭᠡᠷ ᠡein zufriedenes Gemüth ist mehr werth als viele Güter.

entry.title: Drittes Capitel - Regeln der Wortfügung oder Syntax - Bildung der Sätze

paragraphs.paragraph: In ausgebildeten Sätzen oder in solchen, wo ausser den genannten Satztheilen noch das Object (im Acc.) und das Zweckwort (im Dat.) oder auch solche Wörter vorkommen, welche zur nähern Bezeichnung oder Ausschmückung des Subjects und Prädicats dienen, brauchen diese Satztheile nicht immer nach einer und der nämlichen Ordnung auf einander zu folgen; für das Prädicat und die Copula, letztere mag für sich stehen oder mit dem Prädicat verschmolzen seyn, bleibt es bei prosaischen Schriften indess feste Regel, dass sie immer den Schluss des Satzes bilden müssen, z. B. ᠴᠢᠮᠠᠳᠤᠷ ᠨᠢᠭᠡ ᠪᠢᠴᠢᠭ ᠪᠢᠴᠢᠮᠦᠢ ich schreibe dir einen Brief (wörtlich: dir einen Brief ich schreibe), ᠪᠠᠶᠠᠨ ᠡᠴᠡᠭᠡ ᠢᠨᠤ ᠦᠵᠡᠰᠺᠦᠯᠡᠩ ᠎ᠲᠦ ᠥᠺᠢᠨ ᠢᠶᠡᠨ ᠪᠠᠶᠠᠨ ᠺᠦᠮᠦᠨ ᠡᠴᠡ ᠪᠤᠰᠤᠳ ᠲᠤᠷ ᠦᠯᠦ ᠥᠭᠭᠦᠮᠦᠢ oder ᠥᠭᠭᠦᠶᠦ der reiche Vater gibt seine schöne Tochter keinem andern als einem reichen Manne, (wörtlich: der reiche Vater seine schöne Tochter als einem reichen Manne Andern nicht gibt oder will geben). In der Poesie und ihrer Satzordnung herrscht, je nach dem Bedürfnisse des Metrum, die grösste Willkühr, und es steht dabei manchmal buchstäblich das Unterste zu Oben.

entry.title: Drittes Capitel - Regeln der Wortfügung oder Syntax - Bildung der Sätze

paragraphs.paragraph: Haupt- und Nebensätze werden im Mongolischen, das nur wenige Bindewörter und gar keine beziehende Fürwörter (relativa) hat (vergl. §75), theils durch die den Genitiv regierende Postposition ᠲᠤᠯᠠ weil, um-willen, theils durch die Participia gebildet und mit einander verbunden oder zusammengezogen, z. B. ᠭᠠᠵᠠᠷ ᠠᠨᠤ ᠬᠠᠮᠤᠭ ᠪᠦᠭᠦᠳᠡ ᠶᠢ ᠲᠠᠵᠢxᠠᠨ ᠪᠦᠺᠦ ᠶᠢᠨ ᠲᠤᠯᠠᠳᠠ ᠬᠠᠮᠤᠭ ᠠᠮᠢᠲᠠᠨ ᠤ ᠡᠺᠡ ᠴᠤ ᠪᠤᠢ die Erde ist die Mutter aller lebenden Wesen, weil sie Alles ernährt, (wörtlich: die Erde, Alles ernährend weil sie ist, aller Wesen Mutter auch ist), (vergl. das Beispiel §194), ᠨᠠᠳᠤᠷ ᠰᠠᠶᠢᠨ ᠢ ᠦᠵᠡᠭᠦᠯᠦᠭᠴᠢ ᠢᠨᠤ ᠮᠢᠨᠤ ᠢᠨᠠᠬ ᠪᠤᠢ derjenige der mir Gutes erzeigt, ist mein Freund (wörtlich: der mir Gutes Erzeigende mein Freund ist), ᠡᠭᠦᠨ ᠢ ᠥᠭᠦᠯᠡᠭᠰᠡᠨ ᠢᠨᠤ ᠨᠢᠭᠡ ᠬᠤᠳᠠᠯᠴᠢ ᠠᠵᠤᠭᠤ der diess gesagt hat, ist wohl ein Lügner (wörtlich: der diess Gesagthabende ein Lügner ist oder scheint es zu seyn).

entry.title: Drittes Capitel - Regeln der Wortfügung oder Syntax - Bildung der Sätze

paragraphs.paragraph: Da die zur Verbindung gehörigen Conjunctionen im Mongolischen theils völlig fehlen, theils auch oft als entbehrlich weggelassen werden, so genügen die entsprechenden Gerundia und Participia, so wie einige andere Modi, vornehmlich der Conditionalis, zur Bildung des Vorder- und Nachsatzes, z. B. ᠲᠡᠶᠢᠨ ᠺᠡᠮᠡᠨ ᠥᠭᠦᠯᠡᠭᠡᠳ ᠦᠯᠦ ᠦᠵᠡᠭᠳᠡᠺᠦᠢ ᠪᠣᠯᠪᠠᠢ nachdem er diess gesagt hatte, wurde er unsichtbar (wörtlich: also sagend gesprochen habend, nicht gesehen zu werden er wurde). Ferner mit dem Dativ des Participii Präteriti: ᠡᠴᠡᠭᠡ ᠶᠢᠨ ᠡᠨᠡ ᠮᠡᠲᠦ ᠥᠭᠦᠯᠡᠭᠰᠡᠨ ᠳ᠋ᠤᠷ ᠺᠥᠪᠡᠭᠦᠨ ᠢᠨᠤ ᠶᠡᠺᠡᠳᠡ ᠪᠠᠶᠠᠰᠪᠠᠢ als der Vater diess gesprochen hatte, wurde der Sohn sehr erfreut (wörtlich: auf des Vaters also Gesprochenes der Sohn sehr erfreut wurde). Ferner mit dem Conditionalis: ᠴᠢ ᠨᠠᠳᠤᠷ ᠢᠡᠷᠪᠡᠰᠦ ᠪᠢ ᠴᠢᠮᠠᠳᠤᠷ ᠴᠤ ᠢᠷᠡᠰᠦᠭᠡᠢ wenn du zu mir kommst, so komme ich auch zu dir; oder ᠴᠢ ᠨᠠᠳᠤᠷ ᠡᠰᠡ ᠢᠷᠡᠪᠡᠰᠤ ᠪᠡᠷ ᠪᠤ ᠴᠢᠨᠠᠳᠤᠷ ᠢᠷᠡᠰᠦᠭᠡᠢ wenn du gleich nicht zu mir kommst (kämest), so komme ich doch zu dir; oder auch ᠴᠢ ᠨᠠᠳᠤᠷ ᠡᠰᠡ ᠢᠷᠡᠭᠰᠡᠨ ᠪᠦᠭᠡᠰᠦ ᠪᠡᠷ ᠪᠢ ᠴᠢᠨᠠᠳᠤᠷ ᠢᠷᠡᠺᠦ ᠪᠦᠯᠦᠭᠡ wenn du gleich nicht zu mir gekommen wärest, so wäre ich doch zu dir gekommen, oder würde zu dir gekommen seyn. Ferner mit dem Accusativ des Infinitivs und mit Umwandlung des persönlichen Fürworts in das Possessivum ᠴᠢᠨᠤ ᠨᠠᠳᠤᠷ ᠡᠰᠡ ᠢᠷᠡᠺᠦᠢ ᠶᠢ ᠪᠢ ᠺᠡᠵᠢᠶᠡᠲᠡᠨ ᠮᠡᠳᠡᠯᠦᠭᠡ ich habe es längst gewusst, dass du nicht zu mir kommen würdest (wörtlich: dein zu mir Nichtkommen ich längst gewusst habe).

paragraphs.paragraph: Statt fernerer Satzproben lasse ich zur Uebung das zweite Capital des ᠦᠯᠢᠭᠡᠷ ᠤᠨ ᠳᠠᠯᠠᠢ Üligerün Dalai (Meer der Gleichnisse), nebst den nöthigen Erläuterungen der Wort- und Satzformen und der Uebersetzung hier folgen. Es ist dasselbe, als Erzählung und des leichten Styles wegen, vorzüglich geeignet, dem Bau der Mongolischen Sprache kennen zu lernen.

paragraphs.paragraph: III. Vowels and consonants.

As written above there are altogether thirty letters in the Mongolian alphabet. (If <uig rom="">ᠩ</uig> is not included, it can be said that there are but twenty-nine.) Of these, seven are vowels and twenty-three are consonants. Then what is called a vowel and what is called a consonant? The reply is that those unimpeded sounds which are formed by the air coming from the lungs and freely passing through the mouth passage are called vowel sounds. Those impeded sounds which are formed by the air coming from the lungs through the mouth passage are called consonant sounds.
