paragraphs.paragraph: IV. The forming of syllables.

A syllable is formed by joining together a vowel and a consonant. (It is possible even to form a syllable with vowels only.) In forming a syllable, the vowel is the main part. Therefore without a vowel it is not possible to have a syllable. Also generally two separate vowels do not go together in one syllable.

Up until the present, Mongols studying the Mongol language have not really separated the vowels and the consonants but have persistently learned syllables. Therefore it is easy for Mongols to know the syllables and to consider the old twelve syllabaries as properly made up of syllables.
How the vowels and consonants are joined and what kind of syllables they make:
1. Syllables which are made up of vowels only. Ill: <uig rom="">ᠠ ᠡ‍ ᠢ‍ ᠣ ᠣ ᠥ ᠥ</uig>
2. Syllables which are made up of consonants followed by vowels:

The above chart indicates syllables which are formed only with initial consonants and medial vowels. Besides these there are the syllables such as <uig rom="">ᠨᠠ ᠨᠡ ᠨᠤ ᠬᠠ ᠺᠡ ᠺᠢ</uig> made up of initial consonants and final vowels. Also those such as <uig rom="‍">‍ᠨ᠋‍ᠠ ‍ᠨ᠋‍ᠠ ‍ᠨ᠋‍ᠢ ‍ᠨ᠋‍‍ᠨ᠋‍ᠠ ᠺ‍‍ᠡ ᠺ‍ᠢ‍</uig> made up of medial consonants and medial vowels. Further there are those such as <uig rom="‍">‍ᠨ᠋‍ᠠ ‍ᠨ᠋‍ᠠ ‍ᠨ᠋‍ᠢ ‍ᠨ᠋‍‍ᠨ᠋‍ᠠ ‍ᠭ ᠺ‍ᠢ</uig> made up of medial consonants and final vowels.
3. Syllables which are made up of vowels followed by consonants:
4. Syllables which are composed of three letters: a consonant and a vowel followed by another consonant:

The above chart only shows some syllables which are formed with three letters: an initial consonant and a medial vowel followed by a final consonant. Besides these there are those which are formed by initial consonants, medial vowels followed by medial consonants such as <uig rom="">ᠭᠤᠯ</uig> <uig rom="">ᠳᠠᠷ</uig>. Also there are those which are formed by medial consonants, medial vowels followed by final consonants such as <uig rom="">᠎ᠭᠤᠯ</uig> <uig rom="">ᠳᠠᠷ</uig>. And those which are formed by medial consonants, medial vowels followed by medial consonants such as <uig rom="">᠎ᠭᠤᠯ</uig> <uig rom="">ᠳᠠᠷ</uig>.

paragraphs.paragraph: V. The writing of words.

Words are formed by one or a number of syllables. Therefore a word which is made up of a number of syllables can be easily divided into sections when pronounced.

In writing a word, the very first letter is written in the initial form, the last letter is written in the final form and all the rest between are written in the medial form. Illustration of the use of letters in writing words is shown below:
1. The letter A.

2. The letter E.
Comments: The letters ᠠ and ᠡ though they are distinct in the initial form, yet in the medial and the final forms there is no distinction. When writing a foreign word, the letter ᠡ is written ᠸ, distinguishing it from ᠠ. In using the final form of ᠠ when joining it to the consonants ᠪ, ᠫ, ᠹ, ᠺ it is written in the foreward tail form thus ᠪᠠ ᠫᠠᠹᠠᠺᠠ. The final form of this same letter when joined to the consonants ᠬ, ᠭ, ᠶ, ᠮ, ᠨ, ᠷ is written in the offshoot form thus ᠬ ᠠ ᠭ ᠠ ᠶ ᠠ ᠮ ᠠ ᠨ ᠠ ᠷ ᠠ. In using the final form of ᠡ when joining it to the consonants ᠪ, ᠫ, ᠹ, ᠺ it is written in the foreward tail form thus ᠪᠠ ᠫᠠᠹᠠᠺᠠ. The final form of this same letter when joined to the consonants ᠶ, ᠮ, ᠨ, ᠷ is written in the offshoot tail form thus ᠶ ᠠ ᠮ ᠠ ᠨ ᠠ ᠷ ᠠ.

3. The letter I.
Comments: The medial form of the letter ᠢ when following a consonant is written with a single long tooth but when following a vowel, it is written with a double tooth. The particle ᠎ᠢ is written separately from the original word. ᠭᠠᠷ᠎ᠢ

4. The letter AW.
Comments: In using the final form of ᠣ when it follows the consonants ᠪᠫᠺ it takes the form of ‍ᠣ‍ thus ᠪᠤᠫᠤᠺᠤ. But in words which are taken from a foreign language, the final form of ᠣ is written ‍ᠣ‍.

5. The letter O.
Comments: The form of AW and O are exactly alike. It is not possible to distinguish them, yet at times the AW is written doubled which distinguishes it from O. Illustration: ᠬᠣᠤᠷ᠎ᠠ ᠬᠤᠷ᠎ᠠ

6. The letter U.
Comments: The medial form of the letter ᠦ‍ with the long tooth is written as ᠦ when it appears in the first syllable of a word which begins with a consonant. In other words the ᠦ‍ is always written with a long tooth when it appears as a first syllable of a word. In all other positions it does not have the long tooth. This letter appears as ‍ᠦ after ᠪ, ᠫ, ᠺ, ᠺ.

7. The letter OO.
Comments: The letters ᠦ‍ U and ᠦ‍ OO are the same. Whenever writing a foreign word these letters always appear with the long tooth as: ᠳᠡᠥᠪᠥ

8. The letter N.
Comments: The medial form ‍ᠨ᠋‍ with a dot is used before a vowel while the medial form ‍ᠨ‍ without a dot is used before a consonant. In other words at the beginning of a syllable it is dotted but at the end of a syllable it is not dotted.
The consonant ᠨ when appearing in final form is the same as the final backward tail form of ᠠ and ᠡ. There is a way of knowing which it is: If the preceding letter is a vowel, the final is an ᠨ. If the preceding letter is a consonant then the final is an ᠠ or ᠡ. (The way of knowing whether the final is an ᠠ or ᠡ is to find out whether the word itself is masculine or feminine.)

9. The letter H.
Comments: In masculine wordsᠬ is used and in feminine words ‍ᠬ‍ is used. When joining a forward tail form of ᠡ after the ᠢ a tooth is added and written between. (If such an ᠡ is not added the form would be just the consonant ‍ᠭ.) Though the letter ‍ᠬ‍ does not appear properly as a final in a word or syllable, yet joined with the offshoot form of ‍ᠨ‍‍ᠨ‍ it appears as such.

10. The letter G.
Comments: In feminine words ‍ᠬ‍ ‍ᠬ‍ ‍ᠭ are used; in masculine wordsᠭ ‍ᠭ᠋‍ ‍ᠨ‍‍ᠨ‍ ‍ᠬ ‍ᠭ᠍ are used. With the medial form the double dot is used before a vowel and the dotless form is used before a consonant. In other words at the beginning of a syllable the dotted form is used and at the end of a syllable the dotless form is used. Though the final form is ‍ᠬ yet when this is followed by the offshoot form of ‍ᠨ‍‍ᠨ‍ then it takes the dotted form thus ‍ᠭ᠍.

11. The letter B.
Comments: When joining ᠠ and ᠡ in their medial form to the ᠪ, the ‍ᠨ‍ is directly added. But when joining the forward tail ending form to the ᠪ then an extra tooth is added. (If this extra tooth were not added there would be no distinction between the ᠪᠠ or ᠪᠠ and the ᠪ.)

12. The letter P.
Comments: When joining a forward tail ending form to the ᠡ it follows the same rule of adding a tooth as with ᠪ.

13. The letter S.
Comments: When the vowel ᠢ follows the consonant ᠰ it is pronounced as ᠱ. But when the particle ᠢ follows the final s, it then retains its ᠰᠢ pronunciation.
14. The letter SH.
